There was a baby elephant in the jungle and he was so excited to find the biggest mango ever! He grabbed it and was about to eat it when a monkey stepped out of the trees and said "That mango belongs to me!"

The elephant was scared and backed away but the monkey said "I have an idea! We can play a clapping game. Whoever claps the loudest gets the mango!" 

The elephant didn't understand but the monkey said "It's very simple! Just clap your hands and I'll clap mine and whoever makes the biggest noise wins!" 

The elephant was excited and the monkey said "On the count of three. Ready? One, two, three!"

The two of them clapped their hands and the elephant was surprised to see that the monkey had a much bigger and thicker mouth so he made more noise! The monkey smiled and said "I win!" As he took the mango, he laughed and said "See you soon".

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to run around his house all day long. He would run on the floor and have so much fun. One day, Timmy's mom told him not to run because he might get hurt. But Timmy thought he was strong and could never get hurt.

One day, while running around, Timmy tripped and fell on the floor. He hurt his arm and started to cry. His mom came running to help him. She told him that running can be harmless, but sometimes accidents happen. Timmy learned that it's important to be careful and listen to his mom.

From that day on, Timmy still loved to run, but he always made sure to be careful and not run too fast. He learned that it's better to be safe than sorry.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to play with his toy truck. One day, he went outside to play in the dirt. He used his toy truck to load the dirt and move it from one place to another. Tim had so much fun playing with his truck in the dirt.

After a while, Tim's mom called him inside to do some math. Tim liked to count and add numbers. His mom gave him some blocks to help him learn. Tim counted the blocks and added them together. He was good at math and liked learning new things.

When Tim was done with his math, he looked at his hands. They were filthy from playing with the dirt outside. His mom told him to wash his hands before they could have a snack. Tim washed his hands and they were clean again. Then, he and his mom shared a yummy snack and talked about their day.

Once upon a time, there was a pink bunny named Binky. Binky loved to dance and hop around in the grass. One day, Binky saw a big bird in the sky. The bird was circling around and around. Binky said, "Hello birdie, why are you flying so high?" The bird said, "I am looking for a place to strike my nest." Binky didn't know what "strike" meant, so she asked the bird. The bird said, "It means to hit something really hard." Binky was scared of the bird's nest, so she continued to dance and hop around in the grass.

The little boy was proud. He wanted to show everyone his new toy. It was a red car that could reverse. He liked that it made funny noises. 

He was playing in his room when he heard a loud noise coming from outside. He opened the window to see what was happening. He saw a big witch! She was very scary. 

The witch saw the little boy. She asked him where she could find more children like him. The little boy was scared. He pointed down the street. 

The witch thanked the little boy and flew away. The little boy felt proud that the witch asked him for help. He continued playing with his toy and had a lot of fun.

Mummy was playing with her little boy Toby. She said, "Toby, I want to teach you something special." Toby looked scared.
"What is it?" Toby asked.
Mummy smiled. She pointed at the pond and said, "Look, there's a frog." Toby was excited! He ran over to the pond and saw the small frog hopping around. Mummy said, "I'm going to teach you how to be kind to animals. Can you do that?" Toby nodded.

Mummy gave Toby some food to give to the frog. Toby carefully placed the food near the frog and waited. The frog slowly inched toward the food. Toby was so excited.

Mummy said, "See, you did it! You taught the frog a lesson about being kind." Toby smiled and said, "I like teaching frogs!"

Once upon a time there was a nice boy named Jack. He wanted to go for a drive so he asked his mom for the license. His mom said yes but first Jack had to unlock the door.

"Do I need a key to unlock it?", Jack asked.

His mom said, "No, you need a special license to unlock it. You need to go to the store to get one."

So, Jack went to the store and found a license that wasn't too expensive. He put the cheap license in the door and it unlocked it!

Jack was so excited - he finally got to go for a drive. He waved goodbye to his mom, jumped in the car and drove away. 

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy. He was so happy because he had a big yard all to himself. He could play and explore all he wanted.

One day, he found a funny-looking something in the corner. It was small and fit in his hand. He touched it and it was fun! He saw it had something inside. He wanted to fit it together and find out what was inside!

He tried and tried to fit the pieces together but it was too hard. He realized he needed help. So, he asked his mom to come outside and help. 

She smiled and said, "I'm here to help!" Her warm touch made the pieces fit perfectly! When they were done, they saw it was a new toy! He was so excited and ran inside to play! 

The end.

Sara and Ben are friends. They like to play at the gym. The gym has many toys and balls and mats. Sara and Ben have fun at the gym.

One day, Sara and Ben go to the gym. But the gym is not the same. The gym is filthy. There is dirt and trash and bugs everywhere. The toys and balls and mats are broken and dirty. Sara and Ben are sad and scared.

"Who did this to the gym?" Sara asks.

"I don't know. Maybe a bad person or a big animal," Ben says.

"We can't play here. It's too yucky and dangerous," Sara says.

"Let's go tell the teacher. Maybe she can help," Ben says.

Sara and Ben run to the teacher. They tell her what they saw. The teacher is shocked and angry.

"Who could change the gym like this? This is not okay. We have to clean it up and fix it," the teacher says.

The teacher calls some other teachers and helpers. They go to the gym with Sara and Ben. They bring brooms and bags and tools. They work hard to clean and fix the gym. They throw away the trash and bugs. They wash the dirt and dust. They mend the toys and balls and mats. They make the gym nice and clean and safe again.

Sara and Ben are happy and grateful. They thank the teacher and the helpers. They go back to the gym. They play with the toys and balls and mats. They have fun at the gym.

Mama was measuring something. It was a big oak tree in their garden. She was very impatient. She kept on measuring it over and over again.

Mama was very excited. She was making something special for Daddy. She wanted it to be perfect.

Mama was so impatient. She kept on measuring and measuring. She measured it from the top, from the sides and from the bottom.

At last, she was finished. She smiled, she was very pleased. It was perfect!

Mama knew Daddy would be so happy. She couldn't wait to show him what she had made. She was so excited!

Once upon a time, there was a pig. This pig was different. He had a big, red spot on his face. The other pigs did not have this spot. They did not like the different pig.

One day, a mean pig said, "You are not like us. Go away!" The different pig was sad. He wanted to be friends with the other pigs. He tried to play with them, but they ran away.

The different pig was very sad. He saw a big tree. He wanted to slap the tree to let out his feelings. He slapped the tree, but the tree fell down! It hit the mean pig's house. The mean pig was very mad. The different pig had to leave the farm.

Once there was an old man who had almost no hair on his head. He was a very bald old man. He had a lot of strange gear that he wanted to spread far and wide. Every day, he put pieces of the gear into a big bag and set off on his journey. He spread the gear all over the world, until there was gear in every corner of the planet. 

But no matter how far he spread the gear, he always came back to the same place. One day while the old man was standing in a field, a little girl with pigtails walked up to him. She asked him why he spread the gear everywhere.

The old man smiled and said, â€œI spread gear so everyone can have something special. I spread gear because I want everyone to be happy.â€ The little girl was so happy she hugged the old man, and as she hugged him, the gear began to spread around them. That old man and that little girl are still spreading the gear today.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Mary. She had a pet rabbit called Bobo. Mary loved Bobo very much.

One day Mary took Bobo outside. She saw an old velvet swing hanging from a tree. Mary asked Bobo, "Can you swing on it?"

Bobo hopped up to the swing and said, "I can try!" He hopped onto the swing and hung on tight.

Together, Mary and Bobo had a lot of fun swinging on the old velvet swing. They hung on it for hours, until the sun went down. 

Finally, Mary said, "We have to go home now." And the two said goodbye to the old velvet swing and went home together.

Once upon a time, there was a bunny called Benny. He stayed in his home, which was full of soil.

One day, Benny noticed a cat in the garden. He started to make silly noises and he hopped around the soil.

Suddenly, the cat started to meow and Benny knew that meant he should behave. He stopped hopping and he stood very still like a statue.

The cat came to Benny and said, "Hello Benny! You were being silly!" Benny was so embarrassed.

He said, "I'm sorry. I'll try to behave better next time." The cat said, "It's okay Benny! Just remember to be a good rabbit and behave." 

Benny smiled, said thank you and the cat hopped away. From that day onwards, Benny always remembered to be good and behave.

Once upon a time, there was a smart bird. The bird wanted to explore the world, so one day it decided to fly to a distant land. After a long trip, it arrived at the top of a big mountain. The bird had never seen a mountain before and was curious. 

When it got nearer to the mountain, it realized that it was a volcano! At first, the bird was scared, but it decided to be brave and open the volcano. 

Inside the volcano, it found lots of precious gems and stones! However, the bird realized that the volcano was home to animals and it should not take the things that did not belong to it. So, it left the volcano without taking anything. 

The bird learned a valuable lesson that day: being smart is not only about knowing what things to take, but also what things not to take.

Bella was walking down the hallway when she stumbled on the floor. She was feeling bad, so she decided to take the elevator. 

When she stepped inside the elevator, it began to make funny noises. Bella was scared and stepped back, but the doors closed before she could get out. 

The elevator went up and down, but it was taking too long. Bella was getting scared because now it was dark and noisy. She wanted to get out! 

Suddenly, the elevator stopped and the doors opened. Bella quickly stumbled out and ran down the hallway to her parents. She was so glad she was done with the bad elevator.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play at the park with his friends. One day, they went to the big slide and Timmy went down it really fast. He yelled "Whee!" as he slid down.

After that, they went to the swings and Timmy felt like he was zooming through the air. He loved the feeling of the wind in his hair. Suddenly, Timmy's friend found a penny on the ground. Timmy said, "Wow, you're so lucky!"

They played until the sun went down and it was time for Timmy to go home. He went to bed feeling happy and lucky to have such great friends. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a generous musician named Tom. He played music for kids in the park. He had a big drum, a small flute, and a shiny guitar. Every day, Tom would go to the park and play songs for the kids to dance and sing along.

One day, Tom met a little girl named Lucy. She was sad because she couldn't count. Tom wanted to help Lucy, so he had an idea. He said, "Lucy, I can teach you how to count with my music!"

Tom played a song on his guitar. He sang, "One, two, three, four, five," and Lucy listened carefully. Soon, Lucy started to count along with Tom's song. She smiled and clapped her hands.

After a while, Lucy could count all the way to ten! She was so happy, and she thanked Tom for helping her. From that day on, Lucy and Tom became good friends. They spent many days in the park, counting and playing music together.

The hook was organized on the wall. It had lots of different things hanging from it. Grandpa showed Tommy all of the things, and told him to take care of them.

Tommy was excited to try the hook. He took an old baseball and passed it around. Everyone laughed as they watched Tommy play and pass the ball.

Grandpa then showed Tommy a hat to give to Grandma. Tommy passed the hat to Grandma and she smiled. Grandma thanked Tommy for being so organized.

Tommy nodded and felt proud. He was happy that he knew how to use the hook and make people happy.

Lily and Ben are twins. They like to play in their house. They have many toys and books. But they also like to explore new places.

One day, they find a door in the hall. The door is green. It has a lock and a key. Lily and Ben are curious. They want to see what is behind the door.

"Let's open it!" Lily says. She takes the key from the hook. She puts it in the lock. She turns it. The door opens.

"Wow!" Ben says. He sees a stair. The stair goes up and up. It is dark and dusty. He wants to go up the stair.

"Come on, Lily!" Ben says. He urges Lily to follow him. He starts to climb the stair.

"Wait, Ben!" Lily says. She is scared. She does not want to go up the stair. She thinks it is dangerous. She wants to stay in the hall.

"No, Lily!" Ben says. He is excited. He does not think it is dangerous. He thinks it is fun. He wants to see what is at the top of the stair.

"Please, Lily!" Ben says. He urges Lily again. He is almost at the top of the stair.

"Okay, Ben!" Lily says. She loves Ben. She does not want to make him sad. She decides to follow him. She climbs the stair.

They reach the top of the stair. They see a window. The window is big and bright. They look out of the window. They see the sky and the trees and the birds. They smile.

They hear a voice. The voice is loud and angry. It is their mom.

"Lily! Ben! What are you doing up there? Come down right now!"

Lily and Ben are scared. They run down the stair. They close the door. They put the key back on the hook. They hug each other.

They are sorry. They know they did something wrong. They promise to never open the green door again.

One day, a train was going down the track. The train had a big engine that made loud noises. The engine was red and shiny. The train was going very slow because it had a lot of heavy things on it. 

The conductor of the train saw a little boy on the side of the track. He waved to the boy and said, "hello!" The boy waved back and said, "hi!" The conductor smiled and continued down the track. 

As the train went by, the little boy watched the engine and thought it was so cool. He liked how it was big and shiny. He also thought it was funny how the train was going so slow. The little boy waved goodbye to the train and went back to playing with his toys.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy liked to play outside with his friends. One day, they decided to build a fort in the woods. They used a saw to cut some branches and made a big pile. 

While they were building the fort, Timmy saw a squirrel running up a tree. He got nervous because he thought it might be a scary animal. But then the squirrel stopped and looked at Timmy. 

Suddenly, the wind started to blow and it got really cold. Timmy's friends told him to freeze and be quiet. They saw a big deer walking by and didn't want to scare it away. Timmy was so amazed by the deer that he forgot to be nervous. They all watched as the deer walked away into the woods. Timmy and his friends had a great adventure that day! The end.

There was once a popular acorn named Wally. He always liked to store things away in the forest. Wally was a very ambitious acorn. Every day he dreamed of finding something bigger and better to store away. Little did he know that this ambition would lead him to his downfall.

One day as he was storing away some twigs and leaves in a hollow tree, he heard a rustling in the bushes. Looking around for the source of the rustling, he saw a hungry fox. The fox eyed him hungrily and started to move towards him. 

"Uh oh," said Wally, quickly grabbing a few nuts to distract the fox. The fox diverted his attention and eagerly chased after the nuts. Just before the fox ran off Wally called out, "Be careful, friend!" 

Wally continued to store things away in the forest, but he was now more wary of who else he shared the woods with. Little did he know that his kind words would save his life in the future. 

One day, a drought hit the forest and left Wally with no food and water. He was beginning to weaken when one day, the same fox who he had given the nuts to, came to his aid. The fox had remembered Wally's kindness and came with an acorn- the same type of acorn that Wally was!
