Once upon a time there was a prince who lived in a castle. Every day, the prince was very calm.

One day, the prince looked out of his window, and he saw something very special in the sky. It was a shining star! The prince was very excited. He wanted to see the star up close. 

So the prince asked his servants for help. They helped him to get a ladder and climb up a very tall hill. When the prince got to the top of the hill, he was amazed.

The star was so bright and beautiful. Its light shone so bright that the prince could feel it on his face. The prince felt very happy and peaceful.

He stayed and watched the star twinkle until it was time to go back home. He promised himself that he would come back to see the star again soon.

Since that day, the prince has visited the star every day to see its peaceful light shine.

Lily and Tom are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they meet a big dog. The dog is fierce. It barks and growls at them. Lily and Tom are scared.

They run to the exit. But the dog runs after them. It is faster than them. It catches up with them. It jumps on Tom and bites his leg. Tom cries out loud.

Lily sees a stick. She picks it up. She hits the dog with the stick. The dog lets go of Tom. It yelps and runs away. Lily helps Tom get up. They hug each other.

They see a lady. She is the dog's owner. She is sorry. She says the dog is not bad. It is just scared of new people. She gives Tom a band-aid for his leg. She says sorry again.

Lily and Tom forgive her. They say goodbye to her and the dog. They go home. They are brave. They are still friends.

Once upon a time, there was a stretchy cat. He was the stretchiest cat in the world! He was always stretching himself, from his big toes all the up to his ears. One day, the stretchy cat came across a wet spot on the ground. His friends warned him not to go near it because it might be dangerous, but the stretchy cat wasn't scared! He decided to stretch as far as he could and touch the wet spot.

When the stretchy cat finally touched the wet spot, something magical happened! The wet spot changed into a big, tasty cake! He was so excited, he couldn't believe his eyes! The stretchy cat immediately started eating the cake and it was the most delicious treat he had ever tasted.

The stretchy cat enjoyed his tasty treat and was so thankful that he had decided to stretch and take a chance. He knew that he would always love stretching and he hoped his friends would learn to take chances too. The end!

One day, a large worm was in the garden. It saw a big shoe. The worm did not want to get stepped on. So, the worm said, "Please do not step on me!"

A little boy heard the worm. He looked down and saw the worm. The boy said, "I will not step on you, worm. But you must help me find my toy."

The worm and the boy looked for the toy. They looked under rocks and in the grass. They could not find the toy. The boy got mad. He said, "You did not help me find my toy. Now, I will step on you!"

The worm was sad. It tried to run away. But the boy stepped on the worm. The worm was gone. The boy did not find his toy. No one was happy.

Ben likes to do many things. He likes to play with his cars, to draw with his crayons, and to read his books. But his favorite thing to do is to pretend he is a superhero. He has a red bathrobe that he wears as a cape. He thinks it makes him powerful and fast.

One day, he was playing in his room with his bathrobe. He jumped on his bed and shouted, "I am Super Ben! I can fly and save the world!" He flew to his window and looked outside. He saw a cat stuck on a tree. He said, "Oh no! A cat needs my help! I will rescue it!"

He ran downstairs and opened the door. He saw his mom in the kitchen. He said, "Mom, I have to go and save a cat! I am Super Ben!" His mom smiled and said, "OK, Super Ben, but be careful and don't go too far. And put on your shoes, it's cold outside."

Ben put on his shoes and ran to the tree. He saw the cat meowing and looking scared. He said, "Don't worry, cat, I am here to help you. I am Super Ben!" He tried to climb the tree, but it was too high and slippery. He said, "Oh no! How can I reach the cat?"

He looked around and saw a ladder leaning on a fence. He said, "Aha! I can use the ladder!" He dragged the ladder to the tree and set it up. He climbed the ladder and reached the cat. He said, "There you go, cat, you are safe now. Come with me." He picked up the cat and put it in his bathrobe. He climbed down the ladder and hugged the cat. He said, "You are a good cat. Do you want to be my friend?"

The cat purred and licked his face. He said, "I think you do. Let's go home and play." He ran back to his house with the cat in his bathrobe. He saw his mom waiting for him. He said, "Mom, look, I saved a cat! Can I keep it?" His mom looked at the cat and said, "Wow, Super Ben, you are very brave and kind. You can keep the cat, but you have to take good care of it. What will you name it?" Ben thought for a moment and said, "I will name it Power. Because it is powerful, like me." His mom smiled and said, "That's a great name. Come on, let's go inside and give Power some food and water. And you, Super Ben, you need a bath. You are very dirty from your adventure." Ben said, "OK, Mom, but can I wear my bathrobe after the bath? I still want to be Super Ben." His mom said, "Of course, you can. You are always Super Ben to me."

Once upon a time there was a frightened bird. He was very scared because there was a missile near his nest. He didn't know what to do.

Then, a little mouse came hopping by. He asked the bird why he was so sad.

The bird said, "I'm fearful of the missile near my nest. I'm afraid it will hurt me!"

The little mouse said, "Don't worry my friend. I'll help you!"

The mouse hopped up to the missile, gave it a big kiss, then quickly hopped away. 

The bird was amazed. He saw that the missile was no longer there. The mouse had made it disappear.

The bird was so happy that he flew down and gave the mouse a big hug and a kiss.

From then on, the bird and the mouse were the best of friends. They helped each other whenever they were in need.

Tom and Sam are brothers. They like to play with their toy boat. They have a big tub of water in the yard. They put the boat in the water and make it sail. They pretend they are pirates and look for treasure.

One day, they hear a loud noise. It is a real boat on the river. The boat is big and has a big sail. It has a flag with a skull and bones. Tom and Sam are scared. They think it is a pirate boat.

They run to their mom and tell her what they see. Mom smiles and says, "Don't worry, boys. That is not a pirate boat. That is a boat from a museum. It is very old and very wise. It knows a lot of stories about the sea. It is here to teach people about history."

Tom and Sam are curious. They want to learn more about the boat. Mom says, "Maybe we can go and see it tomorrow. We can ask the people on the boat to tell us some stories. Would you like that?"

Tom and Sam nod and say, "Yes, please!" They are happy and excited. They go back to their tub and make their toy boat sail. They pretend they are sailors and look for adventure.

Once upon a time there was a soldier, who was brave and strong. One day, the soldier was walking in the park, when he saw a happy, clear fish swimming in the pond. He watched it spinning around in circles, and thought it was the most beautiful sight!

The soldier went back to the pond the next day, but the fish had gone. He looked high and low, but he could not find it. He was so sad, he almost wanted to cry!

But suddenly he heard a voice. It was the voice of the clear fish, saying, "Don't worry, soldier. Just look up at the sky. I will be spinning up there in the clouds!"

The soldier looked up and sure enough, in the clear sky he could see the fish spinning in circles! From then on the soldier was never alone, wherever he went he could look up and see the fish spinning and smiling at him.

Once upon a time, there was a car. The car had an engine that was very powerful. All around the car, everyone was alert. The car was going forward but then it started to reverse. The driver used the engine to make the car go back. The car went back and back until it was far away. Everyone watching the car was so surprised! The car had reversed for quite a long way. In the end, the car stopped reversing and went forward again. Everyone cheered because the car had used the engine to reverse!

Once upon a time, there was a little duck named Ducky. Ducky loved to swim in the pond. The pond was big and blue and had fish in it. Ducky liked to swim and play with the fish.

One day, Ducky saw a big, black cloud in the sky. She knew it might rain soon. She wanted to taste the raindrops, so she stayed in the pond. When the rain started to fall, Ducky opened her beak and tasted the raindrops.

But then, the rain got heavier and heavier. The pond started to get bigger and bigger. Ducky realized that she needed to get out of the pond before it flooded. She flapped her wings and flew away, just in time. From that day on, Ducky knew to be careful when it rained.

Once upon a time, there was a bird named Breezy. Breezy loved to fly high in the sky and feel the wind on her feathers. She would soar over the trees and the houses, feeling free and happy.

One day, Breezy saw a big volcano. It was very tall and had smoke coming out of it. Breezy knew she shouldn't fly too close to the volcano because it was dangerous. She decided to stay away and fly in a different direction.

As Breezy was flying away, she saw some trash on the ground. There were cans and papers all over the place. Breezy knew that this was not good for the environment. She wanted to help keep the world clean, so she started picking up the trash with her beak and putting it in a nearby bin.

Breezy learned that it's important to stay away from danger and to keep the world clean. She felt proud of herself for doing a good deed and continued to soar in the sky, feeling happy and free.

Once there was a family who lived in a farm near the mountains. They had lots of animals and grew corn.

One day, mama called the family outside to look at the corn. It was tall, thick and golden. Papa smiled, proud of his work.

Daddy said: "We will give the animals some of this corn to raise. Let's start with the chickens."

Then, mama and papa gave the chickens some corn. They ate it up and said cluck, cluck! They were so happy, now they could raise and be strong.

Mama said: "Look, they love the thick corn." 

The family watched the chickens eat their corn and then papa said: "It's time to pick more corn." 

Mama and papa went inside to get their buckets and bags for picking.

The family cheerfully continued to raise the corn in their farm, every day.

Tom was sad. He wanted to play with his new car, but his mom said no. She said he had to wear his new shirt first. Tom did not like his new shirt. It had red and blue strips on it. He thought it was stupid.

He put on his new shirt, but he did not button it. He ran to his room and grabbed his new car. He wanted to zoom it on the floor. But his mom saw him and stopped him. She said he had to button his shirt first. She said it was cold outside and he would get sick.

Tom sighed. He did not want to button his shirt. He thought it was hard and boring. He wanted to play with his new car. He tried to button his shirt, but he could not. He got angry and pulled his shirt off. He threw it on the floor and yelled, "I hate this shirt!"

His mom was not happy. She picked up his shirt and said, "Tom, that is not nice. You have to wear your shirt. It is a gift from your grandma. She made it for you. She loves you very much."

Tom felt bad. He did not want to make his mom or his grandma sad. He said, "I'm sorry, mom. I love you and grandma too. But I don't like this shirt. Can I wear a different shirt?"

His mom smiled. She said, "OK, Tom. You can wear a different shirt. But you have to say thank you to grandma for this shirt. And you have to be careful with your new car. It is also a gift from her."

Tom nodded. He said, "Thank you, grandma, for this shirt and this car. I will be careful with them." He hugged his mom and put on a different shirt. He buttoned it by himself. He was proud. He ran to his room and played with his new car. He was happy.

One day, a group of 3 year old kids were searching for a new toy. They looked for hours but couldn't decide which toy to get. Suddenly, the kids noticed the staff at the store had lots of games and cute cuddly creatures. They decided to get one of the cuddly creatures.

The kids looked around to find the cleanest and tidiest one. They noticed a big, fluffy bear that was spotlessly clean and very tidy. They decided to take the big, fluffy bear home with them.

Back at home, the kids were very excited to show their new toy to their parents. When their parents saw the big, fluffy bear, they were very happy with how clean and tidy it was.

The kids were delighted that the staff had helped them decide on the perfect toy. They hugged their big, fluffy bear tightly and promised to always keep it clean and tidy.

Sara and Ben are twins. They like to play together, but sometimes they tease each other. One day, they are having lunch with Mom. Mom gives them soup and celery. Sara likes celery, but Ben does not.

"Yuck, I don't want celery. It is green and hard and tastes like grass," Ben says. He pushes his plate away.

Sara smiles and picks up a piece of celery. She crunches it loudly and says, "Celery is yummy and good for you. You are silly, Ben. You don't know what you are missing."

Ben frowns and says, "No, you are silly, Sara. You are eating rabbit food. You will grow long ears and hop around."

Sara laughs and says, "No, I won't. You are just jealous because I like celery and you don't."

She waves the celery in front of Ben's face and says, "Do you want some? Do you want some?"

Ben gets angry and tries to grab the celery from Sara. They start to fight and spill their soup on the table. Mom hears the noise and comes to see what is wrong.

"Stop it, both of you. You are making a mess. Why are you teasing each other?" Mom says.

Sara and Ben look at Mom and feel sorry. They say, "We are sorry, Mom. We were just playing."

Mom says, "Playing is fine, but teasing is not nice. You should share and be kind to each other. Now, help me clean up this mess and finish your lunch. And Ben, try to eat some celery. It is good for you."

Sara and Ben nod and say, "OK, Mom. We will."

They help Mom tidy the table and eat their lunch. They decide not to tease each other anymore. They hug and say, "We love you, Mom. We love you, Sara. We love you, Ben."

Once upon a time, there was a bald man who lived in the city. He loved to walk around and look at all the buildings. One day, he saw a shiny red ball and wanted to grab it. But a big dog saw the ball too and ran to grab it first. The bald man and the dog both wanted the ball and started to fight over it. The man was very sad because he really wanted the ball. Suddenly, a kind little girl came and said, "Don't fight, you can share the ball!" The man and the dog were happy and played with the ball together. From that day on, they became friends and walked around the city together, looking at all the buildings. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved cookies and always asked her mom for one after dinner. One day, her mom gave her a big cookie, but Lily was too excited and dropped it on the ground. She was upset and cried.

Her mom said, "Don't be upset, Lily. We can balance the cookie on your nose."

Lily was confused but let her mom balance the cookie on her nose. She was so proud and happy that she forgot about being upset. But then, her dog ran up to her and barked loudly, making her jump. The cookie fell off her nose and into the dog's mouth.

Lily was upset again, but her mom said, "Don't worry, Lily. We can bake more cookies tomorrow." And Lily smiled, knowing that she would get another cookie soon.

Once upon a time there were two friends. They were both cats and they had so much fun together. 

The cats liked to play in the park, climb trees, and explore the forests. One day, they were walking in the forest and they found something very special. It was a big, shiny paw. 

The cats knew this paw was very unique and wanted to keep it for themselves. They began to quarrel about who would keep the paw. As they argued, they scratched each other with their claws and chased each other around. 

After a while, they stopped arguing. Suddenly, they came up with a unique idea. They decided to keep the paw together. 

So they kept the paw and became best friends forever. They promised to never quarrel over it again.

One day, Bob was walking through a peaceful landscape. He smiled as the birds flew in the sky above. He could see a tree off in the distance and decided to go for a closer look.

When Bob reached the tree he heard a sound. It was a whistle! He looked around but couldn't see anyone. He started to whistle back, and then he saw a squirrel on the ground.

The squirrel said hello to Bob. Bob asked if he could join him and the squirrel said yes. Together they played hide and seek and lots of other games. Bob felt so happy in this peaceful landscape, and he knew he was going to come back to play with his new friend soon.

Ben and Mia like to collect rocks. They have a big box of rocks in their room. Some rocks are shiny, some are smooth, some are colorful. They like to look at their rocks and make shapes with them.

One day, they go to the park with their mom. They see a lot of rocks on the ground. They run to pick them up. "Look, Mia, this one is sparkly!" Ben says. He shows Mia a rock that has glitter on it. "Wow, Ben, that's pretty!" Mia says. She sees a rock that has stripes on it. "Look, Ben, this one is original!" She says. She shows Ben a rock that has different colors on it.

They put their rocks in their pockets. They want to take them home and add them to their box. They keep looking for more rocks. They do not see a big rock in their way. They trip over it and fall down. They scrape their knees and elbows. They feel pain. They cry.

Their mom hears them and runs to them. She hugs them and kisses them. She says, "Oh, no, my sweeties, are you okay?" She looks at their wounds and says, "You have some boo-boos. Let's go home and clean them up. You are very brave."

Ben and Mia nod. They still feel pain, but they feel better with their mom. They remember their rocks. They take them out of their pockets and show them to their mom. They say, "Look, mom, we collect rocks. They are shiny and smooth and colorful and original." Their mom smiles and says, "They are very nice rocks. You are very smart and creative. I'm proud of you." She takes their rocks and puts them in her bag. She says, "Let's go home and put them in your box. Then we can have some ice cream. How does that sound?" Ben and Mia smile and say, "Yes, please!" They hold their mom's hand and walk home. They are happy.

Lily likes to count. She counts her fingers, her toes, her dolls, and her books. She counts everything she sees. One day, she wants to count the caps on the bottles in the kitchen. She climbs on a chair and reaches for the shelf. But she slips and falls. She hits her head on the floor. It hurts a lot. She cries.

Mom hears Lily cry and runs to the kitchen. She sees Lily on the floor with a bump on her head. She hugs Lily and says, "Oh, no, my sweetie, are you okay?" She picks up Lily and takes her to the sofa. She puts some ice on Lily's bump and kisses it. She says, "It will be better soon, don't worry."

Lily stops crying and snuggles with Mom. She says, "I'm sorry, Mom, I wanted to count the caps." Mom says, "I know, honey, you love to count. But you have to be careful. The shelf is too high for you. You could get hurt. Next time, ask me for help, okay?" Lily nods and says, "Okay, Mom, I will." Mom says, "I love you, Lily, you are very smart and brave." Lily says, "I love you, Mom, you are very kind and gentle." They hug and smile. Lily feels better. She counts the ice cubes on her bump. She says, "One, two, three, four, five. Five ice cubes." Mom says, "That's right, Lily, you are very good at counting." They laugh and cuddle. Lily is happy.

One day there was a little mouse who had been looking for something new to explore. As he made his way through the forest, the mouse heard something strange. He stopped and listened closely. He heard a noise that almost sounded like singing. He wanted to find out what it was and see if he could join in. 

The mouse followed the sound until he saw a gloomy trap. He was curious, so he went up to it and peered inside. There was a bird with beautiful yellow feathers singing inside the trap. The mouse felt sorry for the bird and wanted to help it get out. 

The mouse looked around for something that he could use to break open the trap. He found a large rock and he carefully placed it near the trap. With one big push, he was able to break open the trap and the bird flew away happily. 
 
The mouse watched the bird fly away and was glad that he could help. He had a feeling that he had just made this gloomy forest a little brighter.

Once upon a time, there was a princess who was very proud. She liked to wear a beautiful dress every day. But one day, something strange happened.

The princess was playing outside when she saw a missile coming from the sky. She was scared and ran back inside her castle. 

When she entered the castle, she saw the King and said: "Daddy, there was a missile outside the castle". 

The King looked proud. "Don't worry, princess," he said, "That was not a real missile. That was a fireworks missile, and it was very special."

"Special?" asked the princess. 

"Yes, special," said the King. "It was to celebrate something important. A very special mission was completed, and that was why the missile was launched."

The Princess smiled. She was happy to know that the missile was nothing to worry about. From that day on, the princess always smiled proudly whenever she wore her beautiful dress.

One day, a little boy named Tim found a shiny coin on the ground. He was very happy. He wanted to buy a toy with the coin. Tim put the coin in his pocket and went to the store.

At the store, a compassionate old lady was working. She saw Tim and smiled. Tim picked a toy and showed the coin to the lady. She said, "That's a special coin, Tim. You can keep it and have the toy too." Tim was very thankful.

As Tim left the store, he saw a cat. The cat looked sick. It sneezed and Tim felt sad. He remembered the compassionate lady and wanted to help the cat. Tim gave the cat his special coin, and the cat got better. Tim was happy that he could help the cat with his special coin.

Tommy was tired and tired. He rubbed his eyes and yawned. He was so frustrated! He wanted to receive his new toy today.

He waited and waited but nothing came. So, he got up and looked around the room. He saw a stamp and picked it up. He thought he could use it to make his own toy. 

He took the stamp and colored with it. But the colors smeared and the stamp was too hard. He was getting more and more frustrated!

Finally, he gave up. He threw the stamp across the room, but suddenly heard a loud crash. His new toy just broke! Everything was broken. 

Tommy was so sad and angry. He had been so frustrated, and now his dreams were also broken.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to go on walks in the forest with her mommy. One day, while they were walking, they found a big mushroom. It was amazing! It was so big that Lily's mommy said they could both fit under it. So, they sat down and had a picnic under the mushroom. They ate sandwiches and drank juice while they enjoyed the shade. It was a fun day for Lily and her mommy.

Once upon a time, there was a flower. The flower was very small and it lived in a garden. The flower was restless and it wanted to be big and strong. One day, the flower saw a tower in the distance. The tower was very tall and it looked very strong. The flower wanted to be like the tower.

So, the flower tried very hard to grow big and strong. It drank lots of water and it reached towards the sun. Finally, the flower bloomed and it was big and beautiful.

But then, a storm came and the wind blew very hard. The flower was not strong enough to withstand the wind and it was blown away. The flower realized that it was better to be small and safe than big and in danger.

The moral of the story is that it's important to be happy with who you are and not try to be something you're not.

Once upon a time, there was a pipe. It was a cheap pipe. It was so cheap, it was almost falling apart.

One day, the pipe was so wobbly that it started to part. The top part of the pipe flew up in the air and the bottom part fell to the ground. Both parts were very sad.

So the top part said, "If we work together, maybe we can get back together!" The bottom part agreed.

They started looking for things to help put them back together. They found string, glue and tape. They worked hard and eventually, the pipe was put back together. Now it was stronger and more secure.

The top part and the bottom part were so happy that they stayed together forever. They lived happily ever after!

Once upon a time there was a mighty knight named Sir Erik. He lived in a great big castle and enjoyed going on adventures around the kingdom. 

One day, Sir Erik heard loud screams coming from a nearby village. He quickly jumped on his horse and rode to the village as fast as he could.

When he arrived, he saw a group of villagers cowering in fear behind a big tree. He asked them what was going on and they told him that a bad dragon had come to the village and started to cause trouble. 

Sir Erik had a plan. He stood in front of the dragon and shouted, "STOP!" But the dragon didn't listen. Quickly, Sir Erik ran to a nearby shed and grabbed the biggest stick he could find. He struck the dragon hard and it flew away never to be seen again.

The villagers were very happy and said, "Thank you Sir Erik! You saved us from this mighty emergency!" Sir Erik smiled and said, "It's my job as a knight to keep you safe!"

Once upon a time there was a smart glove. The glove was so smart that it could shrink.

One day, a 3 year old boy saw the glove and decided to touch it. As soon as he touched the glove, it started to shrink! The boy was so surprised that he jumped back and said, "Woah!".

Then the glove started talking! It said, "Hello. I'm a shrinking glove. I can shrink and get very small. Do you want to play?"

The boy thought it was a great idea and said, "Yes! Let's play shrinky glove!" So they took turns shrinking and growing the glove. The boy had so much fun with the glove and they played together all day. 

At the end of the day, the boy was very tired and the glove was no longer shrinking. He put the glove on his hand and said, "Goodbye, shrinking glove! I had so much fun playing with you today." 

The glove smiled and said, "Bye bye! I had a great time playing with you too!". And with that, both the boy and the glove went off to have another wonderful day.

Once upon a time, there was a playful puppy named Spot. Spot loved to play with his toys and chew on bones. One day, Spot smelled something yummy coming from the oven. He wanted to see what it was, so he jumped up and accidentally turned the oven on. 

Spot didn't know what he had done and went back to playing with his toys. Soon, the oven started to get really hot and smoke started to come out. Spot didn't know what to do and started to bark for help. 

But it was too late. The oven caught on fire and the whole house burned down. Poor Spot didn't make it out alive. His family was very sad and missed him very much. They learned to always be careful around ovens and to never leave them on when they're not using them.

Once upon a time, in a pretty forest, many animals lived together. They all were friends and played with each other every day. One day, the animals decided to have a big race to see who was the fastest. They were all very excited and started to practice running.

On the day of the race, all the animals lined up to run. The rabbit said, "I am very fast, I will win!" The squirrel said, "No, I am faster, I will win!" All the animals talked about who would win the race. They were all ready to run and have fun.

The race began, and all the animals ran as fast as they could. The rabbit and the squirrel were in the front, running very fast. But then, a pretty butterfly flew by. The rabbit and the squirrel stopped to look at the pretty butterfly. They forgot about the race!

While they were looking at the butterfly, the turtle kept running. He was slow, but he did not stop. The turtle crossed the finish line and won the race! All the animals cheered for the turtle. They learned that it is not always the fastest who wins, but the one who keeps going. And they all had a great day in the pretty forest.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to look up at the night sky and see all the stars twinkle. One night, she saw a very special star that was bigger and brighter than all the others. She whispered to herself, "Wow, that star is so pretty!"

Suddenly, a bald eagle flew down and landed on a nearby tree. "Hello, little girl," said the eagle. "I heard you whispering about the star. It's my favorite too!"

Lily was surprised that the eagle could understand her. "Can you show me where the star is?" she asked. The eagle nodded and flew up into the sky. Lily followed the eagle's lead and looked up at the star. It was even more beautiful up close.

"Thank you for showing me, Mr. Eagle," said Lily. "I'll never forget this moment." The eagle smiled and flew away into the night sky, leaving Lily with a memory she would cherish forever.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Jack. Jack was playing in the park when he saw his friend, Lily. Lily looked sad.

Jack asked, "What's wrong, Lily?"

Lily said, "I lost my way home. Can you bring me home?"

Jack said, "Sure! Let's go!"

On the way home, Jack noticed that Lily looked uncomfortable. He asked, "Are you okay, Lily?"

Lily said, "Yes, I'm just tired."

Jack said, "Don't worry, we'll be home soon." 

Finally, Jack brought Lily home safely. Lily's mommy was so happy to see her. She said, "Thank you, Jack, for bringing Lily home. You're such a good friend!"

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Abigail. She was so excited to go to Grandma's house with her family. Grandma always had the best surprise treats! 

When Abigail got to Grandma's house, Grandma had a special treat for her. She showed Abigail a pot of bubbling spaghetti and a big spoon. Grandma said, "Abigail, I need you to keep stirring this spaghetti so it doesn't stick." 

Abigail happily stirred the spaghetti like Grandma said. As she stirred, the little girl saw something and started to laugh. Grandma smiled and said, "Keep stirring and you'll see why it's so funny!" 

Suddenly, Grandma pulled out four little bowls of spaghetti and a big pile of toppings. She said, "Abigail, you did such a great job stirring the spaghetti, I've made us all our own little spaghetti dinners!" 

Abigail loved her little spaghetti dinner. After eating, she gave Grandma a big hug and said, "That was the best surprise ever!"

Mommy and daddy drove their reliable van to the park. They saw their friend Jack, who was there with his daughter, Kate.

"Let's play together," said Daddy.

Kate, who was three-years-old, asked, "What do you want to play?"

"Let's play pass," replied Daddy.

Jack and Daddy stood on either side of the playground, and threw a ball back and forth. Kate watched them and clapped happily as they shouted, "Pass!"

They continued to play pass until it was time to leave. As they said goodbye, Jack said to Kate, "Remember, it's important to be a reliable friend."

Daddy smiled. As they drove away in the reliable van, he looked back through the window and said, "Kate, Jack is right. You should always try to be reliable."

The moral of the story is that reliability is important in life. Being reliable means you can count on someone to be there when you need them.

Today was a special day. I stood in my room admiring the mystery in front of me. It was gray and had a big button on it. I excitedly pressed the button and a noise sounded throughout the room. I proudly admired my new toy.

I ran around the house, showing my family all I had discovered. I was so proud of the gray mystery in my room. My brother just smiled and encouraged me to keep playing with it.

We all spent some time together, admiring the mystery. I explored all the different buttons, pressing them and learning what they did. Soon my cheeks were red with joy and I was having so much fun.

I even took my mystery outside and showed my friends. Everyone had a great time playing and admiring the gray mystery. We were all happy that I had discovered this special toy.

When the day was over I had to say goodbye to my friends. I went back inside and hugged my gray mystery close. I was happy to know that I had found such an amazing thing.

One day, Henry was walking in the park. As he looked around, he noticed a calm plant. He thought it was very pretty. He wanted to take the plant home, so he tried to pull it out. Suddenly, the plant vanished! He was very surprised. He looked around, but he couldn't see the plant anywhere. He started to cry and was very sad. Then he saw a flower nearby and he was very happy. He carefully picked the flower and went home. He was very happy to have a new flower to take home and put in his room.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One night, Lily was scared because she thought there was a monster in her closet. She called out to her mom, "Mommy, there's a monster in my closet!" Her mom came to her room and said, "Don't worry, Lily. There's no monster here. Let's check your closet together." 

Lily's mom opened the closet and they both looked inside. They found a stuffed toy monster that Lily had forgotten about. "See, Lily? It's just a toy. It's not scary," her mom said. Lily felt relieved and said, "Oh, I remember now. That's my monster toy. It's not real." 

Lily's mom picked up the toy and said, "This monster toy is actually useful. You can use it to practice giving kisses. Look, I'll show you." She gave the monster toy a kiss and then gave Lily a kiss on the cheek. Lily giggled and said, "I want to try!" She gave the monster toy a kiss and then gave her mom a kiss. From that night on, Lily wasn't scared of monsters anymore and she loved using her monster toy to practice giving kisses.

Once upon a time, there was a bird named Blue. Blue loved to fly high up in the sky and feel the wind on his feathers. One day, Blue decided to soar even higher than usual. He flapped his wings and flew up and up until he could see the whole world below him.

As Blue was flying, he saw something shiny on the ground. It was money! Blue thought about picking it up, but he realized that he couldn't carry it with his tiny bird feet. He decided to leave it there for someone else to find.

Blue continued to fly and play in the sky. He loved to do flips and twists in the air. His wings were very flexible and he could do all sorts of tricks. The other birds would watch him and cheer him on.

Eventually, Blue got tired and flew back to his nest. He was happy to have had such a fun day of soaring and showing off his flexible wings. As he fell asleep, he dreamed about all the adventures he would have the next time he flew up high in the sky.

Lily and Ben were playing soldiers in the garden. They had hats, jackets and pistols made of wood. They liked to march and shout orders.

"Attention, soldiers!" Ben said. "We have to capture the enemy base. Follow me!"

They marched across the grass, pretending to shoot at the trees and flowers. They reached a big bush and hid behind it.

"Look, there it is!" Lily whispered. "The enemy base is a red tent. Let's go!"

They ran towards the tent, holding their pistols. But when they got closer, they saw that the tent was not empty. There was a big dog inside, sleeping on a blanket. The dog heard them and woke up. It barked loudly and showed its teeth.

"Run, run!" Ben yelled. "The dog is angry!"

They turned around and ran back to the bush. But the dog was faster. It chased them and bit Ben's pistol. The pistol broke in half and fell to the ground.

"Ow, ow, ow!" Ben cried. "My pistol! The dog broke my pistol!"

Lily felt sorry for Ben. She gave him her pistol and hugged him.

"Here, you can have mine," she said. "It's just a toy, Ben. It's not real. We shouldn't play with things that can hurt others."

Ben nodded and wiped his tears. He hugged Lily back.

"Thank you, Lily," he said. "You are a good friend. You are right. We shouldn't play with pistols. They are bad. Let's play something else."

They left the dog and the tent alone. They went back to the garden and played with their ball. They had more fun and no one got hurt. They learned to be kind and careful.

The little girl was anxious. She wanted to hug her mom so badly. She jumped and waved, but her mom was too far away.

Her mom noticed and waved back. Then, she reached into her pocket and held up a diamond. The little girl's eyes lit up. She knew how special diamonds were.

The little girl ran up to her mom. She was so excited she almost tripped! When she reached her mom, she gave her the biggest hug.

The little girl pulled away and noticed something sparkly in her mom's hand. It was the diamond! Her mom had brought a special present for her.

The little girl hugged her mom even tighter. She was so happy that her mom had thought to bring her something so special.

Once upon a time, in a small room, there was a bookshelf. On the bookshelf, there were many books. One day, a little boy named Tim came into the room. He looked at the bookshelf and saw a big, harsh book. Tim wanted to read the book, but he was too small to reach it.

Tim's friend, a cat named Kitty, saw Tim trying to get the book. Kitty was very sleepy and let out a big yawn. Kitty wanted to help Tim, so she jumped up onto the bookshelf. She used her paw to push the big, harsh book down to Tim.

Tim was so happy to have the book. He sat down on the floor and began to read. Kitty curled up next to him, still yawning. They spent the whole day reading the big, harsh book together. And from that day on, Tim and Kitty became the best of friends.

Tom and Lily were twins who liked to play with their toys. They had many toys, but their favorite was a big train set that had a cord to make it go. They would spend hours making the train go around the tracks and making noises.

One day, a man came to their house and asked their mom if she wanted to sell some things. He said he would pay a lot of money for things he liked. Mom said yes and showed him some old clothes and books. The man looked at them and said they were not expensive enough. He wanted something more.

Then he saw the train set in the twins' room. He smiled and said, "What about this? This is a very expensive toy. I will give you a lot of money for it." Mom looked at the train set and thought it was a good deal. She said, "OK, you can have it. But you have to ask the twins first. It is their toy."

The man went to the twins and said, "Hello, little ones. I like your train set very much. Can I buy it from you? I will give you a lot of money for it. You can buy new toys with it." Tom and Lily looked at the man and then at their train set. They loved their train set and did not want to sell it. They said, "No, thank you. We do not want to sell our train set. It is our favorite toy. We have fun with it. Money is not fun."

The man was angry and said, "But this is a very expensive toy. You are silly to keep it. You can have more toys with the money. Don't you want more toys?" Tom and Lily shook their heads and said, "No, we do not want more toys. We have enough toys. We want our train set. It makes us happy. You are silly to want it. You cannot play with it. You only want money."

The man left in a huff and said, "Fine, keep your train set. You are missing a great opportunity. You will regret it." Mom was surprised and said, "I'm sorry, I thought you would like to sell your train set. It is a very expensive toy. You could have had a lot of money for it." Tom and Lily hugged their mom and said, "We love you, mom. We do not need a lot of money. We have you and our train set. That is enough for us. Money cannot buy happiness."

The moral of the story is: Money cannot buy happiness. It is better to value what you have and enjoy it than to sell it for something you do not need or want. Happiness comes from love and fun, not from money and things.

Once there was a baby. Her name was Jenny and she was very fine. Every night, her mommy and daddy would come tuck her in. Then they would lock the door.

One night, Jenny heard a sound. She opened her eyes and asked, "Mommy, who is that?"

Her mommy said, "It's okay, baby. We just locked the door."

Jenny was glad and she smiled. She said, "Oh, okay. Goodnight Mommy."

Then Jenny went to sleep and the night was fine.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a nosy cat named Mittens. One day, Lily was playing with her toys when she saw Mittens lean against the drawer. 

Lily went to the drawer and opened it. She found a shiny necklace inside. Mittens jumped up and tried to grab it with his paw, but Lily quickly closed the drawer. 

Lily realized that she should be careful with her special things and keep them safe in the drawer. She gave Mittens a cuddle and they continued to play together. From that day on, Lily always made sure to close the drawer tightly so that Mittens couldn't get into it again.

There were two best friends. One day, one of them suggested going on a ship. The other one was jealous and said no. The friend suggested again, but the jealous one still said no. The friend was sad and said goodbye.

The jealous one felt bad and thought of a plan to get back at the other one. He quickly decided to make a ship by himself. The jealous one was so excited and started building right away.

He worked very hard and eventually finished the ship. But before he could show it to the other one, a big storm hit and destroyed the ship. The jealous one was very sad and could not believe it.

When the friend found out he felt sorry for the other one. Even though the jealous one had been mean, the friend wanted to help him. But it was too late. The jealous one had caused a bad ending by being too jealous.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and run around in the grass. One day, she noticed her skin was getting dry and itchy. Her mommy gave her some lotion to put on her skin. Lily was excited to try it out.

As she rubbed the lotion on her arms, she noticed her mommy signing to her. "What are you saying, mommy?" Lily asked. "I'm telling you that the lotion will make your skin feel better," her mommy signed back.

Lily was happy that her mommy taught her how to sign. She felt proud that she could understand her mommy without even using her voice. From that day on, she made sure to put lotion on her skin every day so she could run and play outside without any itchiness.

One day, Sam and his mommy went for a walk. They were both wearing their mittens. Sam looked around and pointed with his mitten. He showed his mommy a tree, a bird, and a kite in the sky. 

"Oh Sam, you are so observant," said Mommy.

On their way home, Sam suddenly stepped on a slippery patch of ice. He started to slide and his feet seemed clumsy. He went faster and faster. 

Mommy was worried and called to Sam, "Be careful! Slow down!"

Then Sam saw something shiny in the snow. He decided to point to it with his mitten. He carefully got closer, and then he smiled. 

It was a bright, shiny button. Sam was very happy. 

Mommy clapped her hands, "That's a great find, Sam!" 

Sam smiled and pointed his mitten towards the button again. That was his favorite thing to do.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a stuffed bear named Teddy. Lily loved to use Teddy to play tea party with her friends. One day, Lily and Teddy went on an adventure in the dark forest. It was very scary because they couldn't see anything. But then, Lily remembered that she had a flashlight in her backpack. She turned it on and the dark forest became bright! Teddy wasn't scared anymore. They continued their adventure and found an ordinary tree. It wasn't special or different from any other tree. But Lily and Teddy thought it was the best tree ever! They hugged it and took a picture to remember their fun adventure.

Once upon a time, there was a big universe. In this big universe, there was a little girl. She was so excited because she had never seen a universe before.

At first, she was scared at how big the universe was. But then, she started to explore it. She was jumping and singing and laughing. She felt so free in the big universe.

Suddenly, the little girl heard a loud scream. It was a huge, loud, scary scream. She became so scared and ran away.

She ran and ran until she got back home. She was so scared she crawled under her bed and hugged her favorite toy. The little girl felt so safe there and the loud scream was gone.

The little girl had seen the big universe and even heard a loud scream. Even though it was scary, she knew she was braver than before.

Lily was a little girl who liked to play in the garden. She liked to see the flowers and the bugs and the birds. One day, she saw something new in the garden. It was white and round and had many tiny parts. She wondered what it was.

She asked her mom, who was watering the plants. "Mom, what is that?" She pointed to the white thing.

"That is a cauliflower, Lily. It is a vegetable that grows in the ground. We can eat it later, if you want." Mom said.

Lily was curious. She wanted to see the cauliflower up close. She walked to the garden bed and bent down. She touched the cauliflower gently. It felt soft and bumpy.

"Hello, cauliflower. I am Lily. Nice to meet you." She said.

The cauliflower did not say anything. It just stayed still. But Lily felt happy. She had made a new friend in the garden.

She ran back to her mom and hugged her. "Thank you, mom, for the cauliflower. I am grateful. Can we eat it for dinner?" She asked.

Mom smiled and kissed her. "Of course, Lily. We can eat it for dinner. I am grateful for you, too. You are my sweet girl." She said.

They went inside the house, holding hands. Lily looked forward to dinner. She wanted to share the cauliflower with her mom and dad. She thought it would be yummy. She was glad she had met the cauliflower.

Lily and Ben were friends who liked to play with numbers. They had a big book with numbers and pictures of different countries. They learned how to count and say the names of the countries.

One day, they decided to play a game. They took turns to point at a country and ask the other to say its name and how many people lived there. They used the numbers in the book to help them.

Lily pointed at a country with a lot of water and green land. She said, "What is this country and how many people live here?"

Ben looked at the book and said, "This is Ireland and there are four million people here."

Lily said, "Good job, Ben! Now it's your turn."

Ben pointed at a country with a lot of sand and sun. He said, "What is this country and how many people live here?"

Lily looked at the book and said, "This is Egypt and there are ninety million people here."

Ben said, "Wow, that's a lot of people! How do they all fit in the country?"

Lily said, "I don't know, maybe they live in big houses or small tents. Maybe they share things and help each other."

Ben said, "That sounds nice. I wish we could visit Egypt and see the pyramids and the camels."

Lily said, "Me too. Maybe we can go there when we are older and learn more about their culture and history."

They continued to play with the numbers and the countries until it was time for dinner. They put the book away and thanked each other for the fun game. They learned that there are many different countries in the world, and that each one has its own people, animals, and things. They also learned that numbers can help them understand and compare different things. They felt happy and curious about the world.

The moral value of the story is that learning about numbers and countries can be fun and educational, and that it can inspire respect and curiosity for other cultures and people.

Once there was a barn on the farm. It was big and strong and brown. Inside, there were lots of animals. One day, it was very hot. The animals felt too hot, so they all spilled out of the barn and into the fields.

They started a competition. The fastest animal would win! All the animals ran as hard as they could. Then, one animal stayed in the sun too long and started to melt. It was sad, but all the animals learned not to stay in the hot sun too long. They were happy to all be safe back in the cool barn.

Lily and Max liked to play hide and seek in the big cardboard box. It was big enough for both of them to fit inside, and they could cut out windows and doors to make it more fun. Sometimes they would take turns hiding and seeking, and sometimes they would hide together and wait for Mom or Dad to find them.

One day, they decided to hide together and see how long it would take Mom to find them. They crawled into the box and closed the flap. They giggled and whispered to each other, hoping Mom would not hear them. They heard Mom's footsteps coming closer and closer. They held their breath and tried to be very quiet.

Mom walked past the box and did not stop. She went to the kitchen and started to make lunch. Lily and Max waited and waited, but Mom did not come back. They started to feel bored and hungry. They wanted Mom to find them and play with them. They felt frustrated.

Lily had an idea. She decided to peek out of the window and see if Mom was still in the kitchen. She lifted the flap and stuck her head out. She saw Mom chopping some carrots and humming a song. She smiled and waved at Mom. Mom saw her and smiled back. She said, "There you are, Lily! I was looking for you and Max. Are you hiding in the box?"

Lily nodded and said, "Yes, we are. We wanted to surprise you, but you did not find us." Mom said, "I'm sorry, I did not know you were hiding. You are very good at hiding. Do you want to come out and have some lunch?" Lily said, "Yes, please. Can Max come too?" Mom said, "Of course. Let's go and get him." She walked to the box and opened the flap. She saw Max sitting in the corner, holding a toy car. She said, "Hello, Max. Are you hiding too?" Max nodded and said, "Yes, I am. But I'm hungry now." Mom said, "Me too. Let's go and have some lunch. You can bring your toy car if you want." Max said, "OK." He grabbed his toy car and followed Mom and Lily to the kitchen. They left the box behind, but they knew they could play with it again later. They were happy.

Once upon a time, there was a very slow dish. It wanted to include more fun in its life. One day, it decided to go on an adventure.

The slow dish started walking. It was very excited! It saw many animals and plants along the way. Then it reached a beautiful park. 

The slow dish loved all the colors. Everything was so bright and pretty! It wanted to explore the park so it kept walking. The dish found many interesting things in the park, like toys and slides. 

Soon, it came across a large playground. There were many children playing. All their laughter made the dish very happy. The dish wanted to join, so it slowly crept closer. Then, it found the perfect spot! 

The dish was now part of all the fun. The children smiled at it and included it in their games. The dish had a wonderful time playing with them. 

At the end of the day, the slow dish was very tired. It was a great day filled with fun and joy. The dish knew it was always welcome and would be included in their games.

Toby was a happy little boy who was trying to organize his toys. He had many paths that he could take when playing. He especially liked the yellow path because it was the most fun.

A little while later, Toby had a surprise visitor. It was his neighbor, Mr. Smith. He smiled and waved at Toby. 

"Hi Toby, I thought I'd take a yellow walk with you," said Mr. Smith. 

Toby was excited and he happily took Mr. Smith's hand. He started to walk down the yellow path and as they walked, Mr. Smith kept looking around as if something was wrong.

Finally, they reached the end of the yellow path, but it was blocked by a large tree. Toby stopped and looked up at the tree.

"Oh no!" said Mr. Smith. "It looks like our yellow path is blocked." 

Toby frowned and started to cry. Mr. Smith tried to console Toby but it was too late. He had set him up for a bad ending and Toby was left feeling disappointed and scared.

Once upon a time, there was an old man who felt very miserable. He was so unhappy that he wanted to eat something special, so he decided to go to the top of a big cliff.

At the top, he saw a beautiful rainbow, and he was so excited that he decided to eat it. But when he tried, he realized that he couldn't eat the rainbow.

Instead, he started to eat the cliff, bit by bit. He enjoyed eating it so much that he kept going until the whole cliff was gone.

When the cliff was gone, the old man was no longer miserable. He was happy, and he had a full tummy too. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Ann. She was very persistent. One day Ann had an idea. She grabbed a rag and some matches. Ann was determined to make something special. She lit the match and placed it under the rag. Suddenly, the rag caught fire and began to dance. Ann was so excited and couldn't believe what had happened. She kept trying and tried different ways of lighting the rag. Finally, after many tries, Ann succeeded! The rag was spinning in the air, making beautiful patterns with the fire. Ann was very proud of her accomplishment and ran to show her parents.

Once upon a time, there was a playful puppy named Max. Max loved to play fetch with his owner, Lily. One day, they went for a walk in the park. Max saw a big field and ran towards it. Lily followed him.

Max entered the field and started to run around. Lily saw a sign that said, "No dogs allowed." She called Max to come back, but he didn't listen. Suddenly, Max saw a ball and ran towards it. He didn't notice the big hole in the ground. Max fell into the hole and hurt his leg.

Lily had to take Max to the vet. The vet said Max couldn't play for a while. Lily felt sad because she knew Max loved to play. From that day on, Lily always checked the signs before entering a new land.

Once upon a time, there was a big, fat bird named Bob. Bob loved to soar high up in the sky and feel the wind in his feathers. One day, Bob saw a little mouse named Timmy trying to thread a needle. 

"Hello, little mouse! What are you doing?" asked Bob.

"I'm trying to thread this needle so I can sew my shirt," replied Timmy.

Bob laughed, "You're too small to thread that needle! But don't worry, I can help you."

Bob flew up to the sky and found a long piece of thread. He brought it back to Timmy and said, "Here you go, little mouse! Now you can sew your shirt."

Timmy was very grateful and thanked Bob. From that day on, Timmy and Bob became good friends and would often go on adventures together, soaring through the sky and helping each other out.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. He loved to play on the slide at the park. One day, he went to the park and saw that the slide was broken. He was sad because he couldn't slide anymore.

Timmy went to his dad and told him about the broken slide. His dad said that they could try to restore it. Timmy was happy to hear that. They went to the park with some tools and started to fix the slide. It was hard work, but they did it together.

When they finished, Timmy was so happy that he went crazy with excitement. He slid down the slide over and over again. He was so grateful to his dad for helping him restore the slide. From that day on, Timmy knew that if something was broken, he could always try to fix it.

Anna and Ben were playing in their room. They liked to pretend they were in a different world. They had a big wardrobe that they used as a door to their world.

"Let's go to the forest today," Ben said. "Maybe we can find some berries to taste."

"OK," Anna agreed. "But we have to be careful. There might be some animals that are not friendly."

They opened the wardrobe and went inside. They found some coats and hats that they put on. They felt warm and cozy. They walked through the wardrobe until they saw some trees and flowers.

"Wow, it's so pretty here," Anna said. "Look, there are some berries on that bush. Let's go and taste them."

They ran to the bush and picked some berries. They were red and juicy. They put them in their mouths and chewed.

"Mmm, they are sweet and yummy," Ben said.

"I like them too," Anna said. "But we should not eat too many. We might get a tummy ache."

They ate a few more berries and then decided to explore the forest. They saw some birds and squirrels and butterflies. They heard some noises and rustles.

"What's that?" Anna asked.

"I don't know," Ben said. "Maybe it's an animal. Let's hide behind that tree and see."

They hid behind the tree and peeked out. They saw a big brown bear coming out of the bushes. It had a big nose and big paws and big teeth. It looked hungry and angry.

"Oh no, it's a bear!" Anna whispered.

"Shh, don't make a sound," Ben whispered. "Maybe it will go away."

The bear sniffed the air and walked towards the bush where they had eaten the berries. It saw the berries and started to eat them. It made loud noises and licked its lips.

"It likes the berries too," Anna said.

"Maybe it will be full and leave us alone," Ben said.

They hoped the bear would go away soon. They were scared and wanted to go back to their room. They wished they had something useful to scare the bear away. They looked around and saw a big stick on the ground.

"Look, there's a stick," Anna said. "Maybe we can use it to make some noise and scare the bear away."

"Good idea," Ben said. "But we have to be quick and quiet. You grab the stick and I'll open the wardrobe."

They nodded and got ready. Anna crawled to the stick and picked it up. Ben crawled to the wardrobe and opened it. They saw their room and felt relieved.

"OK, on the count of three, we run to the wardrobe and bang the stick on the ground," Ben said.

"OK," Anna said.

"One, two, three!" Ben said.

They ran to the wardrobe and banged the stick on the ground. The bear heard the noise and looked up. It saw them and roared. It was angry and chased them.

"Run, run, run!" Anna said.

They ran into the wardrobe and slammed the door behind them. They heard the bear scratching and growling outside. They were safe and happy.

"We did it, we did it!" Ben said.

"We are brave and smart!" Anna said.

They hugged each other and laughed. They took off their coats and hats and put them back in the wardrobe. They decided to play something else in their room. They had enough of the forest for today.

Once upon a time there was a fat cat. His name was Twist. Twist liked to ride his bicycle. Every day he would ride around the block. One day, Twist twisted the handle on his bicycle and took off down the street. He went faster and faster until he could go no more. 

Twist felt so happy. He closed his eyes and smiled. Suddenly, Twist heard something and when he opened his eyes he saw a big hill! He started to pedal up the hill, but it was too hard. Suddenly, Twist felt something bump him and he looked around, it was a fat lady on a bicycle!

She said, "Let me help you, Twist! Hold on to my bike and I will help you up the hill." Twist was so excited and he grabbed onto her bike. They went up, up, up the hill and Twist whooped in joy! He had made it to the top! They waved goodbye and Twist went off on his bicycle again.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She loved to play sport with her friends. Lily's favorite sport was soccer. She had a pink soccer ball that she loved to kick around. 

One day, Lily and her friends were playing soccer in the park. Suddenly, Lily's ball was kicked into a big sack by accident. The sack was so big that they couldn't see the ball anymore. Lily was sad because she thought she lost her pink soccer ball forever.

But then, Lily's friends had an idea. They all grabbed the sack and started shaking it. Suddenly, the pink soccer ball popped out! Lily was so happy and grateful to her friends for helping her find her ball. From that day on, they made sure to be more careful when they played sport in the park.

One day, Mommy had a playful suggestion for the 3 year old. She said, "Let's go outside and play games". The 3 year old was excited and so Mommy quickly got her a cozy jacket to wear. 

When the 3 year old laced up her shoes, Mommy said, "Let's hide and seek!", so the 3 year old ran outside to hide. Once she was covered, Mommy started counting from 1 to 10. 

When Mommy was done counting, she used her playful voice to yell, "Ready or not, here I come!" She looked everywhere, but the 3 year old was so good at hiding that Mommy couldn't find her. 

After a few minutes, Mommy said, "I think I know where you are!" She ran to the tree and when she arrived, there was the 3 year old, hiding behind the big trunk, smiling and giggling.

Once upon a time there was an ant named Sam. Sam was very small and he always enjoyed exploring new places. One day Sam was walking through a deep forest in search of an adventure.

He came across a tall tree and decided to take a closer look. As he examined it he noticed something strange at the bottom of the tree. It was a little rabbit with its foot caught in a thick branch. 

Sam wanted to help the rabbit, so he looked around to see if there was anything he could use. Then he saw a fallen branch that was curved at the end. He picked it up and carefully freed the little rabbit's heel from the branch.

The rabbit was so happy to be free and thanked Sam for his help. As a reward, the rabbit taught Sam one of its special tricks. It showed him how to use sign language so even if you were deaf, you could communicate with others.

Sam thought this was a very important lesson and thanked the rabbit. He learned that communication is essential to life and that you should always help others in need.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play basketball with his friends. One day, Timmy and his friends went to the park to play basketball. Timmy was so excited to play, but the basketball hoop was too high for him to reach. He struggled to throw the ball into the hoop.

After a while, Timmy's friend Tommy came over to help. Tommy was much taller than Timmy and could reach the hoop easily. Together, they were able to shoot the basketball into the hoop. Timmy was so happy that they were able to score a point.

As they continued to play, the sky started to get dark and cloudy. Timmy's mom came to pick him up and they had to leave. Timmy was sad to leave, but he knew he would come back to play again soon. He looked back at the basketball hoop and saw that the sky had cleared up, making it easier to see the hoop. Timmy smiled and waved goodbye to the park, excited to come back and play again.

Lily liked to design things. She used paper, crayons, scissors and glue to make pictures and shapes. She liked to design keys the most. She cut out key shapes from paper and colored them with crayons. She made red keys, blue keys, yellow keys and green keys.

One day, she showed her keys to her friend Ben. Ben liked them too. He asked Lily if he could have a key. Lily said yes. She asked him what color he wanted. Ben said he wanted a green key. Lily gave him a green key. Ben was happy.

Ben said he wanted to try the key on a door. He looked around and saw a green door. He ran to the door and put the key in the hole. He turned the key. The door opened. Ben was surprised. He said to Lily, "Look, your key works!"

Lily ran to the door too. She saw a room with toys and books and a big window. She said to Ben, "Wow, this is a fun room!"

Ben and Lily went inside the room. They played with the toys and read the books. They had a lot of fun. They thanked Lily's key for opening the door. They said it was a magic key. They decided to keep the key and the door as their secret. They said they would come back to the room whenever they wanted. They were very happy.

Once upon a time, in a big jungle, there lived a wild elephant named Elly. Elly was a very big and strong elephant. She had many friends in the jungle, like monkeys, birds, and other animals. One day, a little bird named Billy came to Elly and said, "Elly, can you help me? My friend is stuck in a tree, and I can't get him out."

Elly said, "Of course, Billy! I will help you." So, Elly and Billy went to the tree where Billy's friend was stuck. Elly used her long nose to lift Billy's friend out of the tree. Billy and his friend were very happy. They said, "Thank you, Elly! You are a good friend."

After that day, Elly, Billy, and all the other animals in the jungle became even better friends. They all helped each other when they needed it. Elly learned that it is good to serve and help others. She knew that when you help your friends, they will help you too. And they all lived happily in the jungle, taking care of one another.

The moral of the story is to always help others and serve your friends, because they will be there for you when you need them.

Once upon a time, there was a dog. He had a bone which he wanted to keep for himself. Every day he would find a place to hide his bone. But one day an ignorant rabbit came along. 

The dog asked the rabbit to behave, but the rabbit did not listen. He grabbed the bone from the dog's mouth and ran away with it. The poor dog was fuming and ran after him, he wanted his bone back! 

Filled with rage, the dog chased the rabbit for a long time and eventually caught up with him. He was ready to take back his bone, but the rabbit refused. 

The moral of the story is that when you are selfish and ignore people, you are likely to find trouble. This is exactly what happened to the rabbit. He was ignorant and misbehaved and he did not get away unscathed. The dog ended up taking his bone, and the rabbit was left with nothing.

Once upon a time there was a brave hero who travelled through many lands. He had a clipper and he used it to help those who were in trouble. But one day, he was in a different land where things were very different. A mean monster had wrapped the whole kingdom in darkness and fear. The hero knew he had to do something so he set out to defeat the mean monster. He battled and fought with all his strength. But the monster was too strong and he could not prevail against him. In the end the hero was wrapped up and taken away. The troubled kingdom was left in darkness and despair.

Once upon a time, in a small house, there lived a little girl named Lucy and her toy bear, named Teddy. Lucy and Teddy were best friends. They played together, ate together, and even slept together. One day, Lucy found a small button on the floor. She picked it up and showed it to Teddy.

"Look, Teddy! I found a small button!" said Lucy. Teddy wanted the button too. "I want the button, Lucy!" said Teddy. Lucy did not want to give the button to Teddy. They started to quarrel.

"No, Teddy! I found it first!" said Lucy. Teddy was sad and did not want to play anymore. Lucy saw Teddy's sad face and felt bad. She thought of a great idea.

"Teddy, we can share the button!" said Lucy. Teddy's face lit up with a big smile. They played together with the button, taking turns holding it. They learned that sharing is better than quarreling. And from that day on, they never fought over anything again.

Once there was a little boy named Peter who wanted to find an adventure. One day, he went outside and saw a mist that was very thick and mysterious. He wanted to go explore it but he was afraid. He grabbed his teddy bear and took a deep breath, then he stepped into the mist.

Suddenly he could see something in the mist. It was a tall and very old-looking tree with a large hole in the trunk. He walked close to the tree and heard a strange voice coming from inside. It said, "Demand something special".

Peter closed his eyes and wished for something that was not ordinary. When he opened his eyes again, the mist was clearing and he saw a beautiful pink balloon. He was so excited and he reached out to take it. As he grabbed it, the balloon started to float and led him out of the mist. 

Peter walked home feeling very excited with his balloon. He knew he had gone on an amazing adventure that day.

Once there was a little girl. She was playing in the garden when she found a long rope. She picked it up and started to play with it. The little girl was having a lot of fun. Suddenly, her mom called her for dinner. The dinner was very spicy and the little girl didn't like it. She started to cry. Her mom saw that the little girl was very upset, so she grabbed the rope and showed her how to make a bracelet with it. The little girl was so happy with her new bracelet that she forgot all about the spicy dinner and stopped crying.

Billy was feeling very curious. He was looking around everywhere and couldn't understand why everything seemed so strange. Then, he noticed a steel rod sticking out of the wall. Billy thought it looked interesting, so he decided to take a closer look.

He walked up to it and placed his hand on it. Suddenly, the rod started to slip! Billy was so surprised that he jumped back. The rod continued to move, until it was completely gone.

Billy was scared and tried to figure out what had just happened. Suddenly, he heard a voice from behind him: "I see you are curious about that steel rod, eh?"

Billy turned around and saw an old man smiling down at him. Billy nodded, still not sure what was going on.

The old man laughed. "It's simple, my boy. The rod was meant to be taken out - it's what it's there for. It will slip right back in, whenever you need it!"

Billy smiled. Now that he understood, he was no longer scared. In fact, he was even more curious to learn more about the steel rod!

Once upon a time, there were two friends, Mole and Bunny. They liked to play and have lots of fun together. But one day, something unexpected happened.

Mole was playing outside and dug a hole, but he found it was too deep and got stuck inside. Bunny saw him and started to call for help.

"Help!" He shouted.

He ran around and saw an old man walking by. He stopped him and asked for help.

"Sir, please help us. My friend Mole is in a hole and can't get out. It's very difficult!"

The old man heard Bunny and went over to the hole. He threw a rope down to Mole and said, 
"Grab onto this rope and I will help you get out."

Mole grabbed the rope and the old man pulled him out. He said, "Thank You. I didn't think I would make it out. That was really difficult."

And so, with the help of the old man, Mole was able to get out of the hole. He thanked the old man for his help and the two friends went back to having fun.

Once upon a time there was a girl. She was three years old and she had a special key. The key was to unlock a door. 

The door led to a very special room. It was a room full of shrimp. The shrimp were mild and not too spicy. 

The girl was so excited to eat them! She put the key in the keyhole and she unlocked the door. 

She opened the door and the room was filled with shrimp! She ate so many shrimp and had so much fun. 

When she was all done, she went home. She was so happy she had been able to unlock the door and find all of the delicious mild shrimp.

Once there was a little girl named Amy. She was only three years old. On sunny days, she liked to rock on her porch. She found a big rock and it was the perfect size for sitting on.

Amy was eager to rock on the big rock. She was very excited as she jumped up and down on the porch. She moved the rock back and forth, feeling the warm sun on her little hands. She rocked faster and faster, laughing and having fun.

Amy kept up the rocking until it was time for dinner. She stepped off the porch, but kept looking back at the rock. She couldn't wait for another sunny day so she could rock again.

Once upon a time there was a black tornado. She was very mean and she invited all the clouds to come for a party. They were scared, but didn't want to be rude and said yes.

When they got there, the tornado said they had to play a game. All the clouds had to run around and try to escape the tornado. The tornado said if the clouds could get away, they could stay in the sky.

The clouds all tried their best, but they couldn't get away. The tornado kept chasing them and they ran and ran, but they just couldn't escape.

Finally, the tornado showed mercy on the clouds and let them stay in the sky. She said she was just playing a game and she was happy to have invited them.

The clouds were relieved that the tornado hadn't been so mean after all. They thanked her and the tornado smiled, happy that her little party had ended well.

Mandy was feeling guilty. She had not listened to her Mama. Mama had asked her to please stay in the living room, but she had gone outside. Mama saw Mandy and said, "That's not nice!".

Mandy looked down. She knew she had made a mistake. She said sorry to Mama. 

Then, Mama said "I understand that you wanted to have fun. Let's make a deal: if you help me clean up the kitchen, I'll let you ride my motor."

Mandy was so excited. She started to help Mama right away. She put all the dishes in the sink and put away all the food. After everything was done, Mama took out the motor and gave it to Mandy.

Mandy was so happy that she thanked Mama and gave her a big hug. Mama was happy too and said, "See, when you do what I ask, good things happen. Now, please go and have fun!"

And that's just what Mandy did. She rode her motor in the backyard and was so happy. She learned her lesson that day. Mama was right - doing the right thing can be very rewarding!

Once upon a time, in a big green park, there was a nosy little squirrel. The squirrel liked to jump and play with his friends. One day, it started to freeze outside. The squirrel and his friends felt very cold.

As they played, they saw a beautiful rainbow in the sky. The rainbow had many colors: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, and purple. The squirrel and his friends stopped and looked at the rainbow. They were very happy to see it.

The nosy squirrel had an idea. He thought that if they could touch the rainbow, they would feel warm again. So, the squirrel and his friends jumped and tried to reach the rainbow. They could not touch it, but they had a lot of fun trying. Soon, they forgot they were cold and just enjoyed playing together under the pretty rainbow.

Once upon a time, there was a sleepy cat named Ash. He liked to roll around in the sun all day long. Ash was very happy when he played outside.

One day, Ash found a big ball. It was fun to roll the ball with his paws. He pushed the ball here and there, and it made him very tired.

At the end of the day, Ash was so sleepy. He went back to his warm home and curled up in his soft bed. He closed his eyes and had sweet dreams about rolling in the sun.

Once upon a time, there was a poor little girl. She lived in a small house and her dad was away a lot.

One day, a little boy named Tim was very eager to go to the stadium. He wanted to see his favorite team play. Tim's dad said, "We will go to the stadium soon, Tim."

When they got to the stadium, Tim saw lots of people. They were all eager to watch the game too. Tim and his dad found their seats and sat down. They were so excited for the game to start.
