Tim was very happy when they found each other again. They went back to their seats and enjoyed the game. The stadium was loud and fun, and Tim was very happy that he got to go with his dad.

Sara and Tom are friends. They like to play with toys and books. But one day, Sara gets a new doll. It is big and pretty and has a pink dress. Tom likes the doll too. He wants to play with it.

Sara says, "This is my doll. You can play with your truck." Tom is jealous. He does not want to play with his truck. He wants to play with the doll. He tries to take the doll from Sara. Sara says, "Stop! That is not nice. You have to share."

Tom does not listen. He pulls the doll hard. Sara pulls the doll hard too. They both fall down. The doll falls down too. The doll's dress rips. Sara and Tom are sad. They both cry.

Mom hears them cry. She comes to see what is wrong. She sees the doll and the rip. She says, "What happened? Why did you rip the doll's dress?" Sara and Tom tell Mom what they did. Mom is not happy. She says, "You have to say sorry to each other. And you have to fix the doll's dress. You have to be kind and share."

Sara and Tom say sorry to each other. They hug and say they are still friends. They find some thread and a needle. They try to fix the doll's dress. It is hard, but they do their best. They make the doll look pretty again. They are happy. They play with the doll and the truck together. They share and have fun. They learn a lesson. They do not want to be jealous again. They want to be good friends. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved lollipops and always had one in her hand. One day, she saw a big tree and wanted to climb it. But she was scared and didn't feel brave enough to do it. 

Her friend, a brave dog named Max, came to her and told her that she could do it. He climbed up the tree first to show her how to do it. Lily watched him and then climbed up the tree too. 

But when they reached the top, they saw a bird's nest. The bird didn't like them and started to chirp loudly. Lily and Max got scared and climbed down the tree as fast as they could. They were happy to be back on the ground and ate their lollipops together.

Once upon a time there was an ancient stay. It had been around for many years and was very old. One day a girl called Emily decided to go and collect the stay. She packed some food and set off.

When she arrived she couldn't believe her eyes. The stay was huge and ancient. She walked closer and saw all the carvings on it and marvelled at how old it must be.

Emily collected some stones to take back home as a souvenir of her adventure. She also found shells and pebbles lying around. She managed to fill a bag full of things.

When Emily got back home she showed her family her collection. They were amazed at all her treasures. Emily was very happy she had gone to collect the ancient stay.

Ben and Lily were twins who liked to play with their toys. But sometimes they wanted the same toy and they would fight over it. One day, they saw a big red truck on the shelf. It was their dad's toy when he was little, and he told them not to touch it.

"I want the truck!" Ben said.

"No, I want it!" Lily said.

They both reached for the truck and pulled it hard. The truck fell off the shelf and broke into pieces. Ben and Lily gasped and looked at each other. They knew they were in trouble.

They heard their mom coming upstairs. They quickly hid the broken truck under the bed and pretended to play with their dolls and cars.

"Hi, kids. What are you doing?" Mom asked.

"Nothing, Mom. Just playing," Ben said.

"Can I see what you are playing with?" Mom asked.

Ben and Lily nodded and showed her their toys. Mom smiled and said, "Those are nice toys. Do you share them with each other?"

Ben and Lily looked at each other and nodded again. They hoped Mom would not see the truck under the bed.

Mom said, "That's good. Sharing is caring. You know, I want to discuss something with you. Do you know what discuss means?"

Ben and Lily shook their heads. They did not know what discuss meant.

Mom said, "Discuss means to talk about something. I want to talk to you about the big red truck on the shelf. Do you know whose truck that is?"

Ben and Lily felt their hearts beat faster. They knew Mom had seen the truck.

Mom said, "That truck is your dad's toy. He loves it very much. He got it when he was your age. He told you not to touch it, right?"

Ben and Lily nodded. They felt ashamed.

Mom said, "Then why did you touch it? Why did you break it?"

Ben and Lily did not answer. They looked at the floor.

Mom said, "That was very naughty of you. You did not listen to your dad. You did not respect his toy. You did not tell the truth. How do you think your dad will feel when he sees his broken truck?"

Ben and Lily felt tears in their eyes. They knew they had hurt their dad.

Mom said, "You need to say sorry to your dad. You need to help him fix his truck. You need to learn from your mistake. Do you understand?"

Ben and Lily nodded. They said, "We are sorry, Mom. We are sorry, Dad. We will help you fix the truck. We will not be naughty again."

Mom hugged them and said, "I love you, kids. I know you are sorry. I know you will do better. But you have to be more careful with your toys and your dad's toys. They are not just things. They have stories and memories. They are precious. Do you know what precious means?"

Ben and Lily nodded. They said, "Precious means very important. Very special. Like you and Dad. Like us."

Mom smiled and said, "That's right. You are very precious to me and Dad. And we are very precious to you. And so are our toys. We have to take care of them and each other. OK?"

Ben and Lily nodded. They said, "OK, Mom. We love you. We love Dad. We love our toys."

Mom said, "I love you too, kids. Now, let's go downstairs and see if we can fix the truck. Maybe we can play with it together. What do you say?"

Ben and Lily smiled and said, "Yes, Mom. Let's go. Let's play."

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved his bookshelf because it had all of his favorite books on it. One day, Timmy's little sister, Lily, accidentally knocked over the bookshelf. All of Timmy's books fell on the floor and some of them got damaged. Timmy was very upset and started to cry.

Lily didn't mean to make Timmy upset, but she didn't know how to fix the bookshelf. Timmy's dad saw what happened and came to help. He fixed the bookshelf and told Timmy that accidents happen sometimes. Timmy felt better and gave Lily a hug. He realized that surrendering his anger and forgiving Lily was better than being harsh with her.

From that day on, Timmy and Lily played together nicely and Timmy learned that sometimes it's important to surrender and forgive, even when things don't go as planned.

Lily loved her kitten, Max. She liked to play with him, feed him, and cuddle him. But sometimes, Max was naughty. He liked to scratch the sofa, knock over the vase, and chase the birds.

One day, Lily's mom said, "Lily, we have to organize your room. It is very messy. You have too many toys and books. We need to put some in the box and give them to other kids who need them."

Lily felt anxious. She did not want to give away her toys and books. She liked them all. She said, "No, mom. I need them. They are mine."

Max heard Lily and mom talking. He thought, "Maybe I can help. Maybe I can make Lily happy." He ran to Lily's room and jumped on the bed. He saw a pile of toys and books. He started to push them with his paws. He wanted to organize them. He thought, "This is fun. This is a game."

But he did not organize them. He made them more messy. He scattered them all over the floor. He tore some pages from the books. He broke some toys. He made a big mess.

Lily and mom came to Lily's room. They saw the mess. They saw Max. They were shocked. Lily said, "Max, what did you do? You are so bad. You ruined my toys and books. You are not my friend."

Max felt sad. He did not mean to be bad. He wanted to be good. He wanted to be Lily's friend. He said, "Meow. I'm sorry. I tried to help. I tried to organize. I love you."

Lily looked at Max. She saw his sad eyes. She felt sorry for him. She said, "It's okay, Max. I love you too. You are my friend. But you have to be careful. You have to be gentle. You have to listen to mom."

Mom said, "Lily, I'm proud of you. You are very kind. You forgave Max. But you still have to organize your room. You have to choose some toys and books to give away. You have to share with others. You have to be generous."

Lily nodded. She said, "Okay, mom. I will try. I will organize my room. I will share with others. I will be generous. But can I keep Max?"

Mom smiled. She said, "Of course, you can keep Max. He is part of our family. He is a good kitten. He just needs some training. And some love."

Lily hugged Max. Max licked Lily. They were happy. They organized Lily's room together. They played with the toys and books they kept. They gave away the ones they did not need. They made other kids happy. They learned a lesson. They were good.

Once upon a time, there was a hill. And on the hill lived a duck. The duck was very persistent and never gave up. One day, the duck wanted to visit a new place. He flew far away and soon he landed on the hill. From the hill, he could see the most beautiful scenery. The sun was shining and the sky was so blue.

Every day, he would climb higher and higher until eventually he reached the top. He was so proud and felt very satisfied. From the top of the hill, he could look down and view the most beautiful place he had ever seen.

The duck decided to stay on the hill and he continued to explore new places. He was the happiest duck ever and he enjoyed visiting this hill each and every day. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy called Ted. He wasn't very big and he wasn't very old. He was only three years old.

"I can't do it," Ted said, pointing to the knot.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little bear named Teddy. Teddy was a cute and adorable bear who loved to explore. One day, Teddy decided to go on an adventure to find a cave.

Together, they rushed through the forest looking for a cave. After a while, they finally found one. "Look, Tweetie! We found a cave!" exclaimed Teddy. They went inside the cave and saw some bats hanging upside down. "Wow, this is so cool!" said Tweetie. 

After exploring the cave, Teddy and Tweetie went back home. "Thanks for coming with me, Tweetie. We had so much fun!" said Teddy. "I had fun too, Teddy. Let's go on another adventure soon!" replied Tweetie. And so, Teddy and Tweetie became the best of friends and went on many more adventures together.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim had a big patch on his pants. The patch was cheap, but it made Tim happy. He liked his pants with the patch.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved muffins. She would eat them every day for breakfast. One day, Lily's mommy made muffins for breakfast. But the muffins were weak and didn't taste good.

Once upon a time there was a kind girl named Mary. One day Mary was walking home from school when she found a notebook lying on the ground. She picked it up, brushed off some dirt, and decided to take it home.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily's mommy asked her if she wanted some lemonade. Lily said yes and her mommy went to the kitchen to make it.

Once upon a time, there was a child named Lily. She liked to play with her smooth toys, like her stuffed bear and her shiny ball. One day, Lily went for a walk with her mom. They saw a yield sign, which means they had to stop and let other cars go first.

Tommy thanked Robbert and ran back to where he was organizing his cars. He was sure he would remember this wild adventure for a long time.

Once upon a time, in a peaceful little town, there lived a cat named Tom. Tom loved to play with his ball all day. One day, Tom saw a new thing in the kitchen. It was green and smelled good. It was a mint plant.

Tom's mom said, "Tom, do not touch the mint. It is not for play." But Tom was curious. He wanted to try and play with the mint. So, when his mom was not looking, Tom took a leaf from the mint plant.

Tom played with the mint leaf and his ball. He had so much fun. But soon, his mom found out. She saw the mint leaf on the floor. "Tom, I told you not to touch the mint!" she said. Tom felt bad for not listening to his mom.

In the end, Tom learned to listen to his mom. He knew she was trying to keep him safe. Tom never touched the mint again. Instead, he played with his ball and had fun with his friends. And they all lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a lot of toys and clothes, but she didn't like to share them with her friends. Her mom would always tell her to be kind and share her things, but Lily didn't listen.

One day, Lily's friend came over to play. She saw all of Lily's toys and wanted to play with them too. But Lily didn't want to share. Her friend said, "Can I play with your toys too?" Lily didn't want to, but her mom encouraged her to share. So Lily finally let her friend play with her toys.

After they were done playing, Lily's friend said, "Thank you for sharing your toys with me, Lily. You are a good friend." Lily felt happy inside because she did something nice for her friend. From that day on, Lily learned to share her things and not be spoiled.

One day, a cat named Tom was very hungry. He saw a big, tasty steak on a table. The table was very organized and clean. Tom wanted to eat the steak, but he needed to be careful.

Tom jumped on the table and walked slowly to the steak. He saw water on the table, but he did not think it was a problem. Tom was very happy because he was going to eat the steak.

But then, Tom's foot touched the water. He started to slip and fell off the table. The steak fell too, and Tom did not get to eat it. Next time, Tom would be more careful when he saw water on the table.

Once upon a time, there lived a family of bears. The dad and the mom were very snug together. They liked to share, so every day they would pick some berries and put them in a bowl. 

One day, the dad wanted to do something special for the family. He had an idea. He went out and bought a grill, and then he made some yummy burgers. He put them on the grill and let them cook. 

The bears were so excited! When the burgers were ready, the dad shared them with the mom and the two little cubs. Everyone enjoyed the burgers, they were so good and so tight. 

The family had a lot of fun that day. The dad was proud of how well the burgers had come out. From that day on, the dad would share food made using the grill with the family whenever he could. 

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She went on a trip with her family to visit her grandma. When they got there, Lily's mom asked her to help unpack their bags. Lily was very excited to unpack her own bag, but she was slow because she wanted to look at all her toys.

Suddenly, Lily's dad called out to her, "Lily, can you help me find the cord for the lamp?" Lily knew where the cord was, so she quickly went to her dad and showed him where it was. Her dad was very happy and said, "You're so helpful, Lily!"

After they finished unpacking, Lily's grandma asked her if she wanted to play outside. Lily was very excited and said, "Yes, please!" They played outside for a while and then went back inside for dinner. Lily was very tired from playing, so she fell asleep quickly that night.

Once upon a time, there was a clumsy driver named Max. Max drove a big red car and he loved to go fast. One day, Max was driving down a slippery road when he hit a patch of ice. His car started to spin and spin until it finally stopped.

Max was scared and didn't know what to do. He saw a little girl named Lily walking by and asked for her help. "Can you please call for help? My car is frozen and won't move," Max said. Lily quickly called for help and soon a tow truck arrived to help Max.

Max learned his lesson and promised to drive more carefully in the future. From that day on, Max always checked the weather before he drove his car.

Anna and Ben like to play pretend. They have a big box that they pretend is a car. They take turns to drive the box and go to different places. Sometimes they go to the zoo, sometimes they go to the park, sometimes they go to the moon.

One day, they pretend to go to the bakery. They see a lot of tasty cakes and cookies in the window. They want to try them all. They pretend to buy some with their pretend money. They pretend to eat them and say yum yum.

But then, they see a big spot on the floor. It is brown and sticky. They think it is chocolate. They want to eat it too. They pretend to scoop some with their fingers and put it in their mouths. But it is not chocolate. It is mud. It is very yucky. They spit it out and cry.

Mom hears them and comes to see what is wrong. She sees the mud on their faces and hands and clothes. She is very angry. She tells them to stop playing pretend and go to the bathroom. She says they have to wash and change and say sorry. She says they can't play with the box anymore. She says they are very naughty.

Anna and Ben are very sad. They wish they did not eat the mud. They wish they did not make Mom angry. They wish they could play pretend again. But they can't. They have to go to the bathroom and wash and change and say sorry. They have a bad day.

Once upon a time, there was a special bird. She loved to sing and fly around and make her friends happy. She always sang a song that said "I love the sunshine, I love the soil, I love everything that is clear!"

One day, the bird decided that she wanted to find the most special soil in the world. She flew off to find it, and eventually she came to a place where the soil was a beautiful clear brown color.

The bird was so happy that she started to sing her song again: "I love the sunshine, I love the soil, I love everything that is clear!"

Suddenly, a little boy appeared. He had seen the bird singing and came over to talk to her.

"What do you love it so much?" he asked.

The bird smiled and replied, "I love the soil because it helps us grow things and makes the world a beautiful place."

The boy smiled too and said, "I love the soil too!"

And from that day onwards, the bird and the boy became the best of friends. They both loved the beautiful clear soil, and loved to talk about it whenever they could.

Once upon a time, there was a grumpy bear named Biggie. Biggie didn't like to share his toys with his friends. One day, his friends came over to play with him. They asked Biggie if they could play with his favorite figure. But Biggie said no and kept the figure to himself.

His friends were sad and didn't want to play with him anymore. Biggie felt lonely and realized that he made a mistake. He decided to include his friends in his playtime and share his toys with them. They all played together happily and Biggie learned that sharing is important. From that day on, he was no longer grumpy and his friends loved playing with him.

Once upon a time, there was a friendly leatherworker who really liked to sort things. He sorted twine, needles and leather so he could find them when he needed them.

One day, he decided to make something special out of leather. He worked very hard and soon, something amazing began to take shape. When he finished, it was even better than he had hoped for!

He couldn't wait to show it to the world, so he went to the local craft fair. Everyone who saw it was amazed. They smiled and gave him lots of compliments. He was so proud of himself!

The leatherworker had created something amazing out of leather. He felt so happy that he had been able to sort it all so perfectly. He would always remember how sorting helped him create something so cool!

Tim and Sam were brothers who liked to play with toys. Tim had many toys because he was wealthy, but Sam had only a few toys because he was poor. Tim did not like to share his toys with Sam, and he always said, "These are mine, go away!"

One day, Tim found a magic wand in his room. He did not know where it came from, but he thought it was a toy. He waved it around and said, "I wish Sam would shrink, so he would not bother me anymore!" Suddenly, Sam became very small, like a bug. Tim laughed and said, "Now you are too tiny to play with my toys!"

Sam was scared and sad. He ran away from Tim and looked for a place to hide. He saw a handle on the door and climbed on it. He hoped Tim would not find him there. He wished he had a friend to help him.

But Tim was not happy either. He realized he had no one to play with, and his toys were not fun anymore. He felt lonely and sorry. He wished he had not been mean to Sam. He looked for his brother and said, "Sam, where are you? I am sorry, I want to play with you!"

Sam heard Tim's voice and saw him looking for him. He decided to forgive him and said, "Tim, I am here, on the handle. Please make me big again, I want to play with you too!" Tim saw Sam and felt relieved. He waved the magic wand and said, "I wish Sam would grow, so he would be my brother again!" Sam became big again, and they hugged each other. They decided to share their toys and be friends.

The moral of the story is: Do not be selfish and greedy, or you might lose what you love. Be kind and generous, and you will have more happiness.

Once upon a time, there was a girl called Sally. Sally loved to play in the sunshine near her home. One day, Sally's dad came to her with a special surprise - a raft! He taught Sally how to paddle the raft so that it glided through the water.

Sally and her dad set out in the raft and it felt very peaceful as they floated around the lake. Sally was so sleepy from being out in the sun that she started to feel drowsy. Dad put on some special music, which was like a lullaby. The music made her so cosy and happy that she slept in the raft.

But she was safe, because her dad was there with her, gently guiding the raft back to shore. When they reached home, Sally's mom was waiting with a big hug and a yummy snack. Sally had had such a special day - she could still feel the gentle rocking of the raft as she curled up in bed for the night.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and help her mommy in the kitchen. One day, Lily's mommy asked her to help put the dishes in the dishwasher. 

Lily was excited to help, but the dishes were very rough and hard to hold. She accidentally poked herself on one of the forks and started to cry. 

Her mommy came over and gave her a big hug. "It's okay, Lily. Let me help you with the dishes," she said. 

Lily felt better and watched as her mommy put the dishes in the dishwasher. "Thank you, mommy," she said. 

"You're welcome, sweetie. Now let's go play with your toys," her mommy replied. 

Lily smiled and ran off to play, happy to have helped her mommy and learned how to use the dishwasher.

Mary had a special veil. It glowed with a beautiful pink when the sun shone and it made her look like a Magical Princess. She wore it everywhere and adored it. But one day, when she was wearing it, it started to get noisy. 

At first, it was just a whisper of noise, like a gentle hum. But the longer she wore it, the louder it grew. Mary was scared. She tried to take the veil off, but it was stuck. 

"Mom, help," she cried. "The veil won't come off!"

Mommy held Mary in her arms and tried her best to remove the veil, but it was stuck fast. 

"Let's go find a wise wizard," she said. 

They set out on their journey and the noise coming from the veil only grew louder. After a long day of travelling, the noise was so loud that Mary thought her head would burst. 

The wise wizard heard the noise and knew exactly what was wrong. He told Mary and Mommy that the veil was magical and she had to use a magical spell to break the connection. Mary closed her eyes and concentrated hard. 

Finally, after a long struggle, a spark of light lit up the room, and the veil was gone. Mary looked up in amazement at the wise wizard who had helped her. 

From that day forward, Mary kept her veil

Once upon a time there was a patient gorilla. All his friends wanted to play with him, but he was too shy. One day one of his friends had an idea. She decided to invite the gorilla to a party! The gorilla was scared at first, but he was so excited to be included.

He was the first to arrive at the party. He saw all his friends there, and he was so happy. They all gave him a big hug and they were so excited to see him.

The gorilla was very patient. He let each of his friends have a turn playing with him. At the end of the night, he gave them all big hugs goodbye. The friends all said goodbye and promised to invite the gorilla to the next party!

Heidi was a three year old girl with bright eyes. She had a lot of toys to play with that day. She was playing in her room with a toy farm and pretending that the toy pigs were real. 

Suddenly, she heard a noise outside her window. Heidi stopped playing and walked over to the window to see what was happening. Outside, she saw a long vine dripping with water. It was so green and wet!

Heidi had an idea. She opened the window, put her arm out, and started to wrap the vine around her arm. She pretended it was a snake. It was slimy and wiggled in her hand. She smiled and laughed with delight.

Suddenly, Heidi heard her mom calling her name. She quickly backed away from the window and said, "Oops, I better go." She put the vine back outside, ran back to her toys, and started to play again.

Jimmy was walking in the west, feeling troubled. He was worried about what might happen next. Then he saw a big truck. It made a loud noise, so Jimmy yelled "Oh no!" He felt scared.

Suddenly, his mother appeared. She said, "It's okay, Jimmy. That truck is just going by." Jimmy felt better. He stopped yelling and smiled.

His mother took his hand and they walked west together. The sun was setting and Jimmy felt happy. Everything was OK now. He wasn't troubled anymore.

Once upon a time, there was a little bunny named Benny. Benny loved to play outside in the sun and count the flowers in the field. One day, Benny saw a wild butterfly fluttering around a light. The butterfly was so pretty and Benny wanted to catch it.

Benny chased the butterfly around the light, but the butterfly was too fast. Suddenly, the light went out and Benny was scared. He didn't know how to get back home in the dark. But then he remembered how he counted the flowers in the field. He closed his eyes and counted to ten, and when he opened them again, he saw the light from his home.

The moral of the story is that sometimes we get distracted by pretty things, but we should always remember what we know and count on ourselves to find our way back.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in her backyard. One day, she noticed a big gate at the end of her yard. She had never seen it before.

Lily went to her mommy and said, "Mommy, what is behind the gate?" 

Her mommy replied, "I don't know, let's go check it out." 

As they approached the gate, they heard a loud growling sound. They were both scared and didn't know what to do. Suddenly, a big dog appeared from behind the gate. The dog was angry and barking loudly. 

But then, the dog's owner came out and revealed that the dog was just trying to protect his yard. Lily and her mommy were relieved and happy to have met the friendly dog and his owner. From that day on, they became good friends with their new neighbors.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and her favorite toy was a stuffed bear named Teddy. One day, Lily's mom brought home a big box with a symbol on it. Lily was curious and asked, "What's inside the box, Mommy?"

Her mom said, "It's a surprise, Lily. But I'll let you open it." Lily was so excited and quickly tore open the box. Inside was a new toy for Teddy to play with. "Thank you, Mommy!" Lily said with a big smile.

Later that day, Lily and Teddy went to the park to play. They met a little boy named Max who was sad because he lost his toy car. Lily and Teddy wanted to help Max find his toy. "Let's look under the slide," Lily said. Max looked under the slide and found his toy car. "Thank you, Lily and Teddy!" Max said happily. 

Lily and Teddy were happy to help Max and they all played together at the park. When it was time to go home, Lily's mom said, "I'm so proud of you for helping Max. You are kind and thoughtful." Lily smiled and hugged her mom. It was a happy day for Lily, Teddy, and Max.

Once upon a time, there was a lonely beach far away. It was a happy beach, with lots of fun things to do. One day, some people went to the beach to work. They worked very hard, carrying things in their arms and building things.

At the end of the day, the beach was very different. It now had a big, nice fence around it. The people smiled and patted each other's backs. Then they left.

Now, the beach was lonely. The people had gone home and the sand was quiet. But the beach was happy in its own way, because the people had done a good job. Now the beach was different, but still was very nice.

Lily was a big girl who had a loose tooth. She was very proud of her tooth and wanted to show it to everyone. She hoped that the tooth fairy would come and give her a coin when her tooth fell out.

One day, she was playing with her little brother Max, who liked to copy everything she did. He saw her wiggling her tooth with her tongue and tried to do the same. But he did not have a loose tooth, so he bit his tongue instead. He cried out loud and ran to their mom.

Lily felt bad for Max, but she also felt angry. She thought he was trying to take her tooth away from her. She said to him, "That's my tooth, not yours! You can't have it, it's mine!"

Max looked at her with big, wet eyes. He was confused and hurt. He did not understand why Lily was mad at him. He said, "I'm sorry, Lily. I just wanted to be like you. I love you."

Lily heard his words and saw his face. She realized that he was not trying to steal her tooth, he was just curious and wanted to play with her. She felt sorry for being mean to him. She hugged him and said, "I love you too, Max. I'm sorry, I forgive you. You can wiggle your tongue if you want, but be careful not to bite it."

They smiled at each other and went back to playing. Lily forgot about her tooth for a while, until she felt something fall out of her mouth. She looked down and saw her tooth on the floor. She was so happy and excited. She picked it up and ran to show it to Max and their mom. She said, "Look, look, my tooth came out! I can't wait for the tooth fairy to come!"

Max clapped his hands and said, "Wow, Lily, you did it! You have a big gap in your smile. You look so funny and cute!"

They laughed and hugged each other. They were happy and proud of Lily's tooth. They put it under her pillow and waited for the tooth fairy to come. They hoped she would bring a shiny coin for Lily, and maybe a little something for Max too.

One day, a girl wanted to be a dancer. She was so excited to paint a picture of herself dancing. She got out her brush, the paint and a big piece of paper.

She began to paint. She painted the sky blue, made a big sun with yellow paint, and painted many bright coloured flowers. Then she started to paint herself. She painted herself in a pink dress with sparkly wings.

The girl was so happy and she danced around, twirling and leaping. Suddenly, her mum walked in. She was worried. "Where did you get the paint?" She asked.

The girl was scared. She started to shake and tears welled up in her eyes. She whispered, "It was in the cupboard".

Her mum sighed. "You must always ask me first before taking things from the cupboard. I will go and buy you your own paints so that you can paint safely."

The girl was relieved and thanked her mum. From then on, she had her own paints to use anytime she wanted to paint.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Jack. Jack had a special box full of rice. Every time Jack opened the box, the rice fell out everywhere. It made Jack so sad.

One day, Jack decided to be organized. He neatly lined up the rice in the box and put the lid on top. Then, Jack smiled and clapped his hands.

Just then, something happened! Jack felt a sudden gust of cold wind and heard a loud noise. Suddenly, the lid of the box flew off and the rice went everywhere. Jack started to cry.

Just then, Jack's mom appeared. She had a big smile on her face and hugged Jack. Then, she used some tape to stick the box together and the rice was safe. Jack felt happy again!

One day, a cheerful little girl named Lily went to visit her friend, Tim. Tim lived near the beach. Lily loved the beach because she could find many shells there. She wanted to find a big shell to show her friend.

When Lily got to the beach, she saw Tim. "Hi, Tim!" she said. "Let's look for shells together!" Tim smiled and said, "Yes, let's go!" They walked on the sand and found many shells. Some were big, some were small, but they wanted to find the biggest shell of all.

They walked and walked until they found a huge shell. "Wow!" said Lily. "This is the biggest shell ever!" But when they picked up the shell, a big crab came out. The crab was not happy. It snapped its claws at Lily and Tim. They were scared and ran away. They dropped the big shell and it broke into pieces. They did not find the biggest shell, and they were sad. But they learned to be careful when picking up shells at the beach.

Once upon a time there was a big wild cat. It was terrible and scary. One morning, it went to the woods to stretch. It moved its legs and arms and made itself very long.

Suddenly, a tiny mouse appeared. It was not afraid of the cat. It stood on its hind legs and started to stretch too. The mouse wanted to be as tall as the cat.

The cat was surprised. It looked at the little mouse and couldn't stop watching. Then it smiled and stretched out even longer. The mouse was amazed and thought the cat was so cool.

They both stretched together and enjoyed their day in the woods. The mouse jumped onto the cat's back and they stretched more and more. They stretched so much that they became tiny again and went on their way. 

The mouse and the cat were very happy and said goodbye. From then on, they stretched whenever they were together - and that made them both very happy!

Lily and Max are twins. They like to play and have fun. But sometimes they do not behave. They make noise, run around and do not listen to Mom and Dad.

One day, Mom and Dad take them to the zoo. They have to ride the bus. The bus is big and yellow. It has many seats and windows. Lily and Max are excited. They want to see the animals.

But on the bus, they do not behave. They shout, jump and kick the seats. They make the other people angry. Mom and Dad tell them to stop. They say, "Lily and Max, you have to behave. The bus is not a playground. You have to be quiet and sit still. Or we will not go to the zoo."

Lily and Max do not listen. They think it is fun to be naughty. They laugh and say, "No, no, no. We do not want to behave. We want to play. The bus is fun. We do not care about the zoo."

Mom and Dad are sad and mad. They say, "Lily and Max, this is your last chance. If you do not behave, we will go back home. And you will not see the animals. You will not see the lions, the monkeys, the elephants or the giraffes. You will miss all the fun. Is that what you want?"

Lily and Max look at each other. They think about the animals. They love the animals. They want to see them. They do not want to miss the fun. They do not want to go back home. They say, "Sorry, Mom and Dad. We will behave. We will be quiet and sit still. We want to go to the zoo. Please, please, please."

Mom and Dad smile. They say, "Okay, Lily and Max. We are glad you will behave. We love you. But you have to remember, the zoo is not a playground either. You have to follow the rules. You have to be nice and gentle to the animals. You have to be careful and safe. The zoo is tough. Some animals can bite or scratch or roar. Do you understand?"

Lily and Max nod. They say, "Yes, Mom and Dad. We understand. We will follow the rules. We will be nice and gentle and careful and safe. We will not be naughty. We will be good. The zoo is tough. But we are tough too. We are ready to see the animals. Let's go, let's go, let's go."

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and pick flowers. One day, she found a big box on the ground. She wanted to see what was inside, so she opened it. 

Inside the box was a bag of salt. It was very smelly! Lily didn't like the smell, but she wanted to play with the salt. She poured it all over the ground and made pretty patterns. 

But then, a big rainstorm came. The rain mixed with the salt and made a big mess. The flowers died and the ground became hard and dry. Lily was sad because she didn't know the salt would hurt the flowers. She learned that sometimes things that seem fun can have bad consequences.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy had a big thumb that he liked to suck on. His mom always told him to stop sucking his thumb, but he couldn't help it.

One day, Timmy was walking in the park when he saw a big dog. The dog was very alert and barked loudly. Timmy got scared and wanted to run away, but he tripped and fell.

Suddenly, the dog stopped barking and came over to Timmy. Timmy was scared at first, but the dog licked his face and became his friend. From that day on, Timmy stopped sucking his thumb and played with his new furry friend in the park every day.

Once upon a time, there were two friends called Bill and Ben. They were going on a great adventure, and needed to hurry. They grabbed their trunks and set off.

First, they walked through the grassy field, and the wild flowers smelled sweet. Then, they went to the grocery store and picked up something that smelled spicy.

Finally, they walked to the playground. It was so much fun and they ran around and giggled until they were out of breath. But soon they realised it was getting late, so they had to hurry home.

They both picked up their trunks and raced each other home. And when they arrived, they were both so happy and excited to tell the story of their adventure.

Once upon a time there was a lucky girl named Jenny. She was very happy, always playing in the sunshine. 

One day she found a toy magnet that sparkled in the sun. She picked it up and as she did, it started to burn her hand. 

"Ouch!" she said, shaking her hand. She looked around and noticed an old lady smiling at her.

The old lady said, "Ah, that happens when you find something so special- it's like it burns with joy!"

Jenny looked back at the magnet with a smile. She thanked the old lady before taking the magnet home with her. 

From then on Jenny always felt lucky when she held the magnet, and kept it beside her always.

Once upon a time, there was a happy little boy who lived near a big forest. He liked to explore the path that went into the forest, because it was the most exciting thing around.

One day the boy left his home to explore the path. He followed the path into the forest and he was amazed to find that it led him to a big lake. There was a dock near the lake and he could see a little boat.

The boy was so excited that he decided to go for a ride in the boat. He got in the boat and off he went. The boy felt very safe because the lake seemed harmless and the waves were gentle.

As the sun began to set, the boy realized that he had been gone for too long. He quickly steered the boat back towards the dock, then ran back along the path.

When he finally got home, his family was very happy to see him safe and sound! They all agreed that he should only explore the path when it was light outside so he could always find his way home.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Mary. Mary was a very curious girl and she wanted to learn all the numbers very quickly. 

Every day, she asked her mom to help her with her numbers and her mom was more than happy to teach her. One day, she decided to take a quiz to see how much she had learned.

Mary asked her mom if there was a quiz she could take and her mom smiled. She told Mary that there was an available quiz online and she could take it anytime she wanted. 

Mary was really excited to take the quiz and she clicked on it right away. She was a little nervous, but she did her best and answered all the questions. 

When Mary was finished, she was happy to find out that she had gotten all of the answers right. Mary was very proud of herself for doing so well on the quiz and she could not wait to learn even more numbers.

One day, a little boy named Tim saw a big cloud in the sky. He wanted to catch the cloud. Tim asked his friend, Sam, "How do I catch the cloud?"

Sam did not know. He said, "I don't know, let's ask our teacher." They went to their teacher and asked her how to catch a cloud. The teacher smiled and said, "You can't catch a cloud. They are too high and made of water."

Tim and Sam were sad but they learned something new. They were no longer ignorant about clouds. They went outside and played, looking at the clouds and imagining what shapes they could see.

Once there was a little girl who loved to play outside. She had a special skirt that was made just for her. This skirt was bright and open. The little girl liked to put it on and twirl around in the sunshine. 

Today, she decided she was going to stay outside all day and play in her open skirt. She raced around, laughed and ran in circles. She loved feeling the sunshine and wind on her skin. 

The day was coming to an end, and all the other children had gone home. But the little girl remained in her open skirt. She loved playing in nature and wanted to stay a bit longer. 

So she stayed outside and watched the sunset until it was dark. The little girl smiled because she knew that tomorrow she could put on her open skirt and play outside again. 

The sun, the wind and the open skirt. She loved them all and wanted to remain in that sunny moment forever.

Once upon a time there was a family who lived in a big house. One day Mama and Papa brought home a special present - an attractive vase! It was round with a lot of pretty colours.

Mama hugged Papa with excitement. "Let's put it right by the window," she said.

Papa smiled. He picked up the vase and put it on the table. Then he showed it to the little girl and said, "Look, a beautiful vase! What do you think?"

The little girl was very happy. She hugged the vase and said, "Pretty!" 

Mama and Papa laughed. They hugged the girl and said, "Yes, it's very attractive." 

The girl smiled, hugged her family and went off to play. 

The family enjoyed the vase for many years and it always reminded them of the happy day they brought it home.

Once upon a time there was a little flea. He was white and very small. One day, he was hopping around in the park when he saw a man. The man had a box in his hands and he was looking very happy. The man smiled at the flea and looked down at him.

The man picked up the box and asked the flea if he wanted a ride. The flea was very excited and happily said yes. The man gently lifted the flea up, and the flea crawled into the box. The man smiled and carried the box with the flea inside.

The flea looked around and saw that he was high up in the sky. As they flew, the flea could see all the beautiful colors of the world, which made him feel very happy. The man took the flea to his home and after a while, the man carefully lifted the box and put the flea on the ground.

The flea thanked the man and hopped away into the sunshine. He smiled as he thought of his thrilling adventure. He knew that he would always remember the man lifting him high up in the sky.

Once upon a time, there was a little dog named Spot. Spot was a very happy dog. He had a big yard to play in and a family that loved him. Spot liked to run and jump and play all day long.

One day, Spot saw a big box near the door. He did not know what was in it, but he wanted to see. Spot tried to open the box, but he had a struggle. He pushed and pulled, but the box would not open. Spot was sad.

Then, Spot's family came home. They saw Spot and the box. They opened the box for him. Inside was a new friend for Spot! It was a little cat named Fluffy. Spot and Fluffy played together and had lots of fun. Spot's family gave Fluffy a welcome to their home. Spot was happy to have a new friend to play with.

Ben and Lily were best friends. They liked to play with toys, draw pictures and listen to music. One day, Ben brought a new CD to Lily's house. He said, "This is my favorite music. It is very fun and loud. Do you want to hear it?"

Lily nodded and smiled. She liked music too. Ben put the CD in the player and turned it on. The music was very fun and loud. Ben and Lily started to dance and jump. They had a lot of fun.

But Lily's mom did not like the music. She was upset. She came to the room and said, "What is this noise? Turn it off! It is too loud and rude. It hurts my ears."

Ben and Lily stopped dancing and jumping. They looked at Lily's mom. They were scared. Ben said, "I'm sorry, Lily's mom. This is my favorite music. It is not noise. It is fun and loud."

Lily's mom said, "I don't care. I don't like it. It is not good music. You have to turn it off. And you have to go home, Ben. You can't play here anymore."

Ben and Lily were very sad. They did not understand why Lily's mom was so upset. They liked the music. They liked to play together. They did not want to go home. They did not want to stop being friends.

But they had to accept what Lily's mom said. They turned off the music. Ben took his CD and said goodbye to Lily. He said, "I'm sorry, Lily. I hope you are not mad at me. I still like you. You are still my best friend."

Lily said, "I'm not mad at you, Ben. I still like you too. You are still my best friend. Maybe we can play again another day. Maybe we can listen to another music. A music that Lily's mom likes too."

Ben and Lily hugged and smiled. They hoped they could play again another day. They hoped they could find a music that everyone liked. They hoped they could be happy again.

Once upon a time, there were two friends: a puppy and a kitten. They were the best of friends and loved to play together.

One day, the puppy noticed the kitten had a fluffy toy in his paws. The puppy said, "What's that?" 

The kitten smiled and said, "It's mine. I found it behind the shed. I was trying to lift it, but it's too heavy!"

The puppy said, "Let me help! We can lift it together."

The two friends grabbed the toy and with a lot of strength and energy, they lifted it.

The puppy smiled, "See? That wasn't so hard!"

The kitten looked at the toy and said, "Hey - there must be an owner! All these pieces look very organized. I'm sure the owner will be happy to get it back." 

The two friends found the owner and returned the toy. The owner thanked them for being so kind and organized. 

The puppy and kitten smiled and said, "We're happy to help!" They hugged each other and went happily on their way.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy liked to play games with his friends. They would sit on the couch and play games on Timmy's tablet. One day, Timmy's friend brought a new game that was very competitive. They all wanted to win, so they took turns playing. 

After a while, Timmy's tablet ran out of battery. He asked his dad to help him load the tablet with more power. While they were waiting, Timmy's dad suggested they play a game of their own. They decided to have a race to see who could run the fastest. Timmy's dad let him win, but they both had a lot of fun. 

When Timmy's friends saw how much fun they had, they wanted to join in too. They all ran around the house, laughing and having a good time. Timmy realized that even though the competitive game was fun, playing with his friends and family was even better. From then on, they made sure to have more fun together and not just focus on winning.

Once upon a time, there was a hairy monster who lived in a cave. The monster was very lonely and had no friends to play with.

One day, the monster heard a voice coming from outside the cave. It was a very kind voice and the monster decided to investigate.

When he looked outside, the monster saw a small girl playing by herself. She smiled and asked the monster to play with her.

The monster was very happy and the two friends played together for the whole day. At the end of the day, the girl said she would come back tomorrow and she left.

The next day, the little girl returned with a big surprise. It was a big hairy bear which she had found in the forest. She asked the monster if he wanted to support her in looking after it.

The monster smiled and agreed. He met the bear and the two became friends. Now the monster had two friends to play with. He was no longer lonely, because he had the support of his new furry friends.

Once there was a lady who wanted to design something different. She was really creative, so she thought about all the possibilities. She thought about a rough alligator and how fun it would be. 

She started to work hard, gathering materials from all around. She had felt and pieces of string, and she cut them into shapes with her scissors. Once she was happy with the pieces she put them together.

The lady was really proud of her design. She had made a rough alligator! Its teeth were made from small pieces of felt and its eyes were made from buttons. Its tail was as long as a regular alligator and its body was made of pieces of string. 

The lady was so excited to show off her creation. She took her rough alligator and took it outside. Everyone was so surprised to see her rough alligator! They had never seen anything like it before. 

The lady and her rough alligator were the center of attention. Everyone clapped and cheered as they took turns carrying the alligator around. Everyone was so proud of the lady and her design. She had done an amazing job!

Tim and Sam are brothers. They like to play in their room. They have many toys and books. They also have a big bed that is comfortable. They can jump and roll on the bed.

One day, they are playing with their cars on the bed. They make noises and pretend to drive fast. Tim has a red car and Sam has a blue car. They have fun.

But then, Tim sees a knob on the wall. He is curious. He wants to touch it. He leaves his car on the bed and walks to the wall. He reaches for the knob.

"Tim, no!" Sam shouts. He knows the knob is for the light. He knows Mom and Dad said not to touch it. He is afraid Tim will hurt himself. He runs to the wall and grabs Tim's hand.

"Stop, Tim! That is a bad knob. It can make a big flash and a loud boom. It can make you cry. Mom and Dad will be angry. Come back to the bed. It is safe and comfortable."

Tim is surprised. He does not know the knob is bad. He does not want to make a flash or a boom. He does not want to cry or make Mom and Dad angry. He listens to Sam. He lets go of the knob and follows Sam to the bed.

"Thank you, Sam. You are a good brother. You saved me from the bad knob. I am sorry I was silly. Can we play with our cars again?"

"Yes, Tim. You are welcome. I am happy you are okay. I love you. We can play with our cars again. But we have to be careful and not touch the bad knob."

They hug and smile. They pick up their cars and play on the bed. They are happy and comfortable. They are good brothers.

Once upon a time, there were two friends, Jack and Jill. They had lots of fun playing together. They would play games and tell stories.

One day, Jack was playing with a match. Jill was really nosy and wanted to know what Jack was doing with the match. Jack wouldn't tell her, so Jill decided to look and see for herself.

When Jill revealed what Jack was doing, Jack got really angry. He was mad that Jill had been so nosy! He took the match and threw it away.

From then on, Jack and Jill didn't play together anymore, and they never talked again. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy liked to play outside. He had a swing in his backyard. Timmy loved to swing high in the sky. 

One day, Timmy fell off the swing and hurt his skin. His mommy came outside and saw that Timmy was hurt. She cleaned his skin and put a bandage on it. Timmy felt better.

Later that day, Timmy broke his mommy's vase by accident. He felt guilty and said sorry. His mommy forgave him and gave him a hug. Timmy learned that it's important to be careful and honest when accidents happen.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily was getting ready for bed when she noticed that her favorite dress was still on its hanger in the closet. She felt nervous because she wanted to wear it tomorrow but didn't want to take it off the hanger by herself. 

Lily's mom came in to help and showed her how to remove the dress from the hanger. Lily was so happy and thanked her mom for helping her. She put on her dress and twirled around her room, feeling like a princess. 

From that day on, Lily felt proud and confident in removing her clothes from their hangers all by herself. She even helped her little brother with his clothes too!

Once upon a time there were two best friends, Mary and Jane. Mary was a little bit older than Jane, but they were still very close.

One day, they went out to the playground to play. They saw a big box full of different styles of spray cans. They wanted to try them out to make something pretty.

They each chose their favourite colour and started to spray their artwork onto the ground. Mary's picture was pink and Jane's was yellow. They were both very excited to see the pictures they made.

Suddenly, out of nowhere, a gust of wind swept across the playground. It made Mary and Jane's artwork look rough, and it ruined all of their hard work.

Mary and Jane were disappointed, but then they realized something. No matter what happened, they would still always be best friends. They hugged each other and went off to get ice cream in celebration.

Once upon a time, there was a farmer named Jack. Jack had a big farm with many animals. He had cows, horses, pigs, and chickens. Jack was a mighty farmer and he worked very hard every day to take care of his animals.

One day, Jack saw a little boy walking on the farm. The boy was lost and didn't know how to find his way back home. Jack knelt down to talk to the boy and asked him where he lived. The boy told Jack his address and Jack called his parents to come and pick him up.

The boy's parents were very grateful to Jack for helping their son. They thanked him and gave him some fresh eggs from their own farm. Jack was very happy and he felt proud of himself for being a good person. From that day on, Jack knew that he would always help anyone who needed it, no matter what.

John and his sister Sarah were playing in the living room. John was clapping his hands together and Sarah was looking around. She saw a beautiful ornament on the mantle above the fireplace.

It was silver and round with red and green decorations on it. Sarah thought it was so pretty she wanted to take it down. John started clapping again and Sarah saw her chance. She carefully took the ornament down and hugged it close.

The two children laughed and clapped their hands together. They enjoyed the ornament so much that they decided to keep it. They put it down very gently and it shone in the mild sunlight. 

John and Sarah enjoyed looking at their new ornament every day. They always clapped their hands when they saw it. It made them happy and remind them of their fun day.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a sister named Emily. Emily was very fair, with blonde hair and blue eyes. One day, Lily and Emily were playing in the park. Lily wanted to play on the swings, but Emily wanted to play on the slide. Lily didn't mind and they took turns playing on both. 

After a while, Lily got hungry and asked Emily if she wanted to share her snack. Emily said yes and they sat on the grass to eat. Lily was happy to have such a kind sister. They finished their snack and went back to playing. They played until the sun started to set and it was time to go home. 

Lily was tired and Emily offered to carry her on her back. Lily felt safe and happy with her sister. When they got home, Lily gave Emily a big hug and said thank you. Emily smiled and hugged her back. They went to bed, dreaming of all the fun they would have together the next day. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a wise owl who loved to draw with his pencil. One day, the owl was drawing a beautiful picture when he accidentally dropped his pencil. The pencil rolled away and the owl couldn't reach it.

"Can you help me move my pencil back?" asked the owl to a friendly rabbit passing by.

"Of course!" said the rabbit, hopping over to the pencil. The rabbit picked up the pencil and moved it back to the owl.

"Thank you so much!" said the owl, happy to have his pencil back. "You are very kind and wise, my friend."

From then on, the owl and the rabbit became good friends and would often draw together with their pencils. They would always help each other move their pencils when needed.

Once upon a time, there was a young girl named Lucy. She loved to pretend when she was playing. She often acted like a princess or a firefighter.

One day, she wanted to act like a doctor. But she did not have any medical equipment. Lucy asked her mom, "Mommy, can I be a doctor and help sick patients?" Her mom said, "Honey, you don't have any of the equipment that doctors need to help patients. Why don't you help me take care of the plants and flowers in our garden?"

Lucy thought for a moment and said, "I can try, but I would have been more happy if I acted like a doctor." Her mom smiled and said, "Even though you don't have any medical equipment, you can still be a doctor of sorts. You can help people by being kind and caring. You can take care of animals and help old people when they need it. Doing nice things and being kind is just like being a doctor."

Lucy understood the moral lesson, and she felt proud of herself. Her mom hugged her with love and said, "you are never too young to start helping and being kind." The young girl was happy and acted on her mom's advice right away. From then on Lucy often helped people who were in need of help.

Kallie was a brave girl, who liked adventures very much. She decided one day to explore the woods around her house. Kallie walked in the woods, looking around her. She wanted to find something new and exciting.

Suddenly, she saw a little hut in the distant. She was curious, so she went closer. When she arrived, she realized the hut was very old and she could feel the wind coming in through the cracks in the walls. Kallie started to shiver, but she was also excited to explore. 

She opened the door and stepped in. Inside she saw a cozy room with a fireplace and a warm blanket. She felt safe and happy. Kallie decided to stay for a while and make the hut her own special place for adventures. She could come back and hide away from the world whenever she needed.

The hut was Kallie's secret distant refuge and she loved it more every day.

One day, Tom was playing at the park. He wanted to ride on the slide. Suddenly, his older brother, Jack, came over.

"Tom, let's go ride the horses!" said Jack.

Tom hesitated. He really wanted to go on the slide. But then he thought it would be more fun to ride with Jack. "Ok," he said. He followed Jack to the horse's stable.

Inside, they found two lovely white horses. Tom and Jack said hello to them. Then they got on the horses and began to ride.

They were having a great time until they reached the edge of the forest. Suddenly, the horses stopped and wouldn't move no matter what they did.

Tom noticed a mineral rock blocking their path. He got off his horse and moved it out of the way. The horses could now ride through the forest.

Jack looked at Tom with love. "Thanks, Tom," he said.

Tom smiled. He was glad that he could help his brother. Together, they rode into the forest and had a wonderful time.

Sara and Ben were twins who liked to travel with their mom and dad. They had a big car that could fit all their toys and clothes. Sometimes they went to the beach, sometimes they went to the mountains, and sometimes they went to see their grandma and grandpa.

One day, they went to a farm where they saw many animals. There were cows, horses, sheep, pigs, chickens, and ducks. Sara and Ben wanted to pet them all, but their mom and dad told them to be careful and gentle. They also told them not to touch the fence, because it had electricity to keep the animals safe.

Sara and Ben listened to their mom and dad, but they were very curious. They saw a big horse that had a long mane and a shiny coat. It looked very graceful and friendly. Sara and Ben wanted to pet it, but it was behind the fence. They thought they could reach it if they stretched their arms.

"Look, Ben, the horse is smiling at us!" Sara said. "Let's go and say hello!"

"OK, Sara, but be quiet. We don't want to scare it," Ben said.

They tiptoed to the fence and reached out their hands. But as soon as they touched the wire, they felt a zap and a shock. They screamed and jumped back. The horse neighed and ran away.

"Ow, ow, ow! That hurt!" Sara cried.

"Me too, me too! That was bad!" Ben cried.

Their mom and dad heard them and ran to them. They hugged them and checked them for injuries. They were not hurt, but they had a red mark on their fingers and an itch on their skin.

"What happened, Sara and Ben? Why did you touch the fence?" their mom asked.

"We wanted to pet the horse, mom. It was so pretty and nice," Sara said.

"But the fence has electricity, Sara. We told you not to touch it. It can hurt you and the animals," their dad said.

"We're sorry, mom and dad. We didn't know. We won't do it again," Ben said.

Their mom and dad kissed them and gave them some cream for their itch. They also gave them some water and cookies. They told them they still loved them, but they had to be more careful and listen to them.

Sara and Ben said they were sorry and they loved them too. They learned their lesson and decided to watch the animals from a distance. They still enjoyed their travel to the farm, but they never touched the fence again.

Once upon a time, there lived a little boy called Tom. Tom had a special job, to protect the town from danger. One day, Tom had the perfect plan to protect the town from the bad monsters. 

Tom took some big steps towards the monsters. The monsters didn't know what to do and they quickly started to run away. Tom knew he had to be fast if he wanted to protect the town.

He ran and he ran and he ran. One of the monsters shouted at him, "Where do you think you're going? You can't escape!" But Tom didn't stop, he kept going and going.

Soon he reached a secret door with a sign which read: "Perfect escape". As soon as Tom opened the door, all the monsters ran away never to be seen again. Tom smiled to himself and the town was safe.

Once upon a time there was a careless sailor who set sail in the middle of the night. As the sailor journeyed along on his boat, he noticed something special in the sky. It was a bright, golden star that shined so brightly it lit up the night sky and made the sailor stop in his tracks.

The sailor asked the star, "Why do you shine so brightly? What do you value?"

The star replied, "I value kindness and being helpful to everyone. So I shine ever so brightly so that everyone will be reminded to do the same."

The sailor thought deeply and then said, "Thank you star, I will try to do the same."

The star smiled brightly at the sailor, "You are welcome. I am happy to see my lesson was valued." 

The sailor sailed off happy and content, reminding himself to always keep his virtue of kindness.

Once upon a time there was a princess who lived in a big castle. One day the princess went for a walk in the garden and discovered a brilliant diamond. She was very excited and picked it up to show the queen. 

The queen was amazed. She said, "This is an incredible diamond! Where did you find it?"

The princess smiled and said, "I found it in the garden, mummy! Let's spend it on something nice."

The queen thought for a moment and said, "Yes, let's use the diamond to buy you a big, beautiful dress to wear to the ball."

So they went off to the market and the princess picked out a beautiful dress. The dress sparkled like the diamond and she was very happy. 

The princess wore the dress to the ball and was admired by everyone. That night was an incredible night filled with fun, laughter and music. 

The princess had a wonderful time and went to bed with a smile on her face. She was thankful for the wonderful night she had spent with her family.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys, but his favorite toy was a little truck. He would play with it all the time and pretend it was driving through a mine. One day, Timmy's friend Johnny came over to play. Johnny also had a truck, but it was bigger than Timmy's. They decided to race their trucks, but it was a struggle for Timmy to keep up because Johnny's truck was faster. 

Timmy didn't want to give up, though. He was very competitive and wanted to win. So, he tried his best and even though he didn't win the race, he was proud of himself for not giving up. After the race, they played with their trucks in the mine and had a lot of fun together. Timmy realized that it didn't matter who had the bigger or faster truck, as long as they had fun playing together. From that day on, Timmy and Johnny played together often and had many more adventures with their trucks in the mine.

Once upon a time, a little bear named Benny was very hungry. He wanted to eat some yummy berries, but he didn't know where to find them. Benny walked and walked until he found a big bush with lots of red berries on it. He was so happy and excited!

But then, Benny saw a big bird named Billy also gazing at the berries. Billy looked very mean and ready to fight for the berries. Benny didn't want to fight, but he was so hungry. He tried to ask nicely if he could have some berries, but Billy just squawked and flapped his wings.

Benny didn't know what to do. He didn't want to be mean like Billy, but he was so hungry. Just when he thought he might have to go without berries, a kind squirrel named Sally came along. She saw the conflict and decided to share the berries with Benny and Billy. They all sat together and ate the delicious berries happily ever after.

Once there was a wide river that ran through a meadow. On the opposite bank there was a copper mountain. The mountain was so tall and shiny, it made the meadow look small.

Everyone in the meadow loved the copper mountain, but no one more than Billy. He would spend every sunny day looking across the river at the copper mountain and dreaming about visiting it.

One day, a giant came down from the copper mountain. His name was Dave. Dave said he had come to the meadow because he hated the copper mountain. Everyone was perplexed. What kind of person would hate such a beautiful thing?

But then Billy realized something. Dave must have been living on the copper mountain alone and had no one to talk to. Even the tallest and shiniest mountain can feel lonely if you don't have someone to share it with.

Billy knew what he had to do. He took Dave's hand, and together, they crossed the wide river to the copper mountain. As soon as they were there, Dave's frown went away and a huge smile appeared. Dave had found a good friend and the copper mountain hadn't felt so happy in a long time.

Tom liked to play with his toys, but he was bored of the same ones every day. He wanted something new and fun. He asked his mom if he could go to the pet shop and look at the animals.

"Sure, Tom, but you can't buy any. We have enough pets at home," his mom said.

Tom and his mom went to the pet shop. Tom saw many animals. He saw cats, dogs, birds, fish, hamsters, and rabbits. He liked them all, but he wanted something different. He saw a tank with lizards. They had green scales, long tails, and sticky tongues. They looked cool and funny.

"Mom, can I choose a lizard?" Tom asked.

"No, Tom, lizards are not good pets for you. They need special food and care. They might bite or scratch you. They are not cuddly or friendly. They are boring," his mom said.

Tom was sad. He thought lizards were not boring. He thought they were interesting and fun. He wanted to choose a lizard and play with it. He looked at the lizards again. One of them looked at him too. It blinked its eyes and stuck out its tongue. It seemed to say, "Choose me, choose me!"

Tom smiled. He had an idea. He took his mom's hand and said, "Mom, can I choose a toy lizard instead? They look like the real ones, but they are soft and safe. They are not boring, they are fun!"

His mom looked at the toy lizards. They were colorful and cute. They had buttons and sounds. They were cheap and easy. She nodded and said, "OK, Tom, you can choose a toy lizard. But only one, OK?"

Tom was happy. He thanked his mom and ran to the toy lizards. He looked at them carefully. He wanted to choose the best one. He saw one that looked like the real one that blinked at him. It was green and had a long tail and a sticky tongue. It had a button that made it move and squeak. Tom liked it a lot. He picked it up and said, "I choose you, lizard!"

He hugged his toy lizard and showed it to his mom. His mom smiled and said, "Good choice, Tom. You have a good eye. What will you name your lizard?"

Tom thought for a moment. He remembered the real lizard that looked at him. He said, "I will name him Blink. He is my new friend."

His mom paid for the toy lizard and they left the pet shop. Tom held Blink in his arms and played with him. He was not bored anymore. He was happy. He had chosen a lizard.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the green grass. One day, she saw a big field with lots of sheep in it. She thought they were very cute and unusual. 

Lily wanted to enter the field and get closer to the sheep. She walked slowly towards the gate and opened it. The sheep were all around her, and they started to come closer too. 

Lily was very happy to be with the sheep. She petted them and talked to them. She stayed with them until it was time for dinner. From then on, she visited the sheep every day and they became her new friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little brown dog named Spot. Spot loved to play in the park with his friend, a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily's mom said they only had a minute left to play before they had to go home.

Spot barked, "Stay, Lily! Just one more minute!" But Lily's mom said they had to go. 

Lily hugged Spot and said, "Don't worry, we'll come back tomorrow and play again!" Spot wagged his tail happily and watched as Lily and her mom walked away. He knew he couldn't wait to see her again tomorrow.

Once upon a time, there was a big grill in the park. The grill was very dirty. A small girl named Amy saw the grill and wanted to help clean it.

Amy found a cloth and started to wipe the grill. As she wiped, a crazy bird came by and started to dance. The bird was very funny and made Amy laugh.

Amy and the crazy bird became friends. They cleaned the grill together and had a fun day in the park. Then, they went home to tell their families about their new friend and the clean grill.

Once upon a time, there was an adorable bunny. The bunny wanted to go on an adventure and explore the world! He hopped up to the window and saw a driver outside in his car. 

The bunny asked the driver, "Can I come along on your adventure?" 

The driver said, "Sure! Hop in and we'll go!" 

The bunny was so excited! He quickly hopped into the car and off they went.

Then, the bunny noticed that the driver was driving very fast. He also noticed that the driver was not following the rules of the road. The bunny was a bit scared but he kept quiet.

Suddenly, the driver got into a terrible accident. The bunny was so frightened that he could not move. 

In the end, the bunny learned the important lesson that it's never okay to break the rules. It is important to always be careful, no matter what kind of adventure you are on.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her dolls and teddy bears. One day, she was playing with her dolls when she noticed a big rag on the floor. It looked disgusting and dirty.

Lily's mom came in and saw the rag too. "Lily, please pick up that rag and throw it away," she said. "Okay mommy," replied Lily.

Lily picked up the rag and counted to three before throwing it in the trash can. "Good job, Lily!" said her mom. "Now let's go play with your dolls." And they lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She was very helpful and loved to help her mom and dad around the house. One day, her mom asked her to go upstairs and get her favorite dress. 

Lily ran upstairs and found the dress. She was so happy to be helpful. As she was coming back downstairs, she saw her little brother playing with a toy top. 

"Can I play too?" asked Lily.

"Sure!" said her brother, handing her the top. "Watch it spin!"

Lily spun the top and it twirled around and around. She laughed and her brother clapped his hands. "That was fun!" said Lily. 

From that day on, Lily loved to help her family and spin toys with her brother. And they all lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time there were two friends called Jack and Jill. They lived in the same house and were very happy. 

One day, Jack and Jill decided to play a game together. They got their toys out and introduced pain. Pain was a red ball and it was very round. 

Jack and Jill played for a long time and had lots of fun. But then the pain got too hard. It started to feel dull and nothing felt as fun as it used to.

Jack and Jill didn't know what to do. They looked at each other and suddenly had an idea -they would remove the pain. Jack and Jill quickly took the dull pain away and they were back to having lots of fun!

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was an old man with a cane. He was always angry. He would walk around and yell at everyone he saw. The people in the town did not like him.

One day, the old man saw a little girl playing with her ball. She was very happy. The old man walked up to her and yelled, "Stop playing!" The little girl got scared and started to cry. The old man felt a little bad, but he was still angry.

Later that day, the old man was walking by a big tree. He did not see a big hole in the ground. He fell into the hole and could not get out. He yelled for help, but no one came. The people in the town were too scared of him. The old man stayed in the hole, feeling very sad. The moral of the story is: if you are always angry and yell at people, they will not help you when you need it.

All of the animals in the forest gathered together one day. "Who belongs here?" asked the fox.

The elephant stamped his feet. "Me!" he said. 

The turkey waddled over. "Me too!" he said. 

However the others were not so sure. "You don't seem to fit in," said the deer. "You are too dull."

The turkey was sad. He thought he was an outcast and didn't belong. 

But the fox saw how lonely the turkey was and said, "We all belong here, even if we are different."

The others agreed. They accepted and welcomed the turkey, who was happy to be part of the group.

Moral: Belonging is not about fitting in. It's about accepting each other's differences.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the snow. One day, she saw a reindeer in her backyard. 

"Hi there!" said Lily. "Are you lost?"

The reindeer shook his head. "No, I'm just looking for some food to eat. I'm very hungry."

Lily felt sorry for the reindeer and wanted to help. "Come inside my house, it's warm and comfortable. I'll make you some food to eat."

The reindeer followed Lily inside and they sat down at the table. Lily made some carrots and apples for the reindeer to eat. He was very happy and thanked Lily for her kindness. From that day on, the reindeer visited Lily often and they became the best of friends.

Once upon a time there was a little bear called Tilly. She was so excited because she was going on an adventure. She put on her hat, grabbed her walking stick and let out a loud cheer!

Tilly marched through the meadow and saw a big, high daisy. She stopped and said to herself: "This daisy looks really nice! I'm going to pick it."

Just then a voice said: "Wait! Don't pick the daisy!"

Tilly jumped back in surprise. She looked around and saw a tall man standing there. He said to her: "That daisy is very tall. It won't fit into your pocket."

Tilly smiled and nodded. Then she marched away, with the daisy still standing tall. And she enjoyed the rest of her adventure.

Once upon a time, there was a brave girl called Lucy. She wanted to wander into the big, wide world. One day, she decided to take the chance. She started down the long path that led away from her home. She went further and further until she came to a fountain. 

The fountain was beautiful, but Lucy didn't dare to go any closer. She was scared of what might happen. Suddenly, she heard an angry shout from behind her. It was her mom! She had been looking for Lucy and was very mad that she had wandered off. Lucy felt ashamed and quickly ran back home.

It was a good lesson for Lucy. After that day, she no longer wanted to wander off. Instead, she would always stay around her home.

Once upon a time there was a mom who was very busy. She had to do lots of chores, so she decided to get a dishwasher. But it was very crazy! It made strange noises, and it didn't work the way it should.

The mom said, "I don't know what to do with this dishwasher. Can you help me, please?" But no one answered.

The mom was getting very frustrated. She said, "I'm sorry dishwasher, I'm going to have to give up on you." Then, she gave the dishwasher away.

The mom was sad. She realized she had made a bad decision, and there was nothing she could do to fix it.

The dishwasher was unhappy too, because it didn't want a new home. It wanted to stay with the mom. They both said goodbye and sadly parted ways.

Once there was a little boy who loved to sing. Every morning he would sing the same song and the other children thought it was weird.

One day he went to the park and saw lots of other kids. They were eating treats from their lunch boxes and looking at the birds flying in the sky. The little boy asked one of the kids if he could sing a song. The other kids said it was weird and didn't want to listen.

The little boy was sad and wished he had a friend to sing with him. Suddenly, an old man appeared. He said he used to like to sing too and asked the little boy to come with him. The little boy followed the old man and they went to a place full of treats.
