The old man gave the little boy a treat and they began to sing together. The other kids in the park heard their singing and stopped their games to watch them. Suddenly the park was full of happy singing and the other kids joined in.

The little boy was so happy that he could share his singing with everyone. He smiled and hugged the old man for giving him the treat and for being so kind. The old man smiled and said, "Come back when you want to sing again!".

John and Mommy were playing in the garden. John ran around, looking at the flowers and bees. Mommy said to John, "I'm so patient with you. Would you like some juice?"

John said, "Yes please!"

Mommy went inside and John watched the clouds in the sky. After a little while, Mommy came back with two cups of juice. She gave one cup to John and kept the other cup for herself. 

John took a big drink of the juice. It was delicious. Mommy smiled and said, "You are so patient for waiting for the juice."

John nodded his head and said, "Yes!" He finished the last of the juice and gave Mommy a big hug. They both laughed and had a great day playing in the garden.

Tom and Jen are friends. They like to play on the structure at the park. The structure has slides, swings, and a bridge. Tom and Jen have fun on the structure.

One day, a big boy comes to the park. He is mean. He says the structure is his. He says Tom and Jen are stupid. He pushes them off the slides. He takes their swings. He blocks the bridge. Tom and Jen are sad and angry.

Tom and Jen have an idea. They wait for the big boy to go on the bridge. Then they run to the swings. They swing very high. They swing very fast. They swing at the big boy. They hit him with their feet. The big boy falls off the bridge. He cries. He runs away.

Tom and Jen are happy. They have the structure again. They play on the slides, the swings, and the bridge. They are not stupid. They are smart. They are brave. They are friends.

John was playing in the park with his dog, Spot, when he suddenly decided to throw the ball. Spot ran to get the ball and brought it back to John but then John threw it again. Spot was having so much fun chasing the ball, so John kept throwing it. 

Suddenly, a big dog came near John and Spot. John was very scared, so he quickly threw the ball away. Spot chased the ball, but the big dog chased Spot. Spot yelped and ran away. John felt ashamed that he had scared Spot away. 

The big dog's owner, Mrs. Smith, came over to talk to John. Mrs Smith asked John why he was throwing the ball so wildly. John began to cry and told Mrs. Smith that he was sorry and he was ashamed that he had thrown the ball so far and scared Spot.

Mrs Smith smiled and said it was okay. She put her arm around John and said that Spot was brave for facing the big dog. Then, Spot came back and Mrs. Smith gave John and Spot some treats for being so brave.

Jack and his mom were walking through the park. Jack was very excited and ran around examining everything. Suddenly, his mom felt an important alarm. 

"Stop running around, Jack - I need to send an alarm," said his mom. 

Jack didn't understand what that meant, but he saw his mom taking out her phone. She quickly sent something and then put her phone away. 

"What did you do, mom?" asked Jack. 

"I sent an important message to my friends," said his mom. "It's very important, so I had to let them know right away." 

Jack was curious. He wasn't sure what an alarm was or why it was important, but he knew his mom was taking care of something special.

Once upon, there was a mighty man. His name was Pete. Every day, Pete ordered the clouds in the sky.

One day, Pete stopped ordering the clouds. The clouds grew bigger and bigger. Then it started to rain.

The rain fell from the sky like a mighty waterfall. The water filled the streets and lakes. People had to be careful not to get too close.

But Pete was not worried. He knew that the rain would soon stop and he could start ordering the clouds again.

And that's exactly what happened! The rain stopped and the sky became clear and blue again. Pete smiled and ordered the clouds in their rightful places.

The end.

Max was a very fancy boy. He liked mints, which tasted so good.

One day, his mom gave him a mint. He wanted to eat it, but it was too big.

So he asked his mom for help. She took a knife and cut the big mint into small pieces. She gave one piece to Max. He ate it and it was delicious!

Max thanked his mom for making it so he could eat the mint. She smiled and gave him another piece. Max was very happy.

Katie had a bad day. She had been wearing her new sunglasses on a sunny day and they hurt her eyes. She didn't have a good time and she said she hated them.

That night, Katie asked her mom for a new pair of sunglasses. Her mom said she could have them, but she had to be careful. She promised she would be.

The next day Katie went outside to play in the sun. She put on her new sunglasses, but she was still mad at the old pair. Katie made a funny face and said she hated the old ones.

As she kept on playing, a gust of wind blew her old sunglasses away. She laughed and said it was a bad thing for the old sunglasses. She put on her new pair and said she liked them much better.

Katie had a good time and finally found the perfect pair of sunglasses. She didn't hate her new sunglasses, but she knew she had to be careful with them.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Lucy. She was very excited because today she was going to get some new toys. She was hopping around! When she arrived at the store, she was amazed at all the things she could choose from. There were dolls and games, cars and kindles, trucks and LEGO. She was so excited!

Lucy noticed a box of rubber toys. They were so colourful and bright. She chose one and it was a rubber duck. He was so very clean! Lucy decided that it was the perfect toy.

Lucy went to the check out and paid for her new toy. She was so pleased with her choice. She couldn't wait to show her rubber duck to her mum and dad.

When she got home, Lucy proudly showed her new rubber duck to her parents. They were so pleased for her and were happy that she had chosen something so clean. They then helped Lucy to pick out some other toys to include in her collection. Oh, what fun!

Tom and Sam were brothers who liked to play with their toy boat. They had a big tub of water in the backyard where they could sail their boat and pretend to be pirates. One day, they saw a small hole in the boat, but they did not care. They thought it was still fun to sail.

"Look, Sam, our boat is so fast!" Tom said, as he pushed the boat in the water.

"Yes, Tom, it is!" Sam said, as he watched the boat zoom across the tub.

But their mom saw the hole and she was worried. She came out and said, "Boys, you should not sail your boat with a hole. It will sink and you will lose it. You should fix it or get a new one."

"Mom, we don't want to fix it or get a new one. We like our boat. It is still fun to sail. Please let us play," Tom said.

"Me too, Mom. Please let us play," Sam said.

Mom sighed and said, "Okay, boys, but I warn you, your boat will not last long. Be careful and don't cry if it sinks."

Mom went back inside and the boys kept playing. They did not listen to Mom's warning. They thought she was wrong and they knew better. They were having too much fun to stop.

But soon, the hole got bigger and the water got inside the boat. The boat started to slow down and tilt. The boys did not notice until it was too late. The boat sank to the bottom of the tub and they could not reach it.

"Tom, our boat! It sank! It's gone!" Sam cried.

"Sam, our boat! How did this happen? We can't get it back!" Tom cried.

They ran to Mom and told her what happened. They hoped she could help them. But Mom shook her head and said, "I'm sorry, boys, but I warned you. You did not listen to me. You did not take care of your boat. Now you have to learn your lesson. You have to be more careful and responsible with your things. Maybe next time, you will listen to me."

The boys felt sad and sorry. They wished they had listened to Mom. They wished they had fixed their boat or got a new one. They learned that Mom was right and they were wrong. They learned that fun is not worth losing something you love.

The moral of the story is: You should listen to your parents and take care of your things.

Sara and Tom were very excited to go to the zoo with their mom and dad. They got in the big jeep and drove for a long time. Sara liked to look at the trees and the birds and the clouds. Tom liked to sing songs and make funny noises.

When they got to the zoo, they saw many animals. They saw lions and tigers and bears. They saw monkeys and elephants and giraffes. They saw penguins and flamingos and crocodiles. Sara and Tom wanted to see them all.

They came to a big cage where a man was talking. He said he was going to show them a trick with a snake. Sara and Tom were curious and scared. They held their mom and dad's hands. The man took out a long, green snake from a basket. He said it was a cobra and it was very spicy. He said spicy meant it could bite and make you sick. He said he was going to make the snake dance.

He played a flute and the snake came out of the basket. It raised its head and spread its hood. It looked at the man and moved with the music. Sara and Tom watched with wide eyes. The man moved closer and closer to the snake. He reached out his hand and touched the snake's head. The snake did not bite him. The man smiled and put the snake back in the basket.

The crowd was amazed and happy. They clapped their hands and cheered. Sara and Tom clapped their hands too. They liked the trick. They said wow and cool and awesome. The man bowed and thanked them. He said he was glad they enjoyed the show. He said he had a surprise for them. He said he had a baby snake that was not spicy. He said he would let them touch it if they wanted.

Sara and Tom looked at each other. They wondered if they should touch the baby snake. They were curious and brave. They nodded and said yes. The man took out a small, yellow snake from another basket. He said it was a python and it was very friendly. He said friendly meant it would not bite or hurt them. He said he would let them hold it if they were gentle.

He gave the snake to Sara and Tom. They felt its smooth and soft skin. They felt its warm and strong body. They felt its tiny and sharp teeth. They smiled and giggled. They liked the snake. They said cute and nice and sweet. The man smiled and took the snake back. He said he was proud of them. He said they were very brave and kind. He said he had a gift for them. He gave them each a sticker with a snake on it. He said they could keep it as a souvenir.

Sara and Tom thanked the man. They put the stickers on their shirts. They showed them to their mom and dad. They were very happy. They said they had a lot of fun. They said they learned a lot. They said they wanted to see more animals. They said they loved the zoo.

One day, three friends decided to have a picnic. They gathered together a few supplies and found a spot in the garden. 

The first thing they did was to decorate the picnic spot. One of the friends took out a basket of colorful ribbons, streamers and balloons. The other friend took out several brushes and paints.

The friends worked together to decorate the picnic spot and make it look impressive. They all agreed that the colorful, vibrant decorations looked wonderful.

Suddenly, they heard a voice. It said: "Wow, you decorate so well!" 

The three friends looked around, and saw a little girl, about three years old, standing there watching them. The girl was so impressed by their decorations that she had to come over and tell them! 

The three friends all said hello to the little girl and said that she was welcome to join their picnic. They had a great time eating and playing games, and the decorations made the picnic even more fun.

Molly and her mom were in the backyard one day. Molly wanted to play, but she saw a big, frightening bug. She screamed and jumped back. Suddenly, the bug vanished!

Molly was so excited. She looked around the yard to see if the bug had gone somewhere. But, it had simply vanished!

Molly's mom was so surprised. She said, "That bug was being very rude. It shouldn't have scared you." Molly agreed.

The two of them decided to go and play tag. Molly ran around the backyard until she was so tired she couldn't run anymore. They had a lot of fun, but the bug never came back!

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys, especially his toy cars. One day, he noticed that one of his toy cars was dirty. So, he took a cloth and began to polish it until it was shiny and clean. 

Later that day, Timmy's dad asked him to help with something. He needed Timmy to hold a cable while he fixed it. Timmy didn't know what a cable was, but his dad showed him and explained that it was like a long, skinny rope that carried electricity. 

After they finished fixing the cable, Timmy's dad said, "Good job, son! You did a normal thing today." Timmy didn't know what "normal" meant, but he felt proud that he had helped his dad. From then on, Timmy made sure to keep his toys polished and his dad's cables in good shape.

Once there were two twin brothers. One was pale and the other was dark. They loved to play together. Every day they would go outside and explore the world.

One day they were playing in a field when they discovered a magical pond. As they looked inside, they were amazed by the shimmering fishes swimming around. Suddenly, a large white fish remained in the water, still and silent.

The brothers were amazed and wanted to touch the fish. They ran up to the pond and tried to grab the fish, but it stayed still and remained in the same spot.

The brothers were surprised by the strange fish and tried to touch it again and again. But no matter what they tried, the pale fish remained very still in the pond.

Eventually, the brothers accepted the fish's silent presence and decided to keep playing in the field. The pale fish stayed quiet, watching them explore and have fun. From then on, they always checked on the fish, making sure it remained in the same place.

Ben and Lily liked to play with their toy cars. They had many cars of different colors and sizes. They liked to make them race and crash and honk. But their favorite car was the big red one. It had an engine that made loud noises and lights that blinked. It was very expensive and their dad bought it for them on their birthday.

One day, they were playing with the big red car in the living room. They pretended it was a fire truck and they had to save a cat from a tree. They took turns driving and holding the cat. They had a lot of fun.

"Can I drive now?" Lily asked Ben.

"No, it's my turn. You had it before," Ben said.

"But I want to drive. It's not fair," Lily said.

She tried to grab the car from Ben, but he held it tight. They pulled and pushed and shouted. The car slipped from their hands and flew across the room. It hit the wall and broke into pieces. The engine stopped making noises and the lights stopped blinking. The cat flew out of the window.

Ben and Lily stared at the broken car. They felt very sad and sorry. They knew their dad would be angry. They started to cry.

The end.

One day, a naughty boy was out in the park by himself. Suddenly, he heard a strange noise coming from behind a tree. He spoke to it and out popped a fairy. The fairy said, "I can grant you three wishes if you turn into a good boy". The boy's eyes lit up and he nodded. 

The fairy said, "Let's start. What would you like your first wish to be?". The naughty boy replied, "I want a giant toy!" The fairy granted his wish and the boy was overjoyed.

The fairy then said, "Next, there is one more wish". The boy was so excited he couldn't find the words to say. He spoke to the fairy and said, "I want to be the king of the world!" When the fairy heard this wish, his face turned sad. He said, "Unfortunately, I cannot grant this wish".

The naughty boy was so mad and upset, he started shouting and throwing things. The fairy said, "Remember what I said - be good or there will be no more wishes". The boy didn't listen, so the fairy flew away.

The boy started to realise what he had done, but it was too late. He was left alone, his three wishes gone.

Once there was a person who wanted to remember lots. Every day the person tried hard to remember things. But the person found it hard and was very frustrated.

One day, the person wanted to remember to pick up a toy. But the person forgot. The person felt very sad and worried that they would forget something else.

They asked their friend for help. "Don't worry," their friend said. "We can write it down so you don't forget it!" 

The person was so happy and grateful for the help. They made a list of things to remember each day. Now, even if the person forgets something, they will still remember the other things on the list.

Once there was a tidy dancer. She was ready to send out a dance for a show. But suddenly a storm came and ruined her plan. The tidy dancer was so sad because she couldn't send her dance. She begged the storm to leave so her dance could be sent. The storm listened and the dancer was happy again. She got to send her dance and the show was a success! Everyone was happy and it was a tidy show. All because the tidy dancer got to send out her performance and make it a success.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Mia. She was 3 years old and loved to play. Mia's mum gave her a card and said, "Mia, I have a special card for you!" Mia looked at the card, it was bright and colorful. She smiled and clapped.

Mia then asked, "What is it, mum?" Her mum said, "It's a game! Let's play!" Mia was so excited that she jumped up and clapped again. 

Mia's mum showed her how to play the game. She said, "See, you have to pick one card, and then I pick one card and we see who has the bigger number!" Mia was a bit confused, but her mum was patient and showed her again. Eventually, Mia got it, and they began to play. 

At first, Mia was a bit slow. But after a few goes she was picking and matching cards like a pro! She had so much fun that she kept clapping and cheering. 

Soon it was time to stop. Mum said, "Well done Mia, you're a great player!" Mia smiled and clapped one more time. Then she hugged her mum and said, "Thank you for the fun game!"

Anna and Ben were playing in the snow. They made a big snowman with a hat and a scarf. They gave him a carrot nose and two buttons for eyes. They were very happy.

But then Anna felt something wet on her hand. She looked and saw that her mitten was soaked. She had dropped it in a puddle. She felt very uncomfortable. Her hand was cold and wet.

"Ben, look at my mitten!" she said. "It is wet and cold. I don't like it."

Ben looked at her mitten. He felt sorry for Anna. He had an idea.

"Come on, Anna," he said. "Let's go inside. Mom will give us some hot chocolate. It will make you feel better. You can drink it and warm up your hand."

Anna nodded. She liked hot chocolate. She followed Ben inside. Mom saw them and smiled.

"Hello, you two," she said. "Did you have fun in the snow?"

"Yes, Mom," they said. "But Anna's mitten is wet and cold."

Mom took Anna's mitten and gave her a dry one. She also gave them two mugs of hot chocolate. They drank it and felt warm and cozy.

"Thank you, Mom," they said. "You are the best."

Mom hugged them and said, "You are welcome, my loves. I'm glad you are happy."

Once upon a time, there was a wild mitten. It was brown and furry, and it knew how to move around. Every day it would sneak behind closed doors and explore the house.

One night, the wild mitten was really brave and went outside. It skipped through the grass, but it didn't know that it was getting closer to the road. Suddenly, something zoomed by really fast!

The wild mitten was scared and ran back inside. It tried to close the door, but it was too slow. The fast thing came closer and closer until it was right on top of the mitten.

The bad thing that happened was that the wild mitten got run over. It was very sad. The mitten couldn't move anymore, so it stayed where it was until the morning.

Once upon a time, there was a rich family with a little boy. Every day the boy would go out in the garden and fly his kite. One day, the wind changed and the kite flew high into the sky, higher than the little boy had ever seen before.

The boy's dad came out to the garden and said "My son, let's go and get your kite, okay?". The little boy nodded and went inside to get his coat.

They drove for a long time to find the kite. Eventually, they arrived at a beautiful hill with a big tree. Sure enough, the kite had gotten stuck in the branches of the big tree. Dad climbed up and got it down.

When they got back home, the little boy was very happy. It was nice to have his kite back. He couldn't wait until the next day when the wind would change and he would fly it again.

Once upon a time, there were two friends Ben and Jane. They were playing together in the garden.

"Let's pretend to be teachers," said Jane.

"Okay," said Ben.

They took turns to be the teacher. Jane got a stick and wrote something on the ground.

"What did you write?" asked Ben.

"I mentioned a tutor," said Jane.

"What does a tutor do?" asked Ben.

"A tutor helps you learn," said Jane. "It can be useful if you don't understand something."

Ben thought about it for a bit.

"That sounds good," said Ben.

They continued to play teacher and pretend that they had a tutor helping them. It was a very useful game.

Lily had a bad cough. She did not like it. It made her throat hurt and her eyes water. She wanted to play with her toys, but she felt too sick.

"Mommy, can you fix me?" she asked, holding her teddy bear.

Mommy smiled and hugged her gently. "I will try, my sweetie. You need to take this pill. It will help you feel better."

Lily looked at the pill. It was big and white. She did not want to swallow it. She was afraid it would get stuck in her mouth.

"I don't like it, Mommy. It is too big. It looks yucky."

Mommy kissed her forehead. "I know, Lily. But it is good for you. It will make your cough go away. How about we break it in half and put some honey on it? Then it will be smaller and sweeter."

Lily nodded. She liked honey. It was sticky and yummy. Mommy broke the pill in half and put some honey on each piece. She gave one to Lily and took the other one herself.

"Let's take it together, okay? On the count of three. One, two, three!"

Lily and Mommy put the pill in their mouths and swallowed. It was not so bad. The honey made it slide down easily. Lily felt a little better.

"Thank you, Mommy. You fixed me."

Mommy hugged her again. "You're welcome, Lily. I love you. Now, let's go to bed and rest. Tomorrow, you will be all better."

One day, three year old Zack went to the park with his mom. He saw a beautiful razor in the park, so he asked his mom if he could ride it. 

"No Zack," Mom said. "It's not safe."

Zack got very grumpy, but then he saw a different rollercoaster-like ride.

"Mom, can I ride that?" Zack asked.

"Yes, that one looks safe. Let's go."

So Zack and his Mom went to the ride. Zack rode it and screamed with joy. He went up and down and around and around. He was so excited and happy.

When the ride was over, Zack thanked his mom for taking him out for such a fun day. She smiled and said, "You're welcome, Zack. Anytime!"

Lily and Ben are twins. They like to play with their toys and books. One day, they find a new book on the shelf. It has many pictures of animals and words. Lily and Ben want to learn the words.

They open the book and see a picture of a cow. The word under the cow says "moo". Lily and Ben say "moo" together. They turn the page and see a picture of a bird. The word under the bird says "tweet". Lily and Ben say "tweet" together. They turn the page and see a picture of a fish. The word under the fish says "glub". Lily and Ben say "glub" together.

They like the book very much. They want to make their own book. They get some paper and crayons. They draw their own animals and write their own words. Lily draws a cat and writes "meow". Ben draws a dog and writes "woof". They draw more animals and write more words. They are very happy.

They show their book to Mom. Mom is very proud of them. She says "You made a very nice book. You are very smart. Do you want to print your book?" Lily and Ben nod. They want to print their book. Mom helps them to print their book. She puts the paper in the machine. The machine makes noise and prints their book. Lily and Ben clap. They have their own book.

Mom says "Now you have your own book. You can read it anytime. But first, you need to feed your animals. They are hungry." Lily and Ben remember their animals. They have a cat and a dog. They love their cat and dog. They go to the kitchen and get some food. They feed their cat and dog. Their cat and dog are happy. They lick Lily and Ben.

Lily and Ben hug their cat and dog. They say "We love you. You are our friends. We made a book for you. Do you want to see it?" Their cat and dog nod. They want to see the book. Lily and Ben show them the book. They read the words and point to the pictures. Their cat and dog listen and look. They are very mild. They do not bite or scratch the book. They like the book.

Lily and Ben smile. They say "We are glad you like the book. We made it for you. We learned many words. We had fun. Thank you for being our friends." Their cat and dog wag their tails. They say "You are welcome. You are our friends. We learned many words. We had fun. Thank you for making the book." They all cuddle together. They are very happy. The end.

Once there was a colorful radio. It sat on the countertop and made music. The music made everyone happy.

One day the little girl came over to the countertop to see the radio. She wanted to touch it. She reached out her hand and wiped the radio. Everyone was amazed.

The little girl smiled. She had made the radio look shiny and new. Her mother was so happy she clapped and hugged the little girl.

The radio kept on making music. Everyone in the house was glad that the little girl had wiped it. Now it looked nice and the music made the house feel cheerful. 

The little girl was happy and proud of her work. She had wiped the radio and made it look beautiful.

Once there was a little girl who liked to listen. There was a knob on the door of her room and she liked to turn it. Every time she turned the knob, she listened to something new.

One day, she found a long, thin rope attached to the knob. She pulled on it and it seemed to never end. She wondered what she could find at the end of the rope.

Finally, she found the end and it was a big surprise. There was a door at the end of the rope! She opened the door and found a staircase leading to the roof. She ran up the long stairs and opened another door to the roof.

She was amazed to see the world from above. She listened to the birds in the sky and felt the wind on her face. She loved listening to the new sounds and exploring the new view. 

The girl always remembered that day when she first found the long rope, and every time she turned her knob she would remember the view from the roof and the sounds of the birds.

Once upon a time there was a brave prince. He lived in a castle on a hill with his family. One day, he decided to go for a walk. He moved slowly up the path. As he went, he saw a bright white powder on the ground. He was curious and moved closer to take a look.

The prince poked around the powder with his finger. It was so soft and light. Then suddenly, a loud voice came from behind him.

"What are you doing, young prince?" asked the voice.

The prince turned around and saw an old man in a cloak standing there. "I was just looking at the powder," said the prince.

The man nodded. "That's very special powder," he said. "If you sprinkle it in your castle's garden, the flowers will turn beautiful colors".

The prince was very excited. He thanked the old man and ran back to his castle with his bag of powder.

He was so proud when he returned home and found the garden covered in colorful blooms. From that day on, he always kept a jar of that special powder handy in his castle.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to play outside. One day, she went for a walk with her mommy on their street. But something was wrong. The street smelled really smelly! 

Lily wrinkled her nose and said, "Mommy, what's that smell?" 

"I don't know, Lily," said her mommy. "Let's keep walking and see if we can find out." 

As they walked down the street, they saw a big truck dumping trash on the sidewalk. Lily's mommy said, "That's not right. We need to tell someone." 

Lily repeated, "Tell someone!" and they walked to the town hall to report the smelly street. The town workers came and cleaned up the mess, and the street smelled nice again. Lily was happy that she helped make her street clean and pretty.

Sara and Ben like to play with chalk on the sidewalk. They draw flowers, stars, and cars with many colors. They have fun and laugh a lot.

One day, a big dog comes near them. The dog is black and has a loud bark. Sara and Ben are scared of the dog. They want to run away, but their chalk is on the sidewalk.

"Ben, we have to get our chalk!" Sara says.

"No, Sara, the dog is too big and mean!" Ben says.

The dog sees the chalk and thinks it is a toy. He runs to the sidewalk and grabs a piece of chalk with his mouth. He chews it and makes a mess.

"Hey, that's our chalk!" Sara yells. "Bad dog, bad dog!"

The dog does not listen to Sara. He thinks she is playing with him. He drops the chalk and runs to Sara and Ben. He wants to lick them and jump on them.

Sara and Ben are very afraid. They scream and cry for help.

"Help, help, there is a big dog!" they shout.

A man hears them and comes to see what is wrong. He sees the dog and the children. He knows the dog. He is the dog's owner.

"Rex, stop that!" the man says. "You are scaring the children!"

He grabs the dog by the collar and pulls him away. He says sorry to Sara and Ben.

"I'm sorry, kids, Rex is a friendly dog, but he is very playful. He did not mean to hurt you or your chalk. He just wanted to have fun."

Sara and Ben stop crying. They look at the man and the dog. They are still scared, but they are also curious.

"Is his name Rex?" Sara asks.

"Yes, his name is Rex. He is a good dog, but he needs to learn some manners. He should not take things that are not his, or bother people who do not want to play with him. I will teach him to behave better. Do you want to pet him?"

The man asks.

Sara and Ben are not sure. They look at each other. They see that Rex is wagging his tail and looking at them with big eyes. He does not seem so mean now.

"Maybe we can pet him, but only a little bit," Ben says.

"OK, but be careful. And we have to warn him not to touch our chalk again," Sara says.

They nod and walk slowly to the man and the dog. They reach out their hands and touch Rex's fur. He licks their fingers and makes a happy sound.

Sara and Ben smile. They think Rex is not so bad after all. They are still a little afraid, but they also feel sorry for him. They think he is lonely and bored.

"Maybe we can play with him sometimes, but only with his toys, not with our chalk," Sara says.

"Maybe we can, but only if he listens to us and his owner," Ben says.

They agree and say goodbye to the man and Rex. They pick up their chalk and go back to their sidewalk. They draw some more pictures, but they leave some space for Rex. They think he might like to see them.

They hope he will be a good dog and a good friend. They think he is perfect for them.

Once upon a time, there was a monkey who skipped around in the trees. He was always happy and his days were filled with joy. One day, he heard a terrible noise coming from the nearby forest. He decided to investigate and so he slowly crept forward. 

The noise got louder and louder until he saw something terrible. In the middle of the forest, was a large machine that was recording the birds' song. The monkey felt angry and sad that the birds' song was being taken away. He knew that he had to do something to stop it. 

The monkey came up with a plan. He swung his way from tree to tree, until he was directly above the machine. With one mighty leap, he landed on the machine. He started to rock it back and forth until it broke in two! The recording stopped. 

The other animals were so happy. The birds were especially thankful and praised the monkey for being brave and clever. The monkey smiled and laughed, feeling proud of his brave deed. From then on, the birds were free to sing their songs and the world was once again peaceful.

Once upon a time there was a mommy and a little girl. The little girl wanted to try something new.

"Mommy, can I tie a knot?" asked the little girl.
"Yes, sure" said the mommy.

The mommy helped the little girl tie a knot in her new dress. She was so happy and she showed the knot to everyone. Soon she noticed that the knot was starting to come undone.

"It's falling off!" cried the little girl.

The mommy hugged the little girl and said, "It's ok honey. That's why it's important to tie your knots tight!"

Just then a rude boy walked by laughing.

"That's not nice," said the mommy. "It's not ok to laugh at someone's knot that came undone."

The little girl smiled and said, "It's ok. I know how to tie better now!" She took the ends of the dress and tied a tight knot.

The mommy smiled and said, "Good job! Now your knot won't fall off again."

The little girl was so proud of her tight knot. She danced and laughed, happy that her knot would stay in place.

Once upon a time, there was a big brown ostrich. The ostrich lived in a big field with lots of other animals. One day, the ostrich wanted to learn how to fly like the birds in the sky. 

The ostrich tried and tried but couldn't fly. The other animals laughed at the ostrich and said, "Ostriches can't fly, silly!" 

The ostrich felt sad and alone. It wanted to be like the other birds. So, the ostrich tried to fly again and again. 

But one day, the ostrich jumped off a tall tree and fell to the ground. The other animals rushed over to help, but it was too late. The ostrich had hurt itself badly and couldn't get up. 

The other animals felt very sad that they had laughed at the ostrich. They learned that it's important to be kind and to accept others for who they are.

Once upon a time, there was a wild boy named Jack. He was always very happy and spoke a lot. One day, Jack went to the park with his parents. He ran around the park and had lots of fun.

At the park, Jack saw a well. The well was very deep and dark. He peered down into it and started to talk to it. "Hello Well, how are you today?" he said.

The well started to speak back to him. It said, "I am doing very well, Jack. It's great to meet you!" It was so magical to Jack that a well could actually speak.

Jack waved goodbye to the well and ran off to find more adventures. He never forgot the day he spoke to the wild well.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Bob. He wanted to go for a walk in the bright sunshine. He put on his shoes and took his hat. He grabbed a snack and went outside. 

Bob walked down the street until he saw a palm tree. He walked up to it and touched the big leaves. They felt so cool and soft. He smiled and said out loud, "This tree is so cool!"
 
Suddenly, he noticed a bitter taste in his mouth. He looked up at the palm tree and saw a big green fruit hanging from one of the branches. He had never seen this type of fruit before and he wanted to try it. So, he picked the fruit and took a bite. It was so bitter! He really didn't like it. 

He threw the fruit away, wiped the bitter taste from his mouth, and walked away from the palm tree. As he walked away, he decided to never try a palm fruit again!

Once upon a time, there was a little turtle named Tim. Tim was very slow, but he had a big heart. He liked to play with his friends in the pool. One day, he wanted to invite all his friends to his pool party.

Tim went to each of his friends and said, "Come to my pool party!" His friends were very happy and said, "Yes, we will come!" They all came to Tim's pool party and had lots of fun. They played games, splashed water, and laughed together.

At the end of the party, Tim's friends thanked him for inviting them. They learned that even if someone is slow, they can still be a good friend and have fun with others. The moral of the story is that we should be kind to everyone, no matter how different they are from us.

Lily liked to draw with her pen. She drew flowers and stars and cats on her paper. She was very good at drawing. She wanted to show her mom her drawings, but her mom was busy in the kitchen. Lily decided to carry her pen and paper to the kitchen and surprise her mom.

But on the way, she saw her brother Tom playing with his cars. Tom was stubborn and did not like to share his toys. He saw Lily's pen and wanted it. He said, "Give me your pen, Lily. I need it for my cars."

Lily said, "No, Tom. This is my pen. I use it for drawing. Go find your own pen."

Tom did not listen. He grabbed Lily's pen and tried to pull it away from her. Lily held on to her pen and said, "Stop it, Tom. You are being mean. Let go of my pen."

They both pulled and tugged on the pen. The pen was not strong enough for their pulling. It broke in half with a snap. Lily and Tom both gasped. They looked at the broken pen and felt sad. They had ruined Lily's pen.

Mom heard the noise and came to see what was wrong. She saw Lily and Tom with the broken pen and the paper. She said, "What happened here? Why did you break Lily's pen?"

Lily and Tom both felt sorry. They said, "We are sorry, Mom. We were fighting over the pen. We did not mean to break it."

Mom said, "Fighting is not nice. You should share and take turns with your toys. And you should be careful with your things. Pens are not for pulling. They are for writing and drawing. Look, you have wasted a good pen and made a mess on the paper."

Lily and Tom nodded. They said, "We are sorry, Mom. We will not fight again. We will share and take turns. And we will be careful with our things."

Mom said, "That's good. Now, why don't you go and find another pen and draw something nice together? And then you can show me your drawings. I would love to see them."

Lily and Tom smiled. They said, "Okay, Mom. Thank you, Mom." They hugged Mom and went to find another pen. They drew something nice together and showed Mom their drawings. Mom was proud of them. She said, "You are very good at drawing. And you are very good at sharing and taking turns. I love you both."

Ben and Mia went to the zoo with Mom and Dad. They saw many animals, like lions, elephants, and monkeys. Ben liked the monkeys best. They made funny noises and swung on the ropes. Mia liked the elephants best. They sprayed water with their noses and had big ears.

Then they came to the gorilla house. There was a big gorilla sitting on a rock. He looked very sleepy. He yawned and scratched his head. Ben and Mia wanted to see him do something. They waved at him and called his name. "Hello, gorilla! What is your name? Can you hop like a bunny?"

The gorilla did not answer. He did not hop. He did not even look at them. He closed his eyes and snored. Ben and Mia were disappointed. They thought the gorilla was boring. They wanted to go to the next animal.

But then, something happened. Another gorilla came out of the bushes. He was smaller and faster than the sleepy gorilla. He ran towards the rock and jumped on it. He poked the sleepy gorilla and made a loud noise. "Wake up, wake up! Let's play!"

The sleepy gorilla opened his eyes and growled. He did not want to play. He wanted to sleep. He pushed the smaller gorilla off the rock and chased him away. He hopped and jumped and ran after him. He made a lot of noise.

Ben and Mia were surprised. They laughed and clapped their hands. They liked the gorillas now. They were not boring. They were fun. They watched them hop and play until it was time to go home. They said goodbye to the gorillas and thanked them for the show. "Bye, gorillas! You are very good at hopping. Have a nice nap!"

Sara and Tom are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they find a big box under a tree. The box is colorful. It has red, blue, yellow and green stripes.

"What is in the box?" Sara asks.

"I don't know. Let's open it and see," Tom says.

They open the box. Inside, they see many toys. There are dolls, cars, balls, books and puzzles. They are happy. They take out some toys and play with them.

"This is our secret," Tom says. "We don't tell anyone about the box. OK?"

"OK," Sara says. "We don't tell anyone. We lie if they ask."

They play for a long time. They have fun. They forget about the time. They don't hear their moms calling them.

"Where are Sara and Tom?" Sara's mom asks.

"I don't know. Maybe they are in the swings or the slide," Tom's mom says.

They look for them. They don't see them. They are worried.

They find them under the tree. They see the box and the toys.

"What are you doing here?" Sara's mom asks.

"We are playing," Sara says.

"Where did you get these toys?" Tom's mom asks.

"We found them," Tom says.

"Did you ask anyone if you can take them?" Sara's mom asks.

They are quiet. They don't answer. They know they did something wrong. They feel bad.

They look at each other. They decide to tell the truth.

"We are sorry," Sara says. "We didn't ask anyone. We lied. We wanted to keep the toys. They are so colorful and nice. But they are not ours. We will put them back in the box."

They put the toys back in the box. They close the lid. They say sorry to their moms.

Their moms hug them. They are not angry. They are glad they told the truth.

"It's OK," Sara's mom says. "You made a mistake. But you learned from it. Lying is not good. It can hurt you and others. Sharing is better. Maybe the toys belong to someone who needs them. Maybe they are a gift for someone. You don't know. You have to respect other people's things."

They nod. They understand. They say sorry again.

They go home with their moms. They are still friends. They still like to play in the park. But they don't lie anymore. They don't have secrets. They have fun.

Once upon a time, there was a dog named Max. Max loved to play outside with his friends. One day, something strange happened. Max found a bone in his backyard. He had never seen it before, so it was unknown to him. Max was so happy to have found the bone that he ran around the yard with it in his mouth. 

Max's friends came over to play and saw the bone. They asked Max where he found it, but he didn't know. Max's friends were curious about the unknown bone, so they started to sniff around the yard. They found more bones! Max and his friends were so excited to have found these bones, they played with them all day long. 

The next day, Max's owner came outside and saw the bones. She realized they were from a chicken that had died a long time ago. She took the bones away from Max and his friends to keep them safe. Max was sad that he couldn't play with his new bone anymore, but he was happy that he had a fun day with his friends.

Once, there was a spoon. It was a shiny spoon and it made the people very happy. They used the spoon to eat all kinds of food.

One day, the spoon fell into a hot pan of soup. It made a loud sizzle sound! The soup was so hot, it was almost boiling. The spoon was scared and started to sink. 

Quickly, someone grabbed a lid and quickly covered the pan. The hot soup was trapped inside.

The spoon was safe and the people were happy. They used the spoon again to finish their meal. The end.

Anna and Ben were friends. They liked to play in the park. One day, they saw a bird on the ground. The bird was not moving. It had a broken wing.

"Oh no, the poor bird!" Anna said. "It is hurt. We have to help it."

Ben nodded. He picked up the bird gently. He put it in a box. He and Anna ran to the vet. They hoped the vet could fix the bird.

But the vet was not there. The door was locked. There was a sign that said "Gone for lunch. Back soon."

Anna and Ben did not know what to do. They waited for a long time. But the vet did not come back. The bird was getting weaker. It made soft noises.

"Maybe we can send the bird to another vet," Ben said. "Or to a farm. Maybe someone there can take care of it."

Anna agreed. They looked around. They saw a big truck. The truck had a picture of a cow on it. They thought the truck was going to a farm.

"Let's put the box in the truck," Anna said. "Maybe the truck driver will see it and take it to the farm."

Ben nodded. He and Anna lifted the box. They put it in the back of the truck. They hoped the bird would be okay.

But they did not know that the truck was not going to a farm. The truck was going to a factory. The factory made glue. The glue was made from animals. The truck driver did not see the box. He did not hear the bird.

The truck drove away. Anna and Ben waved goodbye. They thought they had done a good thing. They did not know they had sent the bird to a bad place. They did not know they had sent the bird's spirit away. They did not know they had made a big mistake.

Lily and Sam are best friends. They like to play with blocks and dolls. One day, they want to build a big tower with the blocks. They use many colors, but they like blue the best.

"Look, I have a blue block!" Lily says. "It is very important. It will make our tower strong."

"Me too!" Sam says. "I have a blue block too. Let's put them on top of each other."

They put the blue blocks on the tower. The tower is very tall and pretty. They are happy and proud.

But then, a big wind comes. It blows hard and makes the tower shake. Lily and Sam are scared. They don't want their tower to fall.

"Help!" Lily cries. "Hold the tower, Sam!"

"I will!" Sam says. "I will support the tower. Don't worry, Lily!"

They hold the tower with their hands. They push against the wind. They work together. They are brave and strong.

The wind stops. The tower is still standing. The blue blocks are still on top. Lily and Sam smile and hug.

"We did it!" Lily says. "We saved our tower!"

"We did!" Sam says. "We are a good team!"

They are happy and proud. They are best friends. They like blue the best.

Once, there was a boy. His name was Timmy. He was three years old.

One day, Timmy was at a party. It was a blue party. He was having so much fun with all the toys.

But then, Timmy started to get too wild. He was running around the party, knocking things over. His mum saw this and said, "No, Timmy! That's not okay. We must punish you."

Timmy was very sad. He said, "But why? I was only having fun at the blue party!"

Mum said, "I know, sweetheart. But sometimes, it's not okay to do certain things, even if you're having fun. That's why we need to punish you."

Timmy understood. He knew he had to obey the rules from now on, at all parties.

Bella and her momma were in the kitchen. Bella wanted a cookie, but her momma said she had to pay for it. Bella didn't understand what this meant, but her momma explained. 

Momma: "You need to be patient. That means you have to wait. If you wait, then you can pay for the cookie and you can get it." 

Bella: "Pay? What is pay?" 

Momma: "Pay means that you have to do something before you can get it. Can you be patient while I make you the cookie?"

Bella nodded. Her momma was very patient, so Bella tried to be too. She watched as her momma made the cookie. Then, her momma gave her the cookie and said, "Now you have to pay me back by being a good girl and eating the cookie." 

Bella smiled. She understood now. Paying meant that sometimes you have to wait, but good things usually come if you are patient.

Once there was a little girl. Her name was Mandy and she was three-years-old. One day her mom took her to the park. Mandy was so excited!

They played, they laughed and they had so much fun! The time flew by and soon it was time to leave.

Mandy's mom said, "Come on Mandy, we must hurry. Let's go to the van."

Mandy groaned. She didn't want to leave yet. But she knew that she had to go.

So she helped her mom pick up all the messy toys. Then they ran to the van. Mandy was so glad that her mom knew how to hurry. Then they were off to see what new adventure their day would bring.

One day, a little girl named Lucy went to the park. She saw a boy named Tim. Tim was trying to eat his cake with a fork. The fork was too big and he was having a hard time.

Lucy said, "I recommend you use a smaller fork. It will be easier." Tim listened and used a smaller fork. He was happy because it was easier to eat his cake now. Lucy felt good because she helped her friend.

Lucy and Tim played together all day. They knew they could depend on each other. They learned that it was good to help friends and listen to their advice. The moral of the story is to always be a dependable friend and help others when you can.

Mum was feeling terrible. She was sitting on her bed crying and wouldn't stop. Her little daughter, whose name was Annabelle, saw this. Annabelle climbed up to the wardrobe and opened the doors. She grabbed some of Mum's clothes and a blanket and ran to her Mum. Annabelle put all the clothes and the blanket around her Mum and said: "It's ok, Mum. I can comfort you".

Mum smiled and put her arm around Annabelle. Annabelle snuggled close to her Mum and said: "It will be alright, Mum. Don't worry about the terrible things". Mum's tears started to dry and soon the whole bad feeling was gone. Annabelle felt happy that she could comfort her Mum and make her feel better.

Once upon a time, there were two friends named Parker and Summer. They went to the park together in the morning to play. Parker wanted to buy cold drinks, but Summer did not have enough money. 

Parker said to Summer, "I will supply the cold drinks. It will make us feel better!" 

Summer was so happy and accepted Parker's offer. The two friends went to the store to buy the drinks. Parker bought the cold drinks and then they went back to the park together. 

They found a peaceful spot under a tree, and both of them enjoyed their cold drinks. They also enjoyed the peaceful feeling the park gave them. 

Parker and Summer talked and laughed together until it became hot, so they decided to go back home. 

They had a really nice day, because of Parker's kind offer to supply the cold drinks.

Once upon a time, there was an ordinary sailboat. It lived on the river and was very happy. One day, something special happened! It was not so ordinary.

The sailboat got a special message. A little voice from the sky said, "Sailboat, I want to take you on a special trip!" The sailboat was very excited. "Yes!" it shouted.

But the sailboat was scared too. What if the trip was too hard? What if the sailboat got lost? It couldn't help but cry.

Then, the same voice said, "Don't weep, little sailboat! I promise I will keep you safe. Just have faith!"

The sailboat wiped its tears and jumped in the river. It was the start of an amazing adventure. The sailboat was never so happy!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. Her name was Susie. Susie liked to mix things together and make new creations.

One day, Susie went to the park to play. She found a red feather on the ground and picked it up. She mixed it with some mud and grass to make a feathery mud pie. 

At home, Susie mixed the feather with some paint to make a colourful picture. She also mixed it with water and some spoiled milk until it made a creamy, feathery drink. 

On the way back to the park, Susie mixed the feather with some bubble mixture and made some big, feather-filled bubbles! She was so proud of the things she had mixed. 

Susie had a lot of fun mixing things with her special feather. She was so proud of what she could make.

One day, a fireman named Tom was walking down the street. He saw a wild cat stuck in a tree. The cat was scared and crying. Tom wanted to help the cat, so he got his big ladder from the fire truck.

Tom put the ladder against the tree and climbed up. The wild cat looked at Tom and said, "Please help me, I am scared!" Tom smiled and said, "Don't worry, little cat. I am a fireman and I will help you."

Tom picked up the cat and climbed down the ladder. When they were on the ground, the cat realized that Tom was a kind fireman. The cat thanked Tom and ran back to its family. Tom was happy that he could help the wild cat and went back to the fire station.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Polly. She was three years old and loved to play.

One day, Polly's Mum took her to a restaurant. "Look at all the delicious things on the menu!" said Mum.

Polly looked at the menu, but nothing looked familiar. "Mum, I don't know what any of these are!" she said.

Mum smiled. "Don't worry, Polly," she said. "There is something on the menu that you can perform. It's a bit weird, and you need to use your imagination. Are you ready?"

Polly nodded eagerly. Mum then asked her to imagine that she was a princess, and to perform for the restaurant.

Polly stood up and started spinning and singing, and everyone in the restaurant cheered. Polly felt so proud of herself for performing something so weird!

Once upon a time, there was a gentle man. He lived in a small house near the woods. The man had a big, soft bed where he would lie down every night.

One day, the gentle man found a little lost dog. The dog was hungry and tired. The man took the dog home and gave it some food. The dog was very happy.

That night, the gentle man let the dog lie on the big, soft bed with him. They both slept well and had sweet dreams. From that day on, they were the best of friends.

Lily and Ben are best friends. They like to play with their toys and make funny noises. One day, they find a big box in the garage. They wonder what is inside.

"Let's open it!" Lily says.

"OK!" Ben says.

They pull and tug at the box until it opens. Inside, they see a lot of shiny things. They are snaps. Snaps are small metal things that make a loud sound when you press them together.

"Wow!" Lily says. "Look at all the snaps!"

"Can we play with them?" Ben asks.

"Sure!" Lily says. "But be careful. They are loud and hard."

They take some snaps and start to press them together. They make a lot of noise and laugh. They pretend they are making music or fireworks. They have a lot of fun.

Then, they see something else in the box. It is a small, fluffy animal. It has long ears, a pink nose and a cute tail. It is a bunny. It is adorable.

"Look!" Ben says. "A bunny!"

"Aww!" Lily says. "It is so cute!"

They pick up the bunny and cuddle it. It is soft and warm. It makes a quiet sound. It is happy.

"What is its name?" Lily asks.

"I don't know," Ben says. "Do you have a name for it?"

Lily thinks for a moment. She looks at the bunny and smiles.

"How about Snap?" she says. "Because we found it with the snaps."

"I like it!" Ben says. "Snap is a good name for a bunny."

They hug Snap and put it back in the box. They decide to keep it as their pet. They also keep some snaps to play with. They are very happy. They have a new friend and a new toy. They love Snap and Snap loves them.

Sam and his mom were walking to the station when it started raining. Sam was so excited. He loved playing in the rain and he splashed around and danced in the water.

His mom shouted, "Come on Sam! We need to get to the station before it gets too wet!". Sam smiled and ran after her, laughing and playing.

When they arrived at the station, they saw that it was quite wet. Sam's mom said "See Sam, I told you it would be too wet. We won't be able to wait here until it dries".

Sam yelled, "No mom! I don't want to go yet". His mother sighed and said, "We have to Sam, it's getting too wet".

Sam was about to have a tantrum when he spotted a huge umbrella. He grabbed it and ran back to his mom, saying "Look Mom, now we can wait until it's dry!".

His mom smiled and said, "Good thinking Sam! Let's stay here until the rain stops and the station dries up". And so they shared the umbrella, awaiting the end of the rain and the drying of the station.

Once upon a time there was a big wide tree and next to the tree was a rabbit. The rabbit was hopping happily around the tree and singing a happy song. He had a wonderful rhythm that made everyone around him smile.

Nearby, a small frog was hopping and singing as well. He watched the rabbit and thought â€œMaybe I can sing like that, tooâ€. So he hopped closer to the rabbit for a better view.

The rabbit noticed the frog and said â€œDo you want to sing with me?â€ The frog blinked and nodded, so the two of them hopped around the tree and sang in harmony. It was a beautiful song that made everyone in the forest very happy.

But then, the frog started to regret joining in. He was too shy and not very good at keeping up with the rhythm. He was embarrassed and hopped away.

The rabbit felt sad and sorry that the frog had left. He was so wide and kind and he wished they could have kept singing together. So he sang the song, by himself, and all the creatures in the forest sang along, hoping that one day the frog would come back and join them.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a red cap that she loved to wear. One morning, Lily woke up early and put on her cap. She went outside to play with her friends. They played games and ran around in the sun. 

After a while, Lily got tired and wanted to take a nap. She took off her red cap and lay down on the grass. Her friends came over and saw her sleeping. They thought it would be funny to hide her cap. When Lily woke up, she couldn't find her cap anywhere. 

Lily's friends felt bad and decided to help her find her cap. They looked all over the yard until they found it in a bush. Lily was so happy to have her red cap back on her head. She thanked her friends and they all continued to play together. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside and climb trees. One day, Timmy saw a scary monster in his backyard. The monster had big teeth and red eyes. The monster scared Timmy so much that he ran inside his house and hid under his bed.

Timmy's mom came to his room and asked him why he was scared. Timmy told his mom about the monster in the backyard. His mom went outside to check, but she didn't see anything. She told Timmy that it was just his imagination.

The next day, Timmy went back outside to play. He saw the monster again, but this time the monster was closer. Timmy tried to run away, but the monster grabbed him with its incredible strength. Timmy's mom heard his screams and ran outside, but it was too late. The monster had taken Timmy away.

Timmy's mom searched for him everywhere, but she couldn't find him. She looked in the palm trees and in the bushes, but Timmy was nowhere to be found. Timmy was never seen again.

Lily and Ben are twins. They like to go to new places with Mom and Dad. Today they go to a big museum. The museum has many things from long ago. Mom says they are ancient.

The twins see a big tour bus outside the museum. The bus is red and shiny. It has a picture of a dinosaur on it. Lily and Ben love dinosaurs. They want to go on the bus. Mom and Dad say yes. They buy tickets and get on the bus.

The bus driver is a nice lady. She says hello to everyone. She tells them to put on their seat belts. She says the bus will take them to see ancient things. The bus starts to move. Lily and Ben look out the window. They see the museum, the park, the shops and the cars.

The bus stops at a big gate. The gate has a sign that says "Ancient Park". The bus driver says they are here. She says they can get off the bus and see the ancient things. She says she will wait for them. Lily and Ben are excited. They hold Mom and Dad's hands and get off the bus.

They see many ancient things in the park. They see bones, rocks, pots, coins and statues. They see a big skeleton of a dinosaur. It is very tall and long. Lily and Ben think it is amazing. They take pictures with the dinosaur. They have fun in the park. They learn a lot about ancient things. They thank the bus driver for the tour. They go back to the bus. They are happy and tired. They go home and tell their friends about their adventure.

Once upon a time there was a fat turtle named Tom. Tom lived on the beach and everyday he would spend time looking up at the sky. One day, he noticed a very big, shiny helicopter flying above his head. He had never seen anything like it. All of a sudden, he had an idea! He wanted to become a helicopter! 
Tom asked his friend, the seagull, if he could help him. The seagull said, "Yes, but it will be difficult". So the seagull took Tom and they flew up, up and away. The higher they flew, the bigger the helicopter got. The seagull began to beat his wings as fast as he could until Tom became a real helicopter. 
Tom was so excited and happy. He zoomed around in the sky for hours, happy to be part of the sky. He couldn't believe he had become a real helicopter. Tom never forgot the wonderful day he became a helicopter and ever since then he loved to fly through the sky.

Two friends, Peter and Paul, were playing in the park on a warm summer day. They were having lots of fun, but then Paul wanted to do something different. He suggested that they play a game with a sack he'd brought with him. 

At first, Peter didn't want to, but Paul kept asking and eventually Peter agreed. They started to play the game, which involved throwing the sack around. But it didn't take long before Peter started to get really angry with Paul.

Peter thought it was too dangerous and he shouted at Paul, asking why he couldn't do something normal. Paul just laughed - he thought the game was really exciting and he wanted to keep playing.

The two friends argued for a while, but eventually they made up and decided to do something else instead. With summer still in the air, they both raced off in search of a new adventure.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lucy. She loved to learn and asked her mom for a tutor. Her mom found a very high and sharp tutor for Lucy. She sent Lucy off to learn.

Everyday, Lucy went to the tutor to learn new things. The tutor was very smart and taught her some difficult things. But Lucy was so smart, she kept on learning everything.

After some weeks, the tutor got impressed with Lucy's knowledge and gave her a reward. It was a shiny sharp pencil. Lucy was so happy. She thanked the tutor. 

The tutor smiled and said, "Lucy, you are so sharp! You can learn anything quickly." 

Lucy thanked the tutor and smiled back. She was so proud of herself. From then on, Lucy continued to learn with the tutor everyday. She was very happy.

Emma and Jake went to the opera house to see an opera show. Emma was so glad to go and was so happy, she couldn't wait to watch the show. But Jake was not so excited as he didn't want to go to the show. 

At the show, Emma saw all the beautiful costumes and the wonderful music. She was so glad to watch the show. On the other hand, Jake was not enjoying the show at all. 

Emma could see that Jake did not like the show. She smiled and said, "Jake, don't worry, it doesn't matter if you don't like the show. The important thing is that you have experienced something different."

Jake listened to Emma and smiled. He was glad that he came. Then, he was able to watch the show with a different view and finally, he was able to enjoy the show.

The moral value of this story is that it is important to have an open mind and try new things, even when it may be uncomfortable at first.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her shiny crystal toy. One day, she went to the park to play with her friends. She put her crystal toy in her pocket and ran off to play.

After a while, Lily realized that she forgot her crystal toy in the park. She looked for it everywhere, but she couldn't find it. She was very sad and cried a lot.

Lily's mother saw her crying and asked her what happened. Lily told her that she lost her crystal toy. Her mother hugged her and said, "Don't worry, we will find it together." They went back to the park and searched for the crystal toy. Finally, they found it under a tree.

Lily was very happy and hugged her mother tightly. Her mother said, "Remember, Lily, it's important to take care of your things and not forget them. You don't want to lose something special like your crystal toy." From that day on, Lily made sure to always keep her special things safe and never forget them again.

Anna loved her kitten, Luna. Luna was small and soft and had blue eyes. Anna liked to play with Luna and cuddle her. Sometimes, Anna wondered how much Luna weighed. She wanted to know if Luna was growing well.

One day, Anna had an idea. She asked her mom, "Mom, can I weigh Luna?"

Her mom smiled and said, "Sure, honey. Let's go to the bathroom. There is a scale there."

Anna picked up Luna and followed her mom. She put Luna on the scale and looked at the numbers. She did not know what they meant, but her mom told her.

"Luna weighs four pounds. That's very good for a kitten. She is healthy and strong."

Anna was happy and gave Luna a hug. Luna purred and licked Anna's face. Anna said, "I love you, Luna. You are my best friend."

Her mom said, "You are very thoughtful, Anna. You care about Luna a lot. She is lucky to have you."

Anna and Luna smiled and went back to their room. They played with a ball of yarn and had a lot of fun.

Once upon a time, there was a happy pupil named Timmy. Timmy loved going to school because his teacher, Miss Lily, was very dependable. She always helped him when he needed it.

One day, Timmy went to school and saw his friend Billy crying. "What happened, Billy?" Timmy asked. "I lost my favorite toy," Billy said sadly. Timmy wanted to make his friend smile, so he said, "Don't worry, Billy. We can find it together."

They looked everywhere, but they couldn't find the toy. Suddenly, they heard a loud noise. It was the school bell ringing, which meant it was time to go home. Timmy promised Billy that they would keep looking for the toy tomorrow. But when they came back to school the next day, the toy was gone forever. Timmy felt sad that he couldn't make his friend smile.

Sam was playing in his room. He was having so much fun with his toys. But then, he heard a loud noise. His mother had risen from the bed. 

"Mommy, what happened?" asked Sam. His mother was alert. She looked around the room and said, "Don't worry, everything is ok."

Sam was relieved. He quickly went back to playing with his toys. But then, he heard the noise again. This time, it was even louder. He looked up and saw his mother had risen to the ceiling. She was floating!

Sam couldn't believe what was happening. But his mother told him not to worry. She said, "It's ok, Sam. Just keep playing!" 

Sam was amazed. He thought it was the coolest thing ever! He made sure to stay alert and watch his mother as she slowly floated back down to the ground. It was definitely an experience he'd never forget.

Once upon a time, there were two sisters who lived near the ocean. The oldest sister loved to jog by the beach every day. One day she asked her little sister to join her. The little sister was so excited!

So the two sisters put on their black shoes and began to jog. The oldest sister ran very fast, but the little sister was slower. She soon became tired and wanted to stop, but her sister said, "We can take a break, but let's keep going a little bit longer."

The two sisters continued to jog until they reached a park. There they were able to run on a sandy path underneath tall trees. The little sister now felt strong and kept running. As the sisters jog, they laughed and smiled, happy to be together.

Once upon a time, there was a candle. It was tall and clear. The candle stood in an important place, and was there to record something important. 

Every day, the candle would record the events around it. It watched the sun come up and the sun go down. It saw people coming and going. The candle recorded everything.
 
Soon, it was dark outside, and the candle was lit. Now it glowed and shone brightly, recording even more things. The candle was so clear that it seemed to light up the room. 

The candle glowed and burned for a long time. Eventually, when it finished recording, the candle burned down and went out. But the candle still stands in its spot, watching and recording everything, just like it always did.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and chase butterflies. One day, Lily's cat got very sick and started to suffer. Lily didn't know what to do, so she asked her mom for help. 

Her mom took the cat to the vet, where they gave it medicine to help it feel better. Lily was very happy that her cat wasn't suffering anymore. 

Later that day, Lily went outside to play, but noticed that it was very quiet. She looked around and saw that all the birds had stopped singing. Lily wondered why there was silence in the air. 

Suddenly, a big gust of wind blew through the trees and the birds started singing again. Lily smiled and realized that the silence was gone. It was now clear that the wind had caused the birds to stop singing for a moment.

One day, a little fish named Fin was sad. His tooth hurt a lot. He swam to his friend, Star, the starfish. "My tooth hurts," Fin told Star. Star wanted to help Fin feel better.

Star had an idea. "Let's dive deep into the sea to find something to help your tooth," Star said. Fin and Star dove deep, deep down. They saw many things, like big rocks and pretty shells.

At last, they found a magic clam. The clam opened up and showed them a shiny pearl. "This pearl will make your tooth feel better," said the clam. Fin took the pearl and his tooth stopped hurting. Fin was so happy, and he thanked Star and the magic clam. They all played together in the sea, and Fin was never sad again.

Once upon a time, there was an ant. The ant wanted to make a stack of leaves. The ant worked hard, and soon had a nice stack of leaves. But then, the ant was stopped by a big bug who wanted to bite the leaves. The ant said "No, please, don't bite my stack!" But the bug wouldn't listen, and it kept biting the leaves until the stack was broken.

The ant was so sad. It had worked hard to make a nice stack, and now it was all gone.

Then, a wise butterfly came and said to the ant, "It is not good to bite another creature's work. You must always be kind, and not destroy someone's work."

The ant was very grateful, and started to make a stack of leaves again. This time, the ant worked extra carefully, and the stack of leaves was so beautiful it made everyone happy.

The ant thought to itself, "Kindness and friendship are much better than destruction and anger. From now on, I will always try to be kind and helpful".

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a favorite teddy bear that she loved to hug. One day, Lily and her teddy bear went on a walk. While they were walking, they saw a big tree that made a big shadow on the ground. 

Lily said, "Look, Teddy! A big shadow!" 

Teddy asked, "Can shadows hug?" 

Lily thought for a moment and said, "No, silly Teddy. Shadows can't hug. But I can hug you!" 

Teddy smiled and said, "I love it when you hug me. You make me feel so happy." 

Lily hugged Teddy tight and said, "I love you too, Teddy. You're my favorite toy in the whole wide world. Even though you're not expensive, you're priceless to me." 

From that day on, Lily and Teddy went on many more adventures together, always hugging each other and making each other feel loved.

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. But today it is very cold. The wind blows and the leaves fall.

"Let's go on the swings!" Lily says. She runs to the swings and sits on one. She pushes with her feet and goes high.

"Me too!" Ben says. He runs after Lily and sits on the other swing. He pushes with his feet and goes high too.

They swing and laugh. They feel warm and happy.

But then a big boy comes. He is mean. He sees Lily and Ben on the swings. He wants to swing too.

"Get off the swings!" he says. He pushes Lily and Ben with his hands. They stop swinging and fall to the ground.

"Ow!" Lily says. She hurts her knee. She cries.

"Hey, stop that!" Ben says. He is angry. He stands up and faces the big boy.

The big boy laughs. He teases Ben. He says, "You are a baby. You can't swing. You can't do anything."

Ben feels sad. He wants to swing. He wants to play with Lily. He does not like the big boy.

But then he sees something. He sees a smile. It is Lily's smile. She is not crying anymore. She has a plan.

She picks up a leaf. It is dry and crunchy. She throws it at the big boy's face.

"Ha!" she says. "Take that!"

The big boy is surprised. He feels the leaf on his face. He does not like it.

He tries to wipe it off. But Lily throws another leaf. And another. And another.

Ben sees Lily's smile. He smiles too. He picks up some leaves. He throws them at the big boy too.

"Ha!" he says. "Take that!"

The big boy is angry. He does not like the leaves. He does not like Lily and Ben. He runs away.

Lily and Ben laugh. They hug each other. They are happy.

They go back to the swings. They swing and laugh. They feel warm and happy.

They do not care about the cold. They do not care about the big boy. They only care about each other. They are friends.

John lived in the forest and he loved exploring. One day he picked up his spear and went outside to search for new adventures. As he walked, he heard something moving in the bush. He paused to study it more closely.

He could see a wild bear! John was afraid and wanted to run, but he had seen the bear hunting with its spear before. He stayed very still and the bear looked at him with its harsh eyes.

John started to cry but he remembered that if he moved the bear would think he was prey. Slowly, he stepped back and the bear dropped its spear. John ran back home quickly. He felt relieved to be safe.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Jill. She was very impatient and always wanted things to happen quickly. She was very excited, because today she would learn something new. She was going to learn how to lock a door!

Jill's teacher, Mrs. Jane, showed her how to turn the big metal key and how to handle it gently. She showed Jill how to push and turn the key, and then how to pull the stiff metal handle to lock the door.

Mrs. Jane asked Jill to try it. Jill stuck out her finger, but she was too impatient and pulled a little too hard. The lock didn't work.

Mrs. Jane laughed and said, "That's okay, Jill. Just be gentle. Here, let me show you again." She showed Jill how to turn the key slowly and pull the handle very gently.

This time, the lock clicked and the door was secure! Jill was so proud of herself and said, "Look! I locked it!"

Mrs. Jane smiled and said, "Very good, Jill! You're a pro at locking doors now."

Timmy was very naughty. He loved playing with string. He would pick it up and twirl it around his finger. He would giggle and laugh.

One day, Timmy's mom was watching him and warned him that if he didn't put the string away, she would have to take it away from him. But Timmy didn't listen.

So mom took the string away from him and sighed. Timmy was sad and started to cry.

His mom hugged him and wiped away his tears. She promised him that if he promised not to be naughty with the string anymore, she would give it back to him.

Timmy promised and hugged his mom. He was so happy to have his string back. From then on, he was careful to not be naughty with the string.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Lucy. She had a beautiful coat which was always very warm.

Whenever she put it on, it made her feel so snug and nice. She'd often set it next to her chair at home and look forward to wearing it again.

One day, it was cold outside, so Lucy asked her mom for her warm coat.

"Yes of course, Lucy," said her mom. She set the coat down on the chair for Lucy to put it on.

"Thank you, Mama," said Lucy as she put on her coat and settled down to keep warm. She was so happy to be wearing her favorite coat!

Sara and Tom are friends. They like to play in the park. They see a big swing. Sara wants to swing first. She runs to the swing and sits on it.

"Push me, Tom!" Sara says. "Push me high!"

Tom pushes Sara on the swing. Sara laughs and feels happy. She likes to swing high and fast.

Tom waits for his turn. He is impatient. He wants to swing too. He pushes Sara harder and harder.

"Stop, Tom!" Sara says. "You are pushing too hard! I will fall!"

Tom does not stop. He pushes Sara even harder. Sara feels scared. She tries to hold on to the swing.

But the swing is too fast. Sara loses her grip. She falls off the swing. She lands on the ground. She feels a sharp pain in her knee. She has a cut. She cries.

"Ow, ow, ow!" Sara cries. "Tom, you hurt me! You are mean!"

Tom feels sorry. He did not mean to hurt Sara. He runs to Sara and helps her up.

"I'm sorry, Sara!" Tom says. "I did not mean to hurt you! I just wanted to swing too! Are you okay?"

Sara looks at her knee. She sees blood. She feels sad and angry.

"No, I'm not okay!" Sara says. "You made me fall! You made me cut my knee! I don't want to play with you anymore!"

Sara runs away from Tom. She goes to her mom. Her mom hugs her and cleans her cut. She puts a band-aid on it.

Tom feels bad. He wants to say sorry to Sara again. He wants to be friends. He goes to Sara and her mom.

"Can I play with Sara again?" Tom asks. "I'm sorry I pushed her too hard. I won't do it again."

Sara looks at Tom. She sees his sad face. She remembers that Tom is her friend. She feels a little better.

"Okay, Tom," Sara says. "You can play with me again. But you have to be nice. And you have to wait for your turn."

Tom nods. He is happy. He says thank you to Sara and her mom.

Sara and Tom go back to the park. They take turns on the swing. They swing gently and safely. They have fun. They are friends again.

Sara and Tom were hungry. They wanted to eat some grapes. Mom said they could have some, but they had to wash them first. She gave them a big bowl and a colander.

Sara and Tom took the bowl and the colander to the sink. They turned on the water and put some grapes in the colander. They washed them with their hands. They were careful not to drop any.

"Look, Tom, these grapes are so big and juicy!" Sara said. She picked one and put it in her mouth. It was sweet and crunchy.

"Can I have one too?" Tom asked. He reached for a grape, but he was too small. He could not reach the colander. He felt helpless.

"Wait, Tom, I'll help you!" Sara said. She tried to move the colander closer to Tom, but it was too heavy. She lost her balance and the colander slipped from her hands. The grapes fell out and rolled all over the floor.

"Oh no!" Sara and Tom cried. They looked at the mess. They heard Mom coming. They knew they were in trouble.

"Sara, Tom, what happened here?" Mom asked. She saw the grapes on the floor. She was not happy.
