"Sara, Tom, you were supposed to wash the grapes, not play with them. You made a big mess. You wasted good food. You have to clean it up now. And no more grapes for you today. I'm very disappointed in you."

Sara and Tom felt sorry. They wished they had listened to Mom. They wished they had not been greedy. They wished they had reminded each other to be careful. They learned their lesson. They said sorry to Mom and helped her clean the floor. They hoped Mom would forgive them and give them some grapes another day.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim was a very polite boy. One day, Tim found a tape on the ground. He was very happy and wanted to show it to his friend, Sue.

Tim went to Sue's house and said, "Look, Sue! I found a tape!" Sue looked at the tape and said, "Can I have it, please?" Tim wanted to be polite, so he accepted and gave the tape to Sue.

But the tape was not good. It was sticky and dirty. When Sue tried to use the tape, it made a big mess. Sue was sad, and Tim was sad too. They both wished they never found the tape.

Once upon a time, there was a big elephant named Ella. Ella had a long trunk. She lived in the jungle with her friend, a little bird named Bobo. They were very happy together.

One day, Ella found a big pile of yummy fruits. She was very hungry, but she remembered to share. She called out to Bobo, "Bobo, come here! Let's share these fruits!" Bobo flew over and they ate the fruits together.

The next day, it rained a lot. Ella and Bobo felt miserable because they were wet and cold. Ella had an idea. She said, "Bobo, come under my trunk! We can share it to stay dry!" Bobo went under Ella's trunk and they stayed dry together. They were not miserable anymore. They were happy because they shared with each other.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys and watch cartoons on TV. One day, Timmy's mom told him they were going to the store to buy some things. Timmy asked if they could buy him a new toy, but his mom said they had to buy some food and other things first.

As they walked through the store, Timmy saw a toy he really wanted. He asked his mom if they could buy it, but she said it was too expensive and they had to be cheap today. Timmy was sad, but he understood.

After they finished shopping, Timmy's mom told him they had to rush home because they had to do some math homework together. Timmy didn't like math very much, but he loved spending time with his mom. They worked on the math problems together and Timmy learned a lot. He was happy he got to spend time with his mom and learn something new.

One day, a big dog and a little cat were playing in a field. They liked to run and jump in the thick grass. The dog said, "I enjoy playing with you, cat!" The cat said, "I enjoy playing with you too, dog!"

The dog and the cat found a big ball in the field. They took turns pushing the ball with their noses. They laughed and had fun. The sun was warm and the sky was blue.

As they played, a bird flew down and said, "Can I play too?" The dog and the cat said, "Yes, come play with us!" So the bird, the dog, and the cat played with the big ball in the thick grass. They all enjoyed the fun day in the field.

Ben and Lily were best friends. They liked to play together at the park. They liked to swing on the swings, slide on the slide, and run on the grass. They always helped each other and shared their toys. They were dependable friends.

One day, they saw a big truck parked near the park. It had a shiny buckle on the door. Ben and Lily were curious. They wanted to see the buckle up close. They ran to the truck and touched the buckle. It was cold and hard.

"Wow, look at this buckle!" Ben said. "It's so big and shiny!"

"Can we open the door?" Lily asked. "Maybe there is something inside the truck."

Ben tried to pull the buckle, but it was too tight. He could not open the door. He shook his head. "No, we can't. It's locked. Maybe the truck belongs to someone."

"Maybe we should go back to the park," Lily said. "We don't want to get in trouble."

Ben nodded. He agreed with Lily. They turned around and ran back to the park. They did not see the man who was watching them from behind a tree. He was the owner of the truck. He was angry. He did not like children touching his truck.

He came out from behind the tree and followed Ben and Lily. He shouted at them. "Hey, you two! Stop right there! What were you doing with my truck? You have no right to touch my truck!"

Ben and Lily were scared. They heard the man's voice. They looked back and saw him. He was big and mean. He had a frown on his face. He was holding a stick in his hand.

They ran faster. They wanted to get away from the man. They reached the park gate. They saw their moms waiting for them. They ran to their moms and hugged them. They told them what happened.

Their moms were worried. They looked at the man. He was still shouting and waving his stick. He was trying to get to Ben and Lily. Their moms held them tight. They protected them from the man.

"Go away, you bully!" one mom said. "Leave our children alone! They did nothing wrong!"

"Yeah, go away, you meanie!" the other mom said. "Our children are good and kind! They don't deserve your anger!"

The man was surprised. He saw the moms. He saw their faces. They were angry and brave. They were not afraid of him. He felt ashamed. He realized he was wrong. He lowered his stick. He turned around and walked away. He muttered to himself. "Sorry, sorry, sorry."

Ben and Lily were relieved. They saw the man leave. They felt safe and happy. They thanked their moms. They kissed their moms. They smiled at each other. They were still best friends. They learned a lesson. They decided not to touch strangers' trucks again. They decided to stay in the park and have fun. They decided to always stick together. They were dependable friends.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Sarah. She was so sleepy that she could barely keep her eyes open.

Every day her mommy said to her, "Time for a nap, Sarah!" 

One day, Sarah answered back, "No mommy, I don't want to nap! I'm not that sleepy!" 

Her mommy said, "But Sarah, it's time for you to shut your eyes and rest. You're going to be very tired if you don't get a good nap."

Finally, Sarah could not fight the sleepy feeling any more. She curled up into a cozy ball and shut her eyes for a nap.

When she awoke, Sarah felt so refreshed and happy! That was the best nap ever!

One day, a lovely little dog named Spot lost his toy. He looked everywhere for it. Spot was very sad. He asked his friend, the big cat, "Did you see my toy?"

The big cat said, "No, but let's look together." They looked and looked but could not find the toy. Spot felt very sad and started to cry.

Just then, Spot's mom came and gave him a big hug. She said, "Don't worry, Spot. We will find your toy." With his mom's help, they found the toy under a big tree. Spot was so happy, he gave his mom a big hug and said, "Thank you, Mom!"

Once upon a time, there was a brave boy. He was very small, but was always ready for adventure. One night, he wanted dinner. So he got up and put on his brave face. He put on his hat, grabbed his brave toy sword, and headed for the kitchen.

When he got there, the kitchen was empty and dark. Suddenly, a loud noise came from the fridge. He was very brave and he slowly opened the door. Out from the fridge came a blue monster! He was ready to fight the monster when the monster opened his big mouth and said â€œI want dinner too!â€

The brave boy said, â€œLetâ€™s make dinner together.â€ The two of them chopped, mixed, and stirred until they had made a delicious dinner! They both enjoyed their dinner and were friends ever since.

Once upon a time, there was a boy called Ted. He had an ugly play which he owned all by himself. Everywhere he went, he took it with him. One day, while he was walking with his play, he saw another boy with a beautiful play. He was very excited and wanted to have the same kind of play.

He asked the other boy, "Can I have your play?" The boy replied, "No, I own this play. You need to get your own play". Ted was sad. He wanted the same kind of play, but he followed the boy's instructions and went looking for his own play. 

He searched for a long time, until he finally found the play he was looking for. It was an even more beautiful play than the one he saw before. He was very happy. He bought the play and from then on he owned it all by himself. 

He said to himself, "I am so lucky to own such a beautiful play!"

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Layla. She was watching a fly store around the kitchen when she saw something. It was a prune! She was so happy that she reached out to grab it. But in she was sad when she came closer, because the prune had a big squiggly bite mark right in the middle. 

Layla looked around to see if anyone saw her trying to take the prune. She was surprised to see that a small mouse was sitting on the counter staring right at her! He looked a little sad, so she asked him why.

The mouse said "Someone already ate my prune. I was so hungry and it was the only one!" Layla felt bad for the little mouse, so she told him not to worry. She said she would help him find another prune. She put down some food in one area and the mouse was able to find a new prune to store for later. 

The mouse was so happy, he gave Layla a high-five with his tiny paw. Layla smiled and said goodbye to her new friend. She went back to playing in the kitchen, happy to have made a new mouse friend.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys, but his favorite toy was his toy car that had a little remote control. One day, Timmy's toy car stopped moving because the battery was dead. Timmy's mom told him to throw the battery away, but Timmy thought he could fix it.

Timmy went to his room and looked for something to fix the battery. He found a clear tape and thought it might help. Timmy used the tape to fix the battery and put it back in the car. The car started moving again! Timmy was so happy and proud of himself.

Later that day, Timmy's mom made him a sandwich for lunch. Timmy was so hungry that he ate the sandwich in one bite! But then, he started feeling sick. Timmy's mom asked him if he ate something else, and Timmy remembered that he ate the battery! Timmy's mom took him to the hospital, and the doctor was able to take the battery out of his tummy. Timmy learned that he should never eat things that are not food.

Once upon a time, there was a little worm called Bob. Bob loved to play in the garden. He played all day and got very messy.

One day, Bob saw a pretty ladybird. He waved his feelers in the air and hopped to her. "Hi!" Bob said. "I love you!"

The ladybird was very surprised. She had never heard such words from a worm. She wasn't sure how to respond.

After a moment of hesitation, the ladybird said, "I'm sorry, Bob. I don't love you back. I'm going to fly away now."

Bob felt very sad. He wanted to be loved. But it was too late. The ladybird took off, leaving Bob all alone in the garden. The messy little worm was left all alone with a broken heart.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily went to the park with her mommy. While they were playing, Lily saw a butterfly and got very excited. She wanted to take a closer look, so she ran after it.

Suddenly, she tripped and fell down. She hurt her knee and started to cry. Her mommy came over and asked, "What happened, Lily? Are you okay?" Lily showed her mommy her knee and said, "I fell down and it hurts." Her mommy gave her a hug and said, "Don't be fearful, I'll take care of you."

Lily felt better knowing her mommy was there to help her. Her mommy cleaned her knee and put a band-aid on it. Lily smiled and said, "Thank you, mommy. You're the best." They continued to play at the park, but Lily was careful not to run too fast anymore. She didn't want to hurt herself again.

Once upon a time, a little girl named Lily went to see a play at the theatre. The stage was big and bright, with beautiful flowers and trees all around. Lily was so excited to watch the play.

As the play started, Lily saw a little boy sitting next to her. She said, "Hi, my name is Lily. What's your name?" The boy replied, "My name is Max. Nice to meet you."

During the play, Lily noticed that Max was having trouble seeing the stage. So, she offered to lift him up so that he could see better. Max was so happy and said, "Thank you, Lily. You are so kind."

After the play, Lily's mom asked her how she liked the play. Lily replied, "It was beautiful, but helping Max see the play was even better. It made me feel happy." The moral of the story is that helping others can make us feel good too.

Once upon a time, in a sunny meadow, there lived a fast little kitten. Each day, the kitten would run around the meadow, chasing after butterflies.

One day, she heard something strange coming from the trees. She stopped to listen and heard a strange sound repeating over and over again. It sounded like, "meow, meow". So, the kitten slowly walked closer, and saw a tiny, little kitten meowing. It was so little and scared, so the fast kitten went up to it and said, "meow".

The little kitten stopped meowing and looked up happily at her new friend. It then said, "meow" again and jumped up to give the fast kitten a big hug. The fast kitten was so happy that she said, "meow" back and started to cuddle and play with the little one.

They both continued to play and repeat, "meow". They could not stop and became the best of friends for life.

Lily and Tom went to the market with Mom. They saw many fruits and vegetables. Lily liked the red apples. Tom liked the yellow bananas. Mom said they could each pick one.

"How much is this apple?" Lily asked the seller.

"Two coins, little girl," the seller said.

Lily gave him two coins from her pocket. She was happy. She took a bite of the apple. It was sweet and juicy.

"How much is this banana?" Tom asked the seller.

"One coin, little boy," the seller said.

Tom gave him one coin from his pocket. He was happy. He peeled the banana. It was soft and creamy.

Lily and Tom shared their fruits with each other. They both said they were delicious.

"Mom, do you want some?" Lily asked.

"Thank you, sweetie, but I have my own fruit," Mom said. She showed them a big orange. "This was three coins, but it is worth the price. It is very tasty and healthy."

Lily and Tom nodded. They knew Mom was right. They loved fruits. They finished their fruits and threw the peels in the trash. They thanked the seller and followed Mom to the next stall. They wondered what else they would find at the market.

Once upon a time there was a kind girl called Marie. She was always very compassionate and always sought to help those around her. One day, Marie was walking in the meadow and she saw a spirit flying through the air. She found it beautiful and decided to follow it with her eyes.

After a few moments, the spirit started to fly toward her and Marie was filled with delight. She felt a connection between her and the spirit.

Curious to know why the spirit had come to her, Marie asked â€œWhy are you here?â€

The spirit smiled and said â€œI came to show you something special. Follow me and you will see.â€

Marie had no idea what it meant, but since the spirit was so kind, she decided to follow it. She followed the spirit deep into the forest until they reached a beautiful lake.

Here, the spirit explained to her that kindness and compassion help us to connect us to all living creatures. Marie smiled and thanked the spirit for showing her something that she would never forget.

Once there was a girl named Daisy. Daisy was three years old and she loved to go outside and play. One day she was out in the garden and she saw a tall, green tree. 

Daisy decided to skip around the tree. She skipped and skipped and it made her so happy! Her face lit up and her little heart danced.

She soon noticed leaves falling from the tree. Daisy looked around and saw that the grass hadn't been cut. She thought it looked messy, so she decided to do something about it! 

Daisy grabbed the garden shears and started to cut the grass around the tree. She was so proud of her work when she finished and the grass looked clean and neat. 

Daisy finished by skipping around the tree one final time, smiling with delight. She knew that it was the nicest and cleanest tree in the garden. 

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily and her mom were playing in the park when they saw an ambulance with its lights flashing. 

Lily asked her mom, "What's an ambulance?" 

"It's a big car that takes people to the hospital when they are hurt or sick," her mom replied. 

Just then, they saw a man with a tight bandage on his arm being carried into the ambulance. "Will he be okay?" asked Lily. 

"I hope so," said her mom. "The ambulance will take him to the hospital where the doctors will help him." 

The ambulance drove away and Lily watched it until it disappeared. "The end," she said, and her mom smiled.

Once there was a little boy named Jack. He loved watching the colorful television. One day, his mom asked him to help her number the plates and spoons in the kitchen. But Jack wanted to stay in the living room and watch the television. 

"But Mom!" Jack said pleadingly. "I don't want to number, I want to watch the television!" 

Jack's mom looked at him and said firmly, "Jack, if you don't help me number the plates, then you won't be able to watch the television today." 

Jack was very upset. He thought about it and decided that it would be better to help with number the plates and spoons. So, he and his mom went to the kitchen and got to work. After counting all the plates and spoons, Jack went back to the living room to watch the colorful television. Jack learned to be helpful and was very happy that he got to watch his favorite show.

The little boy was hungry. He wanted to find food, so he went outside to look for it. Suddenly he saw a big box with something inside. He opened the box and in it was a toilet! He was so excited! He ran back inside to show his mom and dad.

His mom and dad smiled and said, "It's a gift for you! See if you can win it!" The little boy was very happy. He wanted to win the toilet so badly.

He worked very hard every day. Finally, after a few weeks, he won the toilet! He jumped up and down in excitement and hugged his mom and dad. Now he had a special toilet all for himself.

Every day he was so happy. He always used his special toilet whenever he was hungry. He thought it was the best toilet in the world.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Jenny. Jenny liked to pretend. Every day she would pretend that she was a princess in a beautiful castle.

One day, Jenny gathered some sticks and started to make a delicate little cross. It was the prettiest cross that Jenny had ever built. She was so proud. 

Suddenly, Jenny heard a loud rumble in the distance. She ran to see what it was, but it was too late. A fierce storm was coming straight for her.

Jenny quickly tried to hide from the storm but it was too powerful. She was blown away and the delicate little cross was destroyed. Jenny screamed in fear as the storm passed.

At the end of the storm, Jenny was very sad. Her delicate little cross had been destroyed. She sat in the mud, imagining she was a princess in her castle and wishing the ferocious storm had never come.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. She loved to be creative and play with her toys. One special day, she had a great idea. She wanted to make a potato jump! She ran to her bedroom, grabbed her toys, and raced to the kitchen.

In the kitchen, she got a big potato and put it on the kitchen table. She grabbed her toy truck and pushed it against the potato. Suddenly, the potato began to jump! The little girl was so excited. She laughed and giggled with glee.

The little girl spent the rest of the day making her potato jump higher and higher. She was so creative, she even added a few obstacles for the potato to jump over. In the end, she had so much fun, she even wanted to share her creative idea with her friends.

Once upon a time, there was a princess who loved pretty things. She had a diamond necklace that was very important to her. One day, she went to a big party and wore her diamond necklace. But, when she got there, she saw that everyone was wearing simple clothes. She felt embarrassed because she was the only one wearing fancy clothes. 

The princess wanted to leave the party, but then she saw a little girl who was looking at her diamond necklace with big eyes. The little girl said, "Wow! That necklace is so pretty!" The princess smiled and felt happy. She realized that what's important is not what you wear, but how you make others feel. 

From that day on, the princess wore her diamond necklace proudly and didn't feel embarrassed anymore. She even shared her pretty things with others and made them feel happy too.

Once upon a time, there was a tall sheep named Sally. She was very happy because she had lots of friends. One day, Sally was walking in the meadow when she saw two sheep fighting. 

Sally went up to them and said, "Why are you fighting? That's not nice!" 

One of the sheep said, "We are fighting because we both want this piece of grass." 

Sally replied, "There's enough grass for all of us. We don't need to fight." 

The two sheep stopped fighting and looked at Sally. They realized she was right and felt bad for fighting. From that day on, they all shared the grass and were happy together. The moral of the story is that fighting is not the answer, sharing is better.

Once upon a time, there was a famous duck. He loved to talk to the other animals and they all loved to hear him speak. One day, he was talking with a rabbit and said, "I'm so famous, everyone knows my name!"
The rabbit replied, "That's amazing! How did you become so famous?"
The duck told him, "Well, I just kept talking and doing my best, and eventually people took notice!" 
The rabbit said, "I wish I could be famous too!"
The duck replied, "You can be! Just keep talking and show people how special you are!"
The rabbit thanked him and went off to try to be famous. The duck smiled and watched him go.

Once upon a time there was a monster who lived in a messy house. He liked to make the house messier and messier, so it was always untidy!

One day, a curious little girl came to visit. The monster was frightened, so he started to shake! He shook and shook, until the little girl laughed. She thought it was funny!

The little girl asked, "Why do you shake?" The monster said, "I shake because I am scared of visitors like you."

The little girl laughed and said, "Don't be scared. I'm your friend now." She hugged the monster and said, "I won't make a mess. I'll help you clean up the house too."

The monster was so surprised. He stopped shaking and smiled. Together, they tidied up the house and the monster was very happy to have a new friend!

Once upon a time, there was a lion and he liked to roar. He was proud of how loud he could be. One day, he went to town and noticed something very hot in the sky. It was a bright, shining sun. The lion liked it so much that he started to roar again and again.

He was so loud that the people nearby got mad. They searched for the sound and found the lion! The people said, "Stop that noise!" The lion was embarrassed but he still liked how he sounded.

The people then said, "We can make a deal. You can roar, but you have to do it somewhere else. We can give you a cheap place to stay and plenty of food to eat."

The lion thought this was a great deal and he soon settled into his new home! Now, the lion roars in a far away place and everyone is happy. He still likes to feel the warmth of the sun against his face, but he doesn't roar so loud anymore.

Once upon a time there was a kind bear. The bear was always trying to be helpful and make his friends happy. 

One day the bear's best friend, a small rabbit, was feeling very sad. He was so sad he couldn't even move. The bear didn't know how to help his friend and he felt so sad too.

The bear tried everything he knew to make the rabbit feel better, but nothing seemed to work. 

Finally, the bear decided to surrender to his feelings and gave the rabbit a big hug. The rabbit hugged him back, and finally started to feel a bit better.

But the moment was bittersweet. The bear could see that the sadness in his friend's eyes would not disappear anytime soon. The bear looked his friend in the eyes and said: "I am here for you always". 

The rabbit smiled and said: "I know, thank you my friend". 

The bear gave his friend one last hug and they both knew that better days would come.

Mummy had to take John to the doctors. John was a little patient. He was always very mild. 
When they got to the doctors, mummy had to help John dress in some special clothes. She helped him put on a big, white coat and a big, blue hat.

John was very excited to be at the doctors. He looked around and saw lots of toys and books. He even saw a fish tank with some friendly, bright fish.

Mummy took John to the doctor's office. He waited until it was his turn to meet the doctor. When it was his turn, John and Mummy went in. 

The doctor smiled at John and said hello. He asked Mummy questions about John and then listened to his heart with a special machine. The doctor said that John was very healthy.

John and Mummy were very happy. Mummy helped John dress back in his clothes, and they said goodbye to the doctor. John was proud and excited to have visited the doctor!

Once upon a time there was a man. He was very foolish. He wanted to bring a pumpkin to his house. He thought he could carry it all the way. But he was wrong! As he walked, the pumpkin kept getting bigger and bigger. Soon the poor man couldn't carry it any more.

The man was very sad, but then he had a brilliant plan. He put the pumpkin into a pool and let it soak. After a few hours the pumpkin had soaked up all the water. Now the man could carry it home!

The man was so happy. He took the pumpkin home and had a delicious snack. The foolish man sure learned his lesson: don't try to carry a big, wet pumpkin!

Once upon a time, there was a great princess who lived in a big castle. She had many toys and dresses, but she was not happy. She wanted more things and she was always asking for more. One day, her fairy godmother came to visit her and gave her a magic wand. The fairy said, "You can set anything you want with this wand, but be careful what you wish for."

The princess was so excited and she started to set everything she wanted. She set a big cake, a new puppy, and a pretty necklace. But she still felt unhappy. Then, she remembered what the fairy said and she decided to set something different. She set a table with food for all the poor people in the kingdom. Everyone was so happy and the princess felt great. She realized that helping others made her the happiest of all.

From that day on, the princess used her magic wand to set things that would help others. She learned that being kind and generous was the greatest thing of all. And she lived happily ever after. The end.

Lily and Ben are twins. They like to watch TV after dinner. They watch funny shows and learn new things. They are smart kids.

But today, Mom says they have to prepare for bed early. She says there is a big storm coming and the power might go out. She says they have to brush their teeth, put on their pajamas, and get their flashlights.

Lily and Ben are sad. They want to watch TV more. They ask Mom, "Can we watch one more show, please?"

Mom shakes her head. She says, "No, sweeties, you have to prepare for bed now. The storm might be loud and scary. You need to be safe and cozy in your beds. Maybe we can watch TV tomorrow, if the power is back on."

Lily and Ben nod. They understand. They love Mom and they trust her. They do what she says. They prepare for bed. They hug Mom and say good night. They go to their room and turn on their flashlights. They snuggle in their beds and listen to the storm. They are not afraid. They are smart and brave. They close their eyes and dream of TV.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She had a big eraser that she loved to use when she drew pictures. One day, Lily's friend came to play with her. Her friend wanted to borrow the eraser to fix her own drawing. Lily said yes and gave her the eraser. 

After a while, Lily's friend gave the eraser back to her. But Lily noticed that the eraser was warm. She asked her friend why it was warm. Her friend said that she had held it in her hand for a long time. 

Lily was happy to have her eraser back and thanked her friend. They continued to play together and had lots of fun. The end.

Two friends, Jack and Jill, were playing together in the garden. He was sorting a pile of toys and she was singing a happy song.

Suddenly, Jack frowned. He saw a powerful trouble near the pond. It was a big, scary monster. He was so scared that his legs shook and he couldn't move!

Jill saw Jack's fear and knew she had to help. She ran to the monster, smiled bravely and said "Hello Monster! What are you doing here in our garden?"

The monster looked surprised. He said, "I was just looking for trouble, but I didn't expect to find someone so powerful!"

Jill smiled and said, "Well, you can't find any trouble here. So why don't you help us sort our toys while you are here?"

The monster was so impressed by Jill's courage that he agreed. So the three of them happily sorted the toys and played together in the garden.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy lived in a house on top of a big hill. One day, Timmy went for a walk down the hill and he found a valley. The valley was very dry because it hadn't rained for a long time. 

Timmy saw a little girl sitting on a rock in the valley. He asked her, "Why are you sad?" The little girl said, "I lost my puppy." Timmy smiled and said, "Don't worry, we can find your puppy together." 

They searched and searched, and finally, they found the puppy hiding behind a bush. The little girl was so happy that she smiled and hugged her puppy. Timmy was happy too, and they both walked back up the hill together.

Once upon a time a naughty bunny hopped out the door on a sunny day. It hopped up to a porch and stopped. It looked around and observed everything.

The bunny saw a frog by the pond. The frog croaked, "Hey bunny! What are you up to on this nice day?"

The bunny smiled. "I'm doing some observing," it said.

The frog giggled. "That's funny. Where are you observing?"

"On the porch," said the bunny. "I'm seeing all the flowers and bugs and things. It's really fun!"

The frog said, "It sure sounds like it. Well, you have fun, naughty bunny."

The bunny laughed and hopped away. It observed lots of cool things, hopping along until it got home. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a lonely boy named Tim. He had zero friends. One day, he went to the park to play.

At the park, he saw a girl named Sue. She was playing alone too. Tim hurried to her and asked, "Do you want to play with me?"

Sue smiled and said, "Yes, let's be friends!" They played together all day. They were not lonely anymore. Tim and Sue were very happy to have each other as friends.

Once upon a time, in a big green forest, there lived an enormous snake. This snake was very long and very big. All the animals in the forest were afraid of the snake.

One day, the snake was very hungry. It wanted to find some food to eat. The snake saw a little bird who had just received a big juicy worm. The snake wanted to eat the bird and the worm.

But the little bird was very smart. It flew up high in the sky and dropped the worm on the snake's head. The snake was surprised and happy. It ate the worm and did not bother the bird. From that day on, the snake and the bird became good friends.

One day, a little boy woke up early with the sun. He went to his kitchen and saw a gray bird out the window. He went outside holding his toy and was surprised to see two birds fighting. The boy wanted to stop them, so he clapped his hands and shouted, "Stop!" 

The fighting birds looked at him and quickly flew away. The boy was relieved and smiled. He looked up to the sky, which was now bright and blue. 

The little boy went back inside and closed the door. He was happy that he had stopped the birds from fighting. He was proud that he had been brave enough to try. 
 
From then on, the little boy remembered to be brave and kind when he saw fights, and to always close the door when he was done having fun outside.

Once upon a time, there was a busy pirate named Tom. He had a big ship and liked to smile a lot. Tom had many friends on his ship. They all worked together to find treasure.

One day, Tom and his friends saw an island. They thought there might be treasure there. They got off the ship and started to dig. They were all very busy looking for treasure. Tom was so happy that he could not stop smiling.

But then, it started to rain. The rain made the ground very wet and muddy. Tom and his friends could not find any treasure. They tried to go back to their ship, but it was gone! The rain had made the ship float away. Tom and his friends were very sad. They could not smile anymore because they were stuck on the island with no treasure and no ship.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside with her friends. One day, they saw a big billboard with a picture of a puppy on it. Lily asked her friends if they knew what the billboard said. They didn't know, so she decided to ask her mom.

"Mom, what does that sign say?" Lily asked.

"It's an advertisement for a pet store. They are having a competition to see who can adopt the most puppies," her mom replied.

Lily and her friends were so excited to visit the pet store and see all the cute puppies. They decided to ask their parents if they could adopt one too. They knew it would be a very competitive event, but they were determined to win.

One day a mighty leaf was blowing in the wind. It flew so high that it reached the sky.

The leaf looked at the clouds and asked, "What can I do today?"

The clouds said, "Work!"

The leaf thought for a moment and then decided to take action. It flew down to a tree and started to work. It waved around the branches and helped them stay strong. The other leaves on the tree admired its hard work.

Then, all of a sudden, a little girl walked up. She looked at the mighty leaf with excitement and asked, "What are you doing?"

The leaf smiled and said, "I'm working!"

The little girl smiled with delight and said, "You're so strong!"

The leaf felt proud of its work and thanked the clouds for helping it find its purpose. Together with the other leaves, it kept working hard every day.

One day, there was a pretty bird in the park. A little girl saw the bird and wanted to take it home. She ran to catch the bird, but it flew away. The little girl was sad and cried.

Later that day, the little girl's mom had a meeting with her boss. The little girl went with her mom to the meeting. She was bored and wanted to play. She saw a toy on the table and wanted to take it. But her mom said no.

The little girl was upset and started to cry again. Her mom hugged her and said, "It's okay, we can play with your toys when we get home." The little girl stopped crying and was happy again.

Once upon a time, there was a small fairy living in a house. She was very hungry and wanted something to eat. One day, she decided to go for a walk. It was a nice day, so she flew around the garden and met a little bird.

The bird said, "Hello! What's your name?"

The fairy answered, "My name is Emily. What's yours?"

The bird replied, "My name is Jim. I'm learning to fly. Can you help me?"

Emily smiled and said, "Sure! I can teach you how to fly."

So Emily showed Jim how to flap his wings, and he soon learned how to fly. The two of them flew around the garden until they were both tired, and then they went back to the house. 

Emily was very happy that she had been able to help Jim learn how to fly. From then on, they became good friends, and Emily was never hungry again!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to play outside. One day, she found a great big lizard in her backyard. She was a little scared at first, but then she realized the lizard was friendly.

"Hello, lizard!" said Lily.

"Hi there!" said the lizard.

Lily wanted to play with the lizard, so she asked, "Can I attach a string to your tail and we can play tug-of-war?"

The lizard thought for a moment and then said, "Sure, that sounds like fun!"

So Lily attached a string to the lizard's tail and they played tug-of-war together. It was so much fun that they played until the sun went down. From that day on, Lily and the lizard were the best of friends and they played together every day.

Once upon a time, there were two friends called Joe and Luke. They lived next door to each and enjoyed doing things together like playing or having fun. 

One day, Joe and Luke were playing and Joe made a mistake. He was very sorry for it and asked Luke to forgive him. Luke thought for a moment, and then smiled. He said, 'Of course I forgive you.'

Joe was so happy that his friend had forgiven him. To thank him, he offered to take Luke to a special dance. Luke was very shy, but he decided to go with Joe anyway. 

At the dance, Joe and Luke had lots of fun. They danced, laughed and played games. Joe was so glad Luke had decided to come with him. He was even gladder that Luke had forgiven him. 

The two friends had a day together that they would never forget. A day filled with joy, friendship and forgiveness.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play on his big cushion in the living room. One day, Timmy's mom said they were going to the park. Timmy was so excited because he loved the park. 

At the park, Timmy met some new friends. They played on the swings and the slide, but then a big dog came running towards them. Timmy was frightened of the dog and ran away. His friends followed him, but they didn't know where he was going. 

Timmy ran back home and hid behind the cushion. He felt safe there. But then, the dog followed him home and came inside. Timmy's mom tried to get the dog to leave, but it wouldn't listen. The dog was very big and strong. 

In the end, the dog hurt Timmy and he had to go to the hospital. Timmy was very sad and his mom was very upset. They learned that they should have included the dog's owner in their playtime at the park.

Mia and Leo wanted to make a cake with Mom. They helped Mom get the eggs, flour, sugar, and butter from the fridge and the cupboard. Mom gave them a big bowl and a mixer. "You can crack the eggs and put them in the bowl," Mom said. "Then we will add the other things and mix them well."

Mia and Leo took turns to crack the eggs. They tapped them on the edge of the bowl and opened them carefully. Sometimes a little shell fell in, but Mom picked it out. They counted the eggs as they put them in the bowl. "One, two, three, four," they said.

Then Mom added the flour, sugar, and butter. She plugged in the mixer and turned it on. It made a loud noise and the bowl started to spin. Mia and Leo watched with wide eyes as the mixer mixed the ingredients into a smooth batter. "Can we taste it?" Mia asked. "Not yet," Mom said. "We have to bake it first. But you can lick the mixer when I'm done."

Mom poured the batter into a cake pan and put it in the oven. She unplugged the mixer and gave it to Mia and Leo. They each took a beater and licked the sweet batter. It was yummy. They squeezed the beaters to get every drop. "Mmm, this is going to be a good cake," Leo said.

Mom smiled and cleaned the bowl and the mixer. She set the timer for the cake and told Mia and Leo to play in the living room. "But stay alert," she said. "When you hear the timer beep, come and help me take the cake out of the oven. It will be hot, so be careful." Mia and Leo nodded and ran to the living room. They couldn't wait to eat the cake.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. One day, Tim was exploring in the garden when he discovered something that he had never seen before â€” an object. It was bright and sparkly and Tim thought it was fascinating!

He asked his daddy to help him find out what it was. Together, they looked it up in a big book and discovered that it was a piece of treasure. Tim was so excited!

Tim had a special friend who liked to play games with him. He wanted to show his special friend the treasure, so he invited him over. They both dug around in the garden and eventually found the treasure. It was even shinier now that they could both see it.

The boys were so happy and grateful. They hugged each other with great compassion. They decided to bring the treasure inside and keep it safe in Tim's room. It would be a reminder of the fun they had together and the great adventures they could have.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play in the snow during winter. She would put on her warm coat, hat and mittens and go outside to build a snowman. 

One day, while she was playing outside, she saw some pretty stones on the ground. She decided to collect them and put them in her pocket. She thought they were very shiny and playful. 

When she went back inside, she showed her mom the stones she collected. Her mom thought they were very pretty too and helped her put them in a jar. Now, Lily had a collection of shiny stones to play with whenever she wanted.

One day, a delicate crab was springing around the beach. The crab was so small that all the other creatures on the beach could barely see it. The crab was happy to be playing in the sand.

As the crab kept springing around, he noticed a bird looking down at him. The crab wondered why the bird was looking at him. He was not scared, he just wanted to know what the bird was thinking.

The bird called out to the crab, and he stopped. The bird said, "Hello little crab, why don't you come join me in the sky?"

The crab was so surprised, but he said yes. He started springing toward the bird, and in no time he was up in the sky. He was so high up, yet he felt safe and he was having so much fun!

The crab and the bird spent the whole day flying around together. When it was time to go back home, the crab said goodbye and thanked the bird for the adventure. The crab knew that this was one day he'd never forget.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Mia. Mama and Mia went to get some paper, pencils and crayons. Mama said, "Mia, let's write something!" So Mia started to write.

Mia drew a rocket with happy stars. She was so excited and took the picture to show Mama. Mama smiled and said, "What a good rocket you made!" Mia was happy and proud.

One day, Mia went to school and showed her picture to her teacher. Her classmates saw the picture too and started to laugh. Mia felt embarrassed.

Mama came to pick Mia up and asked what happened. Mia told Mama that they laughed at her picture. Mama hugged her and said, "That was kind of them. But don't worry, everyone makes mistakes and that's what makes us unique."

Moral of the story: You don't have to be perfect to be unique. Everyone makes mistakes and that's okay.

Sam was a thoughtful three year old. He liked to look out of his bedroom window and give a friendly wave to the people who walked past in the street. One day, Sam asked his mom if he could open the window. His mom smiled and said she would permit the window to be opened.

When Sam opened his window, he heard a cheerful tune coming from the house across the street. Sam leaned closer and tried to listen to the music. He could eventually make out gentle singing and a violin playing. Sam was mesmerised by the beautiful music.

The music stopped and Sam saw a woman standing in the window opposite. She noticed Sam listening in and began to laugh. She waved and said, â€œHello little one! Thank you for coming to listen to my music.â€ Sam waved back and was filled with joy.

Moments like these made Sam feel thankful for his thoughtful mom, who permitted him to open the window and listen to the wonderful music on the other side.

Once upon a time, there was a kind man who loved to help others. He had a big heart and always shared his toys and treats with his friends. One day, he found a lost puppy and took him home. The puppy was very happy and grateful to have a new home.

The man noticed that his flashlight's battery was low and needed to be changed. He went to the store and bought a new battery. When he got home, he put the new battery in the flashlight and it worked perfectly. He was happy to have gained a new battery.

The man was very generous and decided to give his old flashlight to his friend who didn't have one. His friend was very happy and thanked him for his kindness. The man was glad to have helped his friend and gained a new friendship.

Once upon a time, there was a little mouse named Timmy. Timmy was very curious and loved to explore. One day, he found himself in a big maze. He started to walk around and soon got lost. Timmy was worried and didn't know what to do.

Just then, he saw two big cats fighting. They were making loud noises and Timmy was scared. But then he had an idea. He ran towards the cats and made a lot of noise too. The cats got scared and ran away. Timmy was very happy that he had scared the cats away.

From that day on, Timmy learned that even though he was small, he could still be brave and do big things. He also learned that it's important to help others in need, just like he helped the cats.

Tom and Sam are friends. They like to play with cars and blocks. One day, they go to a party. The party is for Tom's cousin, Lily. Lily is four years old. She has a nice cake and many toys.

Tom and Sam wear nice suits to the party. They want to look good for Lily. But they also want to play with the toys. They see a big train set and a doll house. They run to the toys and start to play.

"Be careful with your suits," Tom's mom says. "They are new and clean. Don't make them dirty or tear them."

Tom and Sam nod. But they forget to be careful. They play too rough with the toys. They spill juice on their suits. They rip their suits on the train tracks. They make their suits dirty and messy.

"Look at your suits!" Lily says. "They are not nice anymore. They are ugly and bad. You are not nice friends. You are rude and mean. Go away from my party!"

Tom and Sam feel sad and ashamed. They say sorry to Lily and to Tom's mom. They remove their suits and put on their old clothes. They learn a lesson. They learn that they should respect their clothes and other people's toys. They learn that being nice is more than wearing nice suits.

Sara and Ben were playing in the kitchen. They wanted to make a cake for Mommy. Sara found a big bowl and some eggs. Ben found some flour and some sugar. They put everything in the bowl and mixed it with a spoon.

"Let's choose an apron," Sara said. "We don't want to get dirty."

They looked at the aprons hanging on the wall. There were many colors and patterns. Sara liked the pink one with flowers. Ben liked the blue one with cars.

"I want this one," Sara said, pointing to the pink apron.

"No, I want this one," Ben said, pointing to the same apron.

They both reached for the apron and pulled it. The apron ripped in half. Sara and Ben were sad. They dropped the apron and looked at each other.

"I'm sorry, Sara," Ben said.

"I'm sorry, Ben," Sara said.

They hugged and said they were sorry. Then they looked at the other aprons. They found a yellow one with stars. They liked it.

"Let's share this one," Sara said.

"OK, let's share," Ben said.

They put on the yellow apron and smiled. They finished making the cake and put it in the oven. They hoped Mommy would like it. They were happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a great watch that she loved to wear. One day, Lily was playing in the park when she met a little boy named Max.

Max said, "Can I please see your watch?"

Lily replied, "Yes, you can see my great watch."

Max looked at the watch and said, "Wow, it's so pretty!"

Lily smiled and said, "Thank you! I love my watch."

Max then asked, "Can I please play with you?"

Lily happily said, "Yes, let's play together!" And they played in the park all day long.

Once upon a time, there was an enthusiastic little girl named Lila. She loved to explore new places and discover something new. 
One day, Lila's mommy let her explore a factory. Lila was so excited! She quickly ran around, touching all the buttons and gadgets. She felt like she was in a giant playground!

Lila soon found a big, shiny machine. She clapped her hands in delight and kept pushing the buttons. Another machine started to whirr and hum. Lila grabbed a big, wobbly wheel and tried to turn it. Suddenly, the wheel moved and the machine began to work.

Lila was so proud of herself! With a happy smile on her face, she let her mommy take her home. From then on, she remembered her adventure in the factory and felt so proud of herself.

Once upon a time, there was a clumsy fish. He swam around in the deep, blue ocean, searching for something tasty.

He saw a rock and decided to give it a try. But the rock was not tasty. He sighed and kept looking.

Then, he noticed a crab scurrying beneath him. He asked the crab, â€œDo you know where I can find something tasty?â€ The crab replied, â€œYes! Swim to the coral reef and you will find something yummy.â€

So the fish swam over to the coral reef and saw many delicious treats. He gobbled them up and released a big, satisfied burp.

The fish was thankful for the tasty treat and asked the crab, â€œCan you help me find food like this again?â€

The crab replied, â€œYes! Just ask me whenever you are feeling hungry. But be careful because the ocean can be dangerous.â€

The fish thanked the crab and continued his journey through the ocean. He was happy to have learned he could find yummy treats if he asked the crab.

Once there was a man who loved to perform. He bought a big expensive gun to use in his shows. It was shiny and made a loud sound that excited the audience.

One day he practiced with his gun at home, but he was too close when he shot it. Suddenly he felt a sharp pain in his hand. He went to the doctor and found out that he had injured himself. The doctor told him he needed to be more careful when he performed.

The man took the doctor's advice and performed more safely. He was a star in his shows and everyone loved the gun. They were amazed when he did the trick with the gun.

The man learned a valuable lesson that day. He was happy he was able to perform without hurting himself again.

Once upon a time there was a neat little boy called Joe. Joe loved melons - he thought they were yummy! One day, Joe saw a huge melon sitting in his garden. It seemed to have come from nowhere! Joe wanted to try it, so he picked it up and took a bite. It tasted amazing!

Joe was very careful, so he put the melon back in the garden and made sure he had left it in a tidy spot. Even though he wanted to eat more, he resisted because he was a nice, tidy boy.

The next day, Joe went back to the garden and looked for the melon. But it wasn't there! It seemed like it had grown wings and flown away! Joe was disappointed. He would never get to try it again! But he was still proud that he had been so tidy and not taken more than he should.

Once upon a time there was a boy called Peter. Peter wanted to show off his special potato to his friends. He was very proud and excited to show everyone. 

Peter took his potato to school one day to show all his friends. When his friends saw it, they were so impressed. 

"Wow, that's a really big potato, Peter!" said one of his friends.

"Yes," said Peter proudly, holding up his potato. "I grew it myself."

But one of Peter's friends, Tim, was feeling jealous. He didn't think Peter should show off his potato like that and he wanted to show off his own special thing. 

"That's nothing special," said Tim, pouting.

"Yes it is," said another friend, defensively. "It's an amazing potato, Peter should display it proudly."

All the friends agreed. Peter smiled, feeling happy, and proudly displayed his potato to everyone.

Once upon a time, there was a small boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside in the garden. One day, he found a small beetle crawling on a leaf. He picked up the beetle and showed it to his mom.

"Look, Mommy, I found a small beetle!" Timmy said.

His mom smiled and said, "Be careful, Timmy. Beetles can bite."

Timmy put the beetle back on the leaf and tasted the sweet strawberries growing in the garden. Later that day, he went back to the garden and saw that the beetle had eaten all of the strawberries!

"Oh no, the beetle ate all the strawberries!" Timmy said.

His mom laughed and said, "That's what happens when you leave beetles alone in the garden." Timmy learned his lesson and made sure to keep an eye on the beetles from then on.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play and learn together. Today, they have math class with Miss Lee. Miss Lee is nice and teaches them how to count and add.

Anna and Ben sit on the floor with some blocks. They make towers and groups of blocks. Miss Lee asks them, "How many blocks do you have in this group?" Anna and Ben count the blocks and say the number.

"Good job, Anna and Ben!" Miss Lee says. "You are good at math. Can you add two more blocks to this group? How many blocks will you have then?"

Anna and Ben nod and reach for two more blocks. But Ben slips on a crayon and falls down. He drops the blocks and they scatter on the floor. Ben hurts his knee and starts to cry.

"Oh no, Ben!" Anna says. "Are you okay?" She runs to him and gives him a hug.

Miss Lee comes to help Ben. She picks up the crayon and the blocks. She says, "I'm sorry, Ben. You slipped on this crayon. It was an accident. Let me see your knee. It's just a little scratch. I have a band-aid for you."

She puts a band-aid on Ben's knee and smiles. She says, "There, you're all better. Do you want to try again?"

Ben sniffles and nods. He says, "Yes, please. I like math. And I like Anna. She is my friend."

Anna smiles and says, "I like you too, Ben. You are my friend. Come on, let's finish our math."

They go back to the floor and find their blocks. They add two more blocks to their group and count them. They say the number and Miss Lee claps.

"Very good, Anna and Ben!" Miss Lee says. "You are smart and kind. I'm glad you are in my class."

Anna and Ben are glad too. They like math and they like Miss Lee. But most of all, they like each other. They are happy friends.

One day, a mom and her daughter went to the beach. The sun was shining, and the water was deep and blue. The daughter loved to play in the sand and the mom loved to watch.

Then, they found an ornament in the sand. It was a pretty shell with colorful stripes.
The daughter picked it up, and the mom said "Let's wash it in the sea!" Together they took it to the water and washed it in the waves.

The daughter loved it and kept it in her pocket. Then they went back to the beach and made a sandcastle.
They stayed and played until the sun went down. 

The little girl took her ornament home and placed it on her dresser. From then on, she thought of the beach every time she looked at it, and it always reminded her of the day she and her mom washed it in the deep blue sea.

Once upon a time, there was a kid named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys and do silly dances. But Timmy's mommy didn't have a lot of money, so she could only buy him cheap toys. Timmy didn't mind though, because he loved all of his toys the same.

One day, Timmy's mommy took him to the park to play with other kids. Timmy saw a big red ball that he really wanted to play with, but the other kids wouldn't let him. Timmy felt sad and didn't know what to do. But then, his mommy came over and asked the other kids if Timmy could play with the ball. The other kids said yes, and Timmy was so happy!

From that day on, Timmy learned that it doesn't matter if your toys are cheap or if you don't have a lot of money. What's important is having fun and being kind to others.

Once upon a time there was a little girl. She was three years old, and her name was Lucy. Every day Lucy enjoyed playing with her toys and her pet shrimp. She was such a happy girl!

One night, Lucy asked her mom if she could bring her pet shrimp to bed with her. She really wanted to cuddle with it while she slept. Her mom was worried the shrimp might fall off the bed, but she said ok and watched as Lucy put her pet shrimp in her bed.

After some giggles, Lucy finally fell asleep. She was so quiet and peaceful. In the morning, Lucy awoke to find that her pet shrimp was gone! She began to look around, but she couldn't find it anywhere.

Suddenly, Lucy's mom entered the room carrying a plate. On it were several tasty shrimp! Lucy smiled and thanked her mom for the tasty surprise. It was then that she realized that the shrimp she had been cuddling with the night before had been her mom's surprise all along!

Andy was playing outside one day with his teddy bear. He went wandering around the yard and soon came across something odd. Andy saw a weird little lizard! He was surprised and excited to find it. 

Andy clapped his hands and said, "What a great find!"

The lizard looked up and said, "Hi, I'm a lizard. What's your name?"

Andy smiled and said, "My name is Andy. What's your name?"

The lizard said, "I don't have a name. Can you think of one for me?"

Andy smiled again and said, "Let's call you Larry the Weird Lizard!"

Larry the Weird Lizard smiled and said, "I like that name! Thanks, Andy. I think we are going to be good friends!" 

And from then on, Andy and Larry were the best of friends. They had lots of fun together in the summer days, playing and exploring the yard.

Molly and her dad were out at the beach. It was a hot summer day, and the sun was shining bright. Molly wanted to take a bath in the ocean.

Molly's dad said, "Molly, it's too difficult for you to bathe in the ocean. You're only three years old. We'll save that for next summer."

Molly was very disappointed. She wanted to try it right that day. Still, she reluctantly agreed.

That night, Molly couldn't sleep. She was so excited to go into the ocean that she thought up a plan. In the morning, while her dad was cooking breakfast, Molly snuck out of the house. She ran to the beach, where she jumped in the water and started to bathe.

But the ocean was too deep for her! She had no idea that the neck of the ocean was so difficult. The waves slammed Molly up against the rocks. Before Molly knew what was happening, she was pulled under the water.

Molly never came back up. She had been so excited to go into the ocean, she didn't think carefully enough. By not listening to her dad, Molly made a mistake that cost her her life.

There was once a boy who was 3 years old. His name was Davey. Davey lived in a small village where all the streets were very quiet and peaceful. One day, Davey wanted to improve the street. He asked his parents if they could help him and they said yes.

So they all started to work and they made the street very nice. Davey got a big shovel and he dug a lot of holes in the ground. His dad put big heavy rocks in the grounds to make the street stronger and smoother. His mum helped to paint the rocks different colors. Everyone worked very hard and it was a lot of fun.

When it was finished, the street looked very different to how it was before. It looked brighter, stronger and smoother. Everyone was so happy with how it had improved and they all celebrated together. Davey had done a great job and he was very proud of himself. 

The street was now a much better place and everyone was very pleased. The villagers all said that Davey was a clever boy for working so hard to improve the street.

One sunny day, Ben and his family went to the farm. They wanted to pick some delicious strawberries. As they walked through the farm, they saw many friendly animals. Ben was so happy to see them.

They soon found a patch of strawberries. Ben couldn't wait to start picking. He got to work and soon he had filled a big basket with strawberries.

The strawberries were so sweet and juicy. Ben smiled happily as he saw how much he had yielded. 

His parents were happy too and praised how much Ben had picked. They made the delicious strawberries into jam, juice and pies.

Ben was so proud of himself that day. He had yielded a lot with his little hands.

Ben and Lily were twins who liked to learn new things. They went to a big place with many books and pictures called a museum. There, they saw many interesting things, like dinosaurs, stars, and paintings.

One day, they saw a man talking to a group of people near a big skeleton. He was giving a lecture about the bones and how they belonged to a giant animal that lived long ago. Ben and Lily wanted to listen, but they were too small to see or hear well.

"Let's go closer," Ben whispered to Lily. "Maybe we can learn something."

"OK," Lily agreed. "But be quiet. We don't want to bother the man or the people."

They tiptoed closer to the front, but they still could not see the skeleton very well. They saw a small stool near the wall and decided to climb on it. From there, they had a better view of the bones and the man.

The man was saying something about teeth and claws and how the animal used them to hunt and eat. Ben and Lily found it very interesting and wanted to know more. They started to discuss what they heard in low voices.

"Wow, look at those teeth!" Ben said. "They are so big and sharp!"

"I know," Lily said. "And those claws! They must have been very strong and fast!"

"Do you think they were scary?" Ben asked.

"Maybe," Lily said. "But maybe they were also friendly to each other."

The man heard them and smiled. He stopped his lecture and walked over to them. He asked them their names and what they thought of the skeleton. Ben and Lily told him what they discussed and asked him more questions. The man answered them kindly and showed them some pictures and models of the animal. He told them it was called a Tyrannosaurus rex, or T-rex for short.

Ben and Lily were very happy and thanked the man for his lecture. They learned a lot of new things and had fun. The man was happy too and told them they were very smart and curious. He invited them to come back anytime and see more interesting things at the museum. Ben and Lily nodded and said they would. They waved goodbye to the man and ran to find their mom and dad. They wanted to tell them all about the T-rex and the lecture.

Once upon a time, a little girl named Lily went to the park with her mom. Lily saw a rat and she felt scared. 

"Mommy, what is that?" Lily asked, pointing at the rat.

"That's a rat, sweetie," her mom replied.

Lily was curious and wanted to know more about the rat. She asked her mom if they could go closer to the rat. 

Her mom said, "Sure, but be careful." 

As they got closer, the rat ran away and surprised them. 

Lily laughed and said, "That rat is silly!"

Once there was a little girl. Her name was Jane. One day when Jane was walking, she saw a big sign that said "Happy Club". She was curious, so she entered.

Inside, the club was full of children. They were all laughing and playing together. It seemed like so much fun! Jane wanted to join in, so she smiled and waved at everyone.

Then, a man came out from behind the counter. He was the Happy Club leader! He told everyone that it was time to start the game. Everyone got excited and followed him to the playing area.

Jane was so happy. She had never seen anything like this before! She joined in the game, and had lots of fun. Soon, she was one of the happiest people in the whole club. 

At the end of the day, Jane was sad to leave. But she promised herself she would come back and play at the Happy Club again!

John was a happy little boy. He loved to play with his toy car. He had lots of fun pushing it around the house.

John had a new toy car with four big wheels. He wanted to have a race. He grabbed the car and ran outside. 

John took the car to a big hill. He rolled the car down the hill. It made a loud noise as it went down. John was so excited.

John started to run down the hill after his car. He was running so fast that he fell down. He rubbed his knee to make it feel better.

John looked around and saw a calm lake nearby. He jumped into his car and drove it calmly around the lake. He was having a great time.

"Wow," said John. "Driving my car around this lake is so much fun!"

Charlie and Zoe were the best of friends. Zoe admired Charlie because he was so reliable. They often played together in the garden.

One day, Charlie had an idea. He suggested they explore an old abandoned house at the end of their street. Zoe was excited but a bit scared. Charlie reassured her: "It will be fine, I'm sure of it".

So, the two friends ventured into the house. They were amazed by all the wonderful things they discovered. Old paintings, statues and furniture filled the rooms. They admired all the things in the house for hours.

Finally, when it was time to leave, Charlie said something that made Zoe admire him even more. He said: "You have a really good brain, Zoe. It was our brains that showed us the wonders of this house". With that they left the old house, remembering the wonderful things they had found and understanding the value of their reliable brains.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys in the garden. One day, she found a lime on the ground. It was green and round, just like a ball. She picked it up and showed it to her mom.

"Mommy, look what I found!" she said.

Her mom looked at the lime and said, "Oh no, Lily! That lime is bad. It's not good to eat."

Lily was sad to hear that. She didn't want to eat the lime, but she wanted to play with it. So, she decided to drop it on the ground and watch it bounce. She dropped the lime and it bounced high in the air. She laughed and clapped her hands.

From that day on, Lily always looked for limes in the garden. Even though she couldn't eat them, she loved to play with them and drop them on the ground.

One day, a boy and a girl went to the park with their mom. They saw a big hill and wanted to climb it. Mom said, "Be careful, it is very high and steep. Do not go too far."

The boy and the girl nodded and ran to the hill. They started to climb, but the hill was hard and slippery. The boy slipped and fell. He hurt his knee and cried. The girl helped him up and said, "Are you okay? Let's go back to mom. She will make it better."

The boy shook his head and said, "No, I want to reach the top. I am not a baby. You are a baby. You are scared." He wiped his tears and climbed again.

The girl sighed and followed him. She was not scared, but she was worried. She did not want to make mom angry or sad. She looked up and saw a thick mist on the top of the hill. She could not see anything. She said, "Look, there is mist. We cannot see. It is not safe. Let's go back."

The boy shrugged and said, "I do not care. I want to see what is behind the mist. Maybe there is something cool. Maybe there is a dragon or a castle or a treasure. You are foolish. You do not have fun."

The girl felt hurt and angry. She said, "You are foolish. You do not listen. You do not care. You are mean. I do not want to play with you." She turned around and ran down the hill.

The boy did not care. He reached the top of the hill and looked behind the mist. He saw nothing. Only more mist and more hills. He felt cold and lonely. He wished he had listened to his sister and his mom. He wished he had not been so rude and stubborn. He wished he had someone to play with. He realized he had been foolish. He cried and ran down the hill. He hoped his sister and his mom would forgive him. He hoped they would still love him. He hoped he would learn to be kind and smart.

It was a quiet day outside. The sun was shining and the sky was blue. All of a sudden, it started to rain. The rain was loud and it lasted for a long time. After a while, the sky cleared up and the sun came back out. The rain had made everything wet.

The wind picked up and it started to blow. Everything was getting drier and drier until it was all dry. Even the grass and the leaves were dry. The air was quiet and calm again.

The sun shone brightly in the sky and everyone was happy. It was nice to feel the warmth of the sun after the rain. People were relieved that the rain had stopped and that everything was dry again.

One day, a boy called Jack arrived in a big sack. He was a bit frightened as he didn't know where he was. Everywhere he looked was unknown. Suddenly, he heard a voice. It was a friendly voice and it said "Hello Jack! Welcome to your new home!" Jack was so relieved - it was his friend Mali. She had come to pick him up from somewhere unknown and take him to his new home. Jack felt so happy and excited! He said goodbye to the unknown place and followed Mali to his new home. It was filled with new friends, toys and fun things to do. Jack had never been so happy. He had arrived at his new home and this was the start of his amazing new adventure.

One day, a mommy, daddy, and a little girl named Clara went to the park. Clara was very excited and she couldn't wait to play. When they arrived at the park, Daddy told Clara to stand in front of a bright yellow taxi. 

The taxi was unique! Nobody else had one just like it. Clara was excited to be standing in front of such a cool taxi. She ran all around it, trying to see every part of it. 

Soon, Daddy opened the taxi door and invited Clara to get inside. But it wasn't a regular taxi! It was a special taxi. A taxi for the sky! It was really cool - Clara had never been on one before. 

Daddy and Clara waved goodbye to Mommy as their taxi flew into the sky. What a magical and unique experience! They flew high in the sky until they arrived back home. Clara felt very proud of her unique adventure.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy was scared of monsters. He always heard loud noises at night that made him scared. One day, Timmy's mom gave him a big chocolate cake. Timmy was so happy! He wanted to eat the whole cake by himself, but his mom told him that it would spoil his dinner. Timmy was sad, but he listened to his mom. Later that night, Timmy heard a loud noise coming from his closet. He was so scared that he hid under his blanket. But then he remembered the cake his mom gave him. He got out of bed, grabbed a slice of cake and went to his closet. When he opened the door, he saw a monster! The monster was scary, but Timmy wasn't scared anymore. He offered the monster a slice of cake and they became friends. From that day on, Timmy wasn't scared of monsters anymore.

Once upon a time, there was a little dog named Jack. He was very curious and loved exploring the world. One day, Jack decided to go for a walk. He strolled down the street and saw a brick. It looked so interesting! He decided to stop and take a closer look. 

Jack sniffed the brick and pushed it a few times with his nose. Suddenly, the brick started to move and Jack jumped back in surprise. What was happening? It was magical! The brick was actually rolling away! Jack was so amazed that he started to follow it.

Jack followed the brick for many blocks. He kept trying to catch up with it, but it was too fast for him. After a while, the brick finally started to slow down. It stopped in front of a park. Jack had never been in the park before, but he was excited to explore. 

Jack ran into the park and never forgot the exciting day he had, exploring with the mysterious rolling brick.

Once upon a time, there was a perfect woman. She had long hair that flowed in the wind. She was walking in a big park on a sunny day.

Suddenly, she heard a little voice. It was a 3 year old girl.
"Hi! Can I walk with you?" asked the girl. 
The woman smiled and said, "Yes, of course you can."

The woman and girl walked slowly, through the park. The girl was so excited to have a friend. She asked the woman all kinds of silly questions as they walked. 

The woman thought the girl was so perfect. They talked and laughed and even picked some pretty flowers together. 

Finally, the woman said, "It's time for me to go home now little one." 
The girl said, "Bye, it was nice to walk with you!" 

The woman waved, as she walked away, with a warm smile on her face.

Once there was a boy named Sam. He was three years old, and he loved to play games. One day, his parents brought him a trophy from the store. It was colorful and shiny, and it excited Sam very much. 

He decided to hold it and practice his balance. He leaned back and forth, rocking the trophy. Then he leaned to one side and felt himself falling. His parents ran over to help. 

Sam felt a bit embarrassed, but he was also excited to keep playing. He leaned a little farther each time he tried, until finally he was able to keep the trophy balanced for a good few seconds. 

Sam was so proud of himself. His parents hugged and praised him, telling him how good he was at balancing. Sam felt spoiled and on top of the world. He knew he would treasure his trophy forever!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play on the beach with his mom and dad. One day, Timmy saw a jellyfish on the sand. He thought it was pretty, but he didn't know what it was. 

"Mommy, what's that?" Timmy asked, pointing at the jellyfish. 

"That's a jellyfish, Timmy," his mom said. "But be careful, jellyfish can sting you." 

Just then, a bossy seagull swooped down and tried to eat the jellyfish. 

"No!" Timmy yelled. "Don't eat the jellyfish! I'll save it!" 

Timmy carefully picked up the jellyfish and carried it back to the water. He gently placed it in the waves and watched as it swam away. 

"Good job, Timmy," his dad said. "You saved the jellyfish." 

Timmy smiled, happy to have helped the little creature. From that day on, Timmy always kept an eye out for jellyfish on the beach.

Once upon a time there was a girl named Lola. She really loved playing outside and spending time with her friends. One day, Lola asked her mom if she could go to the park with her friends. Her mom said yes but she had to be careful. She was not allowed to go too far.

Lola was excited, so she grabbed her kite and a string, and off she went. She had a wonderful time in the park. The sun was shining, the birds were singing, and the flowers were so charming.

Just then, Lola had an idea. She motioned for her friends to help her try to fly the kite. They found a big open space and each held onto a corner of the kite. As Lola released the string, the kite went up and up. They were so happy to see it fly in the sky. 

After a while, it was time to go home. Lola thanked her friends for all the fun and promised to come back with her kite another day. Her mom was very happy to see her, and promised to permit Lola to fly her kite at the park again soon. 

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a toy that she loved very much. One day, her friend Emma came over to play. Emma saw the toy and said, "I want it. Can I have it?" Lily said, "No, it's mine."

Emma got jealous and said, "I don't want to play with you anymore." Lily felt sad but she didn't want to give her toy away. Emma went home and told her mom that Lily wouldn't permit her to play with the toy.

The next day, Lily's mom took her to the store to buy a new toy. Lily saw a toy she really liked but it was too expensive. Her mom said they couldn't afford it. Lily felt sad and wished she had given her toy to Emma.

The moral of the story is that being kind and sharing is more important than keeping things for yourself.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily was very sleepy because it was late at night. She looked at the clock and saw that it was almost midnight. She knew she had to go to bed soon.

Lily's mommy came into the room and said, "Lily, it's time for bed. Be careful not to trip on any toys on the floor." Lily yawned and rubbed her eyes. She got into bed and closed her eyes.

Suddenly, Lily heard a loud ticking noise coming from the clock. She opened her eyes and saw that the clock was glowing. It was magical! The clock started to spin and Lily felt like she was flying. She saw all sorts of amazing things before finally falling asleep. From that day on, Lily always looked at the clock before going to bed, hoping it would take her on another adventure.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and pick flowers. One day, she saw a big sunflower in the garden. It was as tall as her daddy! 

Lily asked her mommy, "Can I pick the sunflower?" 

Her mommy replied, "No, it's too big for you to manage. Maybe we can take a picture with it instead." 

Lily was sad, but she agreed. As they took the picture, they noticed the ground was icy. Lily's mommy held her hand tightly so she wouldn't slip. 

After the picture, they went inside to warm up. Lily felt happy that she got to see the big sunflower, even though she couldn't pick it.

Once upon a time there was a girl. Her name was Anna. She lived in a big house with her mom and her dad.

One day, Anna wanted to go to the zoo. But she had to get ready first. She put on her shoes and her coat. Then her mom gave her a wallet. It was red and had glitter on it. It made Anna very happy.

At the zoo, Anna saw all sorts of animals. She saw a tiger, an elephant, and a giraffe. She was so excited!

When it was time to go, Anna remembered her wallet. She looked in her pocket and it was still there. She was glad it was easy to remember. 

The family went home, and Anna put the wallet in a safe place. She would never forget it!

Mama and baby were walking along the beach. The sun was out and the waves were crashing onto the shore. Baby was so excited to explore.

Mama smiled and said, "Let's look for seashells." She gave baby a net and said, "See if you can find some."

Baby was so eager, she started searching immediately. But she was very, very tired. She sat down and all of a sudden, the net began to disappear! Baby looked all around, but it was nowhere in sight.

Mama knew exactly what had happened. She told baby, "Look in the water, it must have gone in there."

Sure enough, baby spotted her net in the waves and quickly pulled it out. Mama gave her a big hug, proud of how resourceful she had been.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Jane. Jane wanted to go out and wander around the park. 

So she put on her shoes and went outside. She wandered around and around, looking at all the trees and animals.

Suddenly, she saw a huge pile of sugar in front of her. The sugar was organized in almost perfect piles. Jane was so excited she ran over and started playing in the sugar.

Suddenly, a voice said, "What do you think you're doing?". Jane was so startled she turned around to find an old lady standing there. 

The old lady said, "Don't you know that's not polite to just wander around and play in someone else's stuff?".

Jane nodded quietly and said, "I'm sorry. I didn't mean to be bad."
