The old lady smiled and said, "It's okay. Just remember to be more organized next time". 

So Jane thanked the old lady and promised to wander around more carefully. Then she went back home happy and full of sugar.

There was a white ball that loved to bounce. It bounced from floor to floor and from room to room, even when no one was around to play with it. 

One day the ball had an idea. It decided to ask for help in finding someone to play with it. It bounced down the hallway and suddenly it heard an encouraging voice. 

Looking over, the ball saw a helpful little girl. She was pointing and saying "That way!" The ball was so excited that it started bouncing as fast as it could in the direction the little girl had indicated. 

Following her advice, the ball eventually found its way into the playroom packed with toys where kids were laughing and having fun. The ball was so happy and was bouncing around so joyfully. 

The little girl had been so helpful. She had found the ball a perfect place to play!

Lila and Ben were playing in the park. They liked to run and jump and slide. They saw a big hill and wanted to climb it. They ran up the hill, but it was hard. They stumbled and fell many times. They got dirty and tired.

"Look, Ben, look!" Lila said. She pointed to the sky. It was orange and pink and purple. It was sunset. It was very pretty.

"Wow, Lila, wow!" Ben said. He liked the colors too. They sat on the hill and watched the sunset. They smiled and hugged.

But they forgot something. They forgot their mom. She was waiting for them at the gate. She was worried and angry. She called their names, but they did not hear her. They were too busy looking at the sunset.

"Where are they? Where are they?" Mom said. She looked around the park. She saw the hill. She saw Lila and Ben. She was not happy.

"Lila! Ben! Come here right now!" Mom said. She walked up the hill. She was not smiling.

Lila and Ben heard Mom. They were scared. They knew they were in trouble. They were foolish. They ran to Mom and said sorry.

"Sorry, Mom, sorry!" Lila and Ben said. They looked down. They felt bad.

Mom hugged them and said, "I'm glad you're safe, but you should not run away like that. You should listen to me. You should come when I call you. Do you understand?"

"Yes, Mom, yes!" Lila and Ben said. They nodded. They understood.

Mom took their hands and said, "Let's go home. It's time for dinner and bed. Maybe tomorrow we can come back and see the sunset again. But only if you behave."

"Okay, Mom, okay!" Lila and Ben said. They walked with Mom to the gate. They learned their lesson. They still liked the sunset, but they liked Mom more.

Once upon a time, there was a poor mom. She drove her car to the store, but had to pause before she went inside. She was worried because she didn't have her driver's license. She didn't know what to do. 

Suddenly, a kind police officer came up to her. He smiled and told her that he could help. He gave her a new license and asked her to be careful when she drove. 

The poor mom was so relieved and grateful. She thanked the officer and drove away, feeling much better. 

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a modern seal. He was always a little bit different from the other seals in the sea. One day, he got a great idea. He wanted to use his flippers to stir up the ocean. 

So, the seal paddled and paddled through the waves. He was stirring up the water so much that it almost felt like a big soup!

The other sea creatures watched the seal stir and wondered what he was doing. Some of them even joined in and started to stir too. They stirred and stirred until the sea was bubbling with excitement.

The modern seal was so happy with what he had done. He had mixed up the sea like a great big bowl of soup! It was now a happy, new place full of life. 

From then on, the modern seal was known as the great stirrer of the sea.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She was very excited to go to her first day of school. She walked into the classroom and saw all the other kids. They looked unknown to her.

Lily sat down at her desk and started to draw a picture. She drew a picture of her dog, Max. Suddenly, a boy came up to her and said, "Hi! My name is Tim. What are you drawing?" Lily said, "I'm drawing my dog, Max." Tim said, "Wow, that's really good! I wish I could draw like that."

Lily smiled and said, "Thanks! I practiced a lot. If you practice too, you can succeed too." Tim nodded and went back to his desk. Lily felt happy that she made a new friend on her first day of school.

Once there was a little girl called Emma who really wanted to help her mom in the kitchen. She asked if she could help cook, but her mom said she was too little.

But then one day, Emma found something that she could help with. She saw her mom cutting some meat and thought that maybe she could help.

So Emma asked her mom, "Can I help cut the meat?"

Her mom was hesitant at first, but then, she smiled and said, "Sure, you can help, Emma, just be very careful because the knife looks sharp."

So Emma carefully held the knife and helped her mom to cut the harmless meat. She was so proud of herself!

Finally, her mom said, "Well done, Emma. You were such a big help! Now let's go and cook it for dinner!"

And so Emma helped to make a delicious dinner for the family and was happy she was able to help.

Once upon a time, there was a smelly skunk named Stinky. Stinky loved to play in the forest and tap his feet on the ground. One day, Stinky met a friendly rabbit named Hoppy. Hoppy asked Stinky if he wanted to play a game of tag. Stinky was excited and agreed to play.

During the game, Stinky accidentally slapped Hoppy with his tail. Hoppy was not happy and told Stinky that it hurt. Stinky felt bad and apologized to Hoppy. Hoppy forgave Stinky and they continued playing.

After the game, Stinky realized that he needed a bath because he was very smelly. Hoppy agreed and helped Stinky find a nearby stream to wash in. Stinky felt much better after the bath and thanked Hoppy for being a good friend. From that day on, Stinky made sure to be more careful with his tail when playing with friends.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Emily. Emily saw something shiny and furry at the store. She asked her mom can she get it. Her mom said it was very expensive and she had to wait. Emily was sad but she waited. 

Finally, Emily's mom said they could get it. Emily was very happy! She got the furry thing and skipped home. When she got home, she saw it was a pink toy cat! Emily loved the toy so much that she kept it forever.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a pet cat named Fluffy. One day, Lily saw a small ant walking on the ground. The ant was very furry and cute.

Lily said to Fluffy, "Look at the ant, Fluffy. It is so furry. I think it is lost."

Fluffy meowed and said, "I think we should help it, Lily."

So, Lily and Fluffy picked up the ant and put it on a leaf. The ant crawled away happily. Lily and Fluffy felt good for helping the furry little ant.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. Every night, she would close her eyes and dream.

In her dreams, she was a brave explorer. She would travel to far away places and go on amazing adventures. She was never scared, and always had lots of fun.

One night, the girl took out a special pen. As she held it, she imagined she was drawing a big picture of her dreams in the night sky. When she was finished, she looked up and saw the dream picture come alive.

The girl could hardly believe her eyes. She watched in quiet amazement until it was time for the sun to come up and the dream to fade away.

The little girl smiled, happy to remember her dream forever. She wished she could go back one day and explore her dream world again.

"What is this strange place?" he sighed.

He heard a voice from inside the igloo.

Kevin stepped inside and saw an old Polar bear sitting in the corner. He was wearing a colorful robe and had a big, friendly smile on his face.

"Welcome, young one," the Polar bear said.

He motioned for Kevin to come closer.

"This is not an ordinary igloo," the Polar bear said. "It is a place of magic. Anything you want can happen here."

Kevin was filled with wonder as he listened to the Polar bear's words. He had never heard of anything like this before.

The Polar bear explained all the wonderful things that he could do with his new magical igloo. Kevin smiled and gave a big sigh of contentment. He was so excited to explore his new world of adventure and magic. He thanked the Polar bear and ventured out of the igloo.

Once upon a time, there was a small boy named Tim. He was only three years old, but he loved to explore. Every day he would go outside and look for new adventures.

One day, Tim heard about a lake nearby. He asked his mom if he could take a visit to the lake and she said "Yes". Then he put on his shoes and grabbed his backpack, and set off on his journey.

When Tim got to the lake, the water looked so clean and sparkly. He started to play around the lake, skipping stones across the lake's surface. After a little while, he noticed something regular and small. He reached into the lake, and brought up a shiny coin! He was so excited and he knew that this was something special he could gain. 

He kept the coin in his pocket as he explored the lake. He looked at the trees, and the little animals around the lake. The lake was a peaceful place and Tim was so happy that he found such a wonderful place to explore. 

When it was time to go home, Tim looked back at the lake and smiled. He knew that he would come back and visit the lake again soon.

Tom and Sue were playing with blocks. They wanted to build a big tower. Tom put one block on top of another. Sue did the same. They worked hard and had fun.

But then, a big dog came. The dog was curious. He wanted to see what Tom and Sue were doing. He came close and sniffed the blocks. He wagged his tail and knocked some blocks down. Tom and Sue were sad.

"Go away, dog!" Tom said. "You are ruining our tower!"

But the dog did not listen. He liked the blocks. He thought they were toys. He picked one up with his mouth and ran away. Tom and Sue chased him.

"Give it back, dog!" Sue said. "We need that block!"

But the dog was persistent. He did not want to give up the block. He ran faster and faster. Tom and Sue could not catch him. They were tired and angry.

They went back to their tower. It was not very big anymore. Many blocks were missing. They felt like giving up.

But then, they had an idea. They looked around and saw some other things. They saw a ball, a hat, a book, and a spoon. They decided to use them to finish their tower.

They put the ball on top of the blocks. They put the hat on top of the ball. They put the book on top of the hat. They put the spoon on top of the book. They made a very funny and colorful tower. They were proud and happy.

The dog came back. He saw the new tower. He was curious again. He wanted to see what Tom and Sue had done. He came close and sniffed the tower. He wagged his tail and knocked the tower down. Tom and Sue were not sad.

They laughed and clapped. They said to the dog, "You are silly, dog! You can have the blocks. We can make a tower with anything!"

The dog was happy too. He licked Tom and Sue and wagged his tail. He played with the blocks and the other things. They all had fun.

The moral of the story is: Be creative and don't give up. You can finish anything with what you have. And sometimes, a silly dog can be a good friend.

Once upon a time, there was a farmer who had a big farm. He had lots of animals like cows, chickens, and pigs. The farmer was always honest and kind to his animals. He fed them every day and took good care of them.

One day, the farmer had to bury a seed in the ground. He dug a small hole and put the seed inside. He covered it with dirt and watered it. The farmer knew that soon a big plant would grow from the seed and he would have more food for his animals.

The farmer continued to work hard on his farm every day. He always made sure to be honest and kind to his animals. And soon enough, the plant grew big and strong, and the farmer had plenty of food to feed his animals. They were all happy and healthy thanks to the farmer's hard work and honesty.

Once upon a time, Anna had a question that she really needed to answer. She asked her mum, but her mum said she had to figure it out herself. Anna was a very stubborn girl and she wouldn't give up easily.

So Anna went outside and asked her friend Lily for help. But even Lily didn't know the answer. Anna was getting very frustrated because she didn't know what to do.

Lily suggested that Anna should ask her neighbour. Anna was hesitant, but decided to try one last time.

As Anna knocked on the neighbour's door, she heard a familiar voice. She hesitantly opened the door and saw her mum on the other side. Anna was surprised to see her mum there and asked her why she was there. Her mum smiled and said that she thought Anna needed her help to answer her question.

Anna was happy that her mum had noticed she was struggling and still wanted to help her. She hugged her mum and thanked her for her help. Anna's mum said she was happy to help, and together they worked out the answer to Anna's question.

Once upon a time, there was a little birdie named Tweet. Tweet loved to fly around and explore nature. One day, Tweet met a new birdie friend named Chirp. Chirp was very anxious because he was new to the area and didn't know anyone.

Tweet wanted to make Chirp feel better, so he started to tease him in a playful way. Chirp started to laugh and soon forgot about his anxious feelings. The two birdies flew around together and had a lot of fun exploring nature.

As they were flying, they saw a big tree with lots of branches. They decided to land on the tree and rest for a while. They looked around and saw all the beautiful flowers and plants. They felt happy and grateful to be able to enjoy the wonders of nature together.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl whose body changed every day. Some days she felt big, and other days she felt small. Every day she felt different.

One day she was so miserable that she wanted to cry. She felt like her body was wrong and wished it would change. She tried to stretch and jump and move, but nothing seemed to work.

Then, the girl's mom came in and said, "I know you are feeling bad and your body is changing, but that's OK. Your body is changing because you are growing and learning new things, and there's nothing wrong with that. It's alright to be different, and you won't always feel so miserable!"

The little girl smiled and hugged her mom. She realized that it was alright to feel different, and that with time, her body would feel better. She was no longer so miserable because she was growing, and nothing bad was happening. From then on, she was happy and excited to see how her body changed each day.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who was very naughty. One day she decided to jump on the sink, even though her mom told her not to. "Please don't jump on the sink," her mom said. But the little girl was too silly and she just ignored her.

Suddenly, the sink broke and all the water started coming out! The little girl was very scared, so she turned to her mom and said, "Please, mom, I'm sorry. I was stupid."

Her mom was very angry and said, "No more jumps on the sink, ok?" The little girl nodded her head and said, "Yes, I won't do it again. I promise." 

Then the mom hugged her little girl and said, "It's ok, I forgive you." 

The little girl was so relieved and happy. From then on, she was always very careful to never jump on the sink again.

Lily and Ben are twins. They like to play with their toys in their room. One day, they find a scale in their closet. It is a big scale that can weigh things.

"Look, Lily, a scale!" Ben says. "Let's weigh our toys and see who has more."

"Okay, Ben, that sounds fun," Lily says. They take out their toys and put them on the scale. The scale has a needle that moves when something is on it.

Lily puts her doll on the scale. The needle moves a little bit. "My doll is light," she says.

Ben puts his truck on the scale. The needle moves a lot. "My truck is heavy," he says.

They take turns putting more toys on the scale. They count how many toys they have. Lily has five toys. Ben has four toys.

"I have more toys than you, Ben," Lily says. "I win!"

"No, you don't, Lily," Ben says. "My toys are heavier than yours. I win!"

They start to argue. They push and pull the scale. The scale falls to the floor. It makes a loud noise. The needle breaks.

"Oh no, we broke the scale!" Lily says. "Mom will be mad at us!"

Ben feels sorry. He hugs Lily. "I'm sorry, Lily. I didn't want to break the scale. It was a reliable scale. It always told us the truth."

"I'm sorry, too, Ben. I didn't want to fight with you. You are my twin. You are my best friend," Lily says.

They hear Mom coming. They hide the scale under the bed. They hope Mom won't find it. They decide to share their toys and play nicely. They love each other.

Once upon a time, there was a king who lived in a big castle. The castle was very lovely with tall towers and a big gate. The king had many helpers who would work for him every day. They would cook food, clean the castle and take care of the king's horse.

One day, the king's helpers decided to build a sandcastle on the beach. They worked hard to make it very big and very lovely. The king saw the sandcastle and was very happy. He said, "This is the most lovely castle I have ever seen!" The helpers were very proud of their work.

After playing at the beach, the king and his helpers went back to the castle. They continued to work and make the castle even more lovely. They added flowers and decorations to make it look even nicer. The king was very grateful for all their hard work. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a big blue bird. The bird was very brave and loved to fly high in the sky. One day, the bird was carrying a big stick in its beak when it accidentally dropped it. The stick fell down and made a loud noise. The bird felt sad and flew down to find the stick. Luckily, a kind rabbit saw what happened and helped the bird find the stick. From that day on, the bird and the rabbit became good friends and went on many adventures together.

Karen was impatient. She wanted to play but it was time to go home. She had a new toy but she couldn't find the battery.

Mommy helped her look. But they couldn't find the battery. Karen's eyes filled with tears.

Then Daddy said, "Let's look in my pocket". And there it was! The battery!

Karen smiled and hugged her Daddy. She was so happy. Then, they went home and Karen played with her new toy. She was no longer impatient.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play with paint. They have many colors of paint. They can make pictures with paint.

One day, they decide to paint the wall. They think it is fun. They do not ask Mom or Dad. They take the paint and brushes and go to the wall. They start to paint.

"Look, Anna, I can make a big sun!" Ben says. He paints a yellow circle on the wall.

"Wow, Ben, that is a nice sun! I can make a flower!" Anna says. She paints a red circle with green lines on the wall.

They paint more and more. They use all the colors. They make a big mess. The wall is full of paint. The paint is wet and smelly.

Mom and Dad come home. They see the wall. They are very angry. They shout at Anna and Ben.

"What did you do? You ruined the wall! You wasted the paint! You made a smelly mess! You are in big trouble!" Mom and Dad say.

Anna and Ben are scared and sad. They cry. They say they are sorry. But Mom and Dad do not listen. They send Anna and Ben to their rooms. They have to clean the wall later. They have no more paint to play with. They have a bad ending.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved playing hide-and-seek with her friends. One day, Lily's favorite toy went missing. She searched everywhere for it but couldn't find it. She felt sad and started to cry.

The next day, Lily's mom gave her a warm hug and told her they would find the toy. Lily didn't believe her but her mom had a plan. She asked Lily's friends to come over and play hide-and-seek again. Lily was excited but also worried she wouldn't find her toy.

As they played, Lily noticed her friends were getting closer and closer to where her toy was hidden. She felt a little nervous but then she heard a scream. One of her friends had found the toy! Lily was so happy and grateful to her mom for helping her find it. From that day on, she never lost her toy again.

There was a healthy town far away. All the people in this town were very friendly.

One day, a little boy named Tom was playing in the town square. He was clapping his hands and dancing around. Everyone stopped what they were doing and watched him.

The little boy saw everyone watching him and said, "Why are you all clapping?" All the people smiled and said, "We are clapping to show how happy we are. Keep dancing and clapping like that."

The little boy smiled and kept clapping. All the people in the healthy town clapped and danced along with him. They were all filled with joy. 

The little boy said, "This is the best day ever!" Everyone smiled and clapped their hands even louder. Tom and all the people in the town kept clapping until the sun went down.

Once upon a time there was a little girl who wanted to go for a walk with her daddy. She was so excited! Daddy said they had to measure how far they could go. So they both got a special stick and they started walking.

They saw some animals, they hearda bird singing, they smelled some flowers. They walked and walked and walked. But then Daddy said it was time to stop. They had measured far enough.

The little girl was happy but also a bit sleepy. So Daddy picked her up and carried her back home. When they got home Daddy tucked her into her bed and kissed her goodnight.

The little girl had a wonderful walk with Daddy. She felt so safe and happy.

Tom and Anna are playing in the park. They see a big dog running after a small cat. The cat is scared and climbs up a tree. The dog barks and jumps, but he cannot reach the cat.

"Look, Anna, the dog is mean and the cat is in trouble!" Tom says.

"Yes, Tom, the cat needs help. Who can help the cat?" Anna says.

Tom thinks hard. He wants to be a hero and save the cat. He sees a long stick on the ground. He picks up the stick and runs to the tree.

"Hey, dog, go away! Leave the cat alone!" Tom shouts. He waves the stick at the dog.

The dog sees Tom and the stick. He thinks Tom is silly and wants to play. He runs to Tom and wags his tail. He tries to bite the stick.

"Tom, be careful! The dog is big and strong!" Anna says.

Tom is scared. He drops the stick and runs back to Anna. The dog chases him and barks.

"Help, Anna, help!" Tom cries.

Anna sees a man walking by. He has a leash in his hand. He is the dog's owner.

"Hey, stop, boy! Come here!" the man says. He calls the dog and puts the leash on him.

"I'm sorry, kids, he is not mean, he is just playful. He likes to chase cats, but he doesn't hurt them. Are you OK?" the man says.

Tom and Anna nod. They are OK, but they are still scared.

"Thank you, mister, you are a hero. You saved us and the cat!" Anna says.

The man smiles. He pets the dog and the cat. The cat comes down from the tree and rubs against the man's leg.

"You're welcome, kids. You are brave and kind. You tried to help the cat. But next time, be careful with dogs you don't know. They might not be friendly. OK?" the man says.

Tom and Anna say OK. They say goodbye to the man, the dog and the cat. They go back to playing in the park. They think they had a big adventure. They think they are heroes too.

Tim and Sue are twins. They like to eat muffins for breakfast. Mom makes them muffins every morning. But today, Mom is sick. Dad has to make the muffins.

Dad is not good at making muffins. He puts too much flour and not enough sugar. He makes the muffins too big and too hard. The muffins look like rocks.

Tim and Sue sit at the table. They see the muffins. They do not want to eat them.

"Yuck!" Tim says. "These are not muffins. These are rocks."

"I don't like them either," Sue says. "They are too big and too hard. They hurt my teeth."

They push the muffins away. They complain to Dad.

"Dad, these are not muffins. These are rocks. We don't want to eat them. We want Mom's muffins. Mom's muffins are soft and sweet and yummy."

Dad feels sad. He tries to make his twins happy. He says, "I'm sorry, Tim and Sue. I know I'm not good at making muffins. But Mom is sick. She needs to rest. Can you please try to eat the muffins? They are not that bad. They have raisins and nuts and cinnamon. They are good for you."

Tim and Sue look at Dad. They see his sad face. They feel sorry for him. They love their dad. They decide to try the muffins.

They take a bite. They chew slowly. They taste the raisins and nuts and cinnamon. They are surprised. The muffins are not that bad. They are a little big and a little hard, but they are also a little tasty.

They smile at Dad. They say, "Dad, these are not rocks. These are muffins. They are not like Mom's muffins, but they are not bad. They are good for you. Thank you for making them."

Dad smiles back. He is happy. He says, "You're welcome, Tim and Sue. You are good twins. You are brave and kind. I love you very much. And I'm sure Mom will love these muffins too. Let's save some for her."

They hug Dad. They finish their muffins. They are full and happy. They hope Mom will get better soon. They hope Dad will make muffins again. But maybe a little smaller and a little softer.

Once upon a time, there was a popular boy named Tom. Tom liked to sort his toys. He had many toys, but his favorite was his trophy. Tom won the trophy in a race. He was very fast.

One day, Tom wanted to show his friends his trophy. He took it to the park. All his friends were there. They were playing and having fun. Tom showed them his trophy. They all liked it.

But then, a big wind came. It blew Tom's trophy away. Tom and his friends tried to catch it. But it was too fast. The trophy was lost. Tom was sad. His friends were sad too. The end.

Once there was a fearful little girl named Ada. She lived in a small village by the sea. One day, Ada was walking by the beach, when she came across a strange copper thing sticking out of the sand. She poked it with her tiny finger and a big roar came from the sea!

Ada was so fearful that she jumped back with a start. But then she heard a voice say, "Hello Ada". She looked around, but she couldn't find who had spoken.

So she poked the copper thing again. When she did, a big creature came out of the sea. It was a giant sea turtle!

Ada was still fearful, but the giant turtle looked friendly. It smiled at her and said, "It's okay, Ada. I won't hurt you. I'm just happy to see you".

Ada smiled back and was no longer fearful. She and the giant turtle became good friends and every day she would come to visit, poke the copper and hear the friendly turtle's voice.

Max was a cheerful boy. He had wings that could help him fly. One day he wanted to try out his wings. He flew around for a long time.

Max flew over the woods, the hills and the fields. He flew high in the sky, close to the clouds. He flew around and around, up and down and all around.

But then he saw something funny. A big bear was doing math! He sat under a tree, counting on his fingers and writing in a book. Max was so surprised.

He flew closer to get a better look. The bear was smiling and he sang a happy song. Max realized that math can be fun.

Max and the bear waved goodbye to each other and Max flew home with a smile on his face.

Once upon a time, there was a little fish named Nemo. He lived in a big ocean with his friends. One day, Nemo wanted to dive really deep to find a shiny rock. He swam down and down until he found it!

When Nemo got back to his friends, he was so excited to show them his shiny rock. But he heard some bad news. One of his friends was feeling weak and needed help. Nemo knew he had to be a good friend and help his friend.

So, Nemo gave his shiny rock to his friend to make him feel better. His friend smiled and felt much better. Nemo felt happy too, because being a good friend is important.

Once upon a time, there was a little spider named Spidey. Spidey lived in a big house with lots of rooms. One day, Spidey saw a big cobweb in the corner of the room. He wanted to clean it up, but he was too small.

Spidey went to his friend, a little mouse named Mickey. "Mickey, can you help me clean up the cobweb?" Spidey asked. "Sure, I can help you," Mickey replied.

As they were cleaning up the cobweb, a big light shone on them. It was the homeowner! The homeowner was frightened when she saw Spidey and Mickey. She didn't like spiders and mice in her house.

The homeowner got angry and sprayed them with bug spray. Spidey and Mickey were very frightened and tried to run away, but it was too late. They both fell to the ground and didn't move anymore. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Mia. Mia loved to eat pasta. One day, she asked her mom to make her some pasta for lunch. Her mom said yes and went to the kitchen to cook.

While her mom was cooking, Mia played with her toys. She was so happy and excited to have pasta soon. After a while, her mom called her to the table. Mia ran to the kitchen and saw a big plate of pasta just for her.

But, oh no! The pasta was spoiled. It did not look or smell good. Mia's mom said they could not eat the pasta. Mia was sad, but her mom promised to make her fresh pasta another day. Mia smiled and hugged her mom, knowing she would have yummy pasta again soon.

Once upon a time, there was a small girl. She had a pencil that she liked very much. One day, she wanted to hang her pencil on the wall. She asked her mommy to help her. Mommy took a small nail and a hammer and hung the pencil on the wall. The girl was very happy to see her pencil hanging on the wall. She smiled and said, "Thank you, mommy!"

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily and her friend Timmy were playing in the park. Suddenly, Timmy dared Lily to go into the old, spooky house at the end of the street. 

Lily was scared because she thought there might be a ghost in the house. But Timmy said he would be loyal and stay outside to make sure nothing bad happened.

"Look, I have a rare candy!" Ben said, holding up a shiny wrapper. "My mom gave it to me for being good."

"Wow, can I have some?" Anna asked, reaching for the candy.

Ben pulled it away. "No, this is mine. You can have a cracker or a carrot."

Anna felt sad. She wanted to try the rare candy. She thought Ben was being mean. She looked at the cooler and had an idea.

She said, "Okay, you can have your candy. But can I have a sip of your juice?"

Ben nodded. He liked his juice. He opened the candy and took a bite. He made a face. It was very sour and bitter. He did not like it at all.

Ben saw that the juice was gone. He felt angry. He wanted some juice. He said, "Hey, that's not fair! You drank all my juice!"

Ben realized that he had been selfish. He felt sorry. He said, "You're right. I'm sorry. I should have shared with you. Do you want to trade? You can have the rest of my candy and I can have a cracker or a carrot."

Anna nodded. She was happy. She said, "Okay, that sounds good. Let's trade. And let's be friends again."

They traded their snacks and hugged. They learned to share and be kind. They enjoyed the rest of their day under the big tree.

Ben and Lily say sorry to each other. They help clean up the mess. They change their dirty clothes. They hug and make up. They are quiet and calm. They do not whistle or throw cereal. They finish their breakfast. They learn their lesson.

"I'm sorry, I love you too."

The little girl was so happy that she had a chance to admire the beautiful bird. Every time she remembered it, she would smile.

Once upon a time there was a little man. He was very curious and he wanted to test everything. One day, he found a yellow bed. He thought it was so pretty! He wanted to test how it felt. He jumped onto the bed and it was so soft! The little man liked it so much he wanted to take a nap. He snuggled up in the yellow bed and soon fell asleep. 

When he woke up he found out he had been dreaming. The little man was sad but then he got an idea. He would test everything else around him so he wouldn't be sad anymore. He found a chair, a toy car, and a big tree. The little man tested each one and was very happy. 

At the end of the day, the little man was very tired. He went back to the yellow bed and happily fell asleep. He was so happy he had found such a cozy place to sleep. In the morning, he tested one last thing. He tested to see if he felt rested and happy. He was very pleased with the result!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to draw with chalk on the sidewalk. One day, she went outside to draw and found that her chalk was all gone. She looked everywhere but couldn't find it. She was sad because she wanted to draw a pretty picture for her mommy.

Just then, her friend Timmy came over. He had some chalk and offered to share it with her. Lily was happy and said thank you. They started to draw together, but then a big dog came by and scared them. They ran away, but Lily accidentally dropped Timmy's chalk and it broke into many pieces.

Timmy was upset and said it was his favorite chalk. Lily felt bad and didn't know what to do. But then she had an idea. She ran to her house and came back with a good idea. She rang Timmy's doorbell and showed him a new box of chalk she had bought for him. Timmy was happy and forgave her. They continued to draw together and had lots of fun. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a chubby cat named Tom. Tom loved to dance. He danced all day and all night. One day, he found a rubber ball. He wanted to dance with it.

Tom tried to dance with the rubber ball, but it was not easy. The ball kept bouncing away from him. He felt sad because he could not dance with the ball. Tom did not give up. He tried again and again.

Finally, Tom found a way to dance with the rubber ball. He put the ball on his head and danced around. The ball stayed on his head while he danced. Tom was happy because he could dance with the rubber ball.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to sit in her soft armchair and read her favorite books. One day, her mom came into the room and asked her if she wanted a snack. Lily said yes and her mom slowly gave her some yummy cookies. 

Lily was happy and enjoyed eating her cookies while sitting in her cozy armchair. She felt very comfortable and didn't want to leave her chair. Her mom smiled and said, "You can stay in your chair as long as you want, Lily." 

Lily was grateful for her mom's kindness and felt very loved. She hugged her mom and said, "Thank you for giving me cookies and letting me sit in my armchair." Her mom hugged her back and said, "You're welcome, Lily. I love you."

Lila and Tom are friends who like to play outside. One day, they find a map in a book. The map shows a big X in the east. Lila and Tom want to find the X. They think it is a treasure.

They take the map and a backpack. They put some snacks and a bottle of water in the backpack. They are very organized. They say goodbye to their moms and start to walk. They follow the map and look for signs.

They see a big tree, a red barn, a yellow bridge and a blue lake. They are on the right path. They are happy and excited. They talk to each other.

"Maybe the treasure is gold or jewels," Lila says.

"Or maybe it is candy or toys," Tom says.

They walk and walk until they see a hill. The map says the X is on the hill. They climb the hill and search for the X. They look under rocks and bushes. They look behind trees and flowers. They look everywhere.

But they cannot find the X. They are sad and tired. They sit on the grass and eat some snacks. They drink some water. They look at the map again.

"Maybe the map is wrong," Lila says.

"Or maybe someone took the treasure," Tom says.

They are about to give up when they hear a voice.

"Hello, children. What are you doing here?"

They look up and see a man. He is wearing a hat and a coat. He has a big smile and a big beard. He is holding a shovel and a bag.

"We are looking for the treasure," Lila says.

"What treasure?" the man asks.

"The treasure on the map," Tom says. He shows the man the map.

The man laughs. He says, "Oh, this is not a treasure map. This is a gardening map. I made it to show where I planted some seeds. The X is where I planted some carrots. They are not ready yet. Do you want to see?"

Lila and Tom are surprised. They say, "Yes, please."

The man takes them to the X. He digs a hole and pulls out a carrot. He gives it to Lila. He digs another hole and pulls out another carrot. He gives it to Tom.

"Here you go. These are your treasures. Fresh and healthy. Enjoy," he says.

Lila and Tom thank the man. They wash the carrots and bite them. They are crunchy and sweet. They are happy and satisfied.

They say goodbye to the man and start to walk back. They still have the map and the backpack. They are very organized. They follow the map and look for signs.

They see the blue lake, the yellow bridge, the red barn and the big tree. They are on the right path. They are happy and excited. They talk to each other.

"Maybe the treasure is not gold or jewels," Lila says.

"Or candy or toys," Tom says.

"Maybe the treasure is something else," they say together.

They smile and hug. They are friends who like to play outside. They have found their treasure.

Once there was a warrior who was looking for a special weapon. He set off on a journey to find this weapon. Along the way he asked many people for help, but no one had what he was looking for.

Then one day he saw a cave in the distance. He decided to rest and investigate. As he walked into the cave, he found a rare weapon at the other end. He was so excited!

The warrior ran back out of the cave to tell his friends about his find. He said, "I've found a rare weapon! I can't believe I found it!"

Everyone was so amazed and happy for him. They cheered and said, "You have found something truly special, warrior! We are so proud of you!"

The warrior took a rest and smiled, knowing that his journey was worth it. He thanked everyone for their kind words and continued on his way with his special weapon.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, she met a nice boy named Jack. They played together and had fun. Jack said to Lily, "I like you a lot. Will you marry me?" Lily felt scared and didn't know what to say. She put her hand on her stomach and thought for a while. Then she said, "I'm not sure. Let's be friends first." Jack smiled and said, "Okay, friends it is!" From that day on, they played together every day and had lots of fun.

Once upon a time, there was a squirrel who lived in a big, wide tree. The squirrel loved to climb and play in the tree all day long. One day, a big bird came and tried to take the squirrel's home away. The squirrel was very scared and didn't know what to do.

But then, the squirrel had an idea! The squirrel climbed up to the top of the tree and grabbed a big acorn. The squirrel threw the acorn at the bird to test if it would scare the bird away. And it worked! The bird flew away and the squirrel's home was safe again.

From then on, the squirrel knew that sometimes you have to test things to see if they will work. And the squirrel lived happily ever after in its big, wide tree.

Allie looked up at the light sky and saw a daisy. She felt happy, so she picked it and smiled. She ran away with the daisy and gave it to her mom. 

But her mom was sad when she saw the daisy. Allie asked what was wrong and her mom told her that picking daisies was wrong. Allie began to feel sad and regret what she had done. 

She ran back to the spot with her mom. Allie sat down in front of the daisy and started to cry. Her mom put her arm around her and said it was okay.

But Allie still felt bad for accidentally picking the daisy. She vowed to never make the same mistake again and now every time she looks at a daisy, she feels a little bit happy and a little bit sad.

Once upon a time, there was a bear called Bill. Bill was very cute and had a charming smile. One sunny day, Bill decided to go for a stroll. He walked to a nearby lake. He stood and watched the water flowing gently down the drain. Then he heard a noise and paused to listen.

Bill turned around and saw a frog sitting by the edge of the lake. The frog said, "Hi!" Bill was very surprised and said, "Hi!"

The frog asked, "Why you pause?" Bill turned red and said, "I pause 'cause I heard the water going in the drain and I wanted to watch." The frog smiled and said, "That's charming!"

Bill and the frog became friends and Bill visited the lake often to play with his new buddy. They laughed and talked and had lots of fun. 

The end.

Little Bo was outside in the rain with her mom. They had gone to the park together and mom had brought them both umbrellas. Bo's umbrella was pink and she loved it. She kept spinning around and looking at the rain drops as they fell. 

Suddenly, Bo heard a funny noise coming from the bush near her. She blinked and saw a small furry thing poking out. She squealed with excitement and ran over to it. 

"Mom!" Bo giggled, "Look what I found!" 

Mom smiled and peeked out from under her umbrella. She asked, "What is it?" 

"It's a wet bunny!" Bo giggled. The bunny shook its head to shake off the water droplets. Bo smiled and picked it up in her arms. "Can I keep it mom?" 

Mom smiled and nodded, "I think it needs a warm home. Let's get it inside and get it some food." 

Bo was so happy. She had made a new friend!

Once, there was a little girl named Lucy. She had a toy chain that she loved very much. It was a pretty chain with many colors. Lucy played with her chain every day.

One day, Lucy saw an icy pond near her house. She wanted to play with her chain on the icy pond. She put on her warm clothes and went outside. She was very excited to play on the ice.

Lucy threw her chain on the icy pond and it slid very fast. She laughed and clapped her hands. Lucy wanted to slide on the ice too, so she ran and slid just like her chain. She had so much fun playing with her chain on the icy pond.

One day, a big, rude dog was in the park. He saw a small, funny cat. The cat was eating a grape. The dog wanted the grape too.

"Give me your grape," said the rude dog. The cat did not want to share. "No, it's mine," said the cat. The dog was angry.

The dog tried to hurry and grab the grape from the cat. But he was too big and clumsy. He fell down and squished the grape. The grape was gone. The dog and the cat were both sad.

Once upon a time, there were two friends walking together in a park. One was very delicate and the other was very strong. They were having a lot of fun together, walking on the path, kicking leaves and laughing. Suddenly, the delicate friend stopped and started to cry. 

Surprised, the strong friend asked, "What is wrong?". 

The delicate friend replied, "I'm scared of getting hurt!"

The strong friend hugged the delicate friend. "It's okay. I will always care for you and make sure no one ever hurts you". 

The delicate friend smiled, feeling safe and happy. They continued to walk on the path, hand in hand, and they knew that no matter what, they would always care for each other.

Lily and Ben are playing in the park. They see a big case on a bench. The case is red and shiny. They are curious.

"What is in the case?" Lily asks.

"Let's find out!" Ben says.

They run to the bench and open the case. Inside, they see many tasty things. There are cookies, cakes, fruits, and juice. They are happy.

"Wow, this is a yummy case!" Lily says.

"Let's eat some!" Ben says.

They take some cookies and cakes and sit on the grass. They enjoy the tasty things. They do not see a man coming to the bench. The man is angry. He is the owner of the case. He was having a picnic, but he went to the bathroom for a moment. He sees Lily and Ben eating his food.

"Hey, you little thieves! Give me back my case!" the man shouts.

He runs to them and tries to catch them. Lily and Ben are scared. They drop the cookies and cakes and run away. They hide behind a tree.

"Sorry, mister, we did not know!" Lily says.

"We thought it was a gift!" Ben says.

The man is still angry. He takes his case and leaves. He does not want to share his food.

Lily and Ben are sad. They liked the tasty things. They wish they had asked first. They learn a lesson. They do not take things that are not theirs. They go home and tell their mom what happened. Their mom hugs them and gives them some milk and bread. They are sorry and hungry. They promise to be good. They hope the man will forgive them. They hope to find a real gift someday.

Tim and Kim are twins. They like to play outside. One day, they find a shiny stone near the river. They want to make it more shiny.

"Let's polish the stone!" Tim says. He takes a leaf and rubs the stone.

Kim nods. She takes another leaf and helps Tim. They rub and rub the stone. But the stone does not get more shiny. It gets dirty.

"Why is the stone not shiny?" Kim asks. She is confused.

Tim is confused too. He looks at the river. He sees the sun on the water. The water is shiny.

"Maybe the water can polish the stone!" Tim says. He runs to the river. He throws the stone in the water.

Kim runs after him. She watches the stone sink in the water. She does not see it anymore.

"Where is the stone?" Kim asks. She is sad.

Tim is sad too. He looks at the water. He does not see the stone. He sees his face. His face is dirty.

"Oh no!" Tim says. He tries to wipe his face with his hand. But his hand is dirty too.

Kim laughs. She sees Tim's face. She sees her face too. Her face is dirty too.

"Let's wash our faces!" Kim says. She splashes water on her face. She splashes water on Tim's face.

Tim laughs. He splashes water on Kim's face. He splashes water on his face.

They wash their faces. They wash their hands. They are clean.

They look at the river. They see the sun on the water. The water is shiny.

They smile. They forget the stone. They play in the water. They are happy.

Once there was a girl who was ready to wake up. She stretched her arms and opened her eyes. Suddenly she smelled something sweet. It was the smell of a fresh peach that was sitting on her bedside table. She was so excited to eat the peach! She grabbed it and bit into it. The sweet, juicy peach was delicious. She ate the whole peach and it made her feel happy and full. It was a perfect way to start her morning. She was ready for the day.

Once upon a time, there was a purple fruit. It floated through the sky and spread far and wide. It landed in a garden, and the fruit split into halves.

The halves of the fruit started to spread. They moved closer and closer together, until they met in the middle. They kept growing until the fruit became a big purple circle.

The purple fruit was so special, it gave off a magical sparkle. Everywhere it touched, the fruit made things grow. Trees, flowers and bushes began to appear.

The garden was now full of purple fruit. Everyone was very happy and shared the fruit with each other. They all enjoyed eating it, and the purple fruit spread lots of happiness.

The end!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a sister named Sarah who loved to swim in the big pool. One day, Lily and Sarah went to the pool. Sarah said to Lily, "Come on, let's swim together!" Lily was scared because she didn't know how to swim. Sarah said, "Don't be serious, I will teach you how to swim."

Sarah held Lily's hand and they jumped into the pool. Sarah showed Lily how to kick her legs and move her arms. Lily was so happy that she learned how to swim. They played together in the pool and had so much fun. When it was time to go home, Lily said, "Thank you, sister, for teaching me how to swim. I love you." Sarah smiled and said, "I love you too, Lily."

Lila and Ben were playing in the snow. They made a big snowman with a hat and a scarf. They gave him a carrot nose and two rocks for eyes. They were very happy with their snowman.

"Look, he is smiling!" Lila said.

"Yes, he is. He likes us," Ben said.

They heard a loud noise. It was a big truck. It was coming fast. It was making the snow fly everywhere. It was coming towards their snowman.

"Oh no! The truck will hit our snowman!" Lila cried.

"Run, Lila, run!" Ben shouted.

They ran away from the road. They hid behind a tree. They watched the truck zoom by. They saw their snowman tremble. They saw his hat and scarf fall off. They saw his nose and eyes fly away. They saw him fall apart.

They were very sad. They had worked hard on their snowman. They loved their snowman. They wanted him to stay.

They looked at the landscape. It was white. It was cold. It was empty. Their snowman was gone.

They hugged each other. They felt warm. They felt safe. They felt not alone.

They decided to make another snowman. They decided to make him far from the road. They decided to make him bigger and stronger. They decided to make him happy.

They smiled. They laughed. They played. They had fun.

Once upon a time, there was an otter who lived in a river. He was a very distant otter, who kept his distance from other animals in the river. He was often alone and didn't like to be disturbed.

One day, he was swimming in the river when suddenly he heard a noise. It was a duck, who was quacking very loudly and trying to get his attention. The otter tried to resist the duck's quacking, but the duck was determined to have a chat. The otter decided to talk to the duck, and they talked and laughed.

The otter and the duck became very good friends. They enjoyed spending time together, talking, playing and swimming in the river. They were never distant again, but close friends forever.

Anna liked cheese very much. She liked to eat cheese with bread, or with fruit, or by itself. She had a big box of cheese in the fridge, and she kept it very organized. She put the cheese in different bags, and wrote the names of the cheese on the bags. She had yellow cheese, white cheese, soft cheese, hard cheese, and many more.

One day, Anna wanted to make a cheese sandwich for lunch. She opened the fridge and looked for her cheese box. But she could not find it. She looked everywhere, but the cheese box was gone. She felt very sad and angry. Who took her cheese box?

She heard a noise from the living room. She ran there and saw her little brother, Ben, sitting on the floor. He had her cheese box, and he was eating her cheese. He had opened all the bags, and mixed all the cheese together. He had cheese on his hands, on his face, and on the floor.

"Ben, what are you doing?" Anna shouted. "That is my cheese! You took my cheese box! You made a big mess! Give it back to me!"

Ben looked at Anna and smiled. He liked cheese too, but he did not care about the names or the bags. He just wanted to taste all the cheese. He did not understand why Anna was so mad.

"Cheese is good," he said. "Cheese is yummy. Come, Anna, have some cheese with me. Cheese is fun!"

Once upon a time, there lived a little girl named Ann. Ann was only three years old, and she loved to smile and laugh.

One day, Ann was playing outside in the yard when she tripped and fell on the ground. She started to cry, as she had hurt her knee.

Just then, a big, roud toad hopped near Ann. He had a big, sharp tooth. Ann was scared and started to cry even more.

The toad said, 'Why are you crying?' Ann told him that she had hurt her knee.

At that moment, Ann's mom came outside and saw what had happened. She scolded the toad and said, 'It's not nice to be so rude to someone.'

Ann learned an important lesson that day: You should always be kind to others, even when you are in pain.

Once upon a time, there was an old dog who loved to play. He would run and jump and wag his tail all day long. One day, a little girl came to visit him and asked him a question. "Do you want to play with me?" she asked. The old dog barked happily and they played together all day.

As the sun began to set, the little girl had to go home. The old dog was sad to see her go, but he knew that she would come back to play again soon. The next day, the little girl came back and they played even more. But this time, the old dog noticed that he was getting tired more quickly than usual.

He realized that he was getting too old to play as much as he used to. From that day on, he made sure to take breaks and rest when he needed to. The little girl understood and they still had fun together, but the old dog knew that he had to take care of himself. And that's the moral of the story - even if you love to play, it's important to take care of yourself when you're feeling tired or old.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play in the water and splash around with her friends. One day, she put on her favorite hat and went to the lake with her mom.

At the lake, Lily met a boy named Max. Max was not very polite and kept splashing water on Lily and her mom. Lily didn't like it, but she didn't say anything because she didn't want to be rude.

Suddenly, Max splashed so much water that Lily's hat fell into the lake. Lily was sad because her hat was her favorite. She tried to get it back, but the water was too deep. Lily and her mom had to go home without her hat, and Lily felt very sad.

From then on, Lily learned to speak up when someone was being rude, so that no one would ever splash her again.

Once upon a time, there was a little dog named Mark. Mark loved to run and play in the mud. One day, after playing, he became very filthy. His fur was full of dirt and mud.

Mark's friend, Cat, saw him and said, "Mark, you are so filthy! Let's get you clean." So, Cat helped Mark wash the dirt and mud off his fur. They splashed water and had a lot of fun.

After they were done, Mark felt tired. He said to Cat, "I need a nap now." So, Mark and Cat found a warm, sunny spot to take a nap together. They closed their eyes and slept, happy to be clean and with a good friend.

Lila and Tom were playing with a big bucket and a small cup. They wanted to fill the bucket with water from the tap. They took turns to hold the cup and run to the tap and back. They poured the water into the bucket and watched it get higher and higher.

"Look, Lila, the bucket is almost full!" Tom said. "Let's fill it to the tip!"

"OK, Tom, but be careful. The bucket is very heavy and the water might spill." Lila said.

Tom nodded and ran to the tap again. He filled the cup with water and ran back to the bucket. He lifted the cup and tried to pour the water into the bucket. But the bucket was too full and the water splashed out. The bucket tipped over and fell on the ground. The water spilled everywhere and made a big puddle.

"Oh no, Tom, what have you done?" Lila cried. "The bucket is broken and the water is gone!"

Tom felt very sad and sorry. He dropped the cup and looked at the mess. He wanted to say sorry to Lila, but he was too scared. He thought Lila would be angry and not want to play with him anymore.

He ran away from the puddle and the bucket and the cup. He ran to his house and hid under his bed. He wished he had been more careful and brave. He wished he had not filled the bucket to the tip. He wished he had not made Lila cry. He wished he had a friend.

Once upon a time, a mommy, a daddy and a little girl named Lily all lived together in a house. Mommy and Daddy had a plan for an amazing day together. They were going to make a yummy treat for Lily with one very special ingredient.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to climb. He climbed trees, walls, and even his bed. Climbing made his muscles strong.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to draw pictures and write stories in her journal. One day, Lily's mommy gave her a new journal with clear pages. Lily was so happy to have a new journal to write in.

Once upon a time there was a family. The family went to the woods to find something special. As they walked through the woods, they saw lots of thick trees.

Once upon a time, there was a broken note. A little girl found it lying in a puddle and wanted to save it. She picked it up, and said to her mum, "Mummy, look! I found a note in the puddle". Mummy told her to put it on the table so it could dry.

One day, a boy named Tim went to the park with his mom. They had to cross a busy road with a lot of traffic. Tim's mom said, "Tim, hold my hand and we will cross the road together." Tim held his mom's hand and they crossed the road.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who loved to crawl. She crawled everywhere. She even gave her stuffed animals piggyback rides. Her mom was totally amazed at how fast she could crawl.
