Once upon a time there was a good baby named Jack. One day he asked his mom for a cookie. His mom said no but Jack still wanted the cookie so he opened the kitchen cabinet. Inside was a big box of cookies and he took one.

Mom quickly saw what Jack had done and she was angry. She knew that Jack had to learn his lesson, so she told him he could not have any more cookies and to put the one he already took back in the cabinet. Jack, feeling sad, put it back inside.

The next day, Jack again asked his mom for a cookie. Mom remembered what he did the day before and she shook her head. She said that she would forgive him if he opened the cabinet and put the cookie back.

But Jack was so sad and angry that he refused. He said he didn't want to put the cookie back and he ran away.

Mom waited and waited but Jack never came back. She sadly realized that sometimes you have to forgive someone if you want them to learn their lesson. If Jack had only forgiven his mother, he would have been able to stay and continue getting good cookies from the cabinet.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to dance all day long. She would dance in her room, dance in the kitchen, and even dance outside in the sun. Dancing made Lily very happy.

One day, Lily saw an expensive dress in a store. The dress was shiny and pretty, just like the ones she saw dancers wear on TV. She wanted to wear the dress for her dance, but she did not understand why it was so expensive.

Lily's mom saw her looking at the dress and said, "Lily, we can make a dress for you to dance in. It will be just as pretty, but not expensive." Lily smiled and hugged her mom. Together, they made a beautiful dress for Lily to dance in. And she danced happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, she went for a walk with her mommy in the park. Lily loved to run and play, but she didn't watch where she was going. Suddenly, she tripped and fell down. 

"Ouch! That hurt!" cried Lily. 

Her mommy helped her up and said, "You need to be careful where you step, sweetie. Look where you're going." 

Lily was grateful for her mommy's help. She gave her a big hug and said, "Thank you, mommy. I'll be more careful next time." 

From that day on, Lily always watched her step and was more careful. She learned that it's important to pay attention to where you're going, so you don't trip and fall.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird named Tim. Tim lived in a dirty cage. He did not like his dirty cage. He wanted to be free and fly high in the sky.

One sunny day, a kind girl named Sue saw Tim in the dirty cage. Sue felt sad for Tim. She wanted to help Tim. Sue had an idea. She would part the cage and let Tim out.

Sue opened the cage and Tim flew out. He was so happy. Tim flew high in the sky. He sang a happy song. Sue smiled and waved at Tim. They both knew they were friends forever.

Lily and Ben were playing in the park. They saw a big, hairy dog. The dog was friendly and wagged its tail. Lily and Ben liked the dog. They wanted to pet it.

"Can we pet the dog?" Lily asked her mom.

"Sure, but ask the owner first," her mom said.

Lily and Ben ran to the owner. He was a nice man with a hat. He smiled at them.

"Can we pet your dog?" Ben asked.

"Of course, his name is Spot," the owner said.

Lily and Ben petted Spot. He licked their faces. They giggled.

"Spot is so soft and warm," Lily said.

"Spot is so big and strong," Ben said.

They had a question. They wanted to know more about Spot.

"Where did you get Spot?" Lily asked the owner.

"I got him from a shelter. He was very sad and lonely there. He needed a home and a friend," the owner said.

Lily and Ben felt sorry for Spot. They were glad he had a home and a friend now.

"What does Spot like to do?" Ben asked the owner.

"Spot likes to run and play and fetch. He also likes to dig and chew and bark. He is very curious and smart," the owner said.

Lily and Ben thought Spot was fun and cool. They wanted to play with him more.

"Can we play with Spot?" Lily asked the owner.

"Sure, but be careful. He has a surprise for you," the owner said.

Lily and Ben wondered what the surprise was. They followed Spot to the grass. Spot started to dig. He dug and dug and dug. He found something. He pulled it out with his teeth. It was a bone.

"Wow, Spot found a bone!" Lily said.

"Spot is a good digger!" Ben said.

They clapped and cheered. Spot wagged his tail. He gave them the bone. They thanked him. They played with the bone and Spot. They had a lot of fun.

The owner watched them. He smiled. He was happy. He thought Spot was lucky. He had a home and a friend. And now he had two more friends. Lily and Ben.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Ann. Ann loved to play outside and look at the clouds. One day, Ann saw a cloud that looked like it needed some color, so she decided to paint it. 

Ann gathered her supplies and went outside to paint the cloud. She took a brush and some paint and began painting. She painted each cloud a different color, green, blue, and yellow. 

Ann added some shapes to each cloud. To the green cloud, she added a circle, to the blue cloud, she added a triangle. When she was finished, she stepped back to admire her work. 

Just then, Ann's mom came outside. "What are you doing," she asked. Ann explained that she was painting the clouds. Her mom said, "Oh, that sounds fun!"

Ann's mom wanted to join in, so she grabbed a brush and some tasty pink paint. Together, Ann and her mom painted the clouds until it was time for dinner. 

Ann and her mom had fun painting the clouds, and the colors looked beautiful in the sunset sky.

Once upon a time, there was a kind boy. His name was Tony and he loved to visit new places. One day, Tony decided to go explore. He hopped on his bike and went to a nearby park.

When he got there, he saw something very interesting: a big open door. Tony said hello and went inside. It was a magical place filled with gorgeous flowers and trees. He saw many animals too, including some friendly ducks.

Tony spent his day playing in the park. He looked at the animals and picked some of the flowers. He even made some flower crowns. He had a fun filled day.

When the day was over, Tony waved goodbye to the park and hopped back on his bike. He was happy that he visited the park and made lots of friends. Tony was a kind boy and he was glad that he was able to explore something new.

Once upon a time there was a honest little flea. One day the flea wanted to climb a very big mountain. So he started to climb and climb and climb.

On the way he met an ant. The ant said, "Hey, little flea, why are you climbing so high?" 

The flea said, "I'm climbing to the top of the mountain"

The ant said, "That's silly, it's too high and much too steep. You can't make it."

The flea did not like being told he couldn't do it. So he kept on climbing and climbing and climbing. After a while the ant said, "Well done. I didn't think you could do it."

The flea was very proud. He made it to the top of the mountain. He was so happy and honest.

Tom and Anna are twins. They like to play with their toys and books. But they do not like to go to bed. Every evening, they complain to their mom and dad.

"Mom, I am not sleepy. Can I read one more book?" Tom asks.

"Dad, I am not thirsty. Can I have some juice?" Anna says.

Mom and dad shake their heads. They say, "No, Tom and Anna. It is time to sleep. You have to be ready for school tomorrow. Brush your teeth and put on your pajamas."

Tom and Anna sigh. They do not want to stop playing. They do not want to go to school. They think it is boring. They walk slowly to the bathroom and the bedroom.

Mom and dad tuck them in. They kiss them good night. They say, "We love you, Tom and Anna. Have sweet dreams."

Tom and Anna close their eyes. They try to sleep. But they still complain in their minds.

"Mom and dad are not fair. They can stay up late. They can watch TV. They can do what they want." Tom thinks.

"Dad and mom are not fun. They make us do homework. They make us eat vegetables. They make us follow rules." Anna thinks.

But soon, they are too tired to complain. They fall asleep. They do not know that mom and dad are also tired. They also have to work. They also have to do chores. They also have to follow rules. They love Tom and Anna very much. They want them to be happy and healthy. They hope they will understand someday.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Claire who liked to watch movies. One day, Claire and her mom were at the store to buy a movie. Claire saw a fun movie that she wanted to get, but her mom said she had to wait.

"Why can't I get it today, Mommy?" Claire asked.

"Well," replied Mommy, "It looks like the movie's a bit too tight to fit in our house. We'll need to weigh it first to make sure it'll fit!"

So Claire and her mom took the movie to the weighing machine. The machine showed that the movie was heavier than Claire thought. Claire was sad.

"Don't worry, Claire," said Mommy. "We can still get the movie! We'll just have to make sure our house fits it first." 

Then Claire and her mom happily went home to check if the movie would fit in their house. In the end, it did fit and Claire was able to finally have her movie!

Sara likes math. She likes to count and add and take away. She has a math book with many pages. She likes to open the book and look at the pictures and numbers.

One day, Sara finds a furry friend in her room. It is a cat. The cat is black and white and has green eyes. The cat is very soft and warm. Sara likes the cat. She wants to play with the cat.

Sara opens her math book and shows it to the cat. She points to the numbers and says them out loud. The cat looks at the book and meows. Sara thinks the cat likes math too. She smiles and hugs the cat.

The cat likes Sara. He likes to listen to her voice and feel her hug. He also likes to look at the book. He sees something shiny on the book. It is a sticker. The sticker is a star. The cat likes shiny things. He wants to touch the sticker.

The cat reaches out his paw and tries to peel off the sticker. He scratches the book and makes a noise. Sara hears the noise and sees the cat. She is not happy. She says, "No, cat! That is my math book! You cannot scratch my math book!"

The cat is scared. He jumps off the bed and runs away. Sara is sad. She likes the cat, but she does not like what he did to her math book. She picks up the book and looks at the sticker. The sticker is still there, but it is torn. Sara sighs and puts the book away. She hopes the cat will come back and say sorry.

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play with blocks and books. They also like to learn new words. One day, they find a big book of spells. It has many pictures and letters.

"Wow, look at this book!" Lily says. "It has spells for magic!"

"Can we do magic?" Ben asks.

"Maybe. Let's try a spell. Here is one for making a flower. It says we need a pot, some dirt, some water, and some seeds. And we need to say the spell."

Lily and Ben get the things they need. They put the dirt in the pot. They make a hole and put the seeds in. They pour some water on top. Then they look at the book and try to say the spell.

"Flower, flower, grow and bloom. Show us your color and your perfume."

They say the spell three times. Then they wait and watch. Nothing happens.

"Maybe we said it wrong," Lily says.

"Or maybe the book is not real," Ben says.

They feel sad. They want to see a flower.

Just then, they hear a knock on the door. It is Lily's mom. She has a surprise for them.

"Hello, Lily and Ben. I have something for you. Look what I found at the market. A beautiful flower!"

She gives them a big, yellow flower. It smells good.

"Wow, thank you, mom!" Lily says.

"Thank you, mom!" Ben says.

They hug Lily's mom. They are happy.

"Mom, you are so dependable. You always make us smile," Lily says.

"You are welcome, my sweeties. And you know what? You are dependable too. You always try your best. You may not succeed at every spell, but you succeed at being good friends. And that is the best magic of all."

Ben and Lily were playing with a basketball in the park. They liked to bounce it and throw it to each other. Sometimes they tried to make it go into the hoop, but it was too high for them.

One time, Ben threw the ball too hard and it hit a man who was walking by. The man dropped his bag and looked angry. He shouted at Ben and Lily.

"Hey, watch where you throw that thing! You could hurt someone!"

Ben and Lily felt scared and sorry. They ran to the man and said:

"We are sorry, mister. We did not mean to hit you. Are you okay?"

The man looked at them and saw that they were just kids. He sighed and picked up his bag.

"I'm okay, but you should be more careful. This is not a place to play with a basketball. You could squeeze it and make it pop. Or you could hit someone else. Do you understand?"

Ben and Lily nodded. They said:

"Yes, mister. We understand. We will not play with the ball here. We will go to another place. Thank you for not being mad at us."

The man smiled and said:

"You're welcome. Just be safe and have fun. And next time, say sorry if you hit someone, okay?"

Ben and Lily said:

"Okay, mister. We will say sorry. Bye!"

They took their ball and ran to another place. They learned to be more careful and to say sorry when they made a mistake. They still had fun with their basketball, but they did not squeeze it or hit anyone.

Once upon a time, there was a kind girl named Lily. She had a bedroom with a big, soft bed. Every night, before going to sleep, she would sing a sweet song to her teddy bear. 

One day, Lily went to visit her friend, Emily. Emily was not very polite and didn't say "please" or "thank you". Lily tried to teach her how to be polite, but Emily didn't listen. 

As they were playing, Lily started to sing a fun song and Emily joined in. They sang together and had so much fun. Emily realized that Lily was right, being polite is important and it's nice to sing with friends. From that day on, Emily always remembered to say "please" and "thank you" and they sang together every time they played.

Janice loved swimming. Every day she put on her bright pink swimsuit and put her goggles on tight. Today, Janice wanted to try something different. She drove to a lake in the countryside and parked her car nearby.

The lake was a beautiful shimmering blue. Janice was the only person there, so she felt a bit lonely. But as soon as she jumped into the lake, she felt so much better. She swam long distances, enjoying the feeling of moving in the water.

As Janice swam, she noticed a boat on the shore. There was someone in the boat, waving to her! It was a little boy with a sausage in his hand. Janice swam closer, and the boy smiled at her.

"Do you want some sausage?" the boy asked.

Janice laughed, and said, "Yes please!" She enjoyed the delicious sausage as she and the boy talked, until the sun began to set. 

When it was time to go, Janice wished the boy goodbye. She thanked him for the sausage, and as she drove home, she smiled and thought about her lovely day.

Lily loved to bounce. She bounced on her bed, on the sofa, on the trampoline. She bounced with her friends, with her toys, with her dog. She bounced every day, because it made her happy.

One day, Lily wanted to bounce with her mom. She ran to her mom, who was sitting on a chair, and said, "Mom, mom, can we bounce together? Please, please, please!"

Mom smiled and said, "Of course, Lily. You are so enthusiastic. But where do you want to bounce?"

Lily thought for a moment. She had bounced everywhere in the house, but she wanted to try something new. She looked out the window and saw the park. She saw the swings, the slide, the sandbox. And she saw something else. Something big and round and colorful.

She pointed and said, "Mom, look! There is a big ball in the park. Can we bounce on it?"

Mom looked and saw the big ball. It was a bouncy castle, a special kind of ball that you can jump on and have fun. Mom said, "Yes, Lily, we can bounce on it. But we have to wear our shoes and our coats, because it is cold outside. And we have to be careful, because there are other kids who want to bounce too."

Lily nodded and said, "OK, mom. Let's go, let's go, let's go!"

Mom and Lily put on their shoes and their coats and ran to the park. They waited in line for their turn to bounce on the bouncy castle. When it was their turn, they climbed inside and started to bounce. They bounced high and low, fast and slow, up and down. They laughed and shouted and had a lot of fun.

Lily was so happy. She hugged her mom and said, "Thank you, mom. This is the best bounce ever!"

Mom hugged her back and said, "You're welcome, Lily. I love you, my bouncing girl!"

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to go to the beach. One day, she went to the beach with her mom and dad. They played in the sand and swam in the sea. Suddenly, Lily saw a red jellyfish on the shore.

"Mommy, daddy, look!" she shouted.

"What is it, Lily?" her mom asked.

"A red jellyfish!" Lily said.

Her dad picked up the jellyfish with a stick and threw it back into the sea. Lily was happy, but then she said, "I'm embarrassed."

"Why are you embarrassed, Lily?" her mom asked.

"Because I shouted very loud and everyone looked at me," Lily said.

"Don't worry, Lily. It's okay to be excited and shout sometimes," her dad said.

Lily smiled and continued to play in the sand with her mom and dad.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to swim in the pool with his friends. One day, Timmy's mom took him to the beach. Timmy saw the big waves and was scared. 

"It's okay, Timmy," said his mom. "We can swim in the shallow water where it's safe."

Timmy felt better and they went to swim. Suddenly, it got dark and Timmy got scared again. "Mom, I don't like the dark," he said.

"It's okay, Timmy," said his mom. "We can go back to the car and go home now."

Timmy felt better and they went back to the car. He was happy to be safe and sound.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily's friend, Timmy, came to visit her. They played with a hoop in the garden. "This is easy!" said Timmy as he spun the hoop around his waist. Lily tried to copy him but the hoop kept falling down. "I can't do it," she said sadly.

"Don't worry," said Timmy. "It takes practice. Let me show you." Timmy helped Lily and soon she was able to spin the hoop too. "Yay, I did it!" exclaimed Lily. "Thanks for visiting me, Timmy. Let's play again soon." And with that, Timmy said goodbye and went back home. Lily was happy to have a friend like Timmy who made things easy for her.

Once upon a time, there were two best friends named Max and Jack. They were playing in the park one day when they saw a large hill in the distance. They decided to go and explore the hill. 

Max and Jack ran up the hill. They found lots of tall grass and some tiny purple flowers growing around the base of the hill. 

When they reached the top of the hill, they saw a big lake in the distance. Max exclaimed, "Wow, a lake!" Jack replied, "Let's go swimming!"

Max and Jack looked around for a few minutes, and then Max decided that they should go swimming. They raced each other down the hill and ran as fast as they could to the lake.

When they reached the lake, they both spotted a big tree by the edge of the lake. Jack said, "Let's go see what's up that tree!" Max nodded and they both ran over to the tree and started to climb it. 

When they reached the top, they spotted a bird in a big nest. They smiled at each other and watched the bird until it flew away. Max and Jack decided it was time to go home and they hurried off to the park. 

Max and Jack had so much fun exploring the large hill that day and were very happy to have each other as friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the summer. The sun was shining and the flowers were blooming. One day, Lily was playing with her toys in the grass when a gust of wind came and scatter her toys all over the yard. 

"Oh no!" cried Lily. She looked around and saw that her toys were scattered everywhere. She had to pick them up one by one and put them back in her toy basket. 

Despite the toy mishap, Lily was still having a fine time playing in the summer sun. She ran around, caught butterflies, and even had a picnic with her teddy bear. When the sun started to set, Lily went back inside with a big smile on her face, happy to have had a fun day in the summer.

Once upon a time, there were two friends named Timmy and Tommy. Timmy wanted to play with his toy car, but Tommy wanted to play with his toy truck. They couldn't agree on what to play with.

Timmy said, "I want to play with my car." Tommy said, "No, I want to play with my truck." They both looked sad because they couldn't decide.

Suddenly, Timmy had an idea. He said, "Let's build a fence and race our toys. My car will go on one side of the fence and your truck will go on the other side." Tommy liked that idea and said, "Okay, I'm ready to build the fence."

They worked together and built a fence. Then they each put their toy on their side of the fence. "Ready, set, go!" they said, and they raced their toys. They both had so much fun and were happy they found a way to disagree and still play together.

Sara and Ben are twins. They like to play with their toys and share their snacks. But sometimes they want the same thing and they fight. One day, they find a big bag of candy in the kitchen. Sara and Ben are very happy. They want to eat the candy.

They decide to measure the candy and split it in half. Sara gets a ruler and a bowl. Ben gets a knife and a plate. Sara puts some candy in the bowl and measures it with the ruler. Ben cuts some candy with the knife and puts it on the plate. They do this until the bag is empty.

But when they compare their candy, they see that Ben has more than Sara. Sara is envious. She thinks Ben cheated. She says, "That's not fair! You have more candy than me! Give me some of yours!" Ben says, "No way! I measured it right. You are greedy! Go away!" They start to yell and pull each other's hair.

Their mom hears the noise and comes to the kitchen. She sees the mess and the candy. She is angry. She says, "What are you doing? You are not supposed to eat candy before dinner! And you are not supposed to fight with your brother/sister! You are both in trouble! No candy for you! Go to your rooms!"

Sara and Ben are sad and sorry. They wish they had shared the candy and played nicely. They have no candy and no fun. They have a bad ending.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sarah. Sarah was excited because it was a very special day - it was time to celebrate!

So Sarah and her Dad went to the shop. They bought balloons and sweets, and lots of presents. Sarah was very thoughtful when she picked the presents. She wanted to find the perfect gifts for all her family and friends.

When Sarah got home, all her friends and family were there. Everyone was so excited. They all sang songs, and laughed. Every single person at the party received a thoughtful present from Sarah.

Everyone continued to celebrate until the sun went down. It had been a wonderful day and Sarah was very happy.

Once upon a time, there was a thick triangle. It was looking for an adventure, but it had no idea where to start. It tried to think of a plan, but it couldn't manage to come up with one.

Just then, a friendly bee came buzzing by. It asked the triangle what was wrong. The triangle explained it wanted to go on an adventure but didn't know how. The bee had an idea!

The bee told the triangle to fly up, up, up into the sky. After an exciting journey, the two arrived at a big, colorful rainbow. The triangle was excited to explore, but it was afraid of how it would manage.

The bee comforted the triangle, saying it would help it along its journey. With the bee's help, the triangle was brave enough to climb the rainbow and explore the colors. The triangle was so proud it had managed the adventure!

The triangle thanked the bee for its help and flew off to find more adventures. With its newfound courage, the thick triangle soon found many more fun things to explore!

One day, a three-year-old girl named Penelope went for a walk with her grandmother. It was a warm, sunny day and they were full of smiles.

They soon came upon a very old, ancient road that stretched out towards a faraway mountain. Grandmother smiled and told Penelope that this was a special road.

Grandmother suggested that they take a turn off the road, but Penelope shook her head. She wanted to stay on the road and explore! So, with a shrug from Grandmother, they continued on their way along the ancient roadway.

Penelope ran ahead, laughing and kicking stones. Grandmother followed slowly, admiring the views of the rolling hills and river that the road passed by.

Finally, after some time, Grandmother suggested that it was time for them to turn back. Penelope smiled and said she had had a wonderful time and looked forward to their next adventure!

Once there was a rabbit called Patch. He was very hungry and went searching for something to eat. Patch hopped down the row until he saw some carrots! He was so excited he couldn't help but to give a little hop. But then he started to sneeze! "ah-choo!" Patch couldn't stop. He hopped and sneezed his way down the row until he finally stopped to rest. By then he was very tired and still hungry. He sighed and kept hopping; hopeful he'd find something else to eat soon. And he did! A few rows ahead he found a patch of lettuce and quickly scarfed down the juicy leaves. Patch was so happy and relieved that he was no longer hungry. He hopped away, never sneezing once!

Jim had a unique glass. It was special. He liked it very much.

One day, Jim went to the park. He brought his glass with him. He saw some animals and played with his friends.

But then, he noticed something strange. His glass was gone!

He looked around and asked his friends. No one had seen it. Jim was very sad.

But then, something wonderful happened. His unique glass flew down from the sky. He had gained it back!

Jim was very happy. He knew his special glass was safe. He ran home with a smile on his face.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. He loved to play outside in the dirt and roll around in the grass. One day, his mom told him it was time to go inside and study. Timmy didn't want to stop playing, but he knew he had to listen to his mom.

He went inside and sat at his round table with his books and pencils. Timmy didn't like studying very much, but he knew it was important. After a while, he finished his work and went back outside to play. But when he looked down at his hands, he saw they were dirty from playing in the dirt earlier.

Timmy realized that even though he loved playing outside, he needed to study and learn new things too. So he went back inside and washed his hands before continuing his studies. From that day on, Timmy never forgot to wash his hands and always made time to study.

Once upon a time there was a little boy who liked to go for walks. One day, as he walked through the park he stumbled over a rock. The little boy became scared and started to cry.

Just then, a kind woman walked over and said, "Why are you crying little one?". The little boy replied, "I stumbled, and it scared me". The woman smiled at him and said, "It's alright, no need to be scared. Let's take a look at your waist".

She held out her hands, and the little boy felt a calmness come over him. He trusted the woman and soon, his waist didn't hurt anymore. The little boy looked up at the woman and said "Thank you". She smiled and said, "You're welcome, now why don't you go on your way, I'm sure your mummy is waiting for you".

The little boy smiled back, feeling happy and safe and then went running down the path, never to forget his kind encounter in the park.

Once upon a time there was an old man who lived alone in a small house. He was very kind and always had a smile on his face.

One day, the old man decided to go for a walk. He grabbed his coat and opened the door.

But as soon as he opened the door, he was hit by a terrible smell! It was a smelly smell coming from the garden.

The old man got curious and went to the garden. He saw a pupil in the garden playing with a ball.

The old man said to the pupil: "What is that smell? It's terrible!"

The pupil said: "It's my ball, it's smelly."

The old man said: "You should always remind yourself that smelly toys need to be washed."

The pupil said: "Thanks, I will remember!"

So they said goodbye, and the old man went back to his house. He was happy that he could help the pupil.

Once upon a time there was a little owl named Bill. Bill liked to work hard even though it was difficult. Every day he went out of his tree and looked for something to do.

One day Bill saw a fragile flower in a field. He wanted to pick it for his mom, but it was so delicate that he was afraid to touch it. Then he thought of a plan.

He decided to use his beak to carefully remove the flower from the ground. He worked slowly and carefully. Finally, the flower was removed. He brought it back to his mom who was so happy when she saw it.

The End

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to eat nuts. One day, his mom gave him a nut to eat. But when he opened it, he saw that it was spoiled. 

Timmy said, "Mommy, this nut is spoiled. I don't want to eat it."

His mom replied, "That's okay, Timmy. We'll throw it away and get you a fresh nut."

Timmy learned that it's important to check if something is spoiled before eating it. He also learned that it's okay to say no if he doesn't want to eat something. From that day on, Timmy always checked his nuts before eating them and never ate a spoiled nut again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Emma. Emma had to prepare for a big day that was coming. She wanted to be successful, so she was very careful with her plans. 

As Emma was preparing, she started to feel an itch. She scratched it, and it kept coming back. Emma felt frustrated, so she decided to take a break and put some cool cream on it. That helped a little, but the itch wouldn't go away. 

Emma decided to take a deep breath and keep on preparing. She knew if she worked hard, she could be successful. So she kept going with her plan and paid extra close attention to not let the itch distract her.

Emma worked hard and in the end, she was successful. She felt proud and happy that she was able to finish her preparations.

The end.

Mia likes to bathe in the big tub with her toys. She has a duck, a boat, a fish and a star. She makes them swim and splash and sing. She likes the bubbles that smell like flowers and make her skin smooth.

One day, she sees a spark in the water. It is shiny and bright and moves fast. She thinks it is a magic star. She tries to catch it with her hand, but it slips away. She tries to catch it with her boat, but it jumps over. She tries to catch it with her fish, but it swims faster.

She asks her mom, who is watching her, what is the spark. Her mom smiles and says it is a ring. She says she dropped it by mistake when she was filling the tub. She says it is a special ring that her dad gave her when they got married. She says it has a diamond that makes the spark.

Mia thinks the ring is very pretty and wants to see it. She helps her mom find it in the water. Her mom thanks her and puts it on her finger. She says she loves her ring and she loves Mia. She gives her a big hug and a kiss.

Mia is happy. She likes to bathe in the big tub with her toys. She likes the bubbles that smell like flowers and make her skin smooth. She likes the spark that is a ring and a magic star. She likes her mom and her dad and their love. She says she loves them too. She sings a happy song.

Once upon a time, there was a big family of snowmen. They liked to have fun and play together.

One day, the snowmen wanted some juice. So, they went to the store but it was closed. They saw a frozen juice box and they wanted it!

But they couldn't move it because it was frozen. Suddenly, an idea came to them. They blew on the box until the icy juice box was useful again.

The snowmen were happy and took the juice box home. They had lots of fun drinking the juice! From that day onwards, they never had to worry about not having enough delicious juice. The end.

Once upon a time there was a poor flower who didn't have anywhere to live. She was so sad and alone, feeling all alone in the world. She looked around for somewhere to call home.

Suddenly, she saw a cupboard, full of things to keep her warm and happy. The flower was so excited. She walked up to the cupboard and sure enough, it was full of things that were just for her. She jumped in delight and thanked the cupboard for taking her in.

The flower was so happy to have a home and settled in the cupboard. Every day, she went out and explored her new home. One day, she saw a beautiful meadow.

The flower had never seen such beauty before! She was in awe and couldn't believe she had a view like this. She begged and begged for the cupboard to let her go to the meadow and eventually it said yes.

The flower walked carefully and slowly until she reached the meadow. As soon as she stepped into the meadow, she started to bloom! All of the other flowers saw her and were so happy that she found a place to call home. The flower knew she was in her right place and was so relieved to have found a home.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to play with her toys. One day, she wanted to watch her favorite show on TV, but it wouldn't work. Her mommy said they needed to fix the network. So, they put some cords and buttons together to fix it.

Lily was so happy when the TV was fixed, but then she noticed her favorite toy was missing. She searched and searched but couldn't find it. She felt sad and uncomfortable. She asked her mommy to help her find it, but they couldn't.

Lily never found her favorite toy and she felt very sad. She realized that sometimes things can't be fixed and that made her feel even more uncomfortable.

Once upon a time, there was something special in the sky. It was big and colorful and very beautiful. It was called a rainbow.

The next day, it started to rain. Even though the rain was falling, the rainbow was still in the sky. The rainbow was very soft and bright.

The rain kept falling, but the rainbow still stayed in the sky. It wanted to resist the rain and still be there for everyone to see.

But after a while, the rainbow had to leave. Even though it tried as hard as it could, it couldn't resist anymore. It said goodbye and flew away.

But in happy news, the rainbow will come back one day. Maybe one day while it's raining, you can look up and see the rainbow in the sky.

Once upon a time, there was a brave and adventurous rabbit. He loved to explore the world and meet new animals.

One day, his friend the squirrel asked the rabbit if he wanted to go to the big forest. But the rabbit wasn't sure if it was a good idea.

"I don't think it's safe," said the rabbit. "There might be snakes!"

The squirrel disagreed.

"There's nothing to worry about," she said. "I've been there before, and nothing bad happened. Besides, we won't get too close."

The rabbit thought about it and decided it was worth taking a chance. Together, they hopped into the forest.

The rabbit was very amazed by all the exciting sights. He found flowers, new trees and cute little bugs. But then, he saw a snake! He quickly hopped away, but the snake wasn't scared or angry. It stayed peacefully in the bushes.

The rabbit learned that it is important to be adventurous and try new things. But it is also important to be careful and know your limits.

Once upon a time, there was a big, noisy party in the forest. Many animals were there, dancing and singing. But then, a little rabbit came and he was scared. He didn't like the loud music and all the people around him. 

Suddenly, a person came and started to shout at the animals. He said that the party had to end because it was too late. The animals didn't want to stop, but the person was very angry. 

The little rabbit was happy when the person left and the party ended. He could finally go back to his cozy burrow and sleep peacefully. From that day on, the animals learned to keep their parties quiet so they wouldn't disturb anyone else.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play in the farm with the animals. One day, they see a big gate. The gate is closed. Behind the gate, there are many cows. The cows are loud and hungry.

Anna and Ben want to feed the cows. They find some grass and hay. They go to the gate. They try to open the gate. But the gate is heavy and hard. They cannot open the gate.

They see a farmer. The farmer is old and kind. He is wise. He knows a lot about the farm and the animals. He sees Anna and Ben. He smiles and says hello.

Anna and Ben ask the farmer if they can feed the cows. The farmer says yes, but they have to be careful. He says the cows are big and strong. He says they have to stay with him. He says he will release the gate for them.

The farmer goes to the gate. He pulls a lever. The gate opens. The cows see the grass and hay. They come out of the gate. They are happy and excited. They moo and run.

Anna and Ben are scared and amazed. They hold the farmer's hand. They give the grass and hay to the cows. The cows eat and lick. They are gentle and friendly.

Anna and Ben are happy and proud. They thank the farmer. They say goodbye to the cows. They close the gate. They go back to their homes. They tell their parents about their adventure. They say they learned a lot from the wise farmer. They say they love the farm and the animals.

Once upon a time, there was a big camp in the woods. The camp was huge and had many tents. People came to the camp to sleep in the tents and have fun. 

One day, a little bear came to the camp. He was very tired and wanted to sleep. He saw a big tent and went inside. 

The people in the tent were surprised to see the little bear. But he looked so cute and tired that they let him sleep with them. The bear was happy and slept all night long. 

In the morning, the bear woke up and played with the people. They had a lot of fun together. When it was time to go, the little bear said goodbye and went back to the woods. He was happy to have made new friends at the big camp.

Mama and Jack were walking in the forest looking for something special.

"Look, an owl!" said Jack excitedly. 

Mama smiled at the normal owl perched in a tree.

"Let's tear open this here bag of berries," said Mama.

Jack pulled the bag open, and it ripped apart. The berries tumbled out onto the ground.

The owl swooped down and started eating the berries. Jack laughed with delight.

The owl flew away and Mama and Jack continued to explore the forest.

Once upon a time, a nosy girl named Molly decided to wake up early one morning to watch the sunrise. She felt curious and excited to see the orange and pink colors appear in the sky.

Molly told her mom, who was a little surprised. She thought it would be too early for Molly to wake up! But she couldn't resist her daughter's enthusiasm.

Molly got dressed quickly, grabbed a blanket and headed to the front yard. There, she found the perfect spot to watch the sun come up. 

As the sky brightened, Molly could see the colors getting more intense. She started to mention the different colors of the sunrise to her mom. The orange, the yellow, and the pink. 

When the sun finally appeared, Molly clapped with joy. She stayed outside until the sun had fully risen, enjoying the bright morning light.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Alice. Alice was only three years old. One day, Alice's mother decided to cook some rice. Alice asked if she could help. Alice's mother said yes, so Alice started to help.

Alice was a bit weak, so her mother showed her how to sprinkle some of the rice into the pot. Together, they added water and waited for the rice to cook.

Alice watched as the rice bubbled and started to fill the pot. After some time, the rice was done. Alice and her mother sat down to eat. The rice was warm, soft and delicious.

Alice learned that with a bit of help, there was nothing she couldn't do - even cooking rice.

Once upon a time, there was a big, round planet in the sky. It was very busy, always spinning, rolling and moving. Everyone on it had lots to do.

One day, a little boy named Joe decided he wanted to get on the planet. He didn't know how, though - until he had an amazing idea! He got a big bouncy ball and started rolling it along the ground. As the ball rolled, it got bigger and bigger. Soon enough, Joe rolled himself up in the ball and before he knew it, he was on the planet.

Joe was amazed! Everywhere he looked was something new. He saw people and animals, trees, rivers and more. Joe had lots of fun exploring the planet - it was so exciting!

Eventually, it was time to leave. Joe waved goodbye and rolled off the planet. He rolled and rolled until he reached home. Joe was so happy to have seen the busy planet.

Moley was a small mole who lived in her burrow at the end of a garden. She loved to dress up in beautiful clothes. 

Every morning, she put on her prettiest robes and politest hats. She felt so special when she was wearing her very best.

One day, Moley dressed in her most beautiful clothes and went down to the pond. She saw her reflection in the water, and she was amazed. "I'm so beautiful," she said, smiling.

Moley enjoyed looking at herself so much that she decided to dress up every day. She was so proud of the beautiful clothes she chose. Her friends were amazed at how stylish she had become. 

Moley was the happiest mole around. She loved to dress up and show off her beautiful fashion!

Once upon a time, there was a big mountain. It was very tall and had a large top. A little girl went up the mountain and saw a beautiful view. She wondered how the view was so pretty. She sat down and looked at the view for a long time. The sun went down and the stars came out. The little girl was happy and went back home.

Tom and his dad went to the stadium to watch a soccer game. They had a big bag with snacks and drinks and a ball. Tom was very excited to see the players and the fans.

Tom and his dad cheered for the blue team and had a lot of fun. They watched the game and saw many goals and tricks. They clapped and shouted and smiled. They were happy and proud of their team. They had a great day at the stadium.

Once upon a time, in a big city, there lived a cat and a dog. They were not friends. The cat liked to rub on things, and the dog liked to dig deep holes. One day, they both wanted to play in the same park.

The cat found a nice tree to rub on, but the dog wanted to dig a deep hole right there. The cat said, "No, I was here first!" The dog said, "But I want to dig here!" They both got mad at each other.

Then, a big bird came and said, "Stop fighting! You can both play here. Cat, you can rub on the tree, and dog, you can dig a deep hole next to it." The cat and the dog agreed, and they played happily ever after.

Molly was playing with her toys and having fun, when she heard an angry voice coming from the kitchen. She peeked in and saw Mommy standing there with a big mop. Mommy had a helpless frown on her face. Molly knew something was wrong.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to listen to the radio and dance to the music. One day, Timmy's mom told him they were going on an adventurous trip to the beach. Timmy was excited and couldn't wait to pack his toys and snacks.

When they arrived at the beach, Timmy saw a big wave coming. He wanted to play in the water, but his mom warned him that the water was too dangerous. Timmy didn't listen and ran towards the water. Suddenly, the big wave hit him and he got separated from his mom.

Timmy was scared and started crying. He looked around and saw a lifeguard who came to rescue him. The lifeguard brought Timmy back to his mom who was waiting for him on the beach. Timmy learned that it's important to listen to his mom and stay safe. From that day on, Timmy never went near the water without his mom.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Jane. Jane wanted to have some fun, so she ran outside to play. She saw a big log and decided she would use it to slide down the hill.

Jane sat on the log and started to slide. The log slid quickly down the hill until something unexpected happened - Jane started to slip! She didn't know what to do, and she was scared.

But then she saw something - it was a bright, yellow object. It was a fake log put there by her friends! Jane felt much better knowing that her friends had made a fun ride for her.

So Jane hopped onto the fake log and slid down the hill. She had a lot of fun slipping down the hill with the help of her friends, and she was very grateful for their help. Jane learned that it's important to have friends who can help you have fun and stay safe.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys in the bathtub. He would pretend to drive a boat and make waves with his hands. One day, Timmy's mom came into the bathroom and said, "Timmy, it's time to get out of the bathtub and get ready for bed."

Timmy didn't want to get out of the bathtub yet. He wanted to keep playing. "But Mommy, I'm being creative!" he said.

"I know, Timmy, but it's time to go to bed," his mom replied.

Timmy sighed and got out of the bathtub. As he got dressed for bed, he thought about all the fun he had driving his boat in the bathtub. He couldn't wait to do it again tomorrow.

Once there was a rude man named Bill. He never helped anyone, not even his mom. One day, his mom asked him to sort the toys in his room. But Bill didn't want to help. His mom shouted at him and he got scared. He decided to do what his mom said. He started to sort the toys and soon he was done.

Next, his mom asked him to mop the floor. Again, Bill didn't want to help but this time his mom didn't shout at him. She just told him that it was very important and asked him kindly. Bill saw the kindness in his mom and decided to help. He went and got the mop and started to mop the floor. He made sure to clean it properly.

When he was done, his mom thanked him. She said that she was proud of his good work and gave him a big hug. Bill felt so happy and proud of himself. He was glad that he listened to his mom and helped her. From that day onwards, Bill started to be more helpful to his mom.

Tom and Sam are friends. They like to play with cars and balls. One day, they go to the park with their moms. They see a big slide. They want to go on the slide.

But there is a law. The law says only one kid can go on the slide at a time. The law is on a sign. Tom and Sam do not read the sign. They do not know the law.

They run to the slide. They both want to go first. They push and pull. They do not share. They do not listen to their moms. They are not nice.

Then, something bad happens. They both fall off the slide. They hit the ground. They hurt themselves. They cry and cry. Their moms come to help them. They are angry and sad.

They say to Tom and Sam: "You broke the law. You did not change your turn. You did not play fair. You did not care. You are sorry now. But it is too late. You have to go home. No more slide. No more park. No more fun."

Tom and Sam are sorry. They say sorry to their moms. They say sorry to each other. But they still have to go home. They are not happy. They have a bad ending.

Tom and Sam were brothers who liked to play outside. They had a big yard with a well and a swing. One day, they wanted to play with the same toy car, but there was only one. They began to quarrel over who would get it.

"Give me the car, it's mine!" Tom shouted.

"No, it's mine, I saw it first!" Sam yelled.

They pulled and pushed and tugged at the car, but neither would let go. They got angry and said harsh words to each other. They did not share or take turns.

The well was near where they fought. It was deep and dark and had no cover. As they quarreled, they did not see where they were going. They got too close to the well and lost their balance. They fell into the well with the car, and no one heard them scream.

Their mother came looking for them, but she could not find them. She called their names, but they did not answer. She searched the yard, but she did not see the well. She was scared and sad and did not know what to do. She cried and cried and wished they had not quarreled.

Once there was a friend- a tough friend. His name was Rocky. Rocky was brave, even when things got tough. Every day, Rocky rocked back and forth in his chair- building strength, getting tougher and tougher.

One day, Rocky decided he wanted to go on a big adventure. So he decided to take a hike. As he walked into the woods, Rocky kept rocking back and forth- still building his strength.

Finally, Rocky came to a big hill with a steep cliff at the top. Rocky took a deep breath- this was going to be tough! But, Rocky kept rocking back and forth, building his strength and courage until he reached the top.

Now that Rocky had reached the top of the cliff, he could see how far he'd come. Everything was suddenly a lot clearer. Rocky shook his head and smiled: he was tough. He had done it!

Once upon a time, there was a beautiful red lady. One day she wanted to marry, so she put on her best dress and went to look for a husband. She could not find one she liked, until she saw a handsome prince. The prince loved the lady too and they decided to get married. 

The day before their wedding, the lady made some dough. She rolled it out and cut it into shapes and made different coloured decorations out of it. The lady used red dough to make a red heart and the prince used blue dough to make a blue crown. 

On the day of their wedding, the lady and the prince each took a decorated piece of dough, said their wedding vows, and then put the pieces of dough together to make a big, beautiful heart. They were married! 

After that, the princess and prince lived together happily ever after. They made a lot more dough with different shapes and decorations and enjoyed it all together.

Lily loved to perform. She liked to sing and dance and act in front of her family and friends. She always wore her best fashion when she performed. She had a pink dress, a blue hat, and a shiny necklace. She felt like a star.

One day, Lily wanted to perform a new show for her mom and dad. She had a big idea. She wanted to tell a story about a princess and a dragon. She needed some help. She asked her brother Tom to play the dragon. Tom was lazy. He did not like to perform. He liked to play with his cars and trucks.

"Please, Tom, please," Lily begged. "It will be fun. You just have to roar and chase me. I will be the princess and you will be the dragon. Mom and dad will love it."

Tom sighed. He did not want to make Lily sad. He agreed to play the dragon. But he did not try very hard. He put on a green shirt and a cardboard tail. He did not roar. He did not chase. He just walked slowly behind Lily.

Lily was not happy. She wanted her show to be exciting. She wanted her brother to be scary. She wanted her mom and dad to clap and cheer. She decided to change her story. She had a new idea.

She ran to her room and got her toy sword. She came back and said, "Now the story is different. I am not a princess. I am a knight. And you are not a dragon. You are a monster. And I will fight you and save the day."

Tom was surprised. He did not like this idea. He did not want to fight. He wanted to stop. But Lily did not listen. She ran at him with her sword. She shouted, "Take that, monster! You are no match for me!"

Tom tried to dodge. He tried to run. He tried to say, "Stop, Lily, stop!" But it was too late. Lily swung her sword and hit him on the head. Tom fell down and cried. Lily dropped her sword and gasped. She did not mean to hurt him. She ran to him and hugged him. She said, "I'm sorry, Tom, I'm sorry. Are you okay?"

Mom and dad heard the noise and came to see what happened. They saw Lily and Tom on the floor. They saw the green shirt and the cardboard tail. They saw the pink dress and the blue hat. They saw the toy sword and the shiny necklace. They understood what happened. They were not angry. They were not amused. They were worried.

They picked up Tom and checked his head. They said, "Oh, Tom, oh, Lily. What were you doing? Why were you fighting? You could have hurt each other. You have to be careful. You have to be kind. You have to play nice."

Lily and Tom felt bad. They said, "We're sorry, mom, we're sorry, dad. We were trying to perform. We were trying to have fun. We did not mean to fight. We did not mean to hurt. We love each other. We will play nice."

Mom and dad hugged them and kissed them. They said, "We love you, too. We're glad you're okay. We're proud of you for performing. But next time, please choose a different story. And please ask us first. We want to see your show. We want to clap and cheer. But we also want you to be safe and happy."

Lily and Tom nodded. They said, "Okay, mom, okay, dad. We will do that. We will choose a different story. We will ask you first. We will be safe and happy. And we will still perform. Because we love to perform."

The end.

Once upon a time there was a graceful sheep. He lived in a meadow and every day he would go out to eat tasty grass and drink from a stream. One day he decided to explore further afield, and no matter how much he struggled, he couldn't find a way back home.

Suddenly, a wolf appeared and said, "I'll help you, little sheep. We'll just have to take a longer route, but I promise to help you find your way." Despite his struggle, the sheep decided to follow the wolf. They walked for hours, and just as the sun was setting, they reached a strange cave.

The wolf smiled and said, "Here we are. You can stay here for the night." The sheep stepped inside, but it was a mistake. The sheep had been tricked. The wolf was actually waiting for him in the cave. He had tricked the poor animal.

The wolf leapt onto the sheep and snapped its neck in his sharp teeth. The miserable sheep exhaled its last breath and the sound echoed around the cave. The graceful sheep was gone forever.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to listen to jazz music with her mom. One day, Lily's mom put on a jazz song and turned the volume up high. Lily loved it and started dancing around the room.

Suddenly, Lily's little brother came in and demanded that they turn off the music. He said it was too loud for him. Lily's mom explained that they were just enjoying the music and asked her brother if he wanted to dance with them.

But her brother still didn't like the music and demanded that they turn it off. So, Lily's mom turned it down a little bit and they all continued to dance and have fun together. From that day on, Lily's brother started to like jazz music too and they would all dance together whenever they put on a jazz song.

Tim and Mia are playing with cubes in the playroom. They like to build towers and houses with the cubes. They have many cubes of different colors and sizes.

"Look, Mia, I made a big tower with red and blue cubes!" Tim says, showing his creation to his sister.

"That's nice, Tim, but I made a better house with yellow and green cubes!" Mia says, pointing to her own work.

They start to argue about whose cubes are better. They want to have all the cubes for themselves. They pull and push the cubes, trying to take them from each other.

"Stop it, Mia, these are my cubes!" Tim shouts.

"No, they are mine, Tim, you are mean!" Mia cries.

They fight so hard that they knock down their towers and houses. The cubes fall and scatter on the floor. Some of the cubes hit them and hurt them. They both start to weep.

Mom hears the noise and comes to the playroom. She sees the mess and the crying children. She is not happy.

"What happened here? Why are you weeping?" Mom asks.

"Tim and Mia are bad! They broke my cubes!" They both say at the same time.

Mom sighs and hugs them. She tells them to calm down and share the cubes. She says that cubes are for playing, not for fighting. She says that they should be nice and lively, not mean and weepy.

She helps them to pick up the cubes and put them back in the box. She gives them each a kiss and a cookie. She tells them to play nicely and have fun.

Tim and Mia say sorry to each other. They smile and hug. They decide to build a new tower and a new house together. They use all the colors and sizes of the cubes. They are happy and lively again. They thank Mom for the cookies and the cubes. They love Mom and they love each other.

John held an insect in his hand. He was very excited! He had never seen an insect so close up before. He thought it was very useful.

John wanted to keep the insect as a pet, so he made it a house from a small paper box and put it in the garden. He put some food in there too, so that it had enough to eat.

John went back to check on the insect every day and he always held it very carefully. The insect liked living in its new house and was very happy.

John and the insect became best friends. They spent lots of time together and played lots of games. John was very happy that he had such a useful and fun pet!

Once upon a time, there was a cheap structure. It did not look very nice, but it was big and fun for children to play in.

One day, a little girl saw the structure and wanted to act in it. She asked her father if she could jump, run, and slide around the structure. Her dad said yes, and so she ran inside and started playing.

The girl acted like she was a princess and a prince. She jumped and ran up and down the structure. Then she slid down the slide. She acted like a fairy, too, and pretended she had magical powers.

She played and pretended until it was time to go. She had had so much fun acting in the cheap structure. The little girl went home with a big smile on her face.

Once upon a time, there was an object. It was sitting on the ground, all alone. The object was clear, like a window.

One day, a little boy saw the object. He wasn't sure what it was, but he wanted to know. He carefully picked it up and looked at it. He saw something special inside.

The boy wanted to share this with his friends. He carefully passed it to them. Each friend looked carefully and smiled.

The object was quickly passed to others. Everywhere the object went, people would smile and laugh. The object made people happy.

The little boy was so glad he passed the object. He was proud that he discovered something that made so many people happy.

Once upon a time there was a chubby little girl called Mary. Mary loved to play with her friends and have fun. One day, Mary decided she wanted a new haircut. She talked to her Mum about it and Mum said she could have one. 

Mary was very excited and she went to the hairdresser. When she was there, the hairdresser started to test out different hairstyles on her. But none of them seemed just right for Mary. After trying on lots of different haircuts, Mary was getting very frustrated.

Finally, the hairdresser found the perfect haircut for Mary. She was so happy she jumped with joy! The hairdresser had given her the perfect haircut and she loved it. 

From then on, Mary always asked for the same haircut every time she went to the hairdresser. She was very pleased with her hair and she felt very happy.

Tom and Sam are brothers. They like to play with their toys in their room. But their room is very messy. They have cars, blocks, books, and balls everywhere. Mom and Dad are not happy.

One day, Mom and Dad say, "We are going to visit Grandma and Grandpa. You can bring some toys, but not too many. And you have to put them in a bag. We will put the bags in the van."

Tom and Sam are excited. They love Grandma and Grandpa. They hope they will have fun. But they do not want to pack their toys. They want to bring them all.

Tom says, "I will bring all my cars. They are my favorite." He grabs a big box and fills it with cars.

Sam says, "I will bring all my blocks. They are my favorite." He grabs a big bag and fills it with blocks.

Mom and Dad come to their room. They see the box and the bag. They shake their heads.

Mom says, "You can't bring all these toys. They are too many and too heavy. You have to choose some and leave some. And you have to be organized. Put the toys you want in a small bag. Put the toys you don't want in a bin. We will donate them to other kids who need them."

Dad says, "You have to learn to share and to be tidy. That is the right thing to do. And you will have more space and more fun. Trust us."

Tom and Sam are sad. They do not want to give away their toys. They do not want to be organized. They think Mom and Dad are mean.

But they have no choice. They have to listen to Mom and Dad. They have to pack their toys. They have to be organized.

They pick some cars and some blocks. They put them in a small bag. They put the rest in a bin. They carry the bag and the bin to the van.

Mom and Dad smile. They say, "Good job, boys. You did well. We are proud of you. Now let's go to Grandma and Grandpa's house. They have a surprise for you."

Tom and Sam are curious. They wonder what the surprise is. They hope it is something good.

They get in the van. They buckle up. They drive away.

They arrive at Grandma and Grandpa's house. They run to the door. They hug Grandma and Grandpa.

Grandma and Grandpa say, "Welcome, boys. We have a surprise for you. Come and see."

They lead them to the backyard. There, they see a big playhouse. It has windows, a door, a roof, and a chimney. It is painted in bright colors. It has a sign that says, "Tom and Sam's Playhouse".

Tom and Sam are amazed. They are happy. They say, "Wow! A playhouse! For us? Thank you, Grandma and Grandpa. You are the best."

Grandma and Grandpa say, "You are welcome, boys. We made it for you. We hope you like it. You can play with your toys in it. But you have to be organized. You have to put your toys in the shelves and the drawers. You have to keep your playhouse clean and neat. That is the rule."

Tom and Sam nod. They say, "OK, Grandma and Grandpa. We will be organized. We will keep our playhouse clean and neat. We understand the rule."

They go inside the playhouse. They put their toys in the shelves and the drawers. They arrange them by color and size. They make their playhouse look nice.

They play with their toys. They have fun. They are organized.

They learn a lesson. They learn to share and to be tidy. They learn to be grateful and to be happy. They learn to be organized.

The end.

Anna loves to hold her dog, Spot. Spot is soft and warm and likes to lick her face. Anna and Spot are best friends. They like to play and run and nap together.

One day, Anna's mom says they are going to the park. Anna is happy. She puts on her coat and shoes and holds Spot's leash. Spot is happy too. He wags his tail and barks. Anna and Spot get in the car and go to the park.

At the park, there are many things to see and do. There are swings and slides and a sandbox. There are other kids and dogs and birds. Anna and Spot have fun. They swing and slide and dig. They meet new friends and share toys.

Anna's mom has a surprise for them. She takes out a bag from her pocket. Inside the bag are treats. They are crunchy and yummy and smell good. Anna's mom gives one treat to Anna and one treat to Spot. Anna and Spot say thank you. They eat their treats and smile. They are happy.

Anna thinks this is a perfect day. She hugs her mom and kisses Spot. She says she loves them. They love her too. They are a perfect family.

One day, Jack wanted to play in the park. He could not find his ball. He got worried. His mommy saw Jack's worry and wanted to fix it. She asked Jack to be careful and look around the house. Jack followed her advice. After a few minutes, Jack saw his ball under the bed. He was so happy. He ran to his mommy and showed her the ball. She was very happy and gave him a big hug. Jack was no longer worried. He played in the park with his ball for the rest of the day.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a gray cat named Mittens. One day, Lily's mommy gave her a present. It was a pretty pink dress. Lily loved it and said, "Thank you, mommy!" 

Later that day, Lily went outside to play with Mittens. She saw her friend, Timmy, and said, "Hi, Timmy! Look at my new present!" Timmy said, "Wow, that's a pretty dress!" 

Lily and Timmy played together for a while. Mittens chased after a butterfly and Lily said, "Mittens, come back!" Mittens ran back to Lily and meowed. Lily giggled and said, "Mittens, you're silly!" 

As the sun started to set, Lily's mommy called her inside for dinner. Lily said goodbye to Timmy and Mittens and ran inside. She told her mommy all about her fun day and said, "I love my new present!"

Lily and Ben were playing in the park. They saw a big statue of a king. The king had a crown and a long robe. He looked very old and serious.

"Who is he?" Lily asked.

"He is an ancient king," Ben said. "He lived a long time ago. He was very strong and brave."

"How do you know?" Lily asked.

"My dad told me. He knows a lot of things," Ben said.

Lily and Ben wanted to climb the statue. They thought it would be fun. But the statue was very high and heavy. They could not reach the king's feet.

"Let's use the seesaw," Ben said. He had an idea. He ran to the seesaw and jumped on one end. He told Lily to sit on the other end.

"Maybe we can make the seesaw go up and down. Then we can touch the king," Ben said.

Lily nodded. She sat on the seesaw. Ben pushed with his legs. The seesaw went up and down. Lily and Ben laughed.

But the king was still too high. They could not touch him. They tried harder and harder. The seesaw went faster and faster.

Suddenly, the seesaw broke. It was too old and weak. It could not weigh Lily and Ben. They fell to the ground. They were not hurt, but they were surprised.

"Oops," Ben said.

"Sorry," Lily said.

They looked at the king. He did not move. He did not smile. He did not care.

Lily and Ben decided to play something else. They ran to the slide. They forgot about the ancient king. He was too high and heavy for them.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to walk in the park with her mommy and daddy. One day, Lily saw some kids playing with a cool toy. She wanted to play with them too but she was too shy to join them.

Lily's mommy told her that it's important to make new friends and join in on the fun. So, Lily took a deep breath and went over to the other kids. They welcomed her with open arms and shared their cool toy with her.

From that day on, Lily learned that it's always better to join in and make new friends. She felt happy and grateful for the new friends she made. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, she went outside to play in the park. While she was running around, she fell down and hurt her knee. It was red and sore, but her mommy gave her a kiss to make it feel better.

As she was walking around, she discovered a shiny rock on the ground. It was so pretty and sparkly! She picked it up and showed it to her mommy. Her mommy said it was very special and that Lily was very lucky to find such a rich-looking rock.

Lily was so happy and proud of herself for discovering the pretty rock. She forgot all about her sore knee and ran around the park, showing everyone her special treasure. From then on, Lily always looked for special rocks whenever she went outside to play.

Once upon a time, there was an enormous lime. It was so big, it was as big as a house! The lime started to roll away through the woods, faster and faster and faster.

Two little children, Jack and Lucy, were playing in the woods when they saw the enormous lime. They ran after it, trying to catch up.

After a while, the lime stopped rolling and it stayed in front of a big tree. Jack and Lucy were very happy.

The two children climbed the tree to get the enormous lime. When they finally reached it, they squeezed it to make some delicious lime juice.

Jack and Lucy stayed in the woods for a picnic and enjoyed some yummy lime juice!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Meg. She had bright brown eyes and loved to play outside in the sunshine.

One day, Meg received a purple envelope in the mail. Inside was a card with a note written in big yellow letters. It said "Be kind to others". Meg was confused. She didn't know what it meant, so she went to ask her mom.

"Mom, what does 'Be Kind to Others' mean?" she asked. Mom smiled and said, "It means that we should always be kind and gentle to people around us. Even if it's just a small gesture, like holding a door open". 

Meg thought about this and it made sense. She smiled and decided she was going to start doing that.

The next day, Meg was outside walking when she saw an old lady. She was wearing a pale dress and looked sad. It made Meg feel sad too. She decided to do something kind and crossed the street to give the lady a big hug. The old lady was so surprised that she began to cry tears of happiness. 

Meg realized that it is so important to be kind to others, even if it is a small gesture. From that day forwards, she never forgot to be kind.

One day, a little boy named Tim went for a wander in his yard. He found an enormous rubber ball. The ball was red, blue, and green. Tim was very happy to find the ball. He wanted to play with it all day.

Tim ran to his friend, Sam. "Look! Look!" said Tim. "I found a big ball!" Sam was excited too. They both wanted to play with the enormous rubber ball. They decided to play catch with it.

Tim and Sam had a lot of fun playing with the enormous rubber ball. They laughed and smiled as they threw it back and forth. The sun was shining, and they played until it was time for dinner. They knew they would have more fun with the ball the next day.

Once upon a time there was a very big bear. He was so big that he could hug two people at once! He loved to make funny jokes and make people laugh. Every day he would go to the park, and welcome everyone he saw with a joke.

The bear met a lot of friends at the park, and he soon realised how important it was to have friends. He always made sure to give everyone a big welcome and tell them a funny joke. Even when it was raining and no one else was at the park, he would still tell jokes and welcome the rain!

One day a little girl came to the park with her mum. Seeing this, the bear got very excited and welcomed them both with a joke. The little girl laughed a lot and soon they were the best of friends. Now whenever the little girl comes to the park, the bear welcomes her with a big hug and a funny joke!

Once there was a woman. Every day she would pay people a visit. She was always very kind. She was so easy to talk to!

One day, she visited a little girl who was only 3 years old. The woman asked the girl, "Do you want to come pay a visit with me?"
The little girl was so excited! She said yes and ran to get her shoes.

The two of them went to the park. They played on the swings and slides. They had such a great time together! 

At the end of the day, the woman said goodbye to the little girl and gave her a big hug. The little girl felt very happy and couldn't wait to pay the woman another visit!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to walk on the road with her friends. One day, they saw a very rich lady walking towards them. The lady was wearing a beautiful dress and had many shiny jewels.

Lily's friends wanted to say hello to the lady, but Lily was too shy. The lady smiled at them and said, "Hello, children! Would you like to see my jewels?" Lily's friends eagerly gathered around the lady and admired her jewels.

Suddenly, the lady dropped her purse on the road. Lily saw this and quickly ran to pick it up. She returned it to the lady, who was very grateful. The lady then said to the children, "Remember, it's not about being rich or having lots of jewels. It's about being kind and helpful to others. Always push yourself to do good things."

From that day on, Lily learned that being kind and helpful was more important than being rich or having lots of things. She always remembered the lady's words and tried to help others whenever she could.

Once upon a time, there was a cool and wise stream. All of the animals loved to play in it. They included birds, ducks and fish. 

The stream was full of beautiful, sparkly rocks. The animals spent many happy days collecting the pretty rocks. 

One day, a wise old owl flew by and saw them playing in the stream. She stopped to watch the animals have so much fun. The owl smiled and kept flying. 

The animals kept playing in the stream and included things like jumping and swimming. And, with the help of the wise old owl, they kept having lots of fun!

Once upon a time, there was a nice girl named Lily. She loved to play outside with her friends. One day, Lily found a big swing near her house. She was very happy and excited.

Lily asked her friends to come and play on the swing with her. They all took turns swinging high in the air. They laughed and had lots of fun. After a while, they got tired and decided to go inside Lily's house for a snack.

Inside the house, there was a big stair. Lily and her friends climbed up the stair to the kitchen. They found some yummy snacks to eat. After they finished eating, they went back outside to play on the swing some more. They had a great day together.

Once upon a time, there was a new kitten. The kitten was excited about exploring, so off it went!

On its adventures, the kitten stumbled upon an x-ray machine. It was big and shiny! Intrigued, the kitten decided to go inside.

The big x-ray machine went "beep!" and suddenly the kitten was surrounded by a bright light. The kitten felt very strange.

But then, something magical happened. When the light disappeared, the kitten was no longer a kitten! It had become a puppy!

The puppy was happy and excited to explore again. It had yielded something new and wonderful in the x-ray machine.

Johnnie was playing with his toy car. He liked to slide the toy car around on the floor. He would zoom past the furniture and slide around the corners.

He heard something outside the window and looked out. He saw lots of cars going by, all moving along on the road. It was traffic, he knew, but it was different. The cars all had different colours, shapes and sizes.

Johnnie was excited. He wanted to be outside, sliding around like the cars. He ran to the door, opened it and ran outside. He ran through the garden and down the street, sliding this way and that. He waved to the cars, who waved back at him.

Johnnie kept sliding around, finding different roads and paths. He was having so much fun that he didn't realize how late it was until it started to get dark.

He went back to the house, tired but happy with his adventures. He had been sliding around like the cars all day, and he had had a lot of fun.

Tom and Anna like to play with their toys. They have many toys, but their favorite is the big box. The big box can be anything they want. Sometimes it is a house, sometimes it is a boat, sometimes it is a car.

One day, they decide to make the box a car. They need wheels for the car. They look around and find some things they can use. They find four lids from the pots, a rope, and a stick.

"Look, Anna, we can use these lids as wheels!" Tom says. He shows Anna how to tie the rope around the lids and the box. "Now we have a car!"

"Wow, Tom, you are very smart!" Anna says. She picks up the stick. "This can be our steering wheel. We can turn it to go left or right." She makes a hole in the box and puts the stick in it. "Now we have a steering wheel!"

They are very happy with their car. They sit inside the box and pretend to drive. They make noises like a car. They go fast and slow, they turn and stop. They have a lot of fun.

Then they see Ben, their neighbor. Ben is sad. He has no toys to play with. He watches Tom and Anna with their car.

"Hi, Ben!" Tom says. "Do you want to play with us?"

Ben nods. He likes Tom and Anna. They are kind to him.

"Come on, Ben, you can sit with us in the car!" Anna says. She makes room for Ben in the box. "We can go anywhere we want!"

Ben smiles. He sits with Tom and Anna in the car. He holds the stick with Anna. They drive together. They make noises like a car. They go fast and slow, they turn and stop. They have a lot of fun.

Tom and Anna are happy to share their car with Ben. Ben is happy to have friends to play with. They are all happy. They have a good day.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Tim. Tim loved to play outside on Sunday. It was hot outside, but he didn't mind. He liked to run and jump and play with his friends. 

One day, Tim saw a big tree in the park. He thought it would be fun to climb up the tree. So, he started to climb. He climbed and climbed until he was very high up in the tree. 

Tim looked down and saw his friends playing below. He thought they looked very small from up high. Tim was happy he climbed the tree, but he was also a little scared. He thought he might fall. So, he carefully climbed back down the tree and went to play with his friends. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who had a loose tooth. Every day, she would wiggle the tooth with her tongue and the tooth would move back and forth. It started to become a game, and the little girl started to giggle with delight.

One day, the little girl asked her mother if it was time to let the tooth go. She was so excited to meet the tooth fairy! Her mother gently nodded her head yes, so the little girl let her tooth out of her mouth. 

The little girl put her tooth under her pillow and waited for the tooth fairy to come visit. Sure enough, the tooth fairy came that night and left the little girl a present! She was so happy. From then on, the little girl carefully looked after her teeth, brushing and flossing gently every day.

One day, a little bird was flying in the sky. The bird was very hungry. It saw some wood on the ground and thought, "Maybe I can eat this wood to fill my tummy."

The bird flew down and started to eat the wood. "Yum!" said the bird. "This wood is spicy!" The bird liked spicy food, so it ate more and more wood.

Soon, a big cat came by and saw the bird eating the wood. The cat was also hungry. The cat said, "Little bird, why are you eating wood? It's not good for you."

The bird didn't listen to the cat. It just kept on eating the spicy wood. The cat was sad because the bird did not listen, so it walked away.

After eating too much wood, the bird's tummy hurt very badly. The bird felt sick and couldn't fly anymore. It wished it had listened to the cat. But now, it was too late.

Once upon a time, there was a monkey named Bobo. Bobo loved to eat bananas. He would climb up the tree and pick the yellow fruit. Bobo was very thin because he only ate bananas.

One day, Bobo went to a show. He saw a clown who did funny things. When the clown finished, everyone applauded. Bobo also clapped his hands and said "Yay!"
