After the show, Bobo went to get a banana. But he saw that there were none left on the tree. He felt sad. Then, the clown came to Bobo and gave him a banana. Bobo was so happy that he jumped up and down and clapped his hands again.

Once upon a time, in a small country, there lived a furry dog named Max. Max loved to play, jump, and run. He had many friends in the country, like birds, cats, and other dogs.

One day, Max found a big book under a tree. He wanted to read the book. So, he sat down and looked at the pictures. The pictures were of animals like him. Max felt happy when he looked at the pictures.

Max wanted to show his friends the book. He took the book to the birds, the cats, and the other dogs. They all sat together and read the book. They saw pictures of animals from other countries. Max and his friends had a fun day reading the book and learning about new animals.

Once there was an airport. All the grown ups were busy and busy, talking on the phones and working. But the children got to PLAY. They had so much fun.

One day two kids, Tom and Jane, were playing at the airport. They ran around and laughed and had a great time. But then a grown up got angry. He said, "You kids need to be quiet!" Tom and Jane got scared and said sorry.

The grown up was still angry, so he said, "You can't play here anymore". Tom and Jane felt sad and started to cry.

The other grown ups saw this and felt sorry for Tom and Jane. One of them said, "Let's take them to the park near the airport where they can play".

Tom and Jane were very happy and ran off to the park. They could play and had so much fun. The grown ups were happy too because the kids were happy. And that is how Tom and Jane stayed out of trouble!

Once there was a little girl. She was very curious about the world around her. One day, she decided to go to school and see what the classroom was like. When she entered, the room seemed very big to her. It was a strange place, and she was not sure what to do.

Suddenly, she noticed a large icy window on one wall of the classroom. She went over to take a closer look. The winter sun shone brightly through it, making the room feel cold. She was so interested by this window that she forgot to mind the teacher and the other students in the room.

The teacher noticed the little girl and gave her a gentle reminder to stay inside the classroom and mind her studies. The little girl smiled and nodded. She couldn't help but feel excited to explore this new environment. 

From then on, she would look forward to visiting her classroom every day. It might have been an icy room but the little girl didn't mind it one bit.

Once upon a time there was a rhinoceros who lived in the jungle. He was very weak and he didn't know what to do. He went to the lion to ask for help. The lion said that he would try to repair the rhinoceros.

So they went to work. The lion used his strong claws to fix the rhinoceros. The rhino thanked the lion and said that he felt much better.

They decided to go for a walk in the jungle. The rhino felt so strong now that he was repaired. He thanked the lion again and said goodbye. They both went off in different directions to explore the jungle.

The rhinoceros was so happy to feel strong again. He knew that he could do anything!

Anna liked to play hide and seek with her big brother Tom. He was good at finding places to hide, but Anna was good at peeking. She would look around the room and try to see a part of Tom that was not regular, like his shoe or his hair.

One day, they were playing in the living room. Tom said he would hide first, and Anna had to count to ten. Anna closed her eyes and counted slowly. When she was done, she opened her eyes and started to peek. She saw the couch, the table, the lamp, and the rug. They all looked regular. She saw the bookshelf, the window, the door, and the clock. They also looked regular. She saw the fireplace, the picture, the plant, and the vase. They looked regular too.

Anna was puzzled. Where was Tom? She walked around the room and peeked some more. She did not see any object that was not regular. She started to feel sad. Maybe Tom was too good at hiding. Maybe he had left the room. Maybe he did not want to play with her anymore.

She was about to give up when she heard a giggle. It came from behind the curtains. Anna ran to the window and pulled the curtains apart. There was Tom, hiding behind a big object that was not regular. It was a teddy bear. Tom had put the teddy bear in front of him and covered himself with the curtains. He thought Anna would not see him.

Anna laughed and hugged Tom. She said, "I found you! You are very clever, but I am very good at peeking. You can't trick me with a teddy bear. That is not a regular object. That is a toy. Let's play again!"

Tom smiled and agreed. He said, "You are right, Anna. You are very good at peeking. You are a smart sister. I like to play with you. Let's play again!" They took turns hiding and peeking, and had a lot of fun.

Tommy was playing in the garden with his toy truck. He liked to make it go vroom vroom on the grass and the dirt. He saw something moving on a leaf. It was a caterpillar. It was orange and fuzzy and had many legs.

"Hello, caterpillar," Tommy said. "Do you want to play with me?"

The caterpillar looked at Tommy with its tiny eyes. It did not say anything. It just crawled slowly on the leaf.

"Come on, caterpillar," Tommy said. "Don't be shy. I won't hurt you. You can trust me. I am your friend."

Tommy reached out his hand to touch the caterpillar. He wanted to feel how soft it was. But the caterpillar did not like that. It felt scared. It curled up into a ball and hid under the leaf.

"Hey, caterpillar, why did you do that?" Tommy asked. "I just wanted to say hi. Please come out and play with me."

But the caterpillar did not come out. It stayed under the leaf. It wanted to be alone. It did not trust Tommy. It did not want to play with him.

Tommy felt sad. He did not understand why the caterpillar did not like him. He thought it was a nice caterpillar. He thought they could be friends. He put his toy truck down and walked away. He looked for something else to play with in the garden.

Sara and Ben were playing with their dolls in the living room. They liked to pretend that their dolls were friends and had adventures together. Sara had a pink doll with long hair and a dress. Ben had a blue doll with a hat and a car.

"Let's go to the park with our dolls," Sara said. "They can have a picnic and play on the swings."

"OK," Ben said. "But we have to be careful. There might be thunder."

They put their dolls in a basket and went outside. The sky was gray and cloudy, but they did not mind. They walked to the park and found a nice spot under a tree. They spread a blanket and took out some cookies and juice for their dolls.

They were having fun, until they heard a loud boom. It was thunder. Sara and Ben looked up and saw lightning flash in the sky. They felt raindrops on their faces.

"Uh-oh," Sara said. "We have to go home. It's not safe here."

"But I don't want to quit playing," Ben said. "Our dolls are having fun."

"Ben, we have to quit," Sara said. "The thunder is scary and the rain is wet. Come on, grab your doll and the basket. We can play again tomorrow."

Sara picked up her pink doll and the blanket. Ben picked up his blue doll and the car. They ran back to their house, holding hands. They were glad to be safe and dry. They put their dolls on the couch and hugged them.

"Maybe tomorrow the sun will come out and we can go to the park again," Sara said.

"Maybe," Ben said. "But I still like thunder. It makes a cool noise."

Sara smiled and kissed his cheek. "You're silly, Ben. I love you."

"I love you too, Sara," Ben said. They snuggled with their dolls and watched the rain.

Amy was walking in the park. She saw a deep purse on the ground. She was very excited and put her hands into the purse. Suddenly, she saw something shiny and sparkly. It was a gold necklace! Amy was so happy, she ran home to show her family her new necklace. They were very excited and hugged her. Amy loved her new necklace and wore it every day. She was so proud of her new deep purse.

Once upon a time, there was a clever cat named Mittens. Mittens loved to drink tea every day. One day, Mittens' friend, a mouse named Jerry, came to visit. Jerry was not feeling well and was suffering from a cold. Mittens noticed that Jerry was coughing and sneezing a lot. 

Mittens asked Jerry if he would like some tea to help him feel better. Jerry nodded his head and Mittens quickly made a cup of tea for his friend. After drinking the tea, Jerry started to feel much better. 

From that day on, Mittens made sure to always have tea ready for his friends who were suffering from a cold. Mittens knew that tea could help make them feel better. And Jerry was grateful for his clever friend who always knew how to help.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. He loved to play outside with his neighbor, Sue. They had lots of fun playing with their red ball.

One day, Tim and Sue found a tasty apple on the ground. They wanted to return it to the tree. They tried to throw it up, but it fell back down. They tried again and again, but the apple just wouldn't go back to the tree.

Finally, Tim's mom came out and helped them. She put the apple in a basket and hung it on the tree. Tim and Sue were happy that they could return the apple. They went back to play with their red ball, and they shared the tasty apple with their neighbor.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the rain, but one day she accidentally dropped her favorite toy down the drain. She was very upset and didn't know what to do.

Lily's dad saw that she was sad and asked her what was wrong. When she told him about her toy, he knew he had to help. He got some tools and started to repair the drain. After a little while, he was able to get the toy out and give it back to Lily.

Lily was so happy and gave her dad a big hug. She learned that even when things go wrong, there's always someone who can help you fix them.

Once upon a time there was an old man who had a modern chest. Every day, he liked to clean it. He would take out all the things inside and wipe it with a cloth.

One day, he was so busy cleaning that he accidentally knocked over the chest. A lot of things fell out and broke! He was sad and tried to put the chest back together but it didn't work.

So he had to buy a new one. He went to the store and bought a modern chest. He put all of the things inside and thought it was perfect.

But when he went to open it the next day, the chest was stuck shut! He tried to open it, but it didn't work. He was so mad and sad that he never went back to clean it again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a blue toy car that she loved to play with. One day, Lily went to the park with her mom and forgot to bring her toy car. She was sad because she wanted to play with it.

When they got home, Lily remembered that she forgot her toy car at the park. Her mom told her not to worry and that they could go back to the park to get it. Lily was happy again.

When they got to the park, Lily found her blue toy car right where she left it. She was so happy to have it back and played with it all day long. From that day on, Lily never forgot to bring her toy car with her again.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved drinking coffee with his mommy every morning. One day, Timmy's mommy spilled the coffee on the floor and it made a big mess. Timmy was sad because he couldn't drink his coffee.

Timmy's mommy tried to clean up the mess, but it was too big. Timmy wanted to help his mommy, so he went to get a towel. When he came back, he saw that his mommy was crying. Timmy didn't know what to do, but he wanted to make his mommy happy.

Timmy had an idea. He went to get his favorite toy, a lucky teddy bear. He showed it to his mommy and said, "Look mommy, lucky bear will make you happy." Timmy's mommy smiled and hugged him. She was happy again. From that day on, Timmy and his mommy drank their coffee with lucky bear every morning.

Once upon a time, there was a dog named Spot. Spot loved to play fetch with his owner, Timmy. One day, Timmy threw Spot's bone very far and Spot chased after it. 

When Spot brought the bone back to Timmy, Timmy said, "Wow, that's an expensive bone! It looks like it's made of gold!" 

Spot didn't know what "expensive" meant, but he was happy to have his bone back. He wagged his tail and barked happily. 

Timmy and Spot played fetch for a while longer until it was time for dinner. Timmy gave Spot a treat and said, "Thanks for playing with me, Spot. You're the best dog ever!" 

Spot barked in agreement and licked Timmy's face. They went inside for dinner, happy and content.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to pick daisies in the field. One day, she found an ancient vase in the grass. 

"Look, mommy! I found a pretty vase!" Lily said, displaying the vase to her mother. 

"That's lovely, dear. Where did you find it?" her mother asked. 

"I found it in the field while I was picking daisies," Lily replied. 

Her mother smiled and said, "Let's display it on the mantel so everyone can see it." 

Lily was happy to show off her special find and placed it carefully on the mantel. From that day on, the ancient vase was proudly displayed in their home.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to play outside. One day, she saw a beautiful butterfly flying around her garden. She tried to catch it, but it flew away. 

Lily asked her mommy, "Where did the butterfly go?" Her mommy said, "It flew away to find some flowers to drink nectar from." 

Lily said, "Oh, I see. Thank you, mommy!" 

Later that day, Lily's wealthy neighbor came over to visit. She saw the butterfly in the garden and said, "What a pretty butterfly! I wish I had one like that." 

Lily said, "You can't have it. It's not yours. It's free to fly wherever it wants." 

The wealthy neighbor was surprised by Lily's wise words and said, "You're right. I'm sorry. Thank you for teaching me that." 

Lily felt happy that she could share her knowledge with her neighbor and that the butterfly could fly freely in her garden.

Once upon a time, there was a great rock. It was so big and smooth that everyone wanted to touch it. One day, there was a child and he wanted to move it. He pushed and pushed with all his might, but the rock wouldn't move. After trying and trying, he stopped and felt so sad.

The next day, he came back with his friends. They all pushed and pulled, but the rock still wouldn't move. They all felt so sad and regretted trying to move it.

The days went by and in time, the child realized that the rock was great just where it was. He didn't need to move it, he was content just looking at it. Eventually, all of his friends realized the same thing- the rock was great!

Once there was a baby duck who loved to carry things. He was small, but very strong and could carry a lot. One night, he saw an attractive butterfly while out on a walk. He wanted to show it to his family, so without thinking, Baby Duck picked it up and started to carry it home.

Suddenly he heard a loud noise and looked up to see an angry bird flying towards him. The bird was so angry it wanted to take the butterfly away from Baby Duck! Baby Duck quickly put the butterfly down and started to run away but it was too late. The angry bird caught up to him and pecked at him until he was too tired to run.

Unfortunately, the butterfly was gone and Baby Duck never found it again. All he had left was some scrapes and bruises from his bad encounter with the angry bird. He was very sad, but at least he learned an important lesson never to carry a butterfly away in the night.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Jack. Jack loved to run and play outside with his friends. One day, Jack's mom told him about a big race that was happening in their town. She said that the winner would get a shiny medal.

Jack was so excited! He wanted to win the medal more than anything. He practiced running every day until the day of the race. When the race started, Jack ran as fast as he could. He was so close to the finish line, but then he tripped and fell. Jack was miserable because he thought he had lost the race.

But then something amazing happened. The boy who was in first place stopped and helped Jack up. He said that he didn't want to win if it meant leaving someone behind. Jack and the other boy crossed the finish line together, holding hands. The judges were so impressed by their kindness that they gave them both a medal. Jack was so happy and grateful that he hugged the other boy. From that day on, Jack knew that winning wasn't everything and that being kind was more important.

Once upon a time, there was a lonely, black cat. The cat lived in a big house all by itself. It had no friends to play with. Every day, the cat would look out the window and see other cats playing outside. The lonely, black cat felt very sad.

One day, a nice family moved into the house. The family had a little girl who loved cats. The little girl saw the lonely, black cat and wanted to play with it. The cat was very happy to see the little girl.

The little girl and the lonely, black cat played together all day. They ran around the house and had lots of fun. When it was time for bed, the little girl let the cat settle in her room. The lonely, black cat was not lonely anymore. It had a new friend, and they lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to bake cakes with her mommy. One day, they decided to make a chocolate cake. Her mommy took out the mixer and started mixing the ingredients together. Lily thought it looked funny when the mixer spun around and around.

After they finished making the cake, Lily's big brother Jack came into the kitchen. He saw the cake and said, "That cake looks yucky. I don't want to eat it." Lily felt sad when she heard Jack tease her cake. She worked hard to make it with her mommy.

Her mommy said, "Jack, that's not nice. Lily worked hard on this cake. We should always be kind to others and not tease them." Jack felt bad and said sorry to Lily. They all sat down and enjoyed a piece of the yummy chocolate cake together. The moral of the story is to always be kind to others and not tease them.

Once upon a time, there was a deep, blue sea. In the sea, there was a big wave. Every morning, the wave would travel far and wide. 

One day, the wave decided to go even further. So, it traveled and traveled until it reached a beautiful polisher. This polisher was very special. Its job was to make things shine. 

The wave said to the polisher, "Please make me shine!" The polisher said, "Of course! I will make you sparkle." 

The polisher worked very hard and soon, the wave was sparkling like never before. It said goodbye to the polisher and set off on a new adventure. 

From that day on, the wave looked very pretty and it was always happy and smiling.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to eat food, especially pink cupcakes. One day, Lily's mom asked her, "Lily, what do you want to eat for lunch?"

Lily replied, "I want food, please. Can I get some pink cupcakes?"

Her mom smiled and said, "Sure, Lily. Let's go get some pink cupcakes from the bakery."

Lily was so happy to get her favorite food. She ate the pink cupcakes and shared some with her mom too. They both enjoyed the delicious food together. From that day on, Lily asked for pink cupcakes every time she wanted a treat.

Lily and Max are friends. They like to play with toys and eat cookies. One day, they go to Max's house after school. Max's mom gives them two cookies each. They are glad.

But then, Lily sees that Max has a cookie with chocolate chips. She likes chocolate chips. She wants Max's cookie. She says, "Give me your cookie, Max. I want it."

Max says, "No, Lily. This is my cookie. You have your own cookie. Go away."

Lily gets angry. She tries to grab Max's cookie. Max holds it tight. They fight over the cookie. They pull and push and shout.

Max's mom hears them. She comes to the room. She sees them fighting. She is not glad. She says, "Stop it, Lily and Max. Fighting is bad. You have to share and be nice. If you don't, you will have no cookies at all."

Lily and Max stop fighting. They feel sorry. They say, "Sorry, Max's mom. Sorry, Max. Sorry, Lily."

Max's mom says, "It's okay. I'm glad you are sorry. But you have to learn to share. Here, I have more cookies. You can each have one more. But this time, you can choose which one you want."

Lily and Max smile. They say, "Thank you, Max's mom. Thank you for the cookies. We will share and be nice."

They choose their cookies. They eat them. They are glad. They hug and play with toys. They are friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved playing in the garden and digging in the soil. One day, she found an old vase buried in the dirt. 

"Look at this vase! It's so old," said Lily.

"It's not old, it's modern," said her mom.

"What does modern mean?" asked Lily.

"It means new and up-to-date," explained her mom.

Lily was so happy to have found the modern vase in the soil. She became even more excited when her mom filled it with fresh flowers. From that day on, Lily made sure to look for more modern treasures in the garden.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Jessica. She was three years old and loved to play. One day, Jessica's mommy took her to the park.

As soon as Jessica arrived at the park, she remembered her favorite thing to do. She wanted to play tag with her mommy. "Let's play tag, Mommy!" said Jessica. Her mommy agreed, and they started running around the park.

Then, Jessica saw an apple tree. It was so light, and the apples were beautiful. Jessica remembered that her mommy told her not to touch the apples, so she clapped her hands and smiled.

"Remember, Jessica, don't touch the apples," her mommy said. Jessica smiled, happy she remembered her mommy's words. Together, Jessica and her mommy had lots of fun at the park that day.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy called Jack. Jack was a very restless child. One day, he went for a walk in the woods and soon he got very tired. So Jack looked around to find a spot to take a nap. 

Then he spotted a big sack under a tree. He quickly laid down inside the sack and soon he was fast asleep. Jack felt so good that he just kept on sleeping. 

The sun was setting and the night was getting darker. Jack was still resting peacefully inside the sack. He didn't wake up even when a beautiful deer walked by. 

Jack slept the entire night inside the sack. In the morning, when the sun came up, he finally woke up. His nap had made him feel so rested, just like fresh pancakes with butter and jam!

Once upon a time, there was a fit man. He had a big red motorcycle and he loved it very much. One day he rode it through a big, dark forest. Suddenly, he heard a tiny voice shouting, "Save me!" 

The man stopped his motorcycle and looked around. He saw a small kitten stuck in a tree. He asked, "What are you doing way up there?" 

The kitten replied, "I was chasing a bird and I got too far away! I can't climb down." 

The man said, "Don't worry. I will save you." He jumped off his motorcycle, climbed up the tree, and carefully grabbed the little kitten. He placed it on his motorcycle seat. 

The kitten purred and said, "Thank you. You are fit and strong." 

The man smiled and said, "You are welcome." He drove the kitten home and they became very good friends.

Once upon a time there was a kid called Bob. Bob was very happy and played all day with his friends. One day, Bob and his friends decided to play near a deep lake. As they were playing, Bob became too close to the edge and he fell into the lake. His friends tried to help but Bob disappeared underwater. 

After Bob vanished, his friends called for help and the police arrived. But it was too late - Bob had drowned. Everyone was very sad and Bob's family felt a deep regret. 

The next day, a wake was held to remember Bob. Everyone was very sad, but they were also happy to remember all the happy times they had together. 

Suddenly, Bob's family heard a loud splash in the lake. They raced to the edge of the lake and there they saw a very scared Bob! He had been underwater all night, but he had managed to find his way out. Bob's family was so happy that they screamed with joy. 

The moral of the story is that we should never regret things that have happened in the past. Bob's family learned this the hard way and now everyone is a lot happier!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a gray cat named Mittens. One day, Lily went to her friend's house to play. She saw her friend's toy and asked if she could borrow it. Her friend said yes and Lily was very happy. 

After a while, Lily got too hot and wanted to go home. She said goodbye to her friend and went back to her house. When she got home, she saw that Mittens was sleeping on her bed. She said, "Mittens, you look so cozy. Can I borrow some of your heat?" Mittens woke up and meowed. Lily took that as a yes and cuddled with Mittens. 

Lily's mom came in and asked, "Why are you so hot?" Lily said, "I borrowed some of Mittens' heat." Her mom smiled and said, "That's very nice of Mittens." Lily was happy that she could borrow her friend's toy and her cat's heat.

One day, a big bus with a nice driver came to town. The driver had a big hat and a big smile. He said, "Hello! I am the driver. Do you want to see my bus?" The bus was very impressive. It was big and shiny, and it had lots of seats for people to sit.

A little boy named Tim came to see the bus. He said, "Wow! That is a big bus! Can I go inside?" The driver said, "Yes, you can! Come on!" Tim went inside the bus and saw many things. The bus had a place to display pictures. Tim saw a picture of a cat, a dog, and a big tree.

The driver told Tim, "I drive this bus to take people from one place to another. We can go fast or slow. We can go near or far. It is fun to drive this bus!" Tim said, "I want to be a driver too when I grow up!" The driver smiled and said, "You can be a great driver, Tim! Just remember to be nice and always help people."

Tim had a fun day with the impressive bus and the nice driver. He went home and told his mom and dad about his day. They were happy that Tim had a good time. Tim knew that one day, he would be a great driver, just like his new friend.

One sunny day, a little girl woke up early to go on an adventure. With her trusty shield and a long stick in her hand, she marched off into the forest. As she walked, she heard a strange noise coming from somewhere. The sound was loud and was disturbing the calm of the forest. The brave girl decided to find its source and marched on.

Eventually, the little girl found a big bird stuck behind a log. She quickly put down her shield so the bird could not run away. Then, she gently spoke to it: "What are you doing here?" The big bird was surprised and afraid. It said, "I was looking for food, but I got scared and ran away. Will you help me?"

The brave girl smiled and said, "I'll help you as soon as I get my shield back. I need it to protect me if I get lost in the forest." The bird was thankful, and so the girl placed her long stick on the forest floor and put her shield back on her shoulder. Together, they managed to get the bird back safely to its nest. 

The little girl and the bird said goodbye, and the girl went on her way. She had learned a valuable lesson: be brave and never give up!

Once upon a time, in a big green park, there was a little tree. The tree was not very big, but it had many nice leaves. It wanted to be useful, so it would offer shade to all the animals in the park. The sun was very hot, and the animals loved to sit under the tree's leaves.

One day, the tree saw a small, tired bird. The bird was very hot from flying in the sun. The tree thought, "I can help the bird!" So, the tree offered its shade to the bird. The bird was happy and thanked the tree. The bird told all its friends about the nice tree that helped it.

Soon, more and more animals came to the tree for shade. The tree was very happy to be useful. It loved making friends and helping the animals stay cool in the hot sun. The tree grew bigger and bigger, and so did its shade. All the animals loved the tree, and they all lived happily in the park.

Once upon a time, there was an old man. He liked to listen to the bells that would ring in the city. One day, he decided to buy a firework. He thought it would be fun.

He lit the firework and waited for it to go off. Suddenly, there was a loud bang and it made the old man jump. He saw the bad firework had burst into lots of little pieces. They were going everywhere!

The old man ran away scared. He left the bad firework behind. As he ran off, he heard the bell ring again. He knew it was time to go home.

Once upon a time, there was a little rabbit named Bun who loved to dig. One day, Bun was digging in the ground when he found a big, round root. "Oh wow!" Bun said, "this root seems very big and yummy!"

Suddenly, Bun heard a voice behind him. "What are you doing?" asked a little bird. "I'm digging for roots," said Bun. "But this one seems too big for me to eat alone." The little bird replied, "I can help you! I know where to find more rabbits who can help us eat it."

So, Bun and the little bird went on a journey to find more rabbits. They met many animals along the way, but none of them seemed to know where the other rabbits were. Bun started to feel troubled, but the little bird said, "Don't worry, we will find them soon!"

Finally, they found a group of rabbits who were happy to help them eat the big, round root. Bun and the little bird were very happy too. They all sat together and enjoyed the delicious root. Bun said, "Thank you for helping me. I'm glad we found each other!" And the little bird replied, "Me too! We make a great team!"

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy had a big box of blocks. He loved to play with them and build towers. One day, Timmy found some really old blocks. They were very ancient! 

Timmy tried to build a tower with the ancient blocks, but they kept falling down. He tried and tried, but it didn't work. Finally, Timmy got an idea. He decided to stack the ancient blocks on top of the new blocks. 

Timmy stood up and carefully placed the ancient blocks on top of the new blocks. To his surprise, the tower stood tall and strong! Timmy was so happy that he jumped up and down. He couldn't wait to play with his new tower of blocks. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and explore the world around her. One day, she went on an adventure in the forest with her friend, Max.

As they walked through the forest, they came across an ancient tree. Lily was amazed by how big and old it was. Max said, "Let's pack a picnic and eat it under the tree!" Lily thought that was a great idea.

They went to the nearby stream to get some water for their picnic. But when they got there, they saw that the water was all muddy and dirty. Lily said, "Oh no, we can't drink this water!" Max replied, "Don't worry, I have an idea. Let's pack some water from home in our backpacks."

Lily and Max packed their backpacks with sandwiches, fruit, and clean water. They had a great picnic under the ancient tree and enjoyed the beautiful nature around them. As they packed up to leave, they heard a loud noise. It was a bear! They quickly ran away, but Lily said to Max, "That was scary! But I'm glad we packed our picnic and water, or else we would have been very hungry and thirsty!"

Once upon a time there was a little boy named Jack. He was playing in his living room when he saw something exciting. He saw a pink eraser! "Wow!" he said. Jack grabbed the eraser and started running around the room. He was having so much fun.

Suddenly, his mom called out from the kitchen, "Jack, dinner is ready!" Jack stopped running and said, "OK mom!" He started to walk towards the kitchen but he was still carrying the eraser.

As he walked, he heard a loud noise coming from the kitchen. He looked inside and saw his mom. She was frowning and not happy. She said, "Jack, why did you come in here with the eraser? Please put it back where you found it." Jack quickly put the eraser back and apologized.

The loud noise was a warning that Jack had done something wrong. He should have listened to his mom. If he had, things wouldn't have gone so badly.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to collect things. One day, she found a brick. It was a big, red brick. Lily thought it was a very special brick.

Lily wanted to build something with her brick. She asked her friends if they had any bricks too. Her friends were very generous. They gave Lily their bricks to use. Soon, Lily had a lot of bricks.

With all the bricks, Lily and her friends built a little house. They were happy and proud of their work. They played in the house all day. From that day on, they always shared and helped each other.

Once upon a time there was a kind witch. She always tried to do nice things and she wanted everyone to get along. One day, a little boy came along who was unhappy. He didn't have any friends and he was very sad. The witch tried to help but the boy didn't want to accept her help. He didn't believe in being nice or wanting to make friends. So the witch tried harder and she was very patient. Finally, the little boy accepted her help and learnt that getting along with others was much more fun.

So, the moral of the story is that if we accept help, then good things can happen. We can all be kind and kind actions often make us feel good.

Sam and Mia are friends who like to play pirates. They have a big cardboard box that they pretend is their ship. They also have a flag, a map, and an anchor. The anchor is a heavy rock with a rope tied to it.

One day, they decide to sail to a new island. They look at the map and follow the clues. They see a big tree, a red flower, and a hill. They are almost there. But then, the wind blows hard and their ship moves fast. Sam and Mia are scared.

"Help! We are going too fast!" Mia says.

"Don't worry! We have an anchor. It will stop us!" Sam says.

He throws the anchor out of the box and into the grass. The rope pulls tight and the ship slows down. The anchor is dependable. It does not let go.

"Phew! That was close!" Sam says.

"Yes, thank you, anchor!" Mia says.

They look around and see the island. It has a big X on it. They smile and jump out of the box. They have found the treasure. They are happy pirates.

Sara and Ben were playing in the garden. They liked to splash in the puddles and make mud pies. But their mom told them to come inside soon, because it was going to rain.

"Come on, Sara, let's go inside. Mom said it will rain," Ben said.

"No, I want to play more. It's fun," Sara said.

She did not listen to Ben. She ran to the big puddle and jumped in. She got very wet and dirty.

Suddenly, the sky became dark and the wind blew hard. It started to rain. Sara was scared. She wanted to go inside, but she could not find Ben. He had gone inside with mom.

Sara cried. She was cold and wet and alone. She looked for a place to hide from the rain. She saw a big box near the fence. She ran to the box and got inside. She hoped it would keep her dry.

But the box was not a good place to hide. It was old and weak. The rain made it wet and soft. It started to fall apart. Sara was still wet and cold. She wished she had listened to Ben and mom.

Then she heard a loud noise. It was a dog. A big, mean dog. It lived in the house next to the fence. It saw Sara in the box. It wanted to bite her. It barked and ran to the box.

Sara was very scared. She did not know what to do. She could not escape from the dog. She screamed for help.

Ben heard Sara scream. He ran to the window and saw the dog and the box. He knew Sara was in trouble. He ran to mom and told her.

Mom and Ben ran to the garden. They saw the dog and the box. They shouted at the dog. The dog was afraid of mom and Ben. It ran away.

Mom and Ben ran to the box. They lifted it up and saw Sara. She was wet and dirty and crying. Mom hugged her and said, "Sara, are you okay? We were so worried about you."

Sara hugged mom and said, "I'm sorry, mom. I'm sorry, Ben. I should have listened to you. I was silly and stubborn. I'm sorry."

Mom and Ben said, "It's okay, Sara. We're glad you're safe. We love you."

They took Sara inside. They gave her a warm bath and dry clothes. They gave her a hug and a kiss. They told her a story and sang her a song. They made her feel better.

Sara learned a lesson. She learned to listen to mom and Ben. She learned to be careful and smart. She learned to be thankful and sorry. She learned to be happy and safe.

Once there was a clever monkey. He lived up in the trees and loved to eat bananas. But one day he couldn't find any bananas anywhere! He started to get really hungry, he could feel it in his stomach. The only thing the monkey could think of was to raise his arms up high in the sky and hope for a miracle.

The monkey waited patiently with his arms in the air, not knowing what else to do. Then suddenly, a soft breeze floated by and brought a ripe yellow banana right to the monkey! He quickly grabbed it and smiled with joy as he ate the sweet banana.

From that day forward, the clever monkey always raised his arms up to the sky in desperate need of a banana. Sure enough, his clever trick always worked and the wind would bring him a delicious snack.

Once upon a time there was a fox and a rabbit. The fox saw a silver ball in the forest. He wanted to play with it.

"Hey! That looks cool!" the fox said.

The rabbit said, "That looks like it belongs to someone. We should not take it." 

But the fox did not listen. He set the silver ball down and started kicking it. He kicked it further and further until it rolled in the river.

The fox and the rabbit ran to the river. But it was too late. The ball was gone.

The fox was sad. But the rabbit said, "This was bad. Now we must go until we find the owner of the silver ball." 

Sadly, they never found it.

Once upon a time, there was a small boy named Josh. He wanted to build something special, so he gathered up some sticks, stones, and leaves. Josh was very patient and carefully put them together. Suddenly, he saw a little lizard. The lizard was very calm and patient too.

Josh got an idea. He started to build a home for the lizard. He worked and worked, using the sticks and stones he found. He was so careful and determined that it took a very long time. But in the end, he had built a perfect little home.

The lizard was so happy that it stayed in the home all the time. Josh visited it every day to say hello. He even brought it some food and water.

The little lizard and Josh were the best of friends, and they were both happy.

Once upon a time, there lived two friends, James and Amy. One day, James went to Amy's house to bring her a present. He was feeling excited and happy about it. 

When James knocked on the door, Amy opened it and asked, "What do you have?" 

James smiled and said, "A present for you! I hope you like it."

But Amy said, "Why did you bring it? Did you expect something in return?"

James felt surprised and sad. He said, "I just wanted you to know that I appreciate you."

Amy felt ashamed and recognized that she had been selfish. She said, "I'm sorry, James. Thank you for the present."

James smiled and said, "You are very welcome!"

The two friends hugged and were happy that their friendship was strong enough to forget the moment of selfishness. From then on, they often exchanged presents to show their appreciation for each other.

Once upon a time, there was a dog named Max. Max was a useful dog. He helped his owner, Jane, with many things. Max could fetch things and open doors. Jane loved Max very much.

One day, Max and Jane went to the park. Max saw a little bird that couldn't fly. The bird was sad. Max wanted to help the bird. Max encouraged the bird to try to fly. Max barked and jumped, showing the bird how to flap its wings.

The bird tried to fly, and it worked! The bird was happy, and Max was happy too. Jane was proud of Max for being so helpful. They went home and had a fun day together.

Tim was walking through the park with his mom. He loved going to the park! He ran towards the big slide and started to climb.

Then his mom yelled, "Tim, come back! It's getting dark."

Tim didn't want to leave the slide. He liked playing there too much. He started to get bossy.

"No! I don't wanna go!" he yelled. 

His mom was patient. She tried to explain.

"It's important to listen," she said calmly. "When the light goes away, it's time to go home." 

Tim heard her words and finally agreed. He followed his mom out of the park, but he was already thinking about the fun he would have at the park the next day.

Once upon a time, there was a curious girl named Jane. She adored watching the video her mother had given her. Every day she would check to make sure it was in her room.

One day, she was playing in the garden and completely forgot about the video. When she got back in the house, it was gone! She searched high and low, but she couldn't find it anywhere.

Jane felt so sad and regretful. She really missed watching the video with her mom.

Finally, her mom found the video under the couch. Jane was so happy and promised herself that she would never forget about it again. That way, she could watch it with her mom every day.

Once upon a time there was a boy named Bob who liked to explore. One day he went on an adventure to the river and he saw an alligator. Bob was very scared but the alligator was very friendly.

The alligator said to Bob, "Hello, Bob. Would you like to come swimming in the clear river with me?"

Bob was still scared but he wanted to be brave and agreed. They both jumped into the river and started swimming.

Suddenly a big wave split them apart. Bob floated one way and the alligator another. Bob tried to swim back to the alligator but he was too tired.

Bob shouted, "Help! I want to swim back to the alligator!"

The alligator heard his plea and swam back to him. They hugged each other and began swimming together again. From that day on, Bob and the alligator had a special friendship. They swam together in the clear river every day.

Once upon a time there were two brothers, Dan and Sam. Dan was the older brother and Sam was the younger brother. One day, the brothers decided to draw pictures. Dan was very careful when drawing his picture and he did it very slowly. On the other hand, Sam was in a rush and he was excited to finish his picture quickly. 

After a while, Dan's picture was almost finished. He had carefully drawn a beautiful house and flowers. But suddenly, a gust of wind blew the paper away and it flew out the window. Dan stood there and sighed. When Sam saw this, he shrugged and said, "It's ok, Dan. You can do it again." 

Dan shook his head sadly and said, "No, it's too hard to draw this picture again. I will never be able to make it look like it did before. It's broken." 

But Sam gave Dan a hug and said, "Just keep on trying and don't give up. Even when something breaks, you can always put it back together if you just keep on trying." 

Moral of the story: Even when things seem broken, you can always try to put them back together if you just keep on trying.

Once upon a time, there was a girl called Mary. Mary went to the factory with her mum. The factory was very weird. When Mary was inside, she counted all the machines. She counted five machines and two workers.

Mary's mum said: "Hey Mary, what are you doing?"

Mary said: "I'm counting the machines and the workers. I'm learning how to count."

Mary's mum said: "That's a good idea. Counting is a very important skill."

Then, Mary saw something strange. There were workers who didn't have any shoes. Mary was surprised. She said: "Mummy, why don't those workers have shoes?"

Mary's mum said: "I'm sorry, honey. Not everybody can afford the things that we have. That's why it's important to share what we have and help others when we can."

Mary learned a lesson that day. She learned that sharing is important and that counting can help us learn how to share with others.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Annie. She was three years old and very attractive. Every day, she hung out with her friends at the park.

One day when she was at the park, she suddenly fell over and bumped her arm. It became so swollen and hurt so much, her parents took her to the hospital to get an x-ray.

At the hospital, they told Annie she had to sit very still while they took an x-ray of her arm. Annie was a bit scared, but she didn't move while they took the x-ray. She even made a funny face when they were done!

Later, the doctor said that the x-ray showed Annie was OK. Her arm was a bit sore, but it would get better soon. She was so relieved. And the best part was, she got to hang out with her friends in the park again!

Once upon a time, there was a mommy and a daddy who were always sad and dull. They never wanted to do anything fun.

One day the mommy said, "Let's go on a holiday!" The daddy thought it was a good idea and they began to plan.

Mommy said, "We should cook something special for our holiday." Daddy said he had a great idea and went to get some food.

He came back with apples, oranges and a few other things. They put them all in a bowl and began to cook.

Mommy said, "Let's make a nice apple pie. It will be yummy!" Daddy agreed and they started to make the pie.

When it was done, they both tasted it and smiled. "It's delicious!" they said.

From that day on, they were no longer dull and sad. They were happy and went on many more holidays.

Bob was walking in the park when he heard a buzzing sound. He looked around and saw a hairy mosquito. He wanted to get rid of it, so he tried to strike it with his hand. But the mosquito was too fast and it kept flying away. Bob tried to strike it again and again, but it was no use.

He was getting very frustrated and angry. He yelled at the mosquito, but it just kept buzzing around. He tried to hit it one more time and this time, he was successful. He saw the mosquito crash to the ground and he was relieved.

Bob was smiling now and no longer angry. His mission was complete and he had gotten rid of the hairy mosquito. What a relief!

Once there was a brown youth. The youth was out picking flowers in a field. He chose the prettiest ones he could find. He picked pink ones, yellow ones and even some blue ones. All of them were so lovely. 

He climbed up a hill that was near the field and stopped to take a rest. When he looked out he saw a little brown dog. He called out to the dog and it came running towards him. The youth and the dog had a lot of fun playing together.

The youth decided to pick some flowers for the dog. He picked a daisy and held it out to the dog. The dog sniffed the flower and wagged its tail. The youth thought the dog looked very happy. He continued picking more flowers and gave them all to the little brown dog. The youth and the dog were very happy together.

Tim and Jen like to play in the kitchen. They find a big bowl and a big spoon. They pretend to make a cake. They stir and stir and stir. They add flour and sugar and eggs and milk. They stir some more.

Mom comes in and sees the mess. She is not happy. She says, "What are you doing? You made a filthy mess! This is not a cake, this is a quiz!" She points to the bowl. "What is this? What is that? How many eggs did you use? How much flour did you spill?"

Tim and Jen do not know the answers. They look at each other. They are scared. They say, "We are sorry, Mom. We just wanted to have fun. We did not mean to make a mess."

Mom sighs. She says, "I know, I know. But you have to be careful in the kitchen. You could hurt yourself or break something. And you have to clean up after yourself. Come on, let's get a cloth and a mop and clean this up. Then we can have a real cake for dessert." She smiles.

Tim and Jen smile too. They say, "OK, Mom. We will help you. We love you. And we love cake." They hug Mom and follow her to get the cloth and the mop. They learn their lesson. They do not play in the kitchen again. They play in the yard instead.

Lily and Tom were on a big boat with their mom and dad. They were going to a new place far away. Lily liked to look at the water and the birds. Tom liked to play with his toy cars and trucks.

One day, the boat stopped at a port. A port is a place where boats can park and people can get off or on. Mom and dad said they had to sign some papers at the port. They said Lily and Tom could stay on the boat with a nice lady who worked there.

Lily and Tom were a little scared. They did not know the lady or the port. They wanted to stay with mom and dad. But mom and dad said they would be back soon and gave them a hug and a kiss.

"Be brave, Lily and Tom," mom said. "We will see you in a little while."

The lady smiled and said, "Don't worry, kids. I will take good care of you. Do you want to see some pictures of the port? I have a book here."

Lily and Tom nodded. They followed the lady to a table where she had a book. The book had many pictures of the port. There were boats, people, animals, and buildings. The lady told them the names of the things they saw.

Lily and Tom liked the book. They learned some new words. They asked the lady questions. The lady answered them. They felt less scared. They felt more curious.

Soon, mom and dad came back. They had signed the papers. They thanked the lady for watching Lily and Tom. They said they were ready to go to the new place.

Lily and Tom hugged the lady and said goodbye. They showed mom and dad the book and told them what they had seen and learned. Mom and dad were proud of them.

"You are very brave, Lily and Tom," dad said. "You made a new friend and learned new things. We are happy you had fun at the port."

Lily and Tom smiled. They were happy too. They went back to the boat with mom and dad. They waved to the lady and the port. They were ready for the next adventure.

There was once a little girl named Liza. She was three years old and she loved to explore. One day, Liza and her mommy went to the harbor. When they got there, Liza saw lots of boats and birds. She was very excited!

Her mommy said to her, "Let's go on a boat ride! What do you think?"

Liza smiled and said, "Yes! That sounds great!"

So they got on a boat and went out on the harbor. But after some time, Liza got tired and felt uncomfortable. 

"Mommy," she said, "I want to go home now."

Her mommy understood and said, "Okay, let's go home. We can come back to the harbor another time."

So they went back home and Liza was feeling much better. She learned that exploring can be fun, but sometimes it's better to go home and rest.

Once upon a time, there was a young girl named Bobbie who enjoyed going to the beach with her family. She was so excited when she saw a cooler that her parents had bought. Bobbie wanted to take it with them the next day.

When the family arrived at the beach, Bobbie decided to put her things in the cooler. Her mom said, "No, we need that cooler for drinks." Bobbie was disappointed.

Suddenly, Bobbie spotted another cooler nearby, and asked her parents if they could use it instead. Her dad replied, "Yes, we can replace our cooler with that one."

The family spent the day at the beach and had lots of fun. Bobbie kept her things in the new cooler. She enjoyed playing in the sand and splashing in the water. 

When it was time to go home, Bobbie thanked her parents for helping her replace the cooler. They were so happy that she was able to enjoy the day at the beach. The family drove home with the cooler full of wonderful memories.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to spend her days playing with her toys and watching cartoons. One day, her mom woke her up early and said, "Lily, today is a serious day. We need to clean the house."

Lily didn't want to clean the house. She wanted to play. But her mom said, "Cleaning is important. We need to take care of our home." So Lily helped her mom clean the house. They swept the floors, dusted the furniture, and washed the dishes.

After they finished, Lily felt proud. She realized that sometimes we have to do things we don't want to do, but it's important to take care of our responsibilities. From that day on, Lily became a responsible little girl who always helped her mom around the house.

Once upon a time there was a comet that could fly. All of the animals were so amazed by it.

One day, a gifted little girl named Lola saw the comet fly by and said, "I must ride it!" She made a wish on a star, and then the comet suddenly came down and stopped right in front of her.

Lola said to the comet, "Please let me ride you!" But the comet said, "No, I'm not allowed to let anyone ride me." This made Lola very sad, so she started to cry.

Just then, a magical fox appeared. He said, "Why don't you ask me? I can help you with your problem."

Lola told him her wish, and the fox said, "I will help you if you promise to be careful." Lola agreed, and the fox made it so she could ride the comet.

Lola thanked the fox, and then hopped onto the comet. She waved goodbye to the fox as the comet flew off into the night sky.

Lola was so happy and had the best ride ever on the comet!

Sarah and her mommy were in the park discussing. Sarah saw a boot and told her mommy about it. Her mommy knelt down and told her it was an elderly boot. It belonged to an old man who was walking around the park earlier. 

Together they decided they would take the boot with them. Sarah brought the boot to the elderly man and he seemed very happy. He thanked her with a big smile and said that he could now go home and continue his walk. 

Sarah and her mommy said goodbye to the elderly man and walked home. Sarah was carrying the boot and felt very proud of herself. She was so glad she had been kind to the elderly man and was happy that he could finish his walk.

Lily liked to draw with her crayons. She was very creative. She drew on paper, on walls, on books, on clothes. She did not care if she made a mess. She did not listen to Mommy and Daddy when they told her to stop.

One day, Mommy and Daddy were very angry. They saw Lily's drawings on their new sofa. They asked Lily, "Did you do this?" Lily was scared. She did not want to get in trouble. She did not tell the truth. She said, "No, it was not me. It was the cat."

Mommy and Daddy did not believe Lily. They knew she was lying. They said, "Lily, you have to wash the sofa. You have to wash all the things you drew on. You have to wash your hands and face. And you have to say sorry. You have to learn to tell the truth."

Lily did not like to wash. She did not like to say sorry. She cried and cried. She said, "I do not want to wash. I do not want to say sorry. I want to draw. I want to be creative."

Mommy and Daddy did not listen to Lily. They made her wash the sofa. They made her wash all the things she drew on. They made her wash her hands and face. And they made her say sorry. Lily was very unhappy. She did not have any fun. She did not have any crayons. She learned that lying was bad. She learned that being creative was not always good. She wished she had told the truth.

Once upon a time there was a little boy, who was three years old. He liked to dress up fancy and he even had a special hat.

One day, he decided to celebrate the birthday of his new leg. He was so excited! He put on his fancy hat and he grabbed his new leg and went outside.

When he arrived outside there were lots of friends waiting for him. They had also dressed up fancy and each of them brought something nice for his leg.

â€œCan I try it on?â€ asked one of the boys.

The little boy nodded and gave it to him. The boy was so happy with his new leg.

â€œLet's celebrate!â€ the little boy said with a big smile on his face.

The friends all started to laugh and to celebrate and to have lots of fun. They played together, laughed together and ate cake together. 

The little boy was so happy that he could celebrate his new leg and have so much fun with his friends.

Once upon a time, there was a big, ancient tree. It was so old that it could understand what the animals said. The tree had a big carpet of soft green grass under it. Many animals came to play on the carpet.

One day, a little rabbit named Tim came to the tree. He saw the carpet and wanted to play on it. He hopped and rolled on the soft grass. Tim was very happy.

The ancient tree saw Tim and smiled. It understood that Tim loved the carpet. So, the tree made the carpet bigger for Tim and his friends. All the animals came to play on the big carpet. They played and laughed under the ancient tree. And they all lived happily ever after.

Once there was a very big sun in the sky. Everyone was happy when it shone down, and they could play outside in the warm light.

One day, a stupid bird thought that it would be fun to fly too close to the sun. It kept on flapping its wings and going higher, until the heat became too much. 

The sun wouldn't allow the bird to come any closer - it was too hot. The bird kept trying, but the sun wouldn't let it get any closer. 

So in the end, the stupid bird had to fly away. From then on, it was always more careful when flying close to the sun.

One day a little girl went for a walk. As she was walking, she saw a big bush. It was very green, and she was very proud of it. She wanted to show everyone how proud she was, so she gave the bush a big hug.

Then the little girl started to repeat the word "proud". She repeated it over and over, until the bush started to feel proud too.

The little girl was very happy. She was so proud, she wanted to hug the bush again! So she did, and she kept repeating the word "proud" as she embraced it.

She knew that bush was very happy now, and that it felt proud. She was happy too, because she was able to make the bush feel proud. 

The little girl and the bush stayed friends for a long time, and every time the little girl hugged it, the bush knew it was very special, and that it was loved.

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play with toys and books. But today they have a problem. They both want the same toy car. They fight for the toy car. They pull and push and shout.

Mom hears the noise. She comes to see what is wrong. She sees Lily and Ben fighting. She is not happy. She says, "Stop fighting! Fighting is bad. You have to share and be nice. Why are you fighting?"

Lily and Ben stop fighting. They look at Mom. They feel sorry. They tell Mom the truth. They say, "We both want the toy car. We like the toy car. We don't want to share the toy car." They are honest.

Mom nods. She says, "I understand. You both like the toy car. But you have to share. Sharing is good. You have other toys and books. You can take turns with the toy car. How about Lily plays with the toy car for five minutes, and then Ben plays with the toy car for five minutes? Is that fair?"

Lily and Ben think. They agree. They say, "OK, Mom. That is fair. We will share and take turns. We are sorry for fighting. We are still friends." They hug Mom. They hug each other. They play with the toy car and other toys and books. They are happy.

Once there was a very strong parent who could manage anything. The parent, Mrs. Williams, had a 3 year old daughter named Sarah who was just learning to do things for herself. 

One day Mrs. Williams said to Sarah, â€œYou are so strong, Sarah. Do you think you can manage to get dressed all by yourself?â€

Sarah was very excited and said, â€œYes, I can manage it!â€

Mrs. Williams smiled and said, â€œOk, you can try. I know you can do it!â€

Sarah tried and she managed to get dressed all by herself. She put on her dress, her shoes, and even her hair bow. When she finished, she ran to her Mom and said, â€œLook Mommy, I managed it!â€

Mrs. Williams hugged Sarah and said, â€œYes, you did it all by yourself! You are such a strong little girl!â€

Sarah was so proud. She smiled and said, â€œYes, I am a very strong girl!â€

Once upon a time there was a great bear. He was very big and strong. His fur was itchy so he liked to bathe in a river.

When he came to the river, he saw a crack in the ground. It was very shiny and it made him curious. He wanted to see what was inside.

So he bent down and looked in. Inside, he saw lots of shiny stones. They were so beautiful. The bear couldn't resist. He reached in and grabbed them. 

The bear put the stones in his bag and was really happy. He was so excited that he decided to take a quick bath in the river. He sat in the water and splashed around. His fur felt fresh and clean.

Then he put on his fur and went off to find more great treasures.

Jack was starting his day. He is only three years old. He could hear it was morning, but he wanted to resist getting out of bed. He knew he had to go to his daycare but he wanted to stay in bed for a little bit longer.

His mom came into the room to wake him up. She said, "Come on, Jack. Let's get up!" He tried to resist again, but she was too strong. Jack had to get up and get ready.

Jack put on his shoes and started walking to daycare. On the way, they saw something they rarely noticed. It was a rare morning rainbow. Jack shouted, "Mom, look!" He smiled and tried to touch it.

Jack and his mom enjoyed the moment together. Jack promised himself he wouldn't resist getting up so early again. He was happy to experience something rare and magical. He was glad he was finally up on this morning.

Once upon a time there was a chubby little ant. He liked playing in the sand. One day, while the little ant was playing, he found something hidden beneath the sand. It was a shiny yellow rock!

The ant carefully picked it up and looked closely. He was most excited and couldn't wait to show his friends. He quickly started to dig around the rock and soon yielded many more shiny rocks! He was so amazed and happy that he gathered all the rocks as carefully as possible into a big pile and took it back home.

The little ant was so proud of all of his shiny rocks and he shared them with all his ant friends. Everyone was amazed and very happy.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a big, dark cave. In this cave, a little boy named Tim and a little girl named Sue lived. They were best friends. They liked to play and have fun every day. But they were scared of the dark.

One day, Tim said, "Sue, let's plan to make the cave bright. We need power to see in the dark." Sue agreed and said, "Yes, we need a plan to make our cave bright and happy."

Tim and Sue thought and thought. They decided to find shiny rocks outside the cave. They went out and found many shiny rocks. They put the shiny rocks all around the cave. Now, the cave was not dark anymore.

Tim and Sue were very happy. They played and had fun with the shiny rocks. They were not scared of the dark anymore. Their plan worked, and they had the power to make their home bright and happy.

From that day on, Tim and Sue lived happily in their bright cave. They knew that with a good plan and the power of friendship, they could do anything.

Once upon a time, there was a big castle with a wise king who lived inside. The king had a big treasure that he kept inside the castle. He had a guard who always watched over the treasure to keep it safe.

One day, a bad guy came and stole the treasure. The guard tried to stop him, but he was too strong. The king was very sad when he found out that his treasure was gone.

But the king was also wise. He knew what to do to restore his treasure. He called for the bravest knights in the land to help him get his treasure back. The knights fought bravely and were able to defeat the bad guy and bring back the treasure to the king's castle. The king was very happy and thanked his brave knights for their help. And from that day on, the guard was even more careful to keep the treasure safe.

Once upon a time, there was a kind boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to ride his bike with a big wheel on the back. He would ride it every day after school. One day, Timmy's mom bought him a big ice cream cone. Timmy was so happy and took a big bite. But then, he realized that the ice cream was starting to spoil. He didn't want to eat it anymore, so he threw it away and went back to riding his bike. Timmy loved his bike so much that he didn't even care about the ice cream anymore.

One day, a little boy named Tom went to the farm with his mom. He liked to see the animals and the plants. He saw some cows, some pigs, some chickens and some corn. He wanted to pick some corn and eat it.

"Mom, can I have some corn?" he asked.

"Sure, Tom, but you have to be careful. Some corn is good and some corn is bad. The good corn is yellow and sweet. The bad corn is brown and rotten. Do you know how to tell the difference?" his mom said.

Tom nodded. He thought he knew everything. He was ignorant. He did not listen to his mom. He ran to the corn field and grabbed the first corn he saw. It was brown and rotten. He did not notice the smell or the bugs. He peeled the husk and took a big bite.

"Yuck!" he spat. "This corn is gross! It tastes like dirt and worms!"

He threw the corn away and ran back to his mom. He was crying and holding his mouth.

"Mom, mom, help me! The corn is bad! It hurts my teeth and my tongue!" he said.

His mom hugged him and gave him some water. She was not angry. She was sorry for him.

"Tom, I'm sorry you ate the rotten corn. You should have listened to me. I tried to teach you how to choose the good corn. The rotten corn can make you sick. You have to be careful and look and smell before you eat. Do you understand?" she said.

Tom nodded. He was sorry too. He learned his lesson. He was not ignorant anymore. He wanted to be smart and careful. He said sorry to his mom and thanked her for the water. He did not want to eat corn anymore. He wanted to see the animals again. He hoped they did not eat the rotten corn too. He hoped they were happy and healthy. He loved the farm and his mom.

One morning, a furry little bunny was feeling very sleepy. He yawned and hopped around looking for somewhere cozy to take a nap. Suddenly he noticed something shiny and sparkly in the grass. It was a copper penny! He smiled and picked it up. He put the penny in his pocket and hopped off in the sunshine.

The bunny hopped across the meadow and past a clump of trees. He kept going until he came to a tall, leafy tree. There was just enough room in the branches for the bunny to sit. He settled down and yawned. His eyes felt heavy, so he snuggled into the furry tree bark and let out a big, content sigh. 

He fell asleep with a smile on his face and the copper penny safe in his pocket.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to explore new places and things. One day, her mommy took her to an interesting place called an "office". Lily had never been to an office before and was excited to see what it was like.

When they arrived, Lily saw a big door that was closed. She asked her mommy if they could open it and see what was inside. Her mommy said they would have to wait until the door was opened by someone who worked in the office.

Lily was patient and waited for a while. Finally, a man came and opened the door. Lily and her mommy went inside and saw lots of people working on computers and talking on phones. Lily thought it was very interesting and wanted to come back to the office again.

Tommy was very excited when he heard his Mommy say they were going to the park. He loved playing there and couldn't wait to go. When he got to the park, he was even more excited because he saw that all his friends were there for a party. 

Everyone was feeling happy and excited about the party. Tommy was getting ready to join in the fun when he heard over the loudspeaker that there was going to be a race. Tommy knew he was the slowest runner in his class so he didn't want to race. 

The starting bell went off and everyone started running around the park. Tommy was still standing in his spot, feeling sad that he didn't want to race. But then his Mommy put her arm around him and said that it was okay if he didn't race, she had something delicious and lots of fun in store. She took Tommy over to a big picnic table and Tommy saw that she had made a delicious cake for everyone to share.

Tommy smiled as he watched everyone eating the cake, but he still had a feeling in his chest he knew as 'hate'. He didn't like races, but he was glad for his Mommy's delicious cake. From that day on, Tommy learned that it was okay to not like certain things and he could still have delicious food and lots of fun.

Once there was a little girl. She was only 3 years old. She wanted to fly on an aeroplane. She went to the airport and looked for a way to get onboard.

When she arrived, she saw everyone signing a big paper. She wanted to sign too, so she asked if she could do it. But the big people said no. She was very sad.

She asked again and again, but the big people wouldn't let her. They said she was too young to fly.

The little girl started to feel very angry and fierce. She started to yell and scream and ran away from the airport.

She never got to fly on an aeroplane. She was very sad, but she was too young to understand why she couldn't go.

Tom and Anna are friends. They like to play together at the park. One day, there is a big event at the park. There are balloons, clowns, and games. Tom and Anna are very excited.

"Look, Anna, there is a clown. He is making funny faces. Let's go and see him," Tom says.

"OK, Tom, let's go," Anna says.

They run to the clown. The clown is nice. He gives them a balloon each. Tom gets a red balloon. Anna gets a blue balloon.

"Thank you, clown," Tom and Anna say.

"You're welcome, kids. Have fun at the event," the clown says.

Tom and Anna are happy. They hold their balloons and look around. They see a big slide. They want to go on the slide.

"Come on, Anna, let's go on the slide. It looks fun," Tom says.

"OK, Tom, let's go," Anna says.

They run to the slide. But there is a problem. There is a big boy on the slide. He is mean. He does not let anyone go on the slide. He pushes and shouts at the other kids.

"Go away, this is my slide. You can't play here," the big boy says.

Tom and Anna are scared. They do not want to fight with the big boy. They do not know what to do.

"Tom, what should we do?" Anna asks.

"Let's ignore him, Anna. He is not nice. He is not our friend. We can play somewhere else. There are many other things to do at the event," Tom says.

"OK, Tom, you are right. Let's ignore him. He is not worth our time. We can have fun without him," Anna says.

They turn around and walk away. They ignore the big boy. They do not look at him. They do not talk to him. They do not care about him.

They find a swing. They take turns on the swing. They laugh and smile. They enjoy the event. They are happy. They are friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to read her mommy's magazines. One day, she found a powerful story about a princess who had to save her kingdom from a dragon. 

As she read the story, tears started to weep from her eyes because she was so happy that the princess saved her kingdom. Lily wanted to be a powerful princess just like her in the story. 

So, she put on her princess dress and tiara and pretended to save her stuffed animals from a dragon. She felt so powerful and brave, just like the princess in the magazine. 

From that day on, Lily loved to read stories about powerful princesses who saved the day. And whenever she felt sad, she would weep a little bit and remember the brave princess who saved her kingdom. The end.

Once upon a time there was a boy named Ben. He was very excited because he was invited to a birthday party. All his friends were going to be there so he couldn't wait to see them. 

At the party, Ben saw that the chairs were very cheap and he felt a little sad. But soon, he joined the other kids in the games and had a lot of fun. 

At the end of the games, the birthday girl had a surprise for them. She said she had invited a very special guest, a famous clown. Everyone was surprised and very excited. 

When the clown came out, he handed a special chair to Ben and said â€œThis is my gift to you!â€ Ben was so happy and thanked the clown. 

The chair was not cheap at all. It was a magical chair and it could turn into anything Ben wanted. What an amazing surprise!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily was very excited because she was going to get a new night light. She asked her mom, "Can we get a night light tonight?" Her mom said, "Yes, we can get a night light tonight."

Lily and her mom went to the store to get a night light. They found a night light that was very cheap. Lily was happy because she knew her mom would get it for her. She said, "Mommy, can we get this one?" Her mom said, "Yes, we can get this one."

When they got home, Lily's mom put the night light in her room. Lily was so happy. She said, "Thank you, mommy. I love my new night light!" Her mom said, "You're welcome, Lily. I'm glad you like it." And they both went to bed with smiles on their faces.

Once upon a time, there was a little seal. The seal was troubled because he wanted to play with his friends, but he couldn't find them. He swam around the ocean, looking for his friends. The seal felt sad.

One day, the seal saw a big sign. The sign had a picture of his friends on it. The seal was very happy. He followed the sign to find his friends.

When the seal found his friends, they were all playing together. The seal joined them, and they had lots of fun. The troubled seal was not sad anymore. They played all day, and they were all very happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the park with her friends. One day, Lily wanted to wear her favorite pink dress, but it was dirty. Her mom said they would wash it later, so Lily had to wear a different dress.

When Lily got to the park, her friends were already playing. They were playing tag and having so much fun. Lily wanted to play too, but she had to delay because she had to tie her shoes. After she tied her shoes, she ran to join her friends.

They played for a long time until it started to get dark. Lily's mom called her and said it was time to go home. Lily was sad to leave, but she knew she would come back and play with her friends again soon.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy lived in a house with his mommy and daddy. One day, Timmy's daddy set up a table outside so they could eat lunch in the sunshine. Timmy was very happy to eat outside.

While they were eating, Timmy saw a bird flying in the sky. The bird looked very alert and was looking for food. Timmy asked his mommy and daddy if they could give the bird some bread. They said yes, and Timmy threw some bread crumbs on the ground.

After lunch, Timmy helped his daddy with some work. They used a saw to cut some wood for a new shelf. Timmy was very excited to help his daddy and he did a great job. When they were finished, Timmy's mommy said they did a great job and gave them both a big hug. Timmy felt very proud.

Once upon a time, there was a big storm. The sky was dark and angry, and it was filled with fierce lightning. Every time the lightning shone, people were scared of the loud thunder.

The storm kept getting worse and worse, until suddenly - it stopped. Then someone said a special word - the word "order".

When the strange word was said, the storm obeyed. The lightning danced around and got softer and softer. Gradually, it stopped altogether and the sky became bright and blue again. Everyone was so happy that peace had been brought back.

The person who said the word was a brave man. He knew how to control the lightning and make the storm go away. Everyone thanked him for using his power to make the fierce lightning go away.

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play with toys and books. One day, they find a quiz book in the library. The quiz book has many questions about numbers.

"Let's play with the quiz book," Lily says. "I like numbers."

"OK," Ben says. "You ask me a question, and I answer. Then I ask you a question, and you answer."

They open the quiz book and look at the first page. Lily reads the question.

"How many fingers do you have on one hand?" she asks.

Ben holds up his hand and counts. "One, two, three, four, five," he says. "I have five fingers on one hand."

"Good job," Lily says. "Now it's my turn. Ask me a question."

Ben looks at the next page. He reads the question.

"What number comes after nine?" he asks.

Lily thinks hard. She remembers the song she learned in school. "One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten," she sings. "Ten comes after nine."

"Good job," Ben says. "You are smart."

They smile at each other and hug. They are happy. They like the quiz book. They like numbers. They like to learn.

They turn the page and see a picture of a soft teddy bear. The quiz book has a question about the teddy bear.

"What color is the teddy bear?" the quiz book asks.

Lily and Ben look at the picture. They see the teddy bear is brown.

"The teddy bear is brown," they say together.

They like the teddy bear. They wish they had a soft teddy bear to cuddle. They close the quiz book and put it back on the shelf. They go to the toy corner and find a soft teddy bear. They share the teddy bear and play with it. They are happy. They are friends.

Tom and Mia are twins. They like to play in their room. They have many toys and books and clothes. But sometimes their room is messy. Mom says they have to organize their things.

One day, Mom gives them a big basket. She says, "This is for your socks. You have to put all your socks in here. Then you can find them easily. Can you do that?"

Tom and Mia nod. They think it is a fun game. They start to look for their socks. They find them under the bed, in the drawers, on the floor, and in the closet. They put them in the basket. They see many colors and patterns. They try to match them.

But Mia is curious. She wonders what else is in the basket. She sees something shiny. She reaches for it. It is a necklace. She likes it. She puts it around her neck.

"Look, Tom, I found a necklace!" she says.

Tom looks at her. He sees the necklace. He remembers. It is Mom's necklace. She lost it a long time ago. She was sad.

"Uh-oh, Mia, that is not your necklace. That is Mom's necklace. She was looking for it. You have to give it back to her," he says.

Mia frowns. She likes the necklace. She does not want to give it back.

"But it is pretty. I want to keep it," she says.

Tom shakes his head. He knows Mom will be happy if they give her the necklace. He says, "No, Mia, you have to be nice. Mom will be happy if you give her the necklace. And she will be proud of us for organizing our socks. Come on, let's go and show her."
