Mia thinks. She loves Mom. She wants to make her happy. She takes off the necklace. She holds Tom's hand. They go to find Mom. They show her the basket of socks and the necklace.

Mom is surprised. She is happy. She hugs them. She says, "Thank you, Tom and Mia. You are very good. You organized your socks. And you found my necklace. I missed it so much. You are very sweet. I love you."

Tom and Mia smile. They are happy. They love Mom. They say, "We love you too, Mom."

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play at the park. He would run and jump and slide down the slide. One day, Timmy found a weird mark on the slide. It was a big, black mark that looked like a monster! Timmy was scared, but he still wanted to slide down the slide. He closed his eyes and slid down the slide as fast as he could. When he got to the bottom, he opened his eyes and saw that the weird mark was gone. Timmy was happy and went to play on the swings. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her dolls and put on makeup. One day, Lily's mommy took her to a museum to see ancient things. 

Lily saw an old vase and said, "Mommy, that's ancient!" 

"Yes, it is," said her mommy. "Do you like it?" 

"I do," said Lily. "Can we manage to take it home?" 

"No, we can't," said her mommy. "But we can take a picture of it." 

Lily smiled and took a picture of the ancient vase. She couldn't wait to show her dolls when she got home.

Sara and Ben are friends. They like to play together. Today is Halloween. They want to wear costumes and get candy.

Sara has a costume. She is a fairy. She has a dress, wings and a wand. She is happy. Ben does not have a costume. He is sad. He does not know what to be.

"Ben, do you want to play guess?" Sara asks. "I will guess what you are."

"Okay," Ben says. He hopes Sara will make him feel better.

Sara looks at Ben. She thinks hard. "Are you a cat?" she asks.

"No," Ben says.

"Are you a pirate?" she asks.

"No," Ben says.

"Are you a ghost?" she asks.

"No," Ben says. He sighs.

Sara sees that Ben is sad. She wants to help him. She has an idea. She runs to her room. She comes back with a big sheet. She puts it over Ben. She cuts two holes for his eyes.

"Look, Ben, now you are a ghost!" she says. "You have a costume!"

Ben looks at himself. He sees the sheet. He smiles. He likes the costume. He is not sad anymore.

"Thank you, Sara, you are a good friend," he says. "You are a smart fairy."

They hug. They are happy. They go out to get candy. They have fun.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to play with clay. One sunny day, he made a big clay cake. He was very happy with his cake.

Tim showed his clay cake to his friend, Sue. Sue said, "Wow, that's a big cake!" Tim replied, "Yes, I made it with my clay. Do you want to play with me?" Sue said yes, and they played together.

As they played, a naughty dog came by. The dog jumped on their clay cake and spoiled it. The cake became disgusting. Tim and Sue were sad. They looked at the dog and said, "Bad dog!"

Tim and Sue decided to make a new clay cake. They worked together and made an even bigger cake. They were happy again. They played with their new cake and had a great day. And the naughty dog never spoiled their clay cake again.

Once upon a time, there were two friends called Tom and Brad. They were always playing together and having lots of fun. 

One day, the two friends went on an adventure to explore a mysterious castle. They crept through its dark corridors until they reached a large door. Tom said, "Let's try it!" But Brad said, "Wait! It's locked!" Tom then found a key and said, "Let's go!"

They opened the door and stepped inside. It was a very comfortable room with a beautiful bed, soft carpet and a big chair. Brad said, "This is awesome! Let's stay here for a while." 
 
But Tom had a bad feeling. He said, "Let's go now. We shouldn't be here." But they decided to stay and explore the castle even more. Suddenly, they heard loud voices outside.

Tom peaked through a window and saw two large monsters. They were having an argument, and it looked like they were going to fight each other. Tom knew it was time to go, but it was already too late. The monsters saw them and a fight began. 

The two friends ran and hid until the monsters went away. They were relieved the fight was over, but now they knew they should never have gone into the mysterious castle in the first place.

Tom and Lily were playing with their toys in the garden. They had a lot of toys, but their favorite was a big green crocodile. They liked to pretend that the crocodile was their friend and that they went on adventures with him.

One day, a new boy moved in next door. His name was Ben. He saw Tom and Lily playing with the crocodile and he wanted to join them. He knocked on the fence and said, "Hi, I'm Ben. Can I play with you?"

Tom and Lily looked at each other. They did not know Ben, but they wanted to be nice. They said, "OK, you can play with us. But you have to follow the rules."

"What rules?" Ben asked.

"The rules are: you have to share the crocodile, you have to listen to us, and you have to be kind," Tom said.

Ben nodded. He climbed over the fence and grabbed the crocodile. He said, "I want to play with the crocodile first. He is mine now."

Tom and Lily were shocked. They said, "No, he is not yours. He is ours. We said you have to share."

Ben shook his head. He said, "No, I don't have to share. I'm the boss. You have to do what I say."

Tom and Lily were angry. They said, "No, you are not the boss. You are bossy. You are not a good friend. You have to include us. We don't want to play with you anymore."

Ben was surprised. He said, "But I want to play with you. I want to play with the crocodile."

Tom and Lily said, "Too bad. You have to learn to be nice. Go away."

They took the crocodile back and turned their backs on Ben. Ben felt sad. He realized he had been rude and selfish. He said, "I'm sorry. I was wrong. Can I play with you again? I promise to be nice and share and include you."

Tom and Lily looked at him. They saw that he was sorry. They said, "OK, you can play with us again. But you have to keep your promise."

Ben smiled. He said, "I will. Thank you for giving me another chance."

They hugged and made up. They played with the crocodile and had fun. They became good friends.

Once upon a time, there was a big lawn. On the lawn, there were many toys. A little boy named Tim loved to play there. One day, Tim saw a new toy on the lawn. He did not recognize it.

Tim was very alert. He looked at the toy and said, "Hi, toy! What is your name?" The toy did not talk back. Tim felt sad. He wanted to play with the new toy.

Then, Tim's mom came out. She saw the toy and said, "Oh, Tim! That is a ball. You can play with it." Tim was happy. He played with the ball on the lawn all day.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the sunshine. One day, she saw a scarecrow in the field. She asked her mommy, "Mommy, what is that?" Her mommy said, "That's a scarecrow. It's there to scare away the birds." 

Lily was a little scared of the scarecrow, but she wanted to get closer to it. She went up to it and touched the cloth that was hanging from its arms. It felt soft and nice. 

Suddenly, the wind blew and the scarecrow's cloth flew up in the air. Lily giggled and said, "That's so cheerful! It looks like it's dancing!" Her mommy smiled and said, "Yes, it does look cheerful." 

From then on, Lily wasn't scared of the scarecrow anymore. She would wave to it every time she passed by and it made her feel happy.

Ben and his dad walked through the swamp. Everywhere there were logs lying around. Dad was looking for a perfect log to take home. 

"Where's the perfect log?", Dad asked Ben.

Ben looked around. Everywhere was wet and somebody had put lots of logs there. 

Dad became impatient. "Maybe if we struggle to find the log it will help," Dad said.

Ben started feeling around the logs and pushing them to see which was the perfect log for Dad. At last, Ben found the perfect log and gave it to Dad.

Dad was so happy. He thanked Ben for his help. Together they took the log home.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Annie. She was only three years old and very curious. One day she decided to follow a butterfly that flew past her window. She ran outside and followed the butterfly as it fluttered in the air.

Annie ran and ran, her eyes following the butterfly in the sky. Suddenly, the butterfly stopped in front of a small notebook. Annie stopped too. She picked up the notebook and looked through its pages. There were pictures of the butterfly, drawn in bright colours. Annie was surprised!

She looked around and saw the butterfly was still there, watching her quietly. Annie decided to draw a picture too. She drew a beautiful picture of the butterfly and added it to the notebook. The butterfly flew away.

Annie smiled and picked up the notebook. She said to herself, â€œThis is my new notebook. I am going to write and draw lots of things in it!â€ Annie looked around one last time, and then she walked back home, holding the notebook tightly in her arms.

Once upon a time, there was a generous man named Tom. Tom liked to help people. He had a big frame house where he lived with his cat, Fluffy. The house had many windows to let the sun in.

One day, Tom saw a little boy named Tim. Tim was sad because he lost his ball. Tom wanted to help Tim. He said, "Don't worry, Tim. I will help you find your ball." So, Tom and Tim went to look for the ball together.

They looked in the park and under the trees, but they could not find the ball. Then, they saw a big tree with a ball stuck in the branches. Tom tried to raise his hand to reach the ball, but it was too high. He said, "I'm sorry, Tim. I can't get your ball." Tim started to cry because he loved his ball. They went home, and the ball stayed in the tree. The end.

Sara and Ben were playing with their toys in the living room. Sara had a doll and Ben had a car. They liked to make up stories with their toys.

"Look, my doll is going to mail a letter to her friend," Sara said. She took a piece of paper and pretended to write on it. Then she folded it and put it in an envelope.

"Who is her friend?" Ben asked.

"Her friend is a fairy who lives in a flower. She is very pretty and has wings," Sara said.

"Can I see the letter?" Ben asked.

Sara gave him the envelope. Ben opened it and looked at the paper. He saw some scribbles and a drawing of a flower.

"This is not a letter. This is ugly," Ben said. He tore the paper in half.

Sara was angry. She snatched the paper from Ben and tried to put it back together.

"That was not nice. You broke my letter. It was not ugly. It was beautiful," Sara said.

"No, it was not. It was ugly. Look, it is only an inch long. That is too small for a letter," Ben said.

Sara started to cry. She ran to her mom and showed her the paper.

"Mom, Ben broke my letter. He said it was ugly and small. He is mean," Sara said.

Mom hugged Sara and looked at the paper.

"I'm sorry, Sara. That was not nice of Ben. Your letter was very creative and lovely. I'm sure your fairy friend would love it," Mom said.

She took a tape and fixed the paper. Then she gave it back to Sara.

"Here, you can mail your letter now. Do you want a stamp?" Mom asked.

Sara nodded. She smiled and wiped her tears. Mom gave her a sticker and put it on the envelope.

"Thank you, Mom. You are the best," Sara said.

She ran back to the living room and put the envelope in a box. She pretended it was a mailbox.

"Bye, bye, letter. Have a nice trip to the flower," Sara said.

She looked at Ben and stuck out her tongue.

"My letter is not ugly. It is beautiful. And it is not small. It is just right for a fairy," Sara said.

Ben shrugged. He didn't care. He went back to playing with his car. He liked to make it zoom and crash. He thought that was more fun than writing letters.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys and make them look pretty. He would decorate them with stickers and paint.

One day, Timmy's friend Billy came over to play. Billy brought a toy missile with him. Timmy thought it was cool, but he didn't know what it was for. Billy explained that it was a weapon that could shoot things far away.

Timmy thought it was neat, but he didn't want to play with it. He was too polite to say no, so he let Billy play with it by himself. But Billy didn't know how to use it properly and accidentally shot it at Timmy. Timmy got hurt and had to go to the hospital.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a small rabbit called Tony. He was hopping through the meadow early one morning and he noticed a shiny bow on the ground. He was very curious and he wanted to pick it up. 

Suddenly, Tony froze in fear - a fox appeared. The fox was very jealous of Tony for finding the bow and it was angrily lurching toward him. Tony hopped away as fast as he could. 

The fox was close behind him and just when Tony thought he couldn't hop any further, a giant bear stepped right in the fox's way. The bear scared the fox away. Tony was so happy and grateful.

He offered a silent thank you to the bear, picked up the bow, and hopped away. Tony taught us a valuable lesson that day: always be thankful and kind, even in the face of danger!

Once upon a time, there was a gifted country which had a kind and generous king. The king's daughter was deeply loved and all the country's inhabitants cherished her warm heart. 

One day, the daughter asked the king: "Father, I want to remain here forever."
The king held his daughter tight and looked deep into her eyes. He replied: "Sweetheart, no matter where you go, know that my love will always remain with you."

The princess smiled, feeling the king's love, warmth and care all around her. She knew she was truly blessed to have such a caring father and have the opportunity to remain in such a wonderful country. 

Since then, the princess and her family have continued to remain in the gifted country and are filled with happiness, health and joy every day. The end.

Once there was a little boy and he loved to push his wagon around. One day he was prancing around, pushing his wagon with glee. His older brother was there, rolling his eyes at the silly display.

The little boy stopped and said to his brother, "Let's split up and see who can push their wagon the farthest!" His brother, not wanting to look bad in front of the little one, agreed to the challenge.

The little boy was off and running, pushing his wagon around the house, through the grass and past the trees. Every now and then he would glance back, watching his brother far behind. Suddenly, he hit a bump in the grass and his wagon flew up in the air, then crashed down onto the ground in pieces.

The little boy was shocked and embarrassed. He stood looking at the now broken wagon and his brother slowly walked closer. His brother took the pieces of the wagon and said, "Looks like we can't split up anymore."

The little boy just nodded in agreement, realizing what his sibling meant. From then on, they would be splitting up the pieces of wood, fixing the wagon and playing together. After all, only silly boys try to split up wagon.

Once upon a time, there was a big scary storm. The sky was dark and the thunder was loud. Suddenly, there was a lot of lightning. It was very bright and colorful.

The storm was not just scary â€“ it was also magical. The lightning shone like little twinkles and made some pretty shapes. It was like the sky was saying 'Welcome!'

The storm lasted a long time. But when it was over, the sky was filled with the most beautiful colors. The sun shone down on the rainbow and everyone cheered.

Finally, the storm was gone and everyone welcomed the bright sunshine and colorful sky.

Once there was a family. They were a very obedient family, and always listened to their parents. One day, the parents said, "Don't go too far", and the family paused before heading out together.

The family walked for a long time. Then, one of the children had an idea. She said, "Let's go further. We'll still be close enough to hear our parents if they call."

The rest of the family agreed. They all kept walking, further and further away.

But then, they heard a loud noise. It was their parents, calling for them to come back. The family stopped, but it was too late.

The parents were very angry. They said, "We told you not to go too far. You didn't obey, so now you can't come back home!"

The family was very sad. They wanted to be together again, but there was nothing they could do. The obedient family had to stay away, and they never saw each other again.

Once upon a time, there was a big, red switch on a wall. The switch was very important. It was in a room with many toys. Everyone who came to play had to remember to use the switch.

One day, a small girl named Lily came to play. She saw the switch and remembered what her mom told her. She knew she had to use the switch. Lily was a very mild and kind girl. She always listened to her mom.

Lily pushed the switch and all the toys came to life. They danced and played together. They had so much fun. Lily was happy she remembered the switch. At the end of the day, she pushed the switch again and the toys went to sleep. Lily went home with a big smile on her face, excited to come back and play again.

Tim and Mia are friends. They like to draw with crayons. They have many colors of crayons. They also have erasers. Erasers can make the crayons go away.

One day, Tim and Mia have a contest. They want to see who can draw the best picture. They have ten minutes to draw. They start to draw on their papers.

Tim draws a big house with a red roof and a blue door. He draws a yellow sun and a white cloud. He thinks his picture is very good.

Mia draws a green dragon with purple wings and orange fire. She draws a brown mountain and a pink flower. She thinks her picture is very cool.

When the time is up, they show their pictures to each other. They both like their pictures. But they want to know who wins.

They ask their teacher, Miss Lee, to judge their pictures. Miss Lee looks at their pictures. She smiles. She says they both did a great job. She says they both win.

Tim and Mia are happy. They hug each other. They say they are both good artists. They decide to share their crayons and erasers. They draw more pictures together. They have fun.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, she went to the market with her mommy. They saw a big basket of peaches. The peaches looked so yummy and juicy!

Lily asked her mommy if they could buy some peaches. But her mommy said they were too expensive. Lily felt sad, but she understood. She knew they couldn't buy everything they wanted.

Later that day, Lily's mommy surprised her with a peach. It wasn't as big as the ones at the market, but it was still delicious. Lily learned that sometimes it's better to appreciate what we have instead of always wanting more.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Tom. Tom loved playing football with his friends. One day, Tom found a football that was bigger than the others. He kicked it with all his might, but it didn't move. "This football is too big," Tom said.

Suddenly, the football started to shrink! It became smaller and smaller until it was the same size as the others. Tom was amazed. "Wow, the football shrunk!" he said.

But one of Tom's friends, a stubborn boy named Jack, didn't believe him. "That's impossible!" Jack said. Tom tried to explain what happened, but Jack wouldn't listen. "I don't believe you," Jack said stubbornly. 

From that day on, Tom played with the shrunken football and had lots of fun with his friends. And even though Jack didn't believe him, Tom knew that the football had really shrunk.

Once upon a time there was a star. It was very hot in the sky and it shimmered brightly. 

One day, an brave adventurer decided to reach up and touch the star. The moment the star was touched, it started to shrink. The adventurer was so excited! He shouted "Wow! It's shrinking!"

The star continued to shrink until it was no bigger than the adventurer's hand. The star was so small now that the adventurer decided to take it home and make a wish.

Back at home, the adventurer closed his eyes and made a wish. He wished for a million stars to rain down from the sky. Suddenly, the star in his hands started to grow bigger and bigger. It was so hot and so brilliant that he had to shield his eyes!

Suddenly, the sky opened up and a million stars began to rain down from the sky. The adventurer whisked his hand around and a million stars flew around it. 

He looked up to the night sky and smiled, for he had made his wish come true!

Once there was a squirrel called Scurry. He was very happy, and loved acorns. Every day he went in search of them, and stored them away. One day, he found a very big acorn up high in a tree. He was so excited, and couldn't wait to take it home!

Scurry turned to go back, but he heard a ssssss sound behind him. He spun around and saw a snake! It was coming right at him! Scurry was so scared, he started to run away. He tried to run but the snake was so fast.

The snake suddenly stopped and turned away. Scurry stopped and looked back. He wanted to take the acorn home, but he was still afraid of the snake. After a few minutes he decided to go back and get the acorn.

He was almost there when the snake suddenly turned back. Scurry was so scared, he didn't know what to do. The snake came closer and closer. Scurry wanted to run away, but he couldn't move. The snake came closer, and suddenly it bit him. Scurry was in so much pain, and he fell to the ground.

The snake slithered away, and Scurry was left there, lying on the ground in pain. He had never made it home with the big high acorn.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play outside in the park. One day, they see a new path in the park. It is wide and smooth and has flowers on both sides.

"Let's go on the new path!" Anna says. She is enthusiastic. She likes to explore new things.

"OK!" Ben says. He is enthusiastic too. He likes to follow Anna.

They hold hands and walk on the new path. They see birds and butterflies and bees. They hear water and wind and leaves. They smell grass and dirt and honey.

They come to a bridge over a stream. The bridge is made of wood and has a railing. They cross the bridge and look at the water. They see fish and frogs and stones.

"Wow, this is so beautiful!" Anna says. She is happy. She likes to see new things.

"Yes, it is!" Ben says. He is happy too. He likes to share with Anna.

They see a man on the other side of the bridge. He is wearing a hat and a vest and has a shovel. He is the gardener. He made the new path and planted the flowers.

"Hello, children!" the gardener says. He is friendly. He likes to talk to people.

"Hello, sir!" Anna and Ben say. They are polite. They like to be nice.

"Did you enjoy the new path?" the gardener asks. He is curious. He likes to know what people think.

"Yes, we did!" Anna and Ben say. They are honest. They like to tell the truth.

"Thank you for making the new path!" Anna says. She is grateful. She likes to thank people.

"Thank you for planting the flowers!" Ben says. He is grateful too. He likes to thank people.

"You're welcome, children!" the gardener says. He is pleased. He likes to hear people thank him.

"Have a good day!" Anna and Ben say. They are cheerful. They like to wish people well.

"Have a good day too!" the gardener says. He is cheerful too. He likes to wish people well.

Anna and Ben wave goodbye to the gardener and walk back on the new path. They are happy. They like to play outside in the park.

The bright morning sun was shining, and Tom eagerly grabbed his walking stick and headed off on his morning adventure. When he arrived at the edge of the forest, he began to whistle a cheerful tune as he strolled along.

Suddenly, he heard a rustling sound in the trees and stopped. Out of the corner of his eye he saw a large prune, hanging from a branch. Tom knew he should not take it without permission, so he called out, "May I please have the prune?" 

In answer, a gruff voice said, "No! That prune belongs to me." Tom was very confused, because he had never seen anyone in the forest before, so he looked up to see who was talking. 

Standing in the tree was an old, tough-looking man, who was holding the prune protectively. Tom was a little scared, but he still tried to explain his desire.

"I want to pick the prune to make a pie for my family. Please, can I have it?" he asked.

The old man looked at Tom and smiled. He tossed the prune down to Tom, saying, "You look eager boy. Here, take the prune and make a delicious pie."

Tom was so happy, and he thanked the old man gratefully. He returned home and with the prune, he made a wonderfully tasty pie that his family loved.

Molly and Tom were best friends who loved to play together. One day, they were playing hide and seek. Tom shouted, "Ready or not, here I come!" He ran around the garden, counting to ten. But when he came back he couldn't find Molly anywhere.

Tom started to worry, but then he heard giggle coming from a bush. He looked inside and found Molly, and she was much smaller!

He said, "Molly, what happened? How did you shrink?" 

Molly just laughed, because she knew the answer. She said, "I used a magic number!" 

Tom couldn't believe it. He asked, "What number did you use?"

Molly smiled and said, "9999 - don't worry it's silly but it worked!" She winked and started to get bigger. Soon, Molly and Tom were back to their normal size and had a lot of fun together.

Once there was a clever little girl. She had a big brain and was always thinking. One day she decided to fill her brain with new knowledge.

The girl started to read books and ask lots of questions. She learned about numbers, shapes, animals and more. Every day the girl filled her brain with so many new things.

When the girl was done learning she felt so proud of what she had learned. She knew so much and it made her feel really clever. From then on she kept on filling up her brain.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to count things. He would count his toys, his snacks, and even the birds outside. One day, Timmy's mom told him that Wednesday was a special day. It was the day of the fair! Timmy was so excited to go to the fair and count all the rides.

When they got to the fair, Timmy saw a boy who didn't have any toys to play with. Timmy felt sad for the boy and decided to share his toys with him. The boy was so happy and thanked Timmy.

Later, Timmy and the boy went to count the rides together. They had so much fun! Timmy realized that sharing his toys made him feel even happier than counting things. He learned that it's important to be kind and share with others.

From that day on, Timmy always remembered the fair on Wednesday and how sharing made him feel so good.

Once upon a time, there was a pilot named Tim. Tim had a big, modern plane. He loved to fly high in the sky. One day, Tim had to step on his plane to go on a trip.

Before the trip, Tim saw a big cloud. It looked like it could be a problem. But Tim was brave and thought he could fly through it. So, he stepped on his plane and flew into the sky.

As Tim flew, the big cloud became a storm. The plane shook and it was hard to fly. Tim was scared, but he remembered the big cloud he saw before. He knew he had to be brave. Tim flew through the storm and made it to the other side. He was happy and proud of himself. Tim learned that even when things are hard, he can be brave and make it through.

Once upon a time, there was a cold winter day. A little rabbit was playing in the woods and he started to shiver. He had been outside for so long and was feeling very cold. 

Then he came upon a vine covered in purple berries. He thought it looked like the most beautiful thing he had ever seen. He reached out to pick one of the purple berries, but when he touched it, he felt it shaking. He was so surprised and started to shiver even more. 

But then he realized that it wasn't the purple berry that was shaking. It was the vine itself that was trembling! He knew that his shivering must have been making the vine shake but he hadn't thought it was possible.

The little rabbit continued to shiver from the cold but couldn't help but smile at the thought of how the vine seemed to be trembling with him.

Sam and Mia like to watch planes in the sky. They sit on the grass and point at the big and small planes that fly over them. They wonder where the planes are going and who is inside them.

One day, they see a very small plane that is flying very low. It is red and white and makes a loud noise. They hear a voice from the plane. It is the pilot. He says, "Hello, kids! Do you want to see my plane?"

Sam and Mia are surprised and excited. They nod and wave at the pilot. The pilot lands his plane on a nearby field. He gets out and walks towards them. He smiles and says, "My name is Tom. I am a pilot. I fly this plane for fun. Do you want to come and look at it?"

Sam and Mia say yes and follow Tom to his plane. They touch the wings and the propeller and the wheels. They look inside the cockpit. It is empty. There are no other people or things in the plane. Just some buttons and levers and a steering wheel.

Tom says, "This is how I fly the plane. I push and pull the levers and turn the steering wheel. I can make the plane go up and down and left and right. Do you want to try?"

Sam and Mia are curious and scared. They look at each other and then at Tom. They say, "Can we?"

Tom says, "Sure, but only for a little bit. And I will be with you. Don't worry, it is safe and fun."

He helps them get into the plane and puts on some headphones for them. He says, "These are to talk to me and to hear the other planes. Can you hear me?"

Sam and Mia say yes. They hear Tom's voice in their ears. He says, "OK, let's go!"

He starts the engine and the plane moves. Sam and Mia feel the wind and the speed. They see the grass and the trees and the sky. They are flying! They laugh and scream and watch everything. They feel like they are birds. They are happy. They are pilots.

Once upon a time there was a little boy called Josh. He was very hungry, so his Mommy made him a steak. Josh bit into it, but it was very tough. He wasn't able to chew it.

Mommy said, "What's wrong, Josh?"

Josh replied, "My steak is too tough. I can't eat it."

Mommy smiled and said, "Let's count to 10 before you eat it, ok?"

Josh nodded and started counting. He got to 10 and tried the steak again. This time it was much easier to chew!

Josh smiled and said, "Thank you Mommy, that was much better!"

Mommy said, "See, how great it is to take our time and count? Patience is a great lesson to learn and it can help us in many situations. Always remember to count before making a decision!"

 Josh nodded and smiled as he enjoyed his steak. He'd learned a valuable lesson and was happy that he can now always count on his Mommy!

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Lilly. Lilly loved pretty and pink things. She had a special pink hat that she wore all the time. 

One day, Lilly went outside and found a minute in the grass. It was very small, and it was pink. Lilly thought it was so special. She wanted to take it home. 

But when she picked it up, it started to separate into tiny pieces. Lilly started to cry. She wanted to keep the minute, but she knew it could not be the same. 

But then an magical thing happened. All of the pieces turned back into the pink minute, and Lilly was so happy. She hugged the little minute tightly and took it home with her. 

The little minute lived with Lilly for the rest of her life and always reminded her to cherish special moments, no matter how small.

Anna and Ben are having lunch with their mom. They are eating pasta with sauce and cheese. Anna likes sauce a lot. She puts a lot of sauce on her pasta. Ben does not like sauce. He only puts a little sauce on his pasta.

"Anna, why do you have so much sauce?" Ben asks. "Sauce is yucky. It is red and wet and sticky."

Anna looks at Ben and smiles. She likes to tease her brother. "Sauce is yummy. It is red and sweet and smooth. You need more sauce, Ben. Here, have some of mine." She takes a large spoon of sauce and tries to put it on Ben's plate.

"Anna, no!" Ben shouts. He moves his plate away. He does not want Anna's sauce. He likes his pasta plain. "Stop it, Anna. You are being silly. Mom, tell Anna to stop!"

Mom hears Ben and Anna. She looks at them and shakes her head. She loves her children, but they are very noisy. She wants them to eat nicely and quietly. "Anna, Ben, please stop fighting. You can have as much or as little sauce as you want. But you have to respect each other's choices. And you have to use your manners. What do you say when you want something or when you don't want something?"

Anna and Ben think for a moment. They know what mom means. They have to be polite and kind. They look at each other and reply.

"Sorry, Ben. I was just joking. You can have your pasta how you like it. Do you want some cheese?" Anna says.

"Sorry, Anna. I was just curious. You can have your sauce how you like it. No, thank you. I don't want cheese." Ben says.

Mom smiles and nods. She is happy that Anna and Ben are being nice to each other. She gives them each a hug and a kiss. She says, "That's good, Anna and Ben. I'm proud of you. Now, enjoy your lunch. And don't forget to say thank you when you are done."

Once upon a time, there was a dog named Max. Max was a good and loyal dog. He loved to play fetch and eat sausage. One day, Max's owner, Sarah, decided to take him on a walk in the park. 

Max was so excited to go on a walk with Sarah. He wagged his tail and barked happily. When they arrived at the park, Sarah let Max off the leash to play. Max ran around and had so much fun. 

But then, Max saw a sausage on the ground. He ran over to it and ate it quickly. Sarah didn't see him eat the sausage. 

Later that day, Max started to feel sick. He had eaten a bad sausage and it made him very sick. Sarah took him to the vet, but unfortunately, Max didn't succeed in getting better. He passed away that night. Sarah was very sad and missed Max a lot.

Once upon a time, there was a lonely truck. The truck was all alone on the side of the road. Suddenly, a little boy appeared. He was only three years old.

The boy came over to the truck and said, "I'm so lonely. Can you help me?"

The truck replied, "Yes, I can help you. Climb up onto the roof and close your eyes."

The little boy followed the truck's instructions and began to rub his tummy. He felt so happy and his loneliness was gone. 

But when the little boy opened his eyes, he realised he was alone again. The truck had disappeared!

The little boy was so sad. He wished he had never asked the truck for help. He was all alone, just like before.

John and his mom went to the beach. John saw a bucket and inside was some salt. He picked it up and said to his mom: "Look! I pick salt!"
John's mom smiled and said: "Yes, you picked salt!"

John carefully felt it. It was smooth and sparkly. He looked around and saw some shorebirds. He said: "Mom, can I pick up a bird?"

His mom shook her head. "No, John, we can't pick up the birds. But you can pick up some shells and look at them. They're smooth too."

John was excited and ran around picking up shells and looking at them. He looked at one shell and then another. He liked to feel how smooth they were.

He had a lot of fun and then it was time to go home. He picked up all of the shells and they started walking back to the car. He had a handful of smooth shells to remember the day.

Once upon a time, there were two friends, Mary and Sue. Mary mentioned that she wanted to blow bubbles. Sue thought this was a great idea and said â€œYes, that sounds fun!â€ 

So Mary and Sue went outside. Mary had a big bottle filled with bubble mixture that she had brought from home.  

They both laughed as each time the bubbles filled the air. Every time Sue would try to catch the bubbles, she would giggle with joy. Mary could not believe how funny it was to see Sue jumping after the bubbles. 

After a while, the bottle of bubble mixture was empty. Sue suggested that they try to make their own bubbles using soap and water. Mary thought this was a great idea so they went back indoors to find the soap. 

They each held an end of the string that they had found and dipped it into a bowl of water and soap. Quickly, bubbles filled the air. They laughed and cheered as they watched the funny bubbles form. 

Eventually, they were exhausted, so they decided to sit down and relax. They had too much fun playing with the bubbles!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved peanuts, especially the spicy ones. One day, she went to the park with her mom and dad. They brought a bag of peanuts for Lily to munch on.

Lily's friend, Timmy, came to play with her in the park. He saw the bag of peanuts and asked if he could have some. Lily said no because they were too spicy for him. Timmy got upset and said, "I want peanuts too!"

Lily didn't want to share her peanuts because they were her favorite. Her mom and dad told her that it's nice to share with friends. Lily thought about it and decided to share her peanuts with Timmy. She held out the bag of peanuts and said, "Here, you can have some too." Timmy was happy and they both enjoyed munching on the spicy peanuts together.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy. He was very loyal and always helped his family. One day he was playing in the kitchen and he accidentally broke his mom's favorite pot. He was very scared and started to cry. 

His mom came in and saw the broken pot and was very mad. She said, "What did you do?" The little boy said he was sorry and promised to never do it again. His mom was angry, but then she remembered how loyal the little boy was. She took a deep breath and hugged him. She said, "I forgive you."

The little boy was so happy and he felt relieved. He hugged his mom and thanked her for forgiving him. From then on, he was extra careful around the stove and made sure that he kept his promise. From that day on, the mom and little boy stayed very loyal to each other.

Once upon a time, there was a big lion. The lion had a very loud roar. One day, the lion met a silly monkey. The monkey said, "Hi there, Mr. Lion! Your skin is very pretty." The lion said, "Thank you, silly monkey. But don't get too close or I might roar at you." The monkey said, "I won't get too close. I just wanted to say hello." The lion and the monkey became friends and they played together every day. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved rockets, and he wanted to go to space. He saw an adorable toy rocket in the store and said, "Mommy, I want that rocket!"

His mommy said, "Okay, Timmy. Let's buy it!" Timmy was so happy and hugged the adorable rocket tightly. 

Later that day, Timmy's friend Billy came over to play. Timmy showed him his rocket and said, "Look, Billy! I have an adorable rocket!" Billy said, "Wow, Timmy! Can I play with it too?" 

Timmy smiled and said, "Sure, Billy. Let's play together!" They pretended they were astronauts and went on a fun adventure to the moon. Timmy was so happy he got what he wanted and had a great time playing with his friend.

Once upon a time, there was a young boy named Ben. He always wanted to help fix things. One day, Ben heard an unusual noise coming from the garden. He went outside to take a look.

Ben discovered it was coming from a smelly old shed. He tried to open the door, but it wouldn't move. So Ben went back inside for a few tools.

He returned with a hammer and a crowbar. After lots of hard work and banging, the shed door finally opened. Behind it, Ben found an old bicycle. It had a punctured tyre and a rusty chain. 

Ben was so excited. He knew he could fix the bike! He asked his dad for some help. 

Dad looked at the bike and said: "It looks like it needs a new tyre and a few new parts. Let's go to the shop and get them." 

So they did. Ben and Dad fitted the bike with new parts and pumped up the tyre. They also gave it a good clean and a lick of paint. Before long, Ben's old bike looked like brand new. 

Ben rode it around the garden with a big smile on his face. He couldn't have been happier.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Sarah. Sarah was very excited because she was going to get a new shirt. Her mum said, "Come and get your shirt, Sarah." 

Sarah ran to the closet and opened the door and there it was. She grabbed her new shirt and what a surprise it was! The shirt was a funny color. She chuckled, "This shirt is so funny!" 

Her mum said, "Let's go outside now and show everyone your new shirt." 

Sarah put on her new shirt and they went outside. Everyone laughed when they saw what Sarah was wearing- it was so funny! 

Everyone wanted to play with Sarah, but her mum said, "Not now, Sarah's too tired. You can play with her later if I allow it." 

Sarah smiled, because she knew her mum was taking good care of her. She said, "Ok, I'm happy to wait until my mum allows it!"

Once upon a time, there was a big blue bird. He had big wings and many feathers. He could fly around and see the world.

One day, while flying, he felt something heavy on his back. He flapped his wings, but it was too heavy. He tried to fly away, but the weight kept him down.

He looked around and saw a giraffe standing nearby. "What is this heavy weight on my back?" the bird asked.

The giraffe warned him, "Be careful! That weight is a big rock. You must get rid of it if you are going to fly."

The bird thanked the giraffe for warning him. Then he used his wings to push the rock off his back. The rock landed with a thud, the bird flew up into the sky. 

He was so happy to be able to fly again. He waved to the giraffe and flew up into the sky and away.

Jack was at the playground. He saw a broken swing. He wanted to repair it. He looked around but nobody was there to help him. Suddenly a big man appeared. He was wearing a big hat and had a dark beard.

"Hello!" said Jack.

"Hi!" said the man. "Do you need help to repair the swing?"

"Yes, please!" said Jack.

The man took out his tools. He knew how to repair it. They talked and laughed as they worked together.

"You speak a very special language," said Jack.

"Oh yes," said the man. "It's my secret language."

When the swing was repaired, Jack thanked the man. He gave Jack a smile, and said goodbye. Jack waved him goodbye and watched him walk away into the dark.

Once upon a time, there was a friendly dog named Spot. Spot loved to play outside and chase after balls. One day, Spot met a friendly cat named Mittens. They became best friends and played together every day.

One day, Spot asked Mittens if she wanted to marry him. Mittens didn't know what that meant, so Spot explained that it meant they would always be together and take care of each other. Mittens thought that sounded nice and said yes.

Spot and Mittens decided to have their wedding on a big boat with a big anchor. They invited all their animal friends to come celebrate with them. It was a beautiful day and everyone had a lot of fun. Spot and Mittens were so happy to be married and to have each other as best friends forever.

Once upon a time, there was a yummy dessert that everyone loved. It was heavy and filled with sweetness.
One day, the dessert got spread everywhere. It spread onto the floors, into the carpets and all over the walls.
The house was covered in dessert! Everyone was so happy. They ate and played in the dessert.
The children loved playing in the sticky stuff. They rolled around and had lots of fun. 
At the end of the day when all the dessert was finished, everyone was content and happy that the dessert had spread across the house.

Lily and Ben liked to play pretend. They had a big box of costumes and toys. Sometimes they were pirates, sometimes they were superheroes, sometimes they were animals. Today they decided to be doctors and patients.

Lily put on a white coat and a stethoscope. She said, "I am Doctor Lily. I will take care of you, Ben. What is wrong with you?" Ben put on a bandage and a hat. He said, "I am Patient Ben. I have a bad headache and a sore throat. Can you help me, Doctor Lily?"

Doctor Lily nodded. She said, "Of course, Patient Ben. Let me check your temperature and your heartbeat. You are very brave and unique. You are the only patient who wears a hat like that." She pretended to use a thermometer and a stethoscope. She said, "Hmm, you have a fever and a fast heartbeat. You need some medicine and some rest."

Patient Ben said, "What kind of medicine, Doctor Lily?" Doctor Lily said, "You need some special medicine. It is very sweet and colorful. It will make you feel better." She went to the box and looked for something. She found a bottle of candy. She said, "Here it is. This is the medicine. You have to take one candy every hour. But be careful, do not take too many. They are very strong."

Patient Ben said, "Thank you, Doctor Lily. You are a very good doctor. Can I have one candy now?" Doctor Lily said, "Yes, you can. But only one. Here you go." She gave him a candy. He said, "Mmm, this is delicious. It tastes like strawberry. I feel better already." Doctor Lily said, "I am glad. Now you have to lie down and rest. I will come back later to check on you." She gave him a pillow and a blanket. He said, "Thank you, Doctor Lily. You are very kind and smart." He lay down and closed his eyes.

Doctor Lily smiled. She said, "You are welcome, Patient Ben. You are very polite and unique. I hope you get well soon." She went to the box and looked for another costume. She said, "Now I want to be something else. What do you want to be, Ben?" Ben opened his eyes. He said, "I want to be something else too. Let's see what we can find." They got up and went to the box. They had fun playing pretend. They were happy and creative.

Mia and her best friend, Lucy, were walking through the park when Mia spotted something interesting. "Look Lucy, a boat!" Mia said. They both ran to the boat and Mia noticed a wire attached to it.

Lucy was so excited, "Let's sail the boat!" Mia was unsure though. "The wire looks so fragile," Mia said.

Lucy tried to encourage her. "Don't be scared, we can do it together!" Mia finally smiled. 

They both grabbed onto the wire and sailed the boat around the park. They laughed and shouted as they sailed faster and faster. Mia and Lucy had so much fun. 

When they reached the end, they said goodbye to the boat and waved as they watched it sail away. They both knew they'd made an amazing adventure together.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to draw pictures, but he didn't have a frame to put them in. One day, Timmy's friend Billy came over to play. Timmy showed Billy all of his drawings, but he was sad because he didn't have a frame to put them in. 

Billy said, "Don't be silly, Timmy! You can borrow my frame." Timmy was so happy and said, "Thank you, Billy!" Timmy put his favorite drawing in the frame and hung it up on his wall. 

Later that day, Timmy's mom came in and saw the drawing in the frame. She said, "Wow, Timmy! Your drawing looks so nice in that frame." Timmy smiled and said, "Billy let me borrow it." 

From then on, Timmy borrowed Billy's frame whenever he had a new drawing he wanted to hang up. Timmy and Billy were happy friends who loved to help each other out.

Timmy was a small three year old. One day, he had a grand ideaâ€”he was going to march all over his house! He put on his fireman hat and marched into the living room. 

"Mom, look at me!" he said. 

His mom was sitting on the couch watching television. "That's so cute, Timmy," she replied. 

Timmy march around the living room and then into the kitchen. He saw his small toy car and decided to march around it. He got his toy drum out and played it while he marched around. 

He marched back into the living room and his mom said, "Wow, you like to march, don't you Timmy?" 

"Yes," he said, still marching around the living room. 

So every day, Timmy would march around his house. He even marched outside and around his yard. He liked to march because it made him happy.

Tom was a little boy who liked to play with his toys. He had a big truck, a soft bear and a red ball. He liked to make noises with his truck, hug his bear and throw his ball.

One day, he was playing with his ball in the garden. He threw it very high and it went over the fence. He ran to the fence and looked for his ball, but he could not see it. He saw a big dog on the other side of the fence. The dog had his ball in its mouth. The dog looked at Tom and growled.

Tom was scared and sad. He wanted his ball back. He tried to climb the fence, but it was too high. He tried to call the dog, but it did not listen. He tried to find a stick, but there was none. He did not know what to do.

He started to weep. He wept very loud and very hard. He wept so much that his eyes were wet and his nose was runny. He wept so much that his mouth was sour and his throat was sore. He wept so much that his arm was tired and his chest was heavy.

His mom heard him weep and came to the garden. She saw him by the fence and asked him what was wrong. He told her about his ball and the dog. She hugged him and said she would help him. She went to the neighbor's house and knocked on the door. She asked the neighbor if he could get the ball from the dog. The neighbor said yes and went to the backyard. He came back with the ball and gave it to Tom.

Tom was happy and grateful. He thanked the neighbor and his mom. He wiped his eyes and his nose. He smiled and said he was sorry for weeping. He hugged his mom and his ball. He went back to play with his toys. He was careful not to throw his ball too high. He was a good boy.

Once there was a dog who was very lonely. He wanted someone to play with him, but no one was around. On a visit to the veterinarian, it was decided that the dog needed a friend. The veterinarian supplied an original puppy, just the right size and shape for the lonely dog.

The dog was overjoyed! He and his new friend played all day, chasing each other around the yard, having fun! They were inseparable. 

At night, they curled up together to sleep, wearing big smiles. The dog had his special friend, and the little puppy felt special too. 

The dog knew the veterinarian had supplied a wonderful friend for him. He was thankful every day for his original puppy.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Mark. Mark was always very healthy, and she loved running around in the park. One day when she was playing in the park, she met a special delivery man.

The delivery man said, "Hello Mark! We have a very special delivery for you today. I'm here to deliver it to you."

Mark asked, "What is it? Can I see it?"

The delivery man smiled and said, "Yes, you can! It's a beautiful, healthy apple!"

Mark was so excited to get the apple. She said, "Thank you for delivering it to me!"

The delivery man smiled and said, "You're welcome Mark, enjoy your healthy snack!"

Mark thanked the delivery man again and said goodbye. Then she took her apple and happily ran off to enjoy her snack.

From that day on, Mark always remembered the special delivery man, who had brought her a healthy snack.

Ben and Lily were best friends. They liked to play in the garden and look for bugs. One day, they found a big green caterpillar on a leaf. It had many legs and a funny face.

"Wow, look at this!" Ben said. "It's so cool!"

"Can we keep it?" Lily asked. "We can make a home for it in a jar."

"OK, but we have to be careful. Caterpillars are very delicate," Ben said. They put the caterpillar in a jar with some leaves and grass. They poked some holes in the lid so it could breathe.

They were very happy with their new pet. They named it Charlie and decided to celebrate. They went to the kitchen and got some cake and juice. They brought them to the garden and had a picnic.

"Happy birthday, Charlie!" they said. "We love you!"

They ate their cake and drank their juice. They sang songs and told stories. They were having so much fun that they forgot about Charlie.

Charlie was not happy. He was hungry and thirsty. He wanted to eat more leaves and drink some water. He also wanted to get out of the jar and explore the garden. He was an adventurous caterpillar. He tried to push the lid, but it was too tight. He tried to chew the jar, but it was too hard. He felt trapped and scared.

He started to feel sick. He curled up in a ball and closed his eyes. He wished he was back on his leaf.

Ben and Lily finished their picnic. They remembered Charlie and ran to the jar. They wanted to play with him and show him some flowers.

But when they looked inside, they saw that Charlie was not moving. He was not breathing. He was not alive.

They were shocked and sad. They cried and hugged each other.

They realized they had been bad friends to Charlie. They had not taken care of him. They had not given him what he needed. They had only thought of themselves.

They buried Charlie in the garden. They said sorry and goodbye. They learned a hard lesson.

They never forgot Charlie. They never caught another caterpillar.

Lily and Ben were playing in the park. They liked to run and jump and slide. Lily wore a new blouse that was pink and had flowers on it. She was very happy with her blouse.

But then Ben saw a big puddle. He wanted to splash in the water. He ran to the puddle and jumped in. He made a big splash and got wet. He laughed and said, "This is fun!"

Lily saw Ben and got angry. She did not want to get wet. She did not want her blouse to get dirty. She ran to Ben and said, "Stop! Stop! You are making a mess! You are ruining my blouse!"

Ben did not listen. He jumped in the puddle again. He made another big splash and got wetter. He laughed and said, "This is more fun!"

Lily got more angry. She tried to pull Ben out of the puddle. But the puddle was deep and slippery. She lost her balance and fell in. She got wet and dirty too. She cried and said, "This is not fun! This is bad! You are bad!"

Ben saw Lily and felt sorry. He did not mean to make her cry. He did not mean to ruin her blouse. He got out of the puddle and helped Lily up. He said, "I'm sorry. I'm sorry. I was just playing. I did not know you liked your blouse so much."

Lily looked at Ben and saw that he was sorry. She looked at her blouse and saw that it was wet and dirty. She felt sad and said, "It's okay. It's okay. I was just angry. I do like my blouse, but I like you more."

Ben smiled and hugged Lily. He said, "I like you more too. Let's go home and get dry and clean. Maybe Mom can wash your blouse and make it nice again."

Lily nodded and hugged Ben back. She said, "Yes, let's go home. Maybe Mom can make us some cookies too."

They held hands and walked home. They were still wet and dirty, but they were happy. They learned to be careful and kind. They learned to say sorry and forgive. They learned to share and play. They were good friends.

Sara and Ben like to play in the garden. They help their mom plant seeds and water them. They watch the seeds grow into flowers and vegetables.

One day, Sara sees a small red radish poking out of the dirt. She pulls it out and shows it to Ben.

"Look, Ben, I found a radish!" she says.

"Wow, Sara, it is so small and red!" Ben says. "Can I hold it?"

Sara gives the radish to Ben. He holds it in his hand and shakes it.

"Why are you shaking it, Ben?" Sara asks.

"I want to see if it makes a sound," Ben says.

He shakes the radish harder and harder, but it does not make any sound. It only gets dirtier and softer.

"Ben, stop shaking the radish!" Sara says. "You are ruining it!"

Sara tries to take the radish back from Ben, but he does not let go. They tug and pull and fight over the radish.

Their mom hears them and comes to the garden. She sees them fighting and the radish in pieces.

"What are you doing, Sara and Ben?" she asks. "Why are you fighting over a radish?"

Sara and Ben stop fighting and look at their mom. They feel ashamed and sorry.

"We wanted to see the radish, mom," Sara says.

"But Ben shook it too hard, mom," Ben says.

Their mom picks up the radish and throws it in the compost bin.

"That was not a nice way to treat the radish, Sara and Ben," she says. "The radish was a gift from the earth, and you should respect it and enjoy it. Next time, if you want to see the radish, you can wash it and cut it and eat it. It is good for you and tasty. Do you understand?"

Sara and Ben nod their heads and say sorry.

"We understand, mom," they say.

Their mom hugs them and smiles.

"Good, Sara and Ben," she says. "Now, let's go and see what else we can find in the garden."

Once there was a little girl. She was playing in her backyard when she saw something. It was a large, fluffy blanket. She was so excited and ran towards it. She asked her mom if she could have it. 

"Please, mommy," she said, "can I have the blanket?"

Her mom smiled and said, "Yes, you can."

The little girl jumped up and down with joy. She wrapped the blanket around her and sat down in the grass. She felt so cozy and comfy. She leaned against the blanket and closed her eyes. 

As she sat there the warm sun made her even more relaxed. It was the best day ever! She felt so happy and content. She stayed there for the rest of the afternoon, just sitting and enjoying the warm sunshine on her blanket.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved going for car rides with her mommy and daddy. One day, they went on a long drive to visit her grandma.

As they drove, Lily got very sleepy. She cuddled her favorite teddy bear and closed her eyes. Her mommy said, "Lily, buckle up so you can sleep safely." Lily smiled and buckled her seatbelt.

After a while, they arrived at grandma's house. Lily was still sleepy, but when she saw her grandma, she smiled and ran to give her a big hug. They had a fun day playing and eating yummy snacks. When it was time to go home, Lily was still sleepy. She buckled up and closed her eyes, dreaming of the fun day she had with grandma.

Sara and Ben were playing with blocks in their room. They liked to build towers and bridges and castles. Sara wanted to make a big tower, but Ben wanted to make a long bridge. They argued and pushed each other's blocks.

"No, I want a tower!" Sara said.

"No, I want a bridge!" Ben said.

They were very stubborn and did not want to share or take turns.

Suddenly, they felt the floor shake and heard a loud noise. It was an earthquake! The blocks fell down and the pictures on the wall moved. Sara and Ben were scared and hugged each other.

"Mommy! Daddy!" they cried.

Their parents came running and took them to a safe place. They saw smoke and fire outside. Some houses were burning. The earthquake had broken some wires and started a fire.

"Oh no, look at the fire!" Sara said.

"It's so hot and bright!" Ben said.

Their parents told them not to worry. They said the firefighters were coming to put out the fire and help the people. They said they were lucky that their house was not burning. They said they should be thankful and kind to each other.

Sara and Ben felt sorry for being stubborn and mean. They said sorry to each other and hugged again. They decided to play with the blocks together and make something nice. They learned that sharing and taking turns was better than fighting and breaking things. They also learned that earthquakes and fires were scary and dangerous, and that they should listen to their parents and stay safe.

Tom and Lily were two rabbits who lived in a big garden. They liked to eat radishes that grew in the garden, but they had to be careful of the farmer. The farmer was a wealthy man who had a big house and many animals, but he did not like rabbits. He wanted to catch them and put them in a cage.

One day, Tom and Lily saw a big bunch of radishes near the fence. They were red and juicy and smelled very good. They decided to sneak out of their hole and nibble on them. But they did not know that the farmer had set a trap. He had tied a string to the radishes and hid behind a tree.

As soon as Tom and Lily bit into the radishes, the string pulled and a net fell over them. They were trapped and scared. They heard the farmer laugh and say, "Ha! I got you, you naughty rabbits! You won't eat my radishes anymore!"

Tom and Lily tried to wiggle and kick, but the net was too strong. They thought they would never see their home again. But then they heard a loud bark. It was Rex, the farmer's dog. Rex was a friendly dog who liked to play with the rabbits. He saw them in the net and ran to help them.

He bit the string and tore the net with his teeth. He freed Tom and Lily and wagged his tail. He said, "Don't worry, friends. I will help you escape. Follow me!"

Tom and Lily thanked Rex and followed him to the fence. They squeezed through a hole and ran back to their hole. They were safe and happy. They said, "Thank you, Rex. You are a good dog. We are sorry we ate the farmer's radishes. We won't do it again."

Rex said, "You're welcome, friends. I'm glad you're okay. The farmer's radishes are not worth it. There are many other things to eat in the garden. Just be careful and have fun!"

Jen and Sam were making a cake with Mom. They had to stir the flour and the eggs and the sugar in a big bowl. Jen liked to stir fast and hard. Sam liked to stir slow and soft. They took turns to stir the bowl.

"Can I stir now?" Sam asked.

"No, it's still my turn," Jen said.

"But you stir too much. You make a mess," Sam said.

"No, I don't. You stir too little. You make a lump," Jen said.

They started to argue and pull the spoon. Mom saw them and said, "Stop! You are both nosy. You have to share and be nice. If you don't, you can't have any cake."

Jen and Sam looked at each other. They did not want to miss the cake. They said sorry and gave each other a hug. They decided to stir together, fast and slow, hard and soft. They made the batter smooth and yummy.

Mom smiled and said, "Good job. Now we can put the batter in the pan and make a line with the chocolate chips on top. Then we can bake the cake and eat it later."

Jen and Sam nodded and helped Mom. They were happy and hungry. They liked to make a cake with Mom.

Once upon a time, there was a family who had a jug. The jug was very fragile and needed to be looked after.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One night, Lily and her mommy went outside to look at the stars. Suddenly, they saw a bright comet in the sky. "Wow, that comet is so pretty!" said Lily. "Yes, it's very powerful," said her mommy.

One day, two friends went for a walk in the park. They saw a big puddle and decided to share it! They took turns splashing around, and it was great fun.

Once upon a time, there was a boy called Sam. He was three years old and he was very curious.

One day, three cute little puppies were playing together in the park. They were so excited to be there! One of the puppies was dressed in bright red clothing and had the biggest and happiest smile on its face. The other two puppies noticed the special puppy and were curious.

Lily and Max were playing with their blocks. Lily wanted to make a big tower, but Max wanted to make a train. Lily was bossy and took Max's blocks. Max was sad and angry.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy liked to play outside with his friends. One day, they went on an adventure in the forest. Timmy saw a big tree with a thick trunk. He pointed to the tree and said, "Look at that big tree!"

Once upon a time, there was a enormous hospital. All the people living nearby were very scared of it because it was so big!
