Finally, the bunny saw another animal in the clearing. It was a small raccoon, looking just as lost as the bunny felt.

The bunny hopped closer and asked the raccoon, "What are you searching for?"

The raccoon answered, "I'm searching for some berries to eat. They were here yesterday, but now they're all gone."

The bunny felt sorry for the raccoon, so it offered to help search. Together they hopped around the clearing, listening for any sound of the berries.

Then, the bunny perked up its ears. It had heard something! In the distance were soft rustling sounds.

The bunny and raccoon followed the noise until they came upon a bush full of juicy, ripe berries. The bunny and raccoon were so happy, they ate as many berries as they could!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside with her friends. One day, they were playing hide and seek when they saw a cop car driving by. The cop was looking for a bad guy who had stolen something.

Lily and her friends remembered to be quiet so the bad guy wouldn't hear them. But then, they heard a loud noise coming from a nearby house. They saw the bad guy running away with the stolen things. The cop chased after him, but the bad guy got away.

Lily and her friends were sad that the bad guy got away. They hoped the cop would catch him soon. But that night, they heard another noise outside. It was the bad guy! He had come back to steal more things. Lily and her friends were scared and didn't know what to do. The bad guy saw them and ran after them. They tried to run away, but the bad guy caught them. The story ended badly because the bad guy was mean and hurt Lily and her friends.

Once there was a strong dog called Lola. Lola was very smart and every day she would study hard. One year she worked really hard and she ended up being the smartest dog in the neighbourhood. Everyone was so proud of her.

Every morning Lola would go out to the park where she would learn new things. She would play with her friends and also take time to study. She loved to study and was getting smarter and smarter each day.

At the end of the year Lola was so strong that she was able to do a lot of things that other dogs couldn't do. Lola was happy and her family was so proud of her. They couldn't believe how much she had learnt in a year. 

Lola was a very special dog and her strength and hard work paid off. She was so proud that she had accomplished so much in a year by studying hard!

Tom and Lily liked to play in the garden. They had a big box of bulbs that they wanted to plant. Bulbs were like seeds, but bigger and round. They could grow into flowers or vegetables.

Tom and Lily were very organized. They made a plan of where to put each bulb. They dug holes in the dirt and put the bulbs inside. They covered them with more dirt and watered them. They were happy and proud of their work.

But then, a big dog came into the garden. The dog was not nice. He smelled the bulbs and wanted to eat them. He dug up the dirt and spread the bulbs everywhere. He bit some of them and left others on the grass. He made a big mess.

Tom and Lily saw the dog and ran to the garden. They were very sad and angry. They shouted at the dog and tried to chase him away. But the dog was bigger and faster. He barked at them and scared them. He did not listen to them.

The dog ran away with some bulbs in his mouth. Tom and Lily looked at their ruined garden. They had no more bulbs to plant. They had no more flowers or vegetables to grow. They cried and hugged each other. They wished they had a fence to keep the dog out. They wished they had a nice dog to play with. They wished they had a happy ending.

Ben and Mia are playing in the park with their mom. They like to swing, slide and run on the grass. They are having fun and laughing.

But then they see a man sitting on a bench. He has a stick in his mouth and he is blowing smoke. The smoke is gray and smelly. It makes Ben and Mia cough and sneeze.

"Mom, what is that man doing?" Ben asks.

"He is smoking, Ben. It is a bad habit. It is not good for him or for us. We should stay away from the smoke," mom says.

"Why is he smoking, mom? Does he like it?" Mia asks.

"I don't know, Mia. Some people smoke because they think it makes them feel better or look cool. But it is really disgusting and harmful. It can make them sick and hurt their lungs and teeth. It can also bother other people who don't smoke," mom says.

"Mom, I hate smoke. It is yucky and stinky. I don't want to be near it. Can we go to another place?" Ben says.

"Me too, mom. I hate smoke. It makes my eyes water and my nose itch. I don't want to breathe it. Can we play somewhere else?" Mia says.

"Of course, my loves. Let's go to the other side of the park. There is a sandbox and a seesaw there. We can have more fun there and enjoy the fresh air," mom says.

Ben and Mia nod and smile. They hold mom's hand and walk away from the man and the smoke. They are happy and healthy. They don't like smoke and they will never smoke. They love their mom and their park.

Once upon a time, there was a small girl who wanted to explore all she could. She looked around and, in the distance, spotted a modern tower that sparkled and glinted in the light. She was drawn to it, so she decided to go closer.

As the girl got nearer, she saw a huge wall. She tried to walk up the wall, but it was too high. The tiny girl could not climb the wall by herself, but then suddenly she felt something furry and warm brush up against her leg. It was a small, white kitten.

The kitten jumped up onto the wall and meowed. The kitten beckoned the girl to come closer and, after a few more mews, the kitten began to climb up the wall. The girl smiled and followed the kitten. When they reached the top, the girl couldn't believe her eyes. There was a modern castle that had a big balcony with a table set up and a delicious looking waffle on it. The girl was so excited and together, she and the kitten, sat down and enjoyed the waffle. Together, they made beautiful memories there and had the best time ever.

Once upon a time, there was a little green frog. He was always curious and loved making new memories. One day, he hopped around and discovered a big pile of yummy snacks. He was so excited that he started to chew them all up.

Just then, he heard a voice. It was his best friend, the spider. "Where did you find all these snacks?" she asked.

The little frog was so happy to have his friend with him that he tried to answer her. "Memories!" he croaked.

The spider was so surprised that she stepped back. She had no idea what he was trying to say. So, she asked him again.

"Memories," the frog repeated as he pointed to the snacks. He explained that each of them reminded him of a special moment, and that was why he was eating them all up.

The spider smiled, understanding what he meant. She gave him a big hug and they both enjoyed the snacks together.

Once upon a time, there was a little mole named Mimi. Mimi was a very bad mole because she liked to dig tunnels everywhere. One day, Mimi was digging a tunnel when she heard a voice calling out to her.

"Hey Mimi, hurry up and come out of that hole!" It was her friend, a little bird named Benny.

Mimi poked her head out of the hole and asked, "What's wrong Benny?"

"I need your help," said Benny. "I lost my favorite worm and I can't find it anywhere. Can you help me look for it?"

Mimi agreed to help and together they searched all over the garden. Finally, Mimi spotted the worm and they both hurried back to Benny's nest to enjoy their tasty snack. From that day on, Mimi realized that it was better to be a good mole than a bad one.

Once upon a time there was a chubby tutor. She was a very nice teacher who often helped her students with their studies. One day, she noticed that a little boy was struggling to learn how to read. She tried her best to help him, but he was still having difficulty understanding.

The tutor wanted to help him more, so she decided to pinch his nose. Herstudent giggled as he felt the pinch and finally began to understand. He was happy and thanked the tutor for her help.

The next day he came back to class even more eager to learn. He was so excited to show the tutor what he had learnt that he started pincing her nose back. They both couldn't help but laugh since it nwas such an innocent gesture.

From then on, the little boy really improved on his studies and the tutor was very proud of him. She realised that the pinch had actually worked and she was glad that she had helped him understand the lesson. 

The little boy was so happy that he was able to learn with the help of his chubby tutor and the pinch on his nose.

Tom and Amy were playing in the garden. They liked to dig holes and look for shiny things. Sometimes they found rocks, sometimes they found shells, sometimes they found coins.

"Look, Amy, I found a mineral!" Tom said, holding up a blue stone. "It is very pretty and smooth. Do you want to see?"

"Yes, please!" Amy said, running over to Tom. She took the stone and looked at it closely. "Wow, it is very pretty and smooth. Where did you find it?"

"I found it in this hole," Tom said, pointing to the ground. "Maybe there are more minerals in there. Do you want to help me dig?"

"Okay!" Amy said, giving the stone back to Tom. They both lay on the ground and used their hands and spoons to dig deeper.

They dug and dug until they saw something shiny at the bottom of the hole. It was a metal box with a lock on it.

"What is that?" Amy asked, curious.

"I don't know," Tom said, excited. "Maybe it has more minerals inside. Or maybe it has toys or candy. Let's open it!"

They tried to pull the box out of the hole, but it was too heavy. They tried to break the lock, but it was too hard. They tried to shake the box, but it did not make any sound.

They were about to give up when they heard a voice behind them.

"Hey, kids, what are you doing?" It was Mr. Brown, the gardener. He saw the hole and the box and frowned. "That's my box. I buried it here a long time ago. It has some old tools and papers in it. Nothing for you to play with."

"Sorry, Mr. Brown," Tom and Amy said, feeling guilty. "We were looking for minerals. We did not know it was your box."

"It's okay, kids, but you should not dig holes in the garden. You might hurt the plants or the worms. And you should not touch other people's things. You might break them or lose them. Do you understand?"

"Yes, Mr. Brown," Tom and Amy said, nodding.

"Good. Now, why don't you fill up the hole and come with me? I have some real minerals for you to see. I collected them from different places. They are very pretty and smooth. Do you want to see?"

"Yes, please!" Tom and Amy said, smiling. They quickly filled up the hole and followed Mr. Brown to his shed. He showed them his minerals and told them their names and colors. They were very happy and learned a lot.

They thanked Mr. Brown and went back to their house. They told their mom and dad about their adventure and showed them their new minerals. They decided to keep them in a special box and not dig any more holes in the garden. They had enough minerals for now.

Lily and Ben were playing in the snow. They made a big snowman with a hat and a scarf. They also made a snow reindeer with sticks for antlers. They were very proud of their snow friends.

"Look, Mommy, look!" Lily shouted. "We made a snowman and a snow reindeer!"

Mommy came out of the house. She smiled and hugged them. "You did a great job, my sweeties! They look very nice!"

"Can we spray them with water?" Ben asked. "So they don't melt?"

"Sure, you can," Mommy said. "But be careful not to spray each other. It's very cold outside."

Lily and Ben ran to get the water spray. They took turns to spray the snowman and the snow reindeer. They made them shiny and wet.

"Wow, they look like real!" Lily said.

"Maybe they will come alive at night," Ben said.

They laughed and imagined what their snow friends would do. They thought they would dance and sing and play with them.

But then they heard a loud noise. It was a snow plow. It was coming down the street. It was very big and fast. It was clearing the snow from the road.

"Oh no!" Lily and Ben cried. "It's going to hit our snow friends!"

They ran to the snowman and the snow reindeer. They tried to push them away from the road. But they were too heavy and too slow.

"Stop, stop!" they shouted to the snow plow. "Don't hurt our snow friends!"

But the snow plow did not hear them. It did not see them. It kept going. It smashed the snowman and the snow reindeer. It made them into a big pile of snow.

Lily and Ben were very sad. They cried and hugged each other. They looked at the pile of snow. They could not see their snow friends anymore.

Mommy came to them. She saw what happened. She felt sorry for them. She hugged them and kissed them.

"I'm so sorry, my sweeties," she said. "The snow plow did not mean to hurt your snow friends. It was just doing its job."

"But we loved them, Mommy," Lily said. "We made them with our own hands."

"I know, my sweeties," Mommy said. "And they will always be in your hearts. And maybe, just maybe, they will come back next winter. And you can make them again."

Lily and Ben looked at Mommy. They wiped their tears. They smiled a little.

"Really, Mommy?" they asked.

"Really, my sweeties," Mommy said. "Now let's go inside and have some hot chocolate. And maybe we can read a story about a snowman and a snow reindeer who came alive at night."

Lily and Ben nodded. They liked that idea. They followed Mommy inside. They still missed their snow friends. But they also felt warm and cozy. And they hoped to see them again.

Once upon a time there was a very creative yellow bird. He liked to do different things and explore his world. One day the bird decided to take a walk and he saw a big tree. The tree was special, it had very yummy fruit that the bird had never seen before. He was excited!

The bird flew up to the tree and ate a piece of fruit. The fruit was so delicious! The bird wanted to bring some of the fruit back home to his family but it was starting to rot. He needed to think of a solution.

The bird was very creative and he came up with a plan. He took some sticks and some string and made a basket. Then he put some of the fruit in the basket to take home. Now the fruit wouldn't rot while he was flying. 

The bird was thrilled and flew back home with the basket of yummy fruit. He was so proud of his creative idea! The family was so happy to have the delicious yellow fruit. 

From then on, the bird always thought of creative ways to make his life easier. He was the happiest bird in the world!

Once there was a boy who had to make an important choice. He saw two billboards. One said it was time to be serious. The other said it was time to play. The boy had to choose which one to follow.

The boy thought about it carefully. He thought about how much fun he would have if he chose the one suggesting play. But he also remembered a promise he made to be serious.

Feeling unsure, the boy decided to ask his mom. Mom said that if he wanted to reach his goals he had to be serious. The boy chose the billboard that said it was time to be serious. 

The boy worked hard and kept the promise to be serious. He was proud of himself for choosing wisely.

Once upon a time, there was a chubby little angel named Cupid. Cupid loved to fly around and spread love to everyone. One day, Cupid was feeling very hungry and needed someone to feed him. He flew down to earth and found a kind little girl who offered him some yummy cookies. 

Cupid was so happy and grateful that he gave the little girl a big hug. As he flew away, the little girl saw that Cupid had dropped his bow and arrow. She picked it up and decided to help Cupid spread even more love. 

From that day on, Cupid and the little girl became great friends and would often fly around together, spreading love and joy to everyone they met. And whenever Cupid got hungry, the little girl would always be there to feed him some delicious treats.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to wear pretty skirts and play outside. One day, Lily saw some big kids racing on their bikes down the street. She thought it looked like fun, so she wanted to join in.

But her mom told her it was too dangerous and she could get hurt. Lily was sad, but she listened to her mom and stayed safe. Later, she realized that her mom was right and she was happy she didn't race with the big kids.

The moral of the story is to always listen to your parents and stay safe. Even if something looks fun, it might not be the best choice.

One day, Grandma and Grandpa came to visit. Grandma had a big, hairy chair. Grandpa said he wanted to serve it to the family. Grandma said it was very comfy.

Grandpa asked the three year-old to try it. The little child giggled when he touched the hairy chair. He said it tickled his fingers! Grandma said that was because it was so soft and furry.

Grandpa showed the little one how to sit in the chair. He said it was a special chair - it could serve Grandma and Grandpa when they wanted to take a nap. Grandma laughed and said it sounded perfect.

The little one was very excited now! He asked Grandpa if he could serve the chair too. Grandpa nodded and said he could. So the little one carefully walked around, serving the chair to everyone. Everyone smiled when he served them the furry chair.

Once upon a time, there was a wise man. He was very old, but he was very wise.
One day, the man wanted to go for a walk. He had a candle with him.
He took a few steps, but then he saw a hill. The hill was too steep for the old man, so he needed help.
He asked a nearby three year old to push him to the top. The three year old was happy to help! He put his hands on the manâ€™s back and pushed him all the way to the top.

The wise old man held up the candle and thanked the three year old with a big smile. 
The three year old smiled back and they went their separate ways.

Once upon a time there was a nice little girl. She had a special sword. Every day she would spray her sword with water, so it could shine.

One day, she heard a strange noise outside her house. She opened the door to see what was going on and saw a dragon! 
The dragon was about to spray fire!

The little girl shouted, "No! Stop!" The dragon looked at her and said, "Why should I stop? I am here to destroy your house!"

The little girl smiled and said, "I want to show you something. It's my special sword. Do you want to see it?"

The dragon nodded and the little girl sprayed her sword with water. The dragon was amazed when he saw how it sparkled and glowed in the sunlight. 

The dragon said, "What a nice sword! I don't want to ruin your house. I think I'll just fly away now."

The little girl smiled and waved goodbye to the dragon as he flew away. From then on, she kept her special sword close by and marveled at its beauty.

Once upon a time, there was a horse named Brownie. Brownie was a big, brown horse who loved to run through the fields. One day, Brownie saw some dark clouds in the sky. He knew that meant it was going to rain soon.

Brownie didn't like the rain because it made the ground slippery and dangerous for him to run on. But he also knew that the rain was good for the plants and animals.

As Brownie was walking through the field, he saw a small bird that was stuck in a puddle. The rain had made the ground so wet that the bird couldn't fly away. Brownie knew he had to help the bird, even though it was dangerous for him to walk in the slippery mud.

With all his might, Brownie carefully walked over to the bird and gently lifted it out of the puddle. The bird was so happy and chirped a sweet song to thank Brownie. From that day on, Brownie didn't mind the rain so much because he knew he could help others in need.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She was very nosy and loved to look at everything around her. One day, she saw a bird in a tree and wanted to get a closer look. She climbed up the tree, but then she fell down and hurt herself.

Her mommy came running and asked, "Lily, what happened?" Lily said, "I wanted to look at the bird, but I fell down." Her mommy said, "Oh no, we need to go to the hospital." They went to the hospital and the doctor helped Lily feel better.

When they got home, Lily said, "Thank you mommy for taking care of me." Her mommy hugged her and said, "I'm just glad you're okay." From then on, Lily learned to be careful and not be so nosy.

Mommy filled the big glove with water. It was so full that it made big bubbles. The water was cold and it made mommy's hand feel better.

Mommy put the glove on Jack's tummy. It was so cold that he giggled and tickled his tummy. He laughed and felt so happy. 

"Yucky!" said Jack. The water was very bitter and tasted yucky. 

Mommy gave Jack a hug and said, "It's okay Jack. It was just cold water to make you feel better."

Jack smiled and hugged mommy tight. He felt better and was so happy that mommy made the glove full of cold water to help him.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Jane. She loved playing outdoors. But one day, she got a little bit scared. It was getting darker outside and Jane was scared of the dark.

But suddenly she saw something pale come out from the bushes. She wanted to stay still and not move, so she just stared at it. It was a stuff!

Jane was so scared that she held her breath and didn't know what to do. Her heart was beating so fast that she thought it might jump out of her chest!

The stuff was just standing there, and it didn't move. So Jane slowly started to walk away. Finally, she was safe and she hurried back home. 

The next day, Jane was happy that she was not scared anymore. She went out in her garden and played with all the stuff that she saw. She was no longer afraid of the dark.

Once upon a time, there was a boat on the sea. It had been in a huge storm and was not in a good shape anymore. All the people on the boat felt really sad and bitter. 

But then, they saw a beautiful wave coming towards them. After the wave had past, they saw that their boat was back in good shape again. 

The wave had fixed their boat and made it like new again. Everyone was so happy and smiled at each other. How wonderful it was to see the wave restore the boat and make it like new again. 

The people were so grateful for the wave and enjoyed their new boat so much. They waved goodbye to the wave as it left, happy that they had been restored.

Ben and Lily were playing in the garden. They saw a big green plant with many leaves. They wondered what was under the ground.

"Let's pull it and see!" said Ben.

"OK!" said Lily.

They both grabbed the plant and pulled hard. Out came a big brown potato. They were surprised and happy.

"Wow, look at this!" said Ben. "It's a potato!"

"What's a potato?" asked Lily.

"It's a food. You can eat it. You can make fries or mash or soup with it," said Ben.

"Yum, I like fries!" said Lily.

They pulled more plants and found more potatoes. They put them in a basket and ran to the house.

"Mom, mom, look what we found!" they shouted.

Mom looked at the basket and smiled.

"Good job, kids! You found some potatoes. Where did you get them?" she asked.

"We pulled them from the garden. They were hiding under the green plants," said Ben.

Mom frowned.

"Oh, no. Those were not our potatoes. Those were Mr. Jones's potatoes. He planted them in his part of the garden. He will be very angry if he sees you took them," she said.

Ben and Lily felt bad. They did not know they did something wrong.

"We're sorry, mom. We didn't know. We thought they were ours," said Lily.

Mom hugged them.

"It's OK. You didn't mean to. But you have to give them back to Mr. Jones and say sorry. He works hard to grow his potatoes. He might share some with you if you ask nicely," she said.

Ben and Lily nodded. They took the basket and went to Mr. Jones's door. They knocked and waited.

Mr. Jones opened the door and saw them. He looked angry.

"Hello, kids. What do you want?" he asked.

Ben and Lily held out the basket.

"We're sorry, Mr. Jones. We took your potatoes. We didn't know they were yours. We thought they were ours. We pulled them from the garden. We're sorry," they said.

Mr. Jones looked at the basket and softened.

"Well, well. You took my potatoes, huh? That was not very nice. But I see you are honest and brave to come and say sorry. That's good. I forgive you. But don't do it again, OK?" he said.

Ben and Lily smiled.

"OK, Mr. Jones. Thank you. Can we have one potato, please? We want to make fries," they asked.

Mr. Jones laughed.

"Sure, sure. You can have one potato. But only one. And don't pull any more plants. They are not toys. They are food. Do you understand?" he said.

Ben and Lily nodded.

"Yes, Mr. Jones. We understand. Thank you. Bye," they said.

They took one potato and ran back to the house.

"Mom, mom, we said sorry to Mr. Jones. He gave us one potato. Can we make fries?" they asked.

Mom smiled.

"Of course, you can. That was very nice of him. And I'm proud of you for saying sorry. Come on, let's go to the kitchen and make some fries. But first, wash your hands. They are dirty from pulling potatoes," she said.

Ben and Lily washed their hands and followed mom to the kitchen. They helped her peel and cut the potato. They watched her fry it in oil. They sprinkled some salt on it. They ate it with ketchup. It was delicious.

They learned a lesson. They learned not to pull plants that are not theirs. They learned to say sorry when they make a mistake. They learned to share and be grateful. They learned that potatoes are not stupid. They are yummy.

One day, a little girl named Mia went for a walk. The wind was blowing soft and nice. Mia liked the wind. She saw a big tree and wanted to climb it. The tree was very tough, but Mia was brave.

As Mia climbed the tree, she saw a small bird. The bird was stirring its nest. "Hi, bird," said Mia. "Why are you stirring your nest?" The bird said, "I am making my home nice and cozy."

Mia smiled at the bird. "That's nice," she said. "I want to help you." So Mia helped the bird stir its nest. They worked together and had fun. When they were done, the bird's nest was very cozy. Mia and the bird became good friends.

Once upon a time, there was a powerful king. He had many laws that everyone in the kingdom had to obey. One day, a naughty girl broke one of his laws. She was very sorry, but the king said that she had to suffer a punishment.

The king made her stand on top of a hill, so everyone could see her. She had to stay there all day and all night. She felt very sad and alone but knew she had to stay until the king said she could leave.

It was too cold, and eventually the naughty girl began to feel really sick. She cried out for help, but nobody was around to listen.

Finally, after days and nights of suffering, the powerful king decided that the punishment was enough. He helped the naughty girl down from the hill, and told her never to break his laws again.

The naughty girl promised she never would, and from then on she was a happy and law-abiding person.

Sam was a cat who liked to sleep on the sofa. He did not like to share the sofa with anyone. He was ignorant and mean to the other animals in the house.

One day, Molly the dog came to the sofa. She wanted to lie down and rest. She saw Sam sleeping on the sofa. She said, "Excuse me, Sam, can I have some space on the sofa?"

Sam opened one eye and looked at Molly. He said, "No, this is my sofa. Go away, you silly dog. You have a bed in the corner. Leave me alone."

Molly was sad and angry. She said, "That's not fair, Sam. You are not the boss of the sofa. You are selfish and rude. I have a right to be on the sofa too."

Sam did not care. He said, "I don't care. I was here first. Go find another place to sleep. This is my sofa and I'm not moving."

Molly had an idea. She saw a mop in the kitchen. She grabbed the mop with her mouth and ran to the sofa. She said, "Fine, Sam, if you won't share the sofa, I'll make you share."

She swung the mop at Sam and hit him with the wet end. Sam was startled and wet. He jumped off the sofa and hissed at Molly. He said, "Hey, what are you doing? Stop that, you crazy dog. You're ruining my fur."

Molly said, "Now you know how it feels to be bothered. Maybe next time you'll be nicer and share the sofa."

She put the mop down and stretched on the sofa. She said, "Ahh, this is much better. The sofa is big enough for both of us, Sam. Why don't you come back and join me?"

Sam was still angry and wet. He said, "No, thank you. I don't want to be near you or your mop. You're a bad dog and I don't like you."

He walked away and found another place to sleep. He was still ignorant and mean, but Molly was happy and smart. She enjoyed the sofa and learned to use the mop.

Anna and Ben went to the park with their mom. They saw a big lake with many birds. They saw ducks, geese, and swans. Anna liked the swans the most. They were white and graceful. She wanted to touch one.

"Mom, can I touch a swan?" Anna asked.

"No, dear, you can't. Swans are not friendly. They can bite you or hurt you with their wings. You have to stay away from them," mom said.

But Anna did not listen. She saw a swan that was close to the shore. She ran to it and tried to grab its neck. The swan was angry. It hissed and flapped its wings. It bit Anna's hand and made her cry.

"Ow, ow, ow! Mom, help!" Anna screamed.

Mom ran to Anna and pulled her away from the swan. She checked her hand and saw a small cut. She took a pink band-aid from her bag and put it on Anna's hand.

"There, there. It's okay. The swan did not mean to hurt you. It was just scared. You should not try to touch wild animals. They need their space and respect," mom said.

"I'm sorry, mom. I was curious. I wanted to see the swan. It was so pretty," Anna said.

"I know, dear. Swans are pretty, but they are not toys. You can look at them from a distance, but you can't destroy them. Destroy means to break or damage something. You don't want to destroy the swans, do you?" mom said.

"No, mom. I don't want to destroy the swans. I want to be nice to them. Can I say sorry to the swan?" Anna said.

"Sure, you can. But you have to be quiet and gentle. And you have to stay with me. Come on, let's go back to the lake and see if the swan is still there," mom said.

Anna and Ben followed mom to the lake. They saw the same swan swimming with its friends. Anna waved to it and said, "Sorry, swan. I won't bother you again. You are very beautiful. Bye, swan."

The swan looked at Anna and nodded its head. It seemed to forgive her. Anna smiled and felt better. She learned a new word and a new lesson. She decided to be more careful with animals and not to destroy them. She hugged mom and Ben and said, "I love you, mom. I love you, Ben. And I love swans, too."

Once upon a time, there was a little bunny. She was so small and soft and her fur was very fluffy. Every morning, she liked to hop around the meadow in the sunshine. 

One morning, the bunny came across a special treat - honey! She had never seen honey before, and she was so excited. She hopped over to the honey and licked it. It tasted so sweet and she wanted more! 

So she hopped around the meadow, trying to find more honey. But the bunny was very careless and didn't look where she was going. She hopped right into a big mud puddle! 

The bunny was very sad, but then she spotted something else - honeybees! She watched them fly around the meadow and she followed them. Sure enough, they flew to a hive filled with honey. The bunny was so happy! She hopped around and ate as much honey as she wanted. 

From that day on, the little bunny was very careful when she hopped around the meadow. Whenever she found honey, she shared it with her friends so that everyone could enjoy it!

Every day the girl was getting better and better at caring for her teeth. She loved the feeling of having a perfect smile. 

One day, she went to the dentist. The dentist said she was doing a great job taking care of her teeth. She was very proud of herself for spending so much time on her teeth. 

The girl smiled a big, perfect smile. She knew that if she kept spending time on her teeth, they would stay perfect forever!

Once upon a time there was a big mountain. Everyone wanted to get to the top, but it was very hard. It was so tall that people couldn't see it.

One special day, a brave man decided to try and get to the top. He was determined that he would make it! He started climbing and climbing and soon he found himself closer to the top than anyone had ever been before.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She was very curious and loved to explore. One day, she was walking in the park when she saw a butterfly. She followed the butterfly and it led her to a tree. There was a boy named Max sitting under the tree.

Lily said, "Hi, my name is Lily. What are you doing?"

Max replied, "I am giving myself a massage. It feels good."

Lily was curious and asked, "Can I try?"

Lily said, "Wow, you're strong! Can you show me how to snap a twig too?"

Once upon a time, in a big forest, there lived a hairy bear. The bear had a big heart and loved to comfort his friends when they were sad. One day, the bear's best friend, a little bird, could not fly. The bird was very sad and scared.

The bear wanted to help the bird fly again. He thought about what he could do. He looked around and saw a big leaf. The bear had an idea. He put the leaf on the ground and asked the bird to sit on it. The bear then took a big breath with his big lung and blew the leaf with the bird on it.

The leaf with the bird on it flew up into the sky. The bird was so happy that he could fly again. The bear was very proud of himself for helping his friend. The bird thanked the bear for his help and comfort. From that day on, the bear and the bird were the best of friends and they lived happily ever after.

Tom and Lily were friends who liked to travel. They had a big red car that could go very fast. One day, they decided to go to the farm and see the animals.

"Look, Lily, there are cows and sheep and pigs!" Tom said, pointing out of the window.

"I like the pigs, they are funny and pink," Lily said. "Can we feed them?"

They parked the car and got out. They saw a man with a hat and a shovel. He was putting hay in a big pile.

"Hello, sir, can we feed the pigs?" Tom asked.

"Hello, kids, yes, you can. Here, take some hay and throw it to them. They love it," the farmer said, giving them some hay.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and explore the world around her. One day, she found a butterfly on a flower. She picked it up and examined it closely. The butterfly had pretty wings with lots of colors.

Anna was a girl who liked to go on trips with her family. She always had a big bag with her toys, books and clothes. She liked to unpack her bag when she got to a new place and see what she could play with.

One day, Anna and her family went to a big house in the woods. It was her grandma's house, but Anna had never been there before. She was excited to see what was inside. She ran to her room and opened her bag. She took out her doll, her puzzle and her crayons. She put them on the bed and looked around.

The room was very old and had many things that Anna did not know. There was a big closet with a lock, a dresser with a mirror and a shelf with books and pictures. Anna saw something shiny on the shelf. She climbed on a chair and reached for it. It was a small box with a key. Anna was curious. She wanted to see what was in the box. She turned the key and opened the lid.

Inside the box, there was a necklace with a pendant. The pendant was a star with a blue stone in the middle. It sparkled in the light. Anna thought it was very pretty. She put the necklace around her neck and looked in the mirror. She felt like a princess.

"Anna, what are you doing?" She heard her mom's voice from the door. Anna turned around and smiled.

"Look, mom, I found a necklace. It was in a box on the shelf. Can I keep it?" She asked.

Her mom looked surprised and came closer. She looked at the necklace and the box. She frowned.

"Anna, this is not yours. This is grandma's. It is very old and very special. It is a family treasure. Grandma told me a story about it. She said it was a gift from a mysterious friend who lived in the stars. He gave it to her when she was a little girl, like you. He said it was a sign of their friendship and that he would always watch over her. Grandma loves this necklace very much. You should not take it without asking. You should put it back in the box and on the shelf. Maybe grandma will tell you the story later, if you are good." She said.

Anna felt sorry. She did not mean to make her mom angry or to take something that was not hers. She took off the necklace and put it back in the box. She closed the lid and locked it. She put the box on the shelf and climbed down from the chair.

"I'm sorry, mom. I did not know. It was so pretty. I just wanted to see it. I will not touch it again. I will ask grandma to tell me the story. Can I still play with my toys?" She said.

Her mom hugged her and kissed her. She was not angry anymore. She was glad that Anna was honest and kind.

"Of course you can, sweetie. You can play with your toys and have fun. But remember, some things are not for playing. They are for keeping and cherishing. They have stories and memories that make them special. Maybe one day, when you are older, grandma will give you the necklace. But for now, you have to respect it and leave it alone. Okay?" She said.

Anna nodded and smiled. She understood. She was happy to have her mom and her toys. She was also happy to have a grandma who had a mysterious friend in the stars. She wondered what he looked like and what he did. She hoped he would watch over her too. She decided to ask grandma later, when they had tea and cookies. She thought it would be a nice story to hear.

Once upon a time there was a little boy. He liked to count. He counted the stars in the night sky. He counted the steps to school.

One day, he heard some strange noises coming from the other room. He peeked through the door, and he saw some jazz music. He liked it, so he began to count along with the music. 

He liked jazz very much. When he wasn't counting, he would listen to the jazz and sway in time to the beat. He thought it was the best sound ever. 

His mom came in and said "That's a bad kind of music." But the little boy said that he thought the jazz was good. His mom shook her head and left the room.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily was very tired and needed to take a nap. She went to her room and found her bed was empty. She looked for her favorite teddy bear, but it was missing too. 

Lily's mom came in and saw that Lily was sad. She asked what was wrong, and Lily told her about her missing teddy bear. Mom said she would help Lily find it. They looked all over the house, but they couldn't find it. 

Finally, Lily's mom suggested that they accept that the teddy bear might be lost forever. Lily was sad, but she knew her mom was right. She got into bed and fell asleep, dreaming of her lost teddy bear.

Once upon a time there was girl. She had lots of lovely clothes to wear. She was very independent and never asked for help. 
One day, the girl went out to play. As she was playing an increase happened. The increase was so big it was scary! It made the girl run back home. 
When she got there, her clothes had all grown too big. No matter what she tried, the clothes kept increasing in size. 
The girl was very sad. She had no clothes that fit her and she couldn't be independent anymore. 
The girl never saw the increase coming, so she never got her clothes back. She had to ask for help every day and was never independent again.

Lily and Tom were friends who liked to play in the park. They liked to run, swing, slide and climb. They also liked to collect pebbles of different colors and shapes. They had a big box where they kept their pebbles at home.

One day, they found a very shiny pebble that looked like a star. They both wanted it for their box. They started to pull and tug at the pebble, each saying "It's mine, it's mine!"

"Stop it, you two!" said Mom, who was watching them. "You are being selfish. You should share the pebble, not fight over it."

"But it's so pretty, Mom!" said Lily. "I saw it first!"

"No, I did!" said Tom.

Mom sighed. She had an idea. She took the pebble and said "How about this? I will tell you a joke, and whoever laughs first can have the pebble. OK?"

Lily and Tom nodded. They liked jokes. They hoped Mom would tell a funny one.

Mom said "What do you call a fish that wears a bow tie?"

Lily and Tom thought hard. They did not know. They looked at Mom, waiting for the answer.

Mom said "Sofishticated!"

Lily and Tom did not understand the word. They looked at each other, confused. Then they started to giggle. They thought Mom was making a silly sound. They laughed louder and louder.

Mom smiled. She said "You both laughed, so you both win. You can take turns to play with the pebble, and then put it in your box together. How does that sound?"

Lily and Tom agreed. They hugged Mom and thanked her for the joke. They decided to share the pebble and be nice to each other. They learned that sharing was more fun than being selfish.

Once upon a time, there was a little rabbit named Benny. Benny loved to play in the fields and eat carrots. One day, while Benny was hopping around, he saw a big hole in the ground. It was very dark and gloomy inside.

Benny hopped closer and saw that it was an entrance to an underground tunnel. Curious, he hopped inside. It was very dark and he could barely see anything. Suddenly, he heard some giggling and saw some shadows moving around. 

It was a group of mice who were teasing him! They were making fun of his long ears and fluffy tail. Benny felt very sad and didn't know what to do. He wanted to leave the tunnel and go back to the sunny fields. But the mice wouldn't let him go. 

Benny thought hard and came up with a plan. He pretended to be scared and started to cry. The mice felt bad and stopped teasing him. Benny quickly hopped away and never went back to the gloomy underground tunnel again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys, especially her teddy bear. One day, her mommy said they were going on a journey to visit grandma and grandpa. Lily was excited!

Mommy packed their bags and they got in the car. The journey was long, but they sang songs and played games to pass the time. When they arrived, grandma and grandpa were so happy to see them. They hugged and kissed Lily and gave her lots of treats.

Lily was so happy and had fun playing with her new friends. It was a busy day, but Lily felt loved and happy.

Lily was anxious. She wanted to wear her new dress to the party. It was pink and shiny and had a big bow. But her mom said it was too cold outside and she had to wear a sweater and pants.

"No, no, no!" Lily cried. "I want my dress! I want my dress!"

"Lily, calm down," her mom said. "You can wear your dress inside the house, but you need to put on something warm over it when we go out. It's snowing and you don't want to get sick, do you?"

Lily pouted. She didn't like the sweater and pants. They were boring and scratchy. She wanted to look pretty and have fun. She didn't care about the snow.

"Please, mom, please," she begged. "Can I just wear my dress? Please, please, please?"

Her mom sighed. She knew Lily loved her dress, but she also wanted her to be safe and comfortable. She had an idea.

"How about this, Lily?" she said. "You can wear your dress, but you also have to wear this coat and these boots. They are pink and shiny too, and they have bows. See? They match your dress. And you can take them off when we get to the party. How does that sound?"

Lily looked at the coat and the boots. They were pink and shiny and had bows. They did match her dress. She smiled. She liked them. They were pretty and warm.

"Okay, mom," she said. "I'll wear them. Thank you, mom. You're the best."

Her mom hugged her. "You're welcome, Lily. You're the best too. Now let's go to the party and have fun."

Sara and Ben are playing with blocks. They want to make a big tower. Sara has a ruler. She likes to measure things.

"Look, Ben, this block is ten long," Sara says, showing him the ruler. "How long is your block?"

Ben puts his block next to Sara's. "My block is eight long," he says. "Your block is longer."

Sara nods. "We can use the ruler to measure our tower. Then we will know how high it is."

They start to stack the blocks on top of each other. They measure each layer with the ruler. They count the numbers out loud.

"One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten. Our tower is ten high!" Sara says.

"Wow, that's very high!" Ben says. "Can we make it higher?"

"Let's try," Sara says. "But we have to be careful. The tower might fall down."

They add more blocks to the tower. They measure it again.

"Eleven, twelve, thirteen, fourteen, fifteen. Our tower is fifteen high!" Ben says.

"That's amazing!" Sara says. "But we don't have any more blocks. We used them all."

They look at their tower with pride. They smile at each other.

The ruler is very useful. It helps them measure their tower. They like to measure things.

But then they hear a voice.

"Kids, it's time for lunch!" Mom says.

They look at the clock. It shows twelve. It is time to eat.

They run to the kitchen. They leave their tower behind.

They will measure it again later. They hope it doesn't fall down.

Once upon a time there was a three year old called Tom. Tom had a job to do. He needed to sort out the freezer.

Tom was frustrated. He tried and tried, but he kept mixing things up. The piles of food were never quite right. It felt like it was an impossible task. He felt miserable.

Suddenly, his mum walked in. "What seems to be the problem?" she asked.
Tom explained to her what he was trying to do. His mum said, "No worries, I'll help you sort it out." 

Tom's mum began to put the piles of food into their correct places. She worked quickly and efficiently. 

Tom felt relieved. He joined his mum in organising the freezer. Together, they managed to do it. 

Tom couldn't believe it. With his mum's help, he had finally sorted the freezer. 

Tom was so pleased that he gave his mum a big hug. His mum smiled with relief "Well done," she said. 

Tom was proud of himself. He had done it! He felt much happier than he did before.

Brownie was really scared, but then he saw something. It was a brown bean! He picked it up and kept it in his pocket.

He kept walking and looking for a way out of the forest, but he got more and more lost. Suddenly, he saw a big, brown bear! He was so scared, he almost fell to the ground.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there lived a kind and patient judge. He liked to help people and make them happy. One day, a little girl named Lucy came to him with a problem.

Lucy had a toy she loved very much, but her friend Tom wanted to play with it too. The patient judge listened to both Lucy and Tom, and then he had an idea. He nodded and said, "Why don't you both share the toy and play together?"

Lucy and Tom thought about it and then they both nodded too. They decided to share the toy and play together. They had lots of fun and became very good friends. The patient judge was happy to see them playing and thanked them for listening to him. And they all lived happily ever after.

Once there was a little girl called Joely. She loved to play outside. One day she came upon a really cool foot. It was different from any foot she had ever seen before. She felt really excited, so she reached out to take it. Suddenly, she felt really uncomfortable. 

Joely tried to take the foot, but it didn't want to come with her. She was so determined that she pulled it harder, and it would not move! Joely realized too late that she should never have touched something that didn't belong to her. 

From this story we learn a valuable lesson: never touch something that isn't yours! Even if it looks fun and exciting, it can end in an uncomfortable way. Joely learned her lesson, and she never tried to take something that wasn't hers ever again.

Once upon a time there was a delicate triangle. It was very pretty, shining brightly in the sun. It called out to all the animals and insects in the meadow. "Come play with me!" it sang.

So the animals and insects all came together and made a big circle around the triangle. The triangle was so happy! Then it invited all the creatures to come together to make a game.

The butterfly was the first one to answer the triangle's invitation. He fluttered over to the triangle and said "Sure, let's play!" He quickly collected some sticks and arranged them in the shape of the triangle.

The other animals and insects joined in, each one helping to build the triangle bigger and stronger, until it was a beautiful, perfect triangle. 

They all cheered for the triangle and played together and laughed. From that day on, the triangle stayed in the meadow and was a safe and happy place for all the creatures to come and play.

Anna and Ben are twins. They like to play with their toys in their room. But their mom says they have to clean up their mess. She says they have to carry their stuff to the toy box.

Anna and Ben do not want to clean up. They want to keep playing. They say, "No, mom, we do not want to carry our stuff. It is too hard. We are too tired."

Mom is not happy. She says, "You have to carry your stuff, or you will not get any cookies. Your room is very smelly. It smells like old socks and cheese. You have to make it nice and clean."

Anna and Ben do not like smelly things. They do not want to miss the cookies. They decide to carry their stuff. But they do not agree on how to do it.

Anna wants to carry her stuff first. She says, "I have more stuff than you. I have dolls and books and puzzles. You only have cars and balls and blocks. Let me carry my stuff first."

Ben does not like that. He says, "No, I have more stuff than you. I have big stuff. You have small stuff. Let me carry my stuff first."

Anna and Ben start to fight. They pull and push and shout. They make more mess. They make mom more angry.

Mom comes to their room. She sees the mess. She sees the fight. She says, "Stop it, Anna and Ben. You are being very naughty. You have to share and help each other. You have to carry your stuff together. Or you will not get any cookies at all."

Anna and Ben do not want to be naughty. They do not want to make mom angry. They do not want to lose the cookies. They say, "Sorry, mom. We will share and help. We will carry our stuff together."

Anna and Ben stop fighting. They start carrying their stuff. They take turns. They say, "Please" and "Thank you". They make their room nice and clean. They make mom happy. They get their cookies. They say, "We love you, mom. And we love our stuff. But we do not love smelly things."
